text: To evaluate the efficacy of a Social Cognitive Theory-based Internet intervention designed to promote and maintain leisure-time physical activity in university-aged female students in Thailand . The 3-month intervention was delivered through a website and e-mails with a follow-up evaluation 3 months after the end of the intervention . Female students ( N = 220 ) were allocated to 4 parallel groups . Significant increases in steps / day , weekly leisure-time activity score , self-efficacy , outcome expectations , and self-regulation , and reduced resting heart rate were observed at the end of the intervention . With the exception of resting heart rate , the intervention effects on these variables also remained at the follow-up . The Internet intervention program was effective in promoting and maintaining leisure-time physical activity in university-aged female students .
rewrite: This study assessed the effectiveness of an Internet intervention grounded in Social Cognitive Theory, aimed at encouraging and sustaining leisure-time physical activity among university-aged female students in Thailand. The 3-month program was implemented via a website and email, with a follow-up assessment conducted 3 months post-intervention. Participants (N = 220) were assigned to four parallel groups. By the intervention's conclusion, significant improvements were noted in daily step count, weekly leisure-time activity scores, self-efficacy, outcome expectations, and self-regulation, alongside a decrease in resting heart rate. Except for resting heart rate, the positive effects on these measures persisted at follow-up. The Internet-based program proved effective in promoting and maintaining leisure-time physical activity in this student population.

text: Increased utilization of online medical information seeking demands investigation of potentially detrimental effects of these activities . The present study investigated whether viewing medical websites may adversely affect anxiety sensitivity ( AS ) , a well-established risk factor for the development of psychopathology . Participants ( N = 52 ) were randomly assigned to view medical symptom related websites or general health and wellness control websites . AS was measured before and after the website viewing . Individuals in the medical website group reported higher AS compared to the control group at post-manipulation after controlling for baseline health anxiety and baseline AS . Additionally , intolerance of uncertainty ( IU ) , an individual difference variable assessing negative beliefs about uncertainty , significantly moderated this effect such that medical website viewing only affected AS in participants with high IU but not in participants with low IU . The limitations of the current study include the lack of individualization of the website viewing and the short duration of the website viewing . The results of this study provide initial evidence that exposure to online medical information could increase risk for anxiety psychopathology in individuals with elevated IU . Additionally , these results provide support for a learning based model of the etiology of AS .
rewrite: Growing reliance on online medical information necessitates examining potential negative impacts of these behaviors. This study explored whether accessing medical websites might negatively influence anxiety sensitivity (AS), a recognized risk factor for psychopathology development. Participants (N = 52) were randomly assigned to view either medical symptom-related websites or general health and wellness control sites. AS was assessed before and after website exposure. After adjusting for baseline health anxiety and baseline AS, the medical website group showed higher AS than the control group post-intervention. Furthermore, intolerance of uncertainty (IU), a trait measuring negative views about uncertainty, significantly moderated this effect, with medical website viewing affecting AS only in high-IU participants, not in low-IU individuals. Study limitations include non-individualized website content and brief exposure duration. These findings offer preliminary evidence that online medical information exposure may elevate anxiety psychopathology risk in those with high IU. They also lend support to a learning-based model for AS etiology.

text: To determine the effects of Thai massage on muscle spasticity in young people with cerebral palsy . Young people with spastic diplegia , aged 6-18 years old , were recruitedfrom the Srisungwan School in Khon Kaen Province . Spasticity of right quadriceps femoris muscles was measured using Modified Ashworth Scale ( MAS ) at pre - and immediately post 30-minute session of Thai massage . Thai massage was applied on the lower back and lower limbs . Wilcoxon Signed Ranks test was used to compare the outcome between pre - and post treatment . Seventeen participants with spastic diplegia aged 13.71 + / - 3.62 years old participated . A significant difference of MAS was observed between pre - and post treatment ( 1 + , 1 ; p < 0.01 ) . No adverse events were reported . Thai massage decreased muscle spasticity and is suggested to be an alternative treatmentfor reducing spasticity in young people with cerebral palsy .
rewrite: This study assessed the impact of Thai massage on muscle spasticity in youth with cerebral palsy. Adolescents with spastic diplegia, aged 6-18 years, were enrolled from Srisungwan School in Khon Kaen Province. Spasticity in the right quadriceps femoris was evaluated using the Modified Ashworth Scale (MAS) before and right after a 30-minute Thai massage session applied to the lower back and lower limbs. The Wilcoxon Signed Ranks test compared pre- and post-treatment outcomes. Seventeen participants with spastic diplegia, averaging 13.71 ± 3.62 years, took part. A statistically significant difference in MAS scores was found between pre- and post-treatment (1+, 1; p < 0.01). No adverse events occurred. Thai massage reduced muscle spasticity, indicating its potential as an alternative therapy for decreasing spasticity in young individuals with cerebral palsy.

text: At present , school-age children suffer high levels of chronic stress that could produce potentially long-lasting effects . The aim of this pilot study was to evaluate the effects of mind-body integration practices and cooperative activities on stress levels and social interaction in 7 - to 9-year-old children . We performed an intervention program once a week during 2 months in which children performed mind-body integration practices and cooperative activities . Our findings showed that these practices reduced cortisol levels and increased social connectedness . Moreover , we found that most of the children used the learned mind-body integration practices in stressful situations in their homes , even 5 months after the intervention . Our results demonstrated the positive impact of these helpful tools and the great plasticity of children 's behavior , which enabled them to incorporate healthy habits . Overall , the intervention enhanced health at an individual level and favored social network diversity at a group level . Our research illustrates how children can incorporate techniques that help them cope with stressful moments and reveals the effectiveness of this experience in reducing cortisol levels . This study contributes to the understanding of how mind-body integration practices and social connectedness can be helpful in reducing chronic stress , a topic that , to the best of our knowledge , has been little studied in children .
rewrite: Currently, school-age children experience significant chronic stress that may lead to enduring consequences. This pilot study aimed to assess the impact of mind-body integration practices and cooperative activities on stress and social interaction among children aged 7 to 9 years. An intervention program was conducted weekly over two months, involving mind-body exercises and group cooperation. Results indicated that these activities lowered cortisol levels and boosted social connectedness. Additionally, most children applied the learned mind-body techniques in stressful home situations, even five months post-intervention. The findings highlight the benefits of these tools and children's behavioral adaptability, allowing them to adopt healthy habits. The intervention improved individual well-being and promoted diverse social networks at the group level. This research shows how children can adopt strategies to manage stress and confirms the effectiveness of such practices in lowering cortisol. It advances knowledge on how mind-body integration and social connectedness can alleviate chronic stress, a subject that remains underexplored in children.

text: ADHD affects between 2 % and 8 % of college students and is associated with broad functional impairment . No prior randomized controlled trials with this population have been published . The present study is a pilot randomized controlled trial evaluating dialectical behavior therapy ( DBT ) group skills training adapted for college students with ADHD . Thirty-three undergraduates with ADHD between ages 18 and 24 were randomized to receive either DBT group skills training or skills handouts during an 8-week intervention phase . ADHD symptoms , executive functioning ( EF ) , and related outcomes were assessed at baseline , post-treatment , and 3-month follow-up . Participants receiving DBT group skills training showed greater treatment response rates ( 59-65 % vs. 19-25 % ) and clinical recovery rates ( 53-59 % vs. 6-13 % ) on ADHD symptoms and EF , and greater improvements in quality of life . DBT group skills training may be efficacious , acceptable , and feasible for treating ADHD among college students . A larger randomized trial is needed for further evaluation .
rewrite: ADHD impacts approximately 2% to 8% of college students and is linked to significant functional difficulties. No previous randomized controlled trials focusing on this group have been reported. This pilot randomized controlled trial examines dialectical behavior therapy (DBT) group skills training tailored for college students with ADHD. Thirty-three undergraduates with ADHD, aged 18 to 24, were randomly assigned to either DBT group skills training or skills handouts over an 8-week intervention period. ADHD symptoms, executive functioning (EF), and related measures were evaluated at baseline, post-treatment, and a 3-month follow-up. Those in the DBT group demonstrated higher treatment response rates (59-65% vs. 19-25%) and clinical recovery rates (53-59% vs. 6-13%) for ADHD symptoms and EF, along with greater enhancements in quality of life. DBT group skills training appears promising, acceptable, and feasible for addressing ADHD in college students. A larger randomized trial is required for additional assessment.

text: In spatial neglect , the functional benefit of rehabilitation methods is subject to debate . A few studies have reported that galvanic vestibular stimulation ( GVS ) is efficacious in spatial neglect . The objective of the present study was to establish whether the effects of GVS persist after the end of stimulation . Four patients with pathological rightward deviation in a bisection task at least three months after right hemisphere stroke . A single-blind , randomized crossover design was used to assess the effects of GVS on performance in line bisection and star cancellation tasks under three different conditions ( cathode-right , cathode-left and sham stimulation ) . There were no significant differences in the performance of either task following GVS ( relative to sham stimulation ) . Galvanic vestibular stimulation did not reduce spatial neglect symptoms in any of the stimulation conditions . Further studies are necessary to understand the disparity between our results and those reported in the literature . Repeated sessions , a higher current intensity and/or alternating-current stimulation may improve this method before it can be used clinically .
rewrite: In spatial neglect, the therapeutic value of rehabilitation approaches remains contentious. Some studies have indicated that galvanic vestibular stimulation (GVS) is effective for spatial neglect. This study aimed to determine if GVS effects continue after stimulation ceases. Four patients with persistent rightward deviation in a bisection task, at least three months post right hemisphere stroke, were included. A single-blind, randomized crossover design evaluated GVS impact on line bisection and star cancellation tasks across three conditions (cathode-right, cathode-left, and sham stimulation). No significant differences in task performance were observed after GVS (compared to sham stimulation). Galvanic vestibular stimulation did not alleviate spatial neglect symptoms under any stimulation condition. Additional research is needed to reconcile the discrepancy between our findings and existing literature. Repeated sessions, increased current intensity, and/or alternating-current stimulation might enhance this method for potential clinical application.

text: To compare the effects of sprint training with or without ball carry on the sprint performance of elite rugby league players . Twenty-four elite rugby league players were divided into a ball-carry group ( BC ; n = 12 ) and a no-ball-carry group ( NBC ; n = 12 ) . The players of the BC group were required to catch and carry the ball under 1 arm during each sprint , whereas the NBC group performed sprints without carrying a ball . The 8-wk training intervention took place during the precompetitive phase of the season and consisted of 2 sessions/wk . Sprint performance was measured before and after the training intervention with 40-m linear sprints performed under 2 conditions : with and without ball carry . Split times of 10 , 20 , and 40 m were recorded for further analysis . A 3-way ( group time condition ) factorial ANOVA was performed to compare changes in sprint performance with and without the ball , before and after the training intervention for both BC and NBC training groups Results : The BC and NBC groups experienced similar improvements in 10 - , 20 - , and 40-m sprint times and accelerations , regardless of the condition under which the sprint tests were performed ( P = .19 ) . Sprint training while carrying a rugby ball is as effective as sprint training without carrying a rugby ball for improving the sprint performance of elite rugby league players .
rewrite: This study examined the impact of sprint training with or without ball carry on elite rugby league players' sprint performance. Twenty-four elite players were assigned to either a ball-carry group (BC; n=12) or a no-ball-carry group (NBC; n=12). The BC group performed sprints while catching and carrying a ball under one arm, whereas the NBC group sprinted without a ball. The 8-week intervention, conducted during the precompetitive season, involved two weekly sessions. Sprint performance was assessed via 40-m linear sprints, both with and without ball carry, before and after training. Split times at 10, 20, and 40 m were recorded. A three-way (group × time × condition) ANOVA was used to analyze changes. Results showed that both BC and NBC groups achieved comparable improvements in 10-, 20-, and 40-m sprint times and accelerations, irrespective of test condition (P=.19). Thus, sprint training with a rugby ball is equally effective as training without a ball for enhancing sprint performance in elite rugby league players.

text: Musicians are a prone group to suffer from working-related musculoskeletal disorder ( WRMD ) . Conventional solutions to control musculoskeletal pain include pharmacological treatment and rehabilitation programs but their efficiency is sometimes disappointing . The aim of this research is to study the immediate effects of Tuina techniques on WRMD of professional orchestra musicians from the north of Portugal . We performed a prospective , controlled , single-blinded , randomized study . Professional orchestra musicians with a diagnosis of WRMD were randomly distributed into the experimental group ( n = 39 ) and the control group ( n = 30 ) . During an individual interview , Chinese diagnosis took place and treatment points were chosen . Real acupoints were treated by Tuina techniques into the experimental group and non-specific skin points were treated into the control group . Pain was measured by verbal numerical scale before and immediately after intervention . After one treatment session , pain was reduced in 91.8 % of the cases for the experimental group and 7.9 % for the control group . Although results showed that Tuina techniques are effectively reducing WRMD in professional orchestra musicians of the north of Portugal , further investigations with stronger measurements , double-blinding designs and bigger simple sizes are needed .
rewrite: Musicians are a group particularly susceptible to work-related musculoskeletal disorders (WRMD). Traditional approaches to managing musculoskeletal pain, such as medication and rehabilitation, often yield unsatisfactory results. This study investigates the immediate impact of Tuina techniques on WRMD among professional orchestra musicians in northern Portugal. A prospective, controlled, single-blinded, randomized trial was conducted. Professional musicians diagnosed with WRMD were randomly assigned to either an experimental group (n=39) or a control group (n=30). Through individual interviews, a Chinese diagnostic assessment was performed to select treatment points. The experimental group received Tuina at real acupoints, while the control group received treatment at non-specific skin points. Pain levels were assessed using a verbal numerical scale before and right after the intervention. Following a single session, pain reduction occurred in 91.8% of the experimental group and 7.9% of the control group. While findings indicate Tuina techniques effectively alleviate WRMD in these musicians, further research with more robust measures, double-blinded designs, and larger sample sizes is warranted.

text: Rumination is one of the hallmark characteristics of both anxiety disorders and depression , and has been linked to deficient executive functioning , particularly working memory ( WM ) . Previous findings show that working memory capacity can be increased through training . The current study explored whether an adaptive stand-alone WM training could increase WMC and consequently reduce rumination , anxiety and depression by means of a double-blind randomized controlled trial in a sample of 98 patients with symptoms of anxiety and/or depression . No positive effect of training on WMC was found . In addition , the results show that a WM training was not associated with a reduction of rumination , depression , nor anxiety . The high drop-out rate in both groups ( 20.11 % from pre - to post-training ) and the overrepresentation of men and use of anti-depressants in the placebo group might have influenced the results . Furthermore , expectations and perceptions about the training might have interacted with performance on WM tasks . Overall , results show that a stand-alone WM training in patients with symptoms of anxiety and/or depression does not result in reduced rumination nor in reduced symptoms of depression and anxiety . We discuss potential explanations for these findings .
rewrite: Rumination is a key feature of both anxiety disorders and depression, and has been associated with impaired executive functioning, especially working memory (WM). Prior research indicates that working memory capacity can be enhanced through training. This study investigated whether an adaptive, stand-alone WM training could improve WMC and thereby decrease rumination, anxiety, and depression, using a double-blind randomized controlled trial with 98 participants showing anxiety and/or depression symptoms. No beneficial effect of the training on WMC was observed. Moreover, the findings indicate that WM training did not correlate with reductions in rumination, depression, or anxiety. The high attrition rate in both groups (20.11% from pre- to post-training), along with an overrepresentation of men and antidepressant use in the placebo group, may have affected the outcomes. Additionally, expectations and perceptions regarding the training could have interacted with performance on WM tasks. In summary, the results demonstrate that a stand-alone WM training in individuals with anxiety and/or depression symptoms does not lead to decreased rumination or reduced symptoms of depression and anxiety. Possible explanations for these results are discussed.

text: To observe the sensitivity of stroke volume variation ( SVV ) for assessing volume change during induction period of general anesthesia . Patients who underwent orthopaedic surgery under general anesthesia and mechanical ventilation were divided into two groups randomly . Patients in the group were subjected to progressive central hypovolemia and correction of hypovolemia sequentially ; patients in the Group were exposed to hypervolemia alone . Each step was implemented after 5 minutes when the hemodynamics was stable . SVV and cardiac index ( CI ) were recorded , and Pearson 's product-moment correlation was used to analyze correlation between SVV and CI . Forty patients were included in this study , 20 cases in each group . For group patients , SVV was increased significantly along with blood volume reduction , and changes in CI were negatively correlated with changes in SVV ( r = -0.605 , P < 0.01 ) ; SVV decreased significantly along with correction of blood volume ; changes in CI were negatively correlated with changes in SVV ( r = -0.651 , P < 0.01 ) . For group patients , along with blood volume increase , SVV did not change significantly ; changes in CI revealed no significant correlation with changes in SVV ( r = 0.067 , P > 0.05 ) . SVV is a useful indicator for hypovolemia , but not for hypervolemia .
rewrite: To evaluate the sensitivity of stroke volume variation (SVV) in detecting volume changes during general anesthesia induction. Orthopaedic surgery patients under general anesthesia with mechanical ventilation were randomly assigned to two groups. One group underwent progressive central hypovolemia followed by volume correction; the other group experienced hypervolemia alone. Each phase was initiated after 5 minutes of hemodynamic stability. SVV and cardiac index (CI) were measured, and Pearson’s correlation was applied to assess their relationship. The study included 40 patients, with 20 in each group. In the hypovolemia group, SVV rose significantly as blood volume decreased, and CI changes were negatively correlated with SVV changes (r = -0.605, P < 0.01); SVV declined markedly with volume correction, and CI changes remained negatively correlated (r = -0.651, P < 0.01). In the hypervolemia group, SVV did not change significantly with increased blood volume, and no significant correlation was found between CI and SVV changes (r = 0.067, P > 0.05). SVV is a reliable marker for hypovolemia but not for hypervolemia.

text: To evaluate the efficacy of faculty-led problem-based learning ( PBL ) vs online simulated-patient case in fourth-year ( P4 ) pharmacy students . Fourth-year pharmacy students were randomly assigned to participate in either online branched-case learning using a virtual simulation platform or a small-group discussion . Preexperience and postexperience student assessments and a survey instrument were completed . While there were no significant differences in the preexperience test scores between the groups , there was a significant increase in scores in both the virtual-patient group and the PBL group between the preexperience and postexperience tests . The PBL group had higher postexperience test scores ( 74.811.7 ) than did the virtual-patient group ( 66.513.6 ) ( p = 0.001 ) . The PBL method demonstrated significantly greater improvement in postexperience test scores than did the virtual-patient method . Both were successful learning methods , suggesting that a diverse approach to simulated patient cases may reach more student learning styles .
rewrite: This study assessed the effectiveness of faculty-led problem-based learning (PBL) compared to an online simulated-patient case for fourth-year (P4) pharmacy students. P4 students were randomly assigned to either an online branched-case learning activity using a virtual simulation platform or a small-group discussion. Student assessments and a survey were administered before and after the experience. Although preexperience test scores showed no significant differences between groups, both the virtual-patient group and the PBL group showed a significant score increase from pre- to postexperience tests. The PBL group achieved higher postexperience test scores (74.8 ± 11.7) than the virtual-patient group (66.5 ± 13.6) (p = 0.001). The PBL method resulted in significantly greater improvement in postexperience scores than the virtual-patient method. Both approaches were effective, indicating that a varied strategy for simulated patient cases may accommodate diverse student learning styles.

text: To determine if training with a chicken wing model improves performance of endoscopic endonasal surgery ( EES ) with microvascular dissection . Randomized experimental study . A single-blinded randomized clinical trial of trainees with various levels of endoscopic experience was conducted to determine if prior training on a nonhuman model augments endoscopic skill and efficiency in a surrogate model for live surgery . Medical students , residents , and fellows were randomized to two groups : a control group that performed an endoscopic transantral internal maxillary artery dissection on a silicone-injected anatomical specimen , and an interventional group that underwent microvascular dissection training on a chicken wing model prior to performing the anatomic dissection on the cadaver specimen . Time to completion and quality of dissection were measured . A Mann-Whitney test demonstrated a significant improvement in time and quality outcomes respectively across all interventional groups , with the greatest improvements seen in participants with less endoscopic experience : medical students ( P = .032 , P = .008 ) , residents and fellows ( P = .016 , P = .032 ) . Prior training on the chicken wing model improves surgical performance in a surrogate model for live EES .
rewrite: To assess whether training with a chicken wing model enhances performance in endoscopic endonasal surgery (EES) involving microvascular dissection. A randomized experimental trial. A single-blinded randomized clinical trial involving trainees of varying endoscopic experience levels was performed to evaluate if prior training on a nonhuman model boosts endoscopic skill and efficiency in a surrogate model for live surgery. Medical students, residents, and fellows were randomly assigned to two groups: a control group that conducted an endoscopic transantral internal maxillary artery dissection on a silicone-injected anatomical specimen, and an interventional group that received microvascular dissection training on a chicken wing model before performing the anatomical dissection on the cadaver specimen. Time to completion and dissection quality were assessed. A Mann-Whitney test indicated significant improvements in both time and quality outcomes across all interventional groups, with the most notable gains observed in participants having less endoscopic experience: medical students (P = .032, P = .008), residents and fellows (P = .016, P = .032). Prior training on the chicken wing model enhances surgical performance in a surrogate model for live EES.

text: To explore the effect of intravariceal-mucosal sclerotherapy using small dose of sclerosant on the recurrence of esophageal varices . We randomly assigned 38 cirrhotic patients with previous variceal bleeding and high variceal pressure ( > 15.2 mmHg ) to receive endoscopic variceal ligation ( EVL ) and combined intravariceal and esophageal mucosal sclerotherapy ( combined group ) using small-volume sclerosant . The end-points of the study were rebleeding and recurrence of esophageal varices . During a median follow-up period of 16 mo , varices recurred in 1 patient in the combined group as compared with 7 patients in the EVL group ( P = 0.045 ) . Rebleeding occurred in 3 patients in the EVL group as compared with 1 patient in the combined group ( P = 0.687 ) . No patient died in the two groups . No significant differences were observed between the two groups with respect to serious adverse events . Intravariceal-mucosal sclerotherapy using small dose of sclerosant is more effective than EVL in decreasing the incidence of variceal recurrence for cirrhotic patients .
rewrite: To investigate the impact of low-dose intravariceal-mucosal sclerotherapy on esophageal varices recurrence. Thirty-eight cirrhotic patients with prior variceal bleeding and elevated variceal pressure (>15.2 mmHg) were randomized to undergo endoscopic variceal ligation (EVL) alone or EVL combined with intravariceal and mucosal sclerotherapy using a minimal sclerosant volume (combined group). Study outcomes included rebleeding and variceal recurrence. Over a median follow-up of 16 months, varices recurred in 1 patient in the combined group versus 7 in the EVL group (P = 0.045). Rebleeding occurred in 3 EVL patients compared to 1 in the combined group (P = 0.687). No deaths occurred in either group, and serious adverse events did not differ significantly between groups. Low-dose intravariceal-mucosal sclerotherapy is superior to EVL alone in reducing variceal recurrence among cirrhotic patients.

text: We compared 2 strategies for disseminating an evidence-based skin cancer prevention program . We evaluated the effects of 2 strategies ( basic vs enhanced ) for dissemination of the Pool Cool skin cancer prevention program in outdoor swimming pools on ( 1 ) program implementation , maintenance , and sustainability and ( 2 ) improvements in organizational and environmental supports for sun protection . The trial used a cluster-randomized design with pools as the unit of intervention and outcome . The enhanced group received extra incentives , reinforcement , feedback , and skill-building guidance . Surveys were collected in successive years ( 2003-2006 ) from managers of 435 pools in 33 metropolitan areas across the United States participating in the Pool Cool Diffusion Trial . Both treatment groups improved their implementation of the program , but pools in the enhanced condition had significantly greater overall maintenance of the program over 3 summers of participation . Furthermore , pools in the enhanced condition established and maintained significantly greater sun-safety policies and supportive environments over time . This study found that more intensive , theory-driven dissemination strategies can significantly enhance program implementation and maintenance of health-promoting environmental and policy changes . Future research is warranted through longitudinal follow-up to examine sustainability .
rewrite: We assessed two approaches for distributing an evidence-based skin cancer prevention initiative. The impact of two dissemination methods (basic versus enhanced) for the Pool Cool skin cancer prevention program at outdoor swimming pools was examined regarding (1) program execution, continuity, and long-term viability, and (2) enhancements in organizational and environmental support for sun safety. The study employed a cluster-randomized design with pools as the intervention and outcome unit. The enhanced group obtained additional incentives, reinforcement, feedback, and skill-development support. Surveys were gathered in consecutive years (2003–2006) from managers of 435 pools in 33 U.S. metropolitan areas involved in the Pool Cool Diffusion Trial. Both groups enhanced their program execution, but pools in the enhanced condition showed notably better overall program continuity across three summer seasons. Additionally, pools in the enhanced condition developed and sustained significantly stronger sun-safety policies and supportive environments over time. This research indicates that more intensive, theory-based dissemination approaches can substantially improve program execution and the durability of health-promoting environmental and policy modifications. Further longitudinal follow-up is needed to investigate long-term sustainability.

text: The aim of this study was to evaluate the surface roughness and morphology of enamel with a surface roughness tester and scanning electron microscopy after the removal of metal brackets and polishing . Ten orthodontic patients were selected for the study . At the conclusion of orthodontic treatment , their metal brackets were removed . For each patient , teeth on one side of the mouth were randomly chosen for finishing and polishing with aluminum oxide discs ( n = 10 ) . Teeth on the other side were finished with multilaminated carbide burs ( n = 10 ) . Dental replicas ( before and after tooth polishing ) were obtained with epoxy resin . Three surface roughness measurements were made in different directions with an angle of 120 among them , and a mean for each dental replica was calculated . The roughness data were statistically evaluated by repeated-measurements analysis of variance . Three specimens from each group were also used for scanning electron microscopy analysis . After resin removal , the average roughness in the carbide bur group ( 0.31 m ) was significantly greater than that in the aluminum oxide disc group ( 0.25 m ) . The aluminum oxide disc polishing system resulted in less enamel roughness than did the multilaminated carbide bur system .
rewrite: This study aimed to assess enamel surface roughness and morphology using a surface roughness tester and scanning electron microscopy following metal bracket removal and polishing. Ten orthodontic patients were included. After treatment completion, their metal brackets were taken off. For each patient, teeth on one side were randomly assigned for finishing and polishing with aluminum oxide discs (n=10). Teeth on the opposite side were finished using multilaminated carbide burs (n=10). Epoxy resin dental replicas were created before and after polishing. Surface roughness was measured three times in directions 120° apart, and a mean value for each replica was determined. Roughness data were analyzed statistically with repeated-measures ANOVA. Additionally, three specimens from each group underwent scanning electron microscopy. Following resin removal, average roughness was significantly higher in the carbide bur group (0.31 m) compared to the aluminum oxide disc group (0.25 m). The aluminum oxide disc polishing system produced lower enamel roughness than the multilaminated carbide bur system.

text: To determine whether plasma sclerostin levels are affected by applying whole-body vibration treatments . Following a pilot study , the pretsent prospective , randomized , controlled single-blind study was performed on 16 healthy volunteer women ( ages 20 to 40 years ) . Subjects were randomly divided into 2 groups , and whole-body vibration was applied to the treatment group but not to the controls . The plasma sclerostin levels were measured before the treatment and at the 10th minute after whole-body vibration on the 1st , 2nd , and 5th days of application . The plasma sclerostin level measured at 10 min after the whole-body vibration treatment increased 91 % ( P = 0.024 ) on the 1st day and decreased 31.5 % ( P = 0.03 ) on the 5th day in the whole-body vibration group . In the control group , there was no change in the plasma sclerostin level at any time . A progressive increase in baseline plasma sclerostin levels during the 5 days of vibration sessions was also found . Our study demonstrated that whole-body vibration can change plasma sclerostin levels , and that this change is detectable 10 min after whole-body vibration treatments .
rewrite: This study aimed to assess the impact of whole-body vibration on plasma sclerostin levels. A prospective, randomized, controlled single-blind trial was conducted with 16 healthy female volunteers (aged 20–40 years), following a pilot study. Participants were randomly assigned to either a treatment group, which received whole-body vibration, or a control group, which did not. Plasma sclerostin levels were measured before treatment and 10 minutes after vibration on the 1st, 2nd, and 5th days. In the vibration group, sclerostin increased by 91% (P = 0.024) on day 1 and decreased by 31.5% (P = 0.03) on day 5. No changes were observed in the control group at any time point. Additionally, baseline sclerostin levels showed a progressive increase over the five-day vibration period. The findings indicate that whole-body vibration alters plasma sclerostin levels, with changes detectable 10 minutes post-treatment.

text: To compare intravitreal bevacizumab versus ranibizumab as adjuvant treatment prior to pars plana vitrectomy ( PPV ) in proliferative diabetic retinopathy ( PDR ) with respect to parameters of surgical complexity . Prospective , randomized , double-masked pilot study of patients requiring PPV for nonclearing vitreous hemorrhage or tractional retinal detachment ( TRD ) secondary to PDR . Patients were randomized to receive either intravitreal bevacizumab or ranibizumab at standard doses 1 week preoperatively . Measured parameters included total surgical time , presence of TRD , intraoperative bleeding , iatrogenic retinal breaks , and use of endolaser and endodiathermy or silicone oil . A total of 29 patients were recruited . For surgical parameters , there were no statistically significant differences between the groups in the univariate analyses . Multivariable analysis showed no statistically significant difference for total surgical time . This pilot study suggests that intravitreal bevacizumab and ranibizumab are equivalent as surgical adjuvants when used as pre-treatment in patients with PDR undergoing PPV .
rewrite: To assess intravitreal bevacizumab against ranibizumab as adjuvant therapy before pars plana vitrectomy (PPV) in proliferative diabetic retinopathy (PDR) regarding surgical complexity measures. A prospective, randomized, double-masked pilot study included patients needing PPV for nonclearing vitreous hemorrhage or tractional retinal detachment (TRD) due to PDR. Participants were randomized to receive standard doses of either intravitreal bevacizumab or ranibizumab one week before surgery. Evaluated parameters comprised total surgical duration, TRD presence, intraoperative bleeding, iatrogenic retinal breaks, and the application of endolaser, endodiathermy, or silicone oil. Twenty-nine patients were enrolled. In surgical measures, univariate analyses revealed no statistically significant differences between groups. Multivariable analysis indicated no statistically significant difference in total surgical time. This pilot study implies that intravitreal bevacizumab and ranibizumab are comparable as surgical adjuvants when administered preoperatively in PDR patients undergoing PPV.

text: To assess the efficacy of massage for decreasing occupational low back pain in workers of a Nursing team in an Emergency Room . A randomized controlled trial , using a socio-demographic/morbidity questionnaire and a Pain Numeric Scale . Forty-five subjects were randomly allocated for intervention ( G1 - Massage by acupressure ) , placebo group ( G2 - application of Garlium Arseneid Laser 904 nm turned off ) and control ( G3 - no intervention ) . The main triggering factor , as well as the worsening of pain , was the patient manipulation , both with a prevalence of 34.9 % . The main treatment for low back pain before this research was the use of medication , with a prevalence of 44.2 % . In accordance with a variance analysis , only G1 presented a significant statistical difference , with a better result after 12 sessions . Massage presented an enormous effect ( d = 4.59 ) , corresponding to 86 % of reduction in the pain level . Massage was effective to decrease occupational low back pain of those Nursing workers .
rewrite: To evaluate the effectiveness of massage in reducing occupational low back pain among Nursing team members in an Emergency Room. A randomized controlled trial was conducted, utilizing a socio-demographic/morbidity questionnaire and a Pain Numeric Scale. Forty-five participants were randomly assigned to an intervention group (G1 - acupressure massage), a placebo group (G2 - application of an inactive Garlium Arseneid Laser 904 nm), and a control group (G3 - no intervention). The primary triggering factor for pain, as well as its exacerbation, was patient handling, both with a prevalence of 34.9%. Before this study, the main treatment for low back pain was medication, with a prevalence of 44.2%. According to variance analysis, only G1 showed a significant statistical difference, with improved outcomes after 12 sessions. Massage demonstrated a substantial effect (d = 4.59), equating to an 86% reduction in pain levels. Massage proved effective in decreasing occupational low back pain for these Nursing workers.

text: This study intended to implement a novel intervention strategy , in Brazil , using an ecohealth approach and analyse its effectiveness and costs in reducing Aedes aegypti vector density as well as its acceptance , feasibility and sustainability . The intervention was conducted from 2012 to 2013 in the municipality of Fortaleza , northeast Brazil . A cluster randomized controlled trial was designed by comparing ten intervention clusters with ten control clusters where routine vector control activities were conducted . The intervention included : community workshops ; community involvement in clean-up campaigns ; covering the elevated containers and in-house rubbish disposal without larviciding ; mobilization of schoolchildren and senior inhabitants ; and distribution of information , education and communication ( IEC ) materials in the community . Differences in terms of social participation , commitment and leadership were present in the clusters . The results showed the effectiveness of the intervention package in comparison with the routine control programme . Differences regarding the costs of the intervention were reasonable and could be adopted by public health services . Embedding social participation and environmental management for improved dengue vector control was feasible and significantly reduced vector densities . Such a participatory ecohealth approach offers a promising alternative to routine vector control measures .
rewrite: This research aimed to deploy a new intervention strategy in Brazil, employing an ecohealth framework to evaluate its effectiveness, cost, acceptance, feasibility, and sustainability in lowering Aedes aegypti vector density. The intervention took place from 2012 to 2013 in Fortaleza municipality, northeastern Brazil. A cluster randomized controlled trial compared ten intervention clusters with ten control clusters receiving standard vector control. The intervention comprised: community workshops; resident engagement in clean-up drives; covering elevated water containers and managing household waste without larvicides; mobilizing schoolchildren and elderly residents; and disseminating information, education, and communication (IEC) materials locally. Variations in social participation, commitment, and leadership were observed among clusters. Findings indicated the intervention package was more effective than routine control. Cost differences were moderate and potentially adoptable by public health services. Integrating social participation and environmental management enhanced dengue vector control feasibility and substantially cut vector densities. This participatory ecohealth method presents a viable alternative to conventional vector control measures.

text: Induction of labor , an increasingly common intervention , is often preceded by the application of an agent to `` prime '' or `` ripen '' the cervix . We conducted a randomized controlled trial to compare clinical , economic , and psychosocial outcomes of inpatient and outpatient cervical priming before induction of labor . In this paper we present the psychosocial outcomes . Women participating in a randomized controlled trial in two Australian metropolitan teaching hospitals completed questionnaires to measure anxiety and depression at enrollment , and to examine satisfaction , experiences , depression , and infant feeding 7 weeks after giving birth . Data analysis was by intention to treat and by having received the intervention as intended ( approximately 50 % in each group ) . Of 1,004 eligible women , 85 percent consented ( n = 407 , outpatient ; n = 414 inpatient ) . No statistically significant or clinically relevant differences were found in immediate anxiety , depression , or infant feeding . Small , statistically significant differences favoring outpatient priming were found in seven of the nine subscales in the 7-week postpartum questionnaire . The direction of the effect was maintained , mostly with a larger effect size in women who received the intervention . Women allocated to outpatient priming were more satisfied with their priming experience than women allocated to inpatient priming . Being informed that they could go home after cervical priming did not increase women 's anxiety .
rewrite: Labor induction, a growingly frequent procedure, is commonly preceded by cervical priming or ripening using an agent. We performed a randomized controlled trial to assess clinical, economic, and psychosocial results of inpatient versus outpatient cervical priming before labor induction. This paper focuses on the psychosocial outcomes. Participants in a randomized controlled trial at two Australian metropolitan teaching hospitals filled out questionnaires measuring anxiety and depression at enrollment, and evaluating satisfaction, experiences, depression, and infant feeding 7 weeks postpartum. Data were analyzed by intention to treat and by actual intervention received (about 50% per group). Out of 1,004 eligible women, 85% consented (n=407 outpatient; n=414 inpatient). No statistically significant or clinically meaningful differences emerged in immediate anxiety, depression, or infant feeding. Minor, statistically significant differences favoring outpatient priming appeared in seven of nine subscales on the 7-week postpartum questionnaire. The trend persisted, often with a stronger effect in women who underwent the intervention. Women assigned to outpatient priming reported greater satisfaction with their priming experience compared to those assigned to inpatient priming. Knowing they could return home after cervical priming did not raise women's anxiety.

text: The purpose of this study was to evaluate the clinical outcomes of cografting of acellular dermal matrix with autologous split-thickness skin and autologous split-thickness skin graft alone for full-thickness skin defects on the extremities . In this prospective randomized study , 19 consecutive patients with full-thickness skin defects on the extremities following trauma underwent grafting using either cograft of acellular dermal matrix with autologous split-thickness skin graft ( nine patients , group A ) or autologous split-thickness skin graft alone ( 10 patients , group B ) from June of 2011 to December of 2012 . The postoperative evaluations included observation of complications ( including graft necrosis , graft detachment , or seroma formation ) and Vancouver Scar Scale score . No statistically significant difference was found regarding complications , including graft necrosis , graft detachment , or seroma formation . At week 8 , significantly lower Vancouver Scar Scale scores for vascularity , pliability , height , and total score were found in group A compared with group B. At week 12 , lower scores for pliability and height and total scores were identified in group A compared with group B. For cases with traumatic full-thickness skin defects on the extremities , a statistically significant better result was achieved with cograft of acellular dermal matrix with autologous split-thickness skin graft than with autologous split-thickness skin graft alone in terms of Vancouver Scar Scale score . Therapeutic , II .
rewrite: This study aimed to assess the clinical outcomes of combining acellular dermal matrix with autologous split-thickness skin versus using autologous split-thickness skin graft alone for treating full-thickness skin defects on the extremities. In this prospective randomized trial, 19 consecutive patients with such defects from trauma received either the combined graft (nine patients, group A) or the skin graft alone (10 patients, group B) between June 2011 and December 2012. Postoperative assessments included monitoring complications—such as graft necrosis, detachment, or seroma—and evaluating Vancouver Scar Scale scores. No statistically significant differences were observed in complication rates between the groups. At week 8, group A showed significantly lower Vancouver Scar Scale scores for vascularity, pliability, height, and total score compared to group B. By week 12, group A continued to demonstrate lower scores for pliability, height, and total score. For traumatic full-thickness skin defects on the extremities, the combined graft method yielded statistically superior results based on the Vancouver Scar Scale score compared to the skin graft alone. Therapeutic, II.

text: Nausea and vomiting are two of the most frequently experienced postoperative side effects complicating one third of the cases . The objective of this study was to determine the effectiveness of gastric decompression in reducing the incidence and complications associated with post-tonsillectomy vomiting in children . This was a randomised control study conducted at the ENT Department , Ayub Teaching Hospital Abbottabad from January to June 2012 . Patients included in this study were divided into two groups , group A undergoing gastric aspiration and group B not undergoing gastric aspiration . Gastric aspiration was done with an oro-gastric tube placed under direct visualisation while the patient was still under general anaesthesia . The incidence of vomiting , episodes of vomiting and the need for rescue anti-emetic prophylaxis were noted . A total of 54 patients were included in the study . Their ages ranged from 5 to 12 years with mean age 7.85 + / - 2.18 years . No statistically significant difference ( p > 0.05 ) was noted between the two groups for the patients experiencing vomiting ( 33 % vs 41 % , p = 0.389 ) , the mean number of episodes of vomiting ( 0.71 vs 0.88 , p = 0.555 ) , and patients requiring rescue anti-emetics ( 11 % vs 15 % , p = 0.500 ) . Gastric aspiration during tonsillectomy is not useful in reducing post-tonsillectomy vomiting .
rewrite: Nausea and vomiting are among the most common postoperative complications, affecting approximately one third of patients. This study aimed to evaluate the efficacy of gastric decompression in lowering the occurrence and related complications of post-tonsillectomy vomiting in pediatric cases. A randomized controlled trial was performed in the ENT Department of Ayub Teaching Hospital Abbottabad between January and June 2012. Participants were allocated into two groups: group A received gastric aspiration, while group B did not. Gastric aspiration was performed using an oro-gastric tube under direct visualization while patients remained under general anesthesia. The frequency of vomiting, number of vomiting episodes, and requirement for rescue anti-emetic medication were recorded. The study enrolled 54 patients, aged 5 to 12 years, with a mean age of 7.85 ± 2.18 years. No statistically significant differences (p > 0.05) were observed between the groups regarding patients experiencing vomiting (33% vs 41%, p = 0.389), mean vomiting episodes (0.71 vs 0.88, p = 0.555), or those needing rescue anti-emetics (11% vs 15%, p = 0.500). Gastric aspiration during tonsillectomy does not effectively reduce post-tonsillectomy vomiting.

text: The risk for malignant melanoma is higher than expected in Parkinson 's disease ( PD ) . The National Institutes of Health ( NIH ) Exploratory Trials in PD ( NET-PD ) Long-term Study 1 ( LS-1 ) trial is a contemporary phase 3 study of subjects with early , treated PD . The objective of this work was to assess the incidence of malignant melanoma in a PD cohort . Incident melanoma cases were identified from the adverse events log . The expected number of cases was calculated , using the expected incidence rates and the number of person-years . A total of 618 females and 1119 males were followed for 6452 person-years ; 19 new melanoma cases were observed . The expected number was 5.29 . The standardized event ratio compared to the general population was 3.6 ( 95 % confidence interval , 2.2-5 .6 ) . The risk for developing melanoma was higher than expected in the NET-PD LS-1 cohort and was similar to the risk reported in earlier comparable clinical trial cohorts . Dermatologic screening may be useful in Parkinson 's disease to identify melanoma at an early stage .
rewrite: The risk of malignant melanoma exceeds expected levels in Parkinson's disease (PD). The NET-PD Long-term Study 1 (LS-1), a modern phase 3 trial by the NIH, focuses on individuals with early, treated PD. This study aimed to evaluate melanoma incidence within a PD cohort. Melanoma cases were tracked through adverse event records. Expected case numbers were derived from incidence rates and person-years of follow-up. Among 618 women and 1119 men, followed for 6452 person-years, 19 new melanomas were identified, compared to an expected 5.29 cases. The standardized event ratio versus the general population was 3.6 (95% CI, 2.2–5.6). Melanoma risk was elevated in the NET-PD LS-1 group, aligning with prior clinical trial data. Dermatological screening could aid in early melanoma detection in Parkinson's disease.

text: Adolescent mothers living with their mothers may be at greater risk of early weaning . This study aims to assess the influence of a breastfeeding promotion strategy directed at adolescent mothers living with their mothers on the prevalence of breastfeeding in the first year of life . A randomized clinical trial with 323 adolescent mothers . Participants were divided into two groups : those who lived with their mothers and those who did not . Participants were randomly assigned to control or intervention groups . Intervention consisted of breastfeeding counseling sessions held at the maternity ward and at home ( at 7 , 15 , 30 , 60 , and 120 days postpartum ) . The intervention effect was assessed by comparing survival curves for breastfeeding in the first 12 months of life . The risk of weaning before 12 months of age was significantly lower in the intervention group for adolescent mothers not living with their mothers ; whereas the risk was not statistically different between intervention and control groups for those living with their mothers . The positive influence of systematic counseling sessions on the prevalence of breastfeeding in the first year of life was significant for adolescent mothers . Living with their mothers reduced such influence .
rewrite: Adolescent mothers who reside with their own mothers might face a higher likelihood of early weaning. This research seeks to evaluate the impact of a breastfeeding promotion strategy targeted at adolescent mothers living with their mothers on breastfeeding rates during the first year of life. A randomized clinical trial involved 323 adolescent mothers. Participants were categorized into two groups: those cohabiting with their mothers and those who were not. They were then randomly allocated to either control or intervention groups. The intervention included breastfeeding counseling sessions conducted in the maternity ward and at home (on days 7, 15, 30, 60, and 120 postpartum). The effect of the intervention was evaluated by comparing survival curves for breastfeeding over the initial 12 months of life. The risk of weaning prior to 12 months was notably lower in the intervention group for adolescent mothers not living with their mothers; however, the risk did not differ significantly between intervention and control groups for those residing with their mothers. Systematic counseling sessions had a significant positive effect on breastfeeding prevalence in the first year for adolescent mothers. Cohabiting with their mothers diminished this effect.

text: Striae distensae ( SD ) is a common skin condition , with a prevalence ranging from 40 % to 90 % , depending on the population studied . To evaluate the efficacy of superficial dermabrasion and compare it with that of topical tretinoin cream in the treatment of narrow and early SD . Prospective , single-center , randomized , open-label study . Thirty-two women presenting with early , untreated SD ( striae rubra ) were included in this study . One group received 16 weekly sessions of superficial and localized dermabrasion , and the other used 0.05 % tretinoin cream daily . Striae width and length were measured and compared between groups and over time . Global Aesthetic Improvement Scale scores and subject satisfaction were also assessed . Biopsies were performed for subjects who agreed to undergo this procedure , followed by histologic analyses of the skin samples . Both treatments were efficacious , with significant improvement in early SD from baseline , but there was no significant difference between the two treatments . Histologic assessment showed improvement in epidermal and dermal layers for the dermabrasion treatment group . Both treatments had similar efficacy , but superficial dermabrasion had a lower frequency of side effects and better adherence of the patients .
rewrite: Striae distensae (SD) is a prevalent dermatological condition, affecting 40% to 90% of individuals across different populations. This study aimed to assess the effectiveness of superficial dermabrasion and compare it with topical 0.05% tretinoin cream for treating narrow, early-stage SD. A prospective, single-center, randomized, open-label trial was conducted with 32 women who had early, untreated SD (striae rubra). Participants were divided into two groups: one underwent 16 weekly sessions of localized superficial dermabrasion, while the other applied tretinoin cream daily. Measurements of striae width and length were taken and analyzed both between groups and over time. Additionally, Global Aesthetic Improvement Scale scores and patient satisfaction were evaluated. For consenting subjects, skin biopsies were performed and histologically examined. Results indicated both treatments were effective, showing significant improvement in early SD from baseline, with no statistically significant difference between them. Histological analysis revealed enhancements in epidermal and dermal layers in the dermabrasion group. While efficacy was comparable, superficial dermabrasion was associated with fewer side effects and higher patient adherence.

text: To assess the efficacy of a - galactomannan oligosaccharide ( - GMOS ) for the control of Salmonella infection in fattening pigs . Three different doses ( 0.5 , 3 and 2 kg - GMOS per ton of feed ) were used during the entire period of growing in three similar and independent field trials carried out in a small fattening unit ( 100 pigs ) . Treatment was randomly assigned to half of the pens . Individual serum samples ( 20-25 per group ) were collected at different times during the fattening period and a similar number of faecal samples during the fattening period and at slaughter . In addition , mesenteric lymph nodes were collected at slaughter . Herdcheck ( ) Swine Salmonella ELISA was used for serological analyses , the ISO 6579:2002 / Amd 1 : 2007 for bacteriology and the PFGE for molecular characterization of Salmonella strains . The addition of 2 kg t ( -1 ) of - GMOS to the pig diet during the entire fattening period was associated with a reduction in Salmonella prevalence , shedding and seroconversion . Feed supplementation with - GMOS may be a useful complementary tool for the control of salmonellosis in fattening pigs . - GMOS may be a complementary way of reducing Salmonella shedding and infection in fattening pigs .
rewrite: To evaluate the effectiveness of α-galactomannan oligosaccharide (α-GMOS) in managing Salmonella infection in fattening pigs, three varying doses (0.5, 3, and 2 kg of α-GMOS per ton of feed) were administered throughout the growth phase in three comparable, independent field trials conducted at a small fattening facility (100 pigs). Treatment was randomly allocated to half of the pens. Individual serum samples (20-25 per group) were gathered at multiple intervals during fattening, with a similar number of fecal samples collected both during this period and at slaughter. Mesenteric lymph nodes were also obtained at slaughter. Serological analyses employed the Herdcheck Swine Salmonella ELISA, bacteriology followed ISO 6579:2002/Amd 1:2007, and PFGE was used for molecular characterization of Salmonella strains. Incorporating 2 kg per ton of α-GMOS into the pig diet over the full fattening period correlated with decreased Salmonella prevalence, shedding, and seroconversion. Dietary supplementation with α-GMOS could serve as a beneficial complementary approach for controlling salmonellosis in fattening pigs. α-GMOS may offer an additional method to reduce Salmonella shedding and infection in these animals.

text: Acute changes in social belonging are important triggers for alterations in health and well-being , yet research has emphasised the negative effects of ` exclusion ' at the expense of evaluating the potentially positive effects of ` inclusion ' . This study examined the impact of acute belonging on physiological and psychological outcomes . A healthy population ( N = 138 ) were randomly allocated to ` included ' or ` excluded ' conditions . Condition-dependent differences in pre/during-task heart rate and pre/post-task self-reports of negative/positive mood , and social self-esteem , were assessed . Included participants showed decreased heart rate and negative mood , and increased social self-esteem . No inclusion-related change in positive mood was shown . An increase in heart rate was observed in excluded participants though no changes in negative/positive mood or social self-esteem were shown . Shifts in social self-esteem acted as a mechanism through which inclusion/exclusion impacted upon negative and positive mood alterations . Results remained significant in presence of covariates ( sex , global self-esteem , rumination and social anxiety ) . Findings suggest that acting to enhance belonging through ` inclusion ' resulted in adaptive physiological and psychological outcomes . Neutral and potentially protective responses were observed in the immediate aftermath of ` exclusion ' . Self-esteem served as one route through which these effects were transmitted .
rewrite: Sudden shifts in social belonging significantly influence health and well-being, but studies have focused on the harms of 'exclusion' while overlooking the possible benefits of 'inclusion'. This research investigated how acute belonging affects physiological and psychological states. A healthy sample (N = 138) was randomly assigned to 'included' or 'excluded' groups. Differences in heart rate before/during the task and self-reported negative/positive mood and social self-esteem before/after were measured. Included individuals exhibited lower heart rate and negative mood, along with higher social self-esteem. Positive mood did not change with inclusion. Excluded participants displayed elevated heart rate, but no shifts in negative/positive mood or social self-esteem. Changes in social self-esteem mediated the effect of inclusion/exclusion on mood variations. Results held after controlling for covariates (sex, global self-esteem, rumination, social anxiety). The findings indicate that promoting belonging via 'inclusion' leads to beneficial physiological and psychological outcomes. 'Exclusion' elicited neutral and possibly protective immediate reactions. Self-esteem functioned as a pathway for these effects.

text: To evaluate the diagnostic performance of three-dimensional ( 3D ) MR maximum intensity projection ( MIP ) in the assessment of synovitis of the hand and wrist in rheumatoid arthritis ( RA ) compared to 3D contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging ( CE-MRI ) . Twenty-five patients with RA underwent MR examinations . 3D MR MIP images were derived from the enhanced images . MR images were reviewed by two radiologists for the presence and location of synovitis of the hand and wrist . The diagnostic sensitivity , specificity and accuracy of 3D MIP were , respectively , calculated with the reference standard 3D CE-MRI . In all subjects , 3D MIP images yielded directly and clearly the presence and location of synovitis with just one image . Synovitis demonstrated high signal intensity on MIP images . The k-values for the detection of articular synovitis indicated excellent interobserver agreements using 3D MIP images ( k = 0.87 ) and CE-MR images ( k = 0.91 ) , respectively . 3D MIP demonstrated a sensitivity , specificity and accuracy of 91.07 % , 98.57 % and 96.0 % , respectively , for the detection of synonitis . 3D MIP can provide a whole overview of lesion locations and a reliable diagnostic performance in the assessment of articular synovitis of the hand and wrist in patients with RA , which has potential value of clinical practice .
rewrite: This study assessed the diagnostic utility of three-dimensional (3D) magnetic resonance maximum intensity projection (MIP) for evaluating hand and wrist synovitis in rheumatoid arthritis (RA), using 3D contrast-enhanced MRI (CE-MRI) as the reference. Twenty-five RA patients underwent MRI. 3D MIP images were generated from the contrast-enhanced scans. Two radiologists independently reviewed the images to identify the presence and location of synovitis. The sensitivity, specificity, and accuracy of 3D MIP were calculated against the 3D CE-MRI standard. In all cases, a single 3D MIP image directly and clearly depicted synovitis presence and location, with synovitis appearing as high signal intensity. Interobserver agreement for detecting articular synovitis was excellent for both 3D MIP (k = 0.87) and CE-MRI (k = 0.91). For synovitis detection, 3D MIP showed a sensitivity of 91.07%, specificity of 98.57%, and accuracy of 96.0%. 3D MIP can offer a comprehensive overview of lesion sites and reliable diagnostic performance in assessing hand and wrist synovitis in RA, indicating potential clinical value.

text: To evaluate the agreement between tumour volume derived from semiautomated volumetry ( SaV ) and tumor volume defined by spherical volume using longest lesion diameter ( LD ) according to Response Evaluation Criteria In Solid Tumors ( RECIST ) or ellipsoid volume using LD and longest orthogonal diameter ( LOD ) according to World Health Organization ( WHO ) criteria . Twenty patients with metastatic colorectal cancer from the CIOX trial were included . A total of 151 target lesions were defined by baseline computed tomography and followed until disease progression . All assessments were performed by a single reader . A variance component model was used to compare the three volume versions . There was a significant difference between the SaV and RECIST-based tumour volumes . The same model showed no significant difference between the SaV and WHO-based volumes . Scatter plots showed that the RECIST-based volumes overestimate lesion volume . The agreement between the SaV and WHO-based relative changes in tumour volume , evaluated by intraclass correlation , showed nearly perfect agreement . Estimating the volume of metastatic lesions using both the LD and LOD ( WHO ) is more accurate than those based on LD only ( RECIST ) , which overestimates lesion volume . The good agreement between the SaV and WHO-based relative changes in tumour volume enables a reasonable approximation of three-dimensional tumour burden . Tumour response in patients undergoing chemotherapy is assessed using CT images Measurements are based on RECIST ( unidimensional ) - based or WHO ( bidimensional ) - based criteria We calculated tumour volume from bidimensional target lesion measurements This formula provides good tumour volume approximation , based on semiautomated volumetry .
rewrite: To assess the concordance between tumor volume from semiautomated volumetry (SaV) and volumes calculated using the longest diameter (LD) per RECIST criteria or using both LD and the longest orthogonal diameter (LOD) per WHO criteria. The study included 20 metastatic colorectal cancer patients from the CIOX trial, with 151 target lesions identified on baseline CT and monitored to progression. All evaluations were conducted by one reader. A variance component model compared the three volume methods. A significant difference was found between SaV and RECIST-based volumes, while no significant difference was observed between SaV and WHO-based volumes. Scatter plots indicated that RECIST-based volumes overestimate lesion size. Intraclass correlation revealed nearly perfect agreement between SaV and WHO-based relative tumor volume changes. Using both LD and LOD (WHO) yields more accurate metastatic lesion volume estimates than LD alone (RECIST), which tends to overestimate. The strong agreement between SaV and WHO-based relative changes allows for a reasonable approximation of three-dimensional tumor burden. Tumor response during chemotherapy is evaluated via CT, using RECIST (unidimensional) or WHO (bidimensional) criteria. Tumor volume derived from bidimensional measurements offers a good approximation, consistent with semiautomated volumetry.

text: To compare the extraction time and infection rate of umbilical cord by applying ethanol , humanmilk or dry care . The parallel single-blinded randomised clinical trial was performed on 300 neonates at Shahid Sadougi University of Medical Sciences and Health Service , Yazd , Iran , between March and September 2010 . The neonates were divided into three random but numerically equal groups . Each group was assigned the application of ethanol or mother 's milk or to keep the stump dry . The neonates were visited on the 3rd and the 7th day after birth and follow-up was maintained telephonically until umbilical separation . Umbilical separation time and umbilical local infection frequency were considered as the study outcome , which was compared among the three groups according to age , gender and delivery type of the neonates . Umbilical separation time in neonates of the human milk group had significant difference with the ethanol group ( p = 0.0001 ) and drying groups ( p = 0.003 ) . Frequency of omphalitis had no significant difference among the three groups . Topical usage of human milk on umbilical cord stamp decreased separation time and incidence rate of omphalitis .
rewrite: This study aimed to evaluate umbilical cord extraction time and infection rates using ethanol, human milk, or dry care. A parallel single-blinded randomized clinical trial involved 300 neonates at Shahid Sadougi University of Medical Sciences and Health Services in Yazd, Iran, from March to September 2010. The neonates were randomly allocated into three equally sized groups, receiving either ethanol application, mother's milk application, or dry stump care. Follow-up visits occurred on the 3rd and 7th postnatal days, with additional telephonic monitoring until cord separation. The primary outcomes—umbilical separation time and local infection frequency—were compared across groups, accounting for neonatal age, gender, and delivery type. Umbilical separation time in the human milk group showed a significant difference compared to the ethanol group (p = 0.0001) and the dry care group (p = 0.003). The frequency of omphalitis did not differ significantly among the groups. Topical application of human milk to the umbilical cord stump reduced separation time and the incidence of omphalitis.

text: Despite their high prevalence in daily life , repeated night-wakings and their cognitive and emotional consequences have received less research attention compared to other types of sleep disturbances . Our aim was to experimentally compare the effects of one night of induced infrequent night-wakings ( of 15 min , each requiring a purposeful response ) and sleep restriction on sustained attention and mood in young adults . In a within-between subjects counterbalanced design , 61 healthy adults ( 40 females ; aged 20-29 years ) underwent home assessments of sustained attention and self-reported mood at two times : after a normal ( control ) sleep night , and after a night of either sleep restriction ( 4h in bed ) or induced night-wakings ( four prolonged awakenings across 8h in bed ) . Sleep was monitored using actigraphy and sleep diaries . Sustained attention was assessed using an online continuous performance test ( OCPT ) , and mood was reported online using the Profile of Mood States ( POMS ) . Actigraphic data revealed good compliance with experimental sleep requirements . Induced night-wakings and sleep restriction both resulted in more OCPT omission and commission errors , and in increased depression , fatigue and confusion levels and reduced vigor compared to the normal sleep night . Moreover , there were no significant differences between the consequences of induced awakenings and sleep restriction . Our pilot study indicates that , similar to sleep restriction , one night of life-like repeated night-wakings negatively affects mood and sustained attention .
rewrite: Although frequent in everyday life, repeated nighttime awakenings and their cognitive and emotional impacts have been studied less than other sleep disruptions. This study experimentally compared the effects of one night of induced infrequent awakenings (each 15 minutes, requiring a purposeful response) and sleep restriction on sustained attention and mood in young adults. Using a within-between subjects counterbalanced design, 61 healthy adults (40 females; aged 20–29) underwent home assessments of sustained attention and self-reported mood twice: after a normal (control) sleep night and after either sleep restriction (4 hours in bed) or induced awakenings (four prolonged awakenings over 8 hours in bed). Sleep was monitored via actigraphy and diaries. Sustained attention was measured with an online continuous performance test (OCPT), and mood was assessed online using the Profile of Mood States (POMS). Actigraphy data showed good adherence to the sleep protocols. Both induced awakenings and sleep restriction led to more OCPT omission and commission errors, along with increased depression, fatigue, and confusion, and reduced vigor, compared to normal sleep. Furthermore, no significant differences were found between the effects of induced awakenings and sleep restriction. This pilot study suggests that, like sleep restriction, a single night of realistic repeated awakenings adversely affects mood and sustained attention.

text: To evaluate the effect of expert guided mentorship on technical score and time for a set of robotic training drills . Prospective randomized controlled trial ( Canadian Task Force classification I ) . Academic institution . Fifty trainees in robotic surgery . Inexperienced trainees underwent either a 20-minute expert guided mentorship session or no intervention . The primary outcomes were technical score and time-to-drill completion for a set of dry lab robotic training drills evaluated at an initial and final skills assessment . The t-test , including paired analyses , was used to evaluate outcomes . Forty-nine of 50 trainees ( 98 % ) completed the study . There were no significant differences in participant characteristics or initial performance between the 2 groups . During the final skills assessment , the intervention group demonstrated significantly better performance on 1 of 8 objective measures . They had a higher mean score for the bead transfer drill when compared with the control group ( 21.6 vs 19.9 ; p = .03 ) . No differences in time-to-drill completion were noted between the 2 groups . Regardless of randomization , all participants had significantly improved scores for each of the drills on the final compared with the initial skills assessment ( p < .01 ) . Although expert guided mentorship in a dry lab simulation environment seems feasible , further investigation is warranted before its widespread use because it may be more resource intensive than other teaching methods , without consistent objective improvements in technical performance .
rewrite: To assess the impact of expert-guided mentorship on technical scores and completion times for robotic training drills. Prospective randomized controlled trial (Canadian Task Force classification I). Academic institution. Fifty robotic surgery trainees. Inexperienced participants received either a 20-minute expert-guided mentorship session or no intervention. Primary outcomes were technical score and time-to-drill completion for dry lab robotic training drills, evaluated at initial and final skills assessments. The t-test, including paired analyses, was used to assess outcomes. Forty-nine of 50 trainees (98%) completed the study. No significant differences were found in participant characteristics or initial performance between groups. At the final assessment, the intervention group showed significantly better performance on one of eight objective measures. They achieved a higher mean score for the bead transfer drill compared to the control group (21.6 vs. 19.9; p = .03). No differences in time-to-drill completion were observed between groups. Regardless of randomization, all participants significantly improved scores for each drill in the final compared to the initial assessment (p < .01). While expert-guided mentorship in a dry lab simulation appears feasible, further study is needed before widespread adoption, as it may be more resource-intensive than other methods without consistent objective gains in technical performance.

text: The present study examines the role of comorbid anxiety on depression outcomes for those receiving cognitive behavioral therapy ( CBT ) for depression by telephone ( T-CBT ) or face-to-face ( FtF-CBT ) . Three hundred twenty-five participants were randomized to T-CBT or FtF-CBT . Comorbid anxiety was measured using the Mini International Neuropsychiatric Interview and Generalized Anxiety Disorder 7 . Depression was measured using the Hamilton Rating Scale for Depression and Patient Health Questionnaire 9 . A hierarchical model including the two-way interaction of treatment assignment and anxiety status indicated a significant effect for all outcome variables ( Ps < .05 ) . Post hoc t tests indicated T-CBT participants with comorbid anxiety disorders had significantly higher symptom severity over time compared to their T-CBT counterparts without anxiety ( Ps < .001 ) and FtF-CBT counterparts with comorbid anxiety ( Ps < .003 ) .
