Sibling oocytes were randomized into groups to be inseminated either by conventional IVF or ICSI . Fertilization rate , embryo quality , implantation rate , and clinical pregnancy rate were examined . There was no difference in the fertilization , implantation , and pregnancy rates between conventional IVF and ICSI in either the O group or OA group ( p > 0.05 ) . Additionally , in the OA group , the good quality embryo rate was similar after IVF or ICSI ( p > 0.05 ) . However , in the O group , the good quality embryo rate was significantly higher after ICSI than after IVF ( p < 0.05 ) . Couples with moderate oligozoospermia or moderate oligoasthenozoospermia did not influence the major indices of IVF . Because of the uncertainties concerning the safety of ICSI , couples with moderate oligozoospermia or moderate oligoasthenozoospermia need not be subjected to this procedure .
rewrite: This study assessed whether couples with moderate male infertility should undergo conventional in vitro fertilization (IVF) or intracytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI). A total of 249 couples with moderate male infertility undergoing their first IVF/ICSI cycle were included. Based on semen analysis results, couples were categorized into two groups: moderate oligozoospermia (O group) and moderate oligoasthenozoospermia (OA group). Sibling oocytes were randomly assigned to be inseminated by either conventional IVF or ICSI. Fertilization rate, embryo quality, implantation rate, and clinical pregnancy rate were evaluated. No significant differences were observed in fertilization, implantation, or pregnancy rates between conventional IVF and ICSI in either the O or OA groups (p > 0.05). Furthermore, in the OA group, the rate of good quality embryos was comparable between IVF and ICSI (p > 0.05). However, in the O group, the good quality embryo rate was significantly higher with ICSI than with IVF (p < 0.05). Moderate oligozoospermia or moderate oligoasthenozoospermia did not affect the primary outcomes of IVF. Given the uncertainties regarding ICSI safety, couples with moderate oligozoospermia or moderate oligoasthenozoospermia may not require this procedure.

text: We examined whether It 's Your Game ... Keep It Real ( IYG ) reduced dating violence among ethnic-minority middle school youths , a population at high risk for dating violence . We analyzed data from 766 predominantly ethnic-minority students from 10 middle schools in southeast Texas in 2004 for a group randomized trial of IYG . We estimated logistic regression models , and the primary outcome was emotional and physical dating violence perpetration and victimization by ninth grade . Control students had significantly higher odds of physical dating violence victimization ( adjusted odds ratio [ AOR ] = 1.52 ; 95 % confidence interval [ CI ] = 1.20 , 1.92 ) , emotional dating violence victimization ( AOR = 1.74 ; 95 % CI = 1.36 , 2.24 ) , and emotional dating violence perpetration ( AOR = 1.58 ; 95 % CI = 1.11 , 2.26 ) than did intervention students . The odds of physical dating violence perpetration were not significantly different between the 2 groups . Program effects varied by gender and race/ethnicity . IYG significantly reduced 3 of 4 dating violence outcomes among ethnic-minority middle school youths . Although further study is warranted to determine if IYG should be widely disseminated to prevent dating violence , it is one of only a handful of school-based programs that are effective in reducing adolescent dating violence behavior .
rewrite: This study investigated whether the It's Your Game...Keep It Real (IYG) program decreased dating violence in ethnic-minority middle school students, a group with elevated risk. Data from 766 primarily ethnic-minority youths across 10 southeast Texas middle schools in 2004 were analyzed for a group randomized trial of IYG. Using logistic regression models, the primary outcome assessed was emotional and physical dating violence perpetration and victimization by ninth grade. Control group students showed significantly greater odds of physical dating violence victimization (adjusted odds ratio [AOR] = 1.52; 95% CI = 1.20, 1.92), emotional dating violence victimization (AOR = 1.74; 95% CI = 1.36, 2.24), and emotional dating violence perpetration (AOR = 1.58; 95% CI = 1.11, 2.26) compared to intervention students. Odds for physical dating violence perpetration did not differ significantly between groups. Program effects differed by gender and race/ethnicity. IYG meaningfully lowered three of four dating violence outcomes among these youths. While more research is needed to justify widespread dissemination for dating violence prevention, IYG is among the few school-based programs proven effective in reducing adolescent dating violence.

text: The purpose of this study is to evaluate the utilization of four approved antihyperuricemic agents in Taiwan before and after two safety announcements rescinded an indication for allopurinol and added a warning on benzbromarone-induced hepatotoxicity in the year 2005 . An interrupted time series design and segmented regression models were used to examine impacts of the safety announcements on the utilization of allopurinol , benzbromarone , probenecid , or sulfinpyrazone . All outpatient prescriptions of the four antihyperuricemic agents were extracted from a longitudinal cohort dataset with 1000000 individuals randomly sampled from the National Health Insurance Research Database . We examined utilization patterns of antihyperuricemic agents before and after the policy intervention ( i.e. , safety announcements and labeling changes of allopurinol and benzbromarone ) in the year 2005 . Following the safety announcements , there was a reduction in the number of allopurinol users in the first year of intervention ( -95.82 users per 100000 persons , 95 % CI , [ -166.84 , -24.80 ] ) and a continuous reduction afterward at a rate of -53.17 per 100000 persons per year . The utilization of benzbromarone grew steadily before 2005 but decreased drastically after the intervention , with a 30.12 % reduction in the number of users by the end of year 2008 . There was no commensurate change in the number of probenecid or sulfinpyrazone users after the intervention . Further research is required to evaluate the direct impacts of the safety announcements on clinical outcomes , treatment costs , and patient 's quality of life .
rewrite: This study aims to assess the use of four approved antihyperuricemic drugs in Taiwan before and after two 2005 safety announcements, which revoked an allopurinol indication and added a hepatotoxicity warning for benzbromarone. An interrupted time series design and segmented regression models were employed to analyze the announcements' effects on the utilization of allopurinol, benzbromarone, probenecid, and sulfinpyrazone. All outpatient prescriptions for these agents were obtained from a longitudinal cohort dataset, comprising a random sample of 1,000,000 individuals from the National Health Insurance Research Database. Utilization patterns were examined before and after the 2005 policy intervention, involving the safety announcements and labeling changes for allopurinol and benzbromarone. After the announcements, allopurinol users declined in the first intervention year (-95.82 per 100,000 persons, 95% CI [-166.84, -24.80]), with a continued annual reduction of -53.17 per 100,000 persons. Benzbromarone use had risen steadily before 2005 but fell sharply post-intervention, showing a 30.12% decrease in users by the end of 2008. No corresponding changes were observed in probenecid or sulfinpyrazone usage following the intervention. Further investigation is needed to evaluate the safety announcements' direct impacts on clinical outcomes, treatment costs, and patient quality of life.

text: To determine whether the insulin resistance that exists in metabolic syndrome ( MetS ) patients is modulated by dietary fat composition . Seventy-five patients were randomly assigned to one of four diets for 12 wk : high-saturated fatty acids ( HSFAs ) , high-MUFA ( HMUFA ) , and two low-fat , high-complex carbohydrate ( LFHCC ) diets supplemented with long-chain n-3 ( LFHCC n-3 ) PUFA or placebo . At the end of intervention , the LFHCC n-3 diet reduced plasma insulin , homeostasis model assessment of insulin resistance , and nonsterified fatty acid concentration ( p < 0.05 ) as compared to baseline Spanish habitual ( BSH ) diet . Subcutaneous white adipose tissue ( WAT ) analysis revealed decreased EH-domain containing-2 mRNA levels and increased cbl-associated protein gene expression with the LFHCC n-3 compared to HSFA and HMUFA diets , respectively ( p < 0.05 ) . Moreover , the LFHCC n-3 decreased gene expression of glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate dehydrogenase with respect to HMUFA and BSH diets ( p < 0.05 ) . Finally , proteomic characterization of subcutaneous WAT identified three proteins of glucose metabolism downregulated by the LFHCC n-3 diet , including annexin A2 . RT-PCR analysis confirmed the decrease of annexin A2 ( p = 0.027 ) after this diet . Our data suggest that the LFHCC n-3 diet reduces systemic insulin resistance and improves insulin signaling in subcutaneous WAT of MetS patients compared to HSFA and BSH diets consumption .
rewrite: To assess if dietary fat composition influences insulin resistance in metabolic syndrome (MetS) patients. Seventy-five participants were randomly allocated to one of four 12-week diets: high-saturated fatty acids (HSFAs), high-MUFA (HMUFA), and two low-fat, high-complex carbohydrate (LFHCC) diets, one supplemented with long-chain n-3 (LFHCC n-3) PUFA and the other a placebo. Post-intervention, the LFHCC n-3 diet lowered plasma insulin, homeostasis model assessment of insulin resistance, and nonesterified fatty acid levels (p < 0.05) relative to the baseline Spanish habitual (BSH) diet. Analysis of subcutaneous white adipose tissue (WAT) showed reduced EH-domain containing-2 mRNA and elevated cbl-associated protein gene expression with LFHCC n-3 versus HSFA and HMUFA diets, respectively (p < 0.05). Additionally, LFHCC n-3 reduced glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate dehydrogenase gene expression compared to HMUFA and BSH diets (p < 0.05). Proteomic analysis of subcutaneous WAT identified three glucose metabolism proteins downregulated by LFHCC n-3, including annexin A2. RT-PCR confirmed annexin A2 reduction (p = 0.027) after this diet. Our findings indicate that the LFHCC n-3 diet decreases systemic insulin resistance and enhances insulin signaling in subcutaneous WAT of MetS patients compared to HSFA and BSH diets.

text: To evaluate pazopanib 10 mg/mL eye drops ( pazopanib ) in healthy subjects and in subjects with previously untreated subfoveal choroidal neovascularization secondary to age-related macular degeneration . Study 1 ( single center , randomized , placebo-controlled , double-masked ) included 3 cohorts of 12 to 13 healthy subjects each who instilled pazopanib or placebo 4 times daily for 2 weeks . Study 2 ( multicenter open-label ) included 19 subjects with neovascular age-related macular degeneration who instilled pazopanib 4 times daily for 12 weeks . Both studies evaluated pharmacokinetics and safety . Study 2 also evaluated efficacy . Steady-state concentrations of pazopanib in plasma seemed to be reached by Week 2 . At Week 4 ( Study 2 ) , there were no meaningful changes from baseline in the mean central retinal thickness ( 37.9 m ) or best-corrected visual acuity ( 0.1 letters ) ( primary endpoint ) , retinal morphology , choroidal neovascularization size , or total lesion size . Complement Factor H genotype had no effect on changes from baseline in the best-corrected visual acuity or central retinal thickness . The most common pazopanib-related ocular adverse events included eye irritation ( Study 1 , n = 7 ) and instillation site pain ( Study 2 , n = 3 ) . No serious adverse events were reported . Pazopanib was well tolerated . In subjects with previously untreated neovascular age-related macular degeneration , pazopanib instilled 4 times daily as monothereapy did not seem to improve the best-corrected visual acuity or decrease the central retinal thickness .
rewrite: This study assessed pazopanib 10 mg/mL eye drops in healthy individuals and patients with untreated subfoveal choroidal neovascularization due to age-related macular degeneration. Study 1 (single-center, randomized, placebo-controlled, double-masked) involved three cohorts of 12–13 healthy subjects each, administering pazopanib or placebo four times daily for two weeks. Study 2 (multicenter, open-label) included 19 neovascular age-related macular degeneration patients who used pazopanib four times daily for 12 weeks. Both trials examined pharmacokinetics and safety, with Study 2 also evaluating efficacy. Pazopanib plasma concentrations appeared to reach steady state by Week 2. At Week 4 in Study 2, no significant changes from baseline were observed in mean central retinal thickness (37.9 μm), best-corrected visual acuity (0.1 letters, the primary endpoint), retinal morphology, choroidal neovascularization size, or total lesion size. Complement Factor H genotype did not influence changes in best-corrected visual acuity or central retinal thickness. Common pazopanib-related ocular adverse events were eye irritation (Study 1, n=7) and instillation site pain (Study 2, n=3). No serious adverse events occurred, and pazopanib was well tolerated. In patients with previously untreated neovascular age-related macular degeneration, pazopanib administered four times daily as monotherapy did not appear to enhance best-corrected visual acuity or reduce central retinal thickness.

text: There is a paucity of literature on the use of honey in wound healing after oral and maxillofacial surgical procedures . To evaluate the efficacy of the healing properties of Obudu honey in patients who developed wound dehiscence after segmental mandibular resections . This was a prospective study of 72 patients who had benign lesions of the mandible , and were treated by segmental mandibular resection , with the surgical wounds developing dehiscence . The subjects were randomized into two treatment groups of A ( control , n = 36 ) and B ( experimental , n = 36 ) . Unlike the control , the wounds in the experimental group were dressed in honey after debridement . The ages of the patients ranged from 21 to 73 years with a mean age of 46.3 2.1 years while the male : female ratio was 3:1 . There was no significant demographic difference about age ( P = 0.44 ) and gender ( P = 0.38 ) between the two groups . The smaller the initial circumference of the surgical wound , the shorter the duration of healing and this was significant ( P = 0.001 ) in either of the treatment groups . Numerically , more healing was completed in the first 5 weeks in subjects in the experimental group ( n = 19 , 52.8 % ) than the control ( n = 13 , 36.1 % ) . However , the duration of healing between the subjects in the control and experimental groups at the end of 9 weeks showed no significant difference ( P = 0.23 ) . Honey speeds up the healing of dehiscence wounds of resected mandible when used as dressing more than the control .
rewrite: Limited research exists on honey's application in wound healing following oral and maxillofacial surgeries. This study assessed the healing effectiveness of Obudu honey for patients experiencing wound dehiscence after segmental mandibular resections. A prospective analysis included 72 patients with benign mandibular lesions who underwent segmental resection and subsequently developed wound dehiscence. Participants were randomly assigned to two groups: Group A (control, n=36) and Group B (experimental, n=36). In contrast to the control, wounds in the experimental group received honey dressings post-debridement. Patient ages varied from 21 to 73 years, averaging 46.3±2.1 years, with a male-to-female ratio of 3:1. No significant demographic differences were observed between groups regarding age (P=0.44) and gender (P=0.38). Smaller initial wound circumferences correlated with shorter healing times, a significant finding (P=0.001) in both groups. Within the first five weeks, a greater proportion of subjects in the experimental group achieved complete healing (n=19, 52.8%) compared to the control (n=13, 36.1%). Nevertheless, by the end of nine weeks, healing duration showed no significant difference between control and experimental groups (P=0.23). Honey accelerates the healing of dehiscence wounds in resected mandibles more effectively than the control when utilized as a dressing.

text: This study was performed to compare the pharmacokinetic properties and relative bioavailability of two isosorbide-5-mononitrate ( 5-ISMN ) sustained-release drugs in healthy Korean subjects under fasting and fed conditions . A total of 60 healthy volunteers ( 30 each in the fasting and fed arms of the study ) were enrolled in the study and were randomized to treatment . After the administration of a single dose of one of the investigational products , blood samples were collected at specific time intervals from 0 to 36 hours . The plasma concentrations of 5-ISMN were measured by LC-MS/MS . The pharmacokinetic parameters were calculated , and the 90 % confidence intervals ( CIs ) of the geometric mean ratio ( test/reference ) of the parameters were obtained by analysis of variance on logarithmically transformed data . The corresponding 90 % CIs of AUClast and Cmax for the test/reference geometric mean ratio were 90.75 - 98.44 % and 92.28 - 98.33 % , respectively , under fasting conditions . In the fed state study , the 90 % CIs for the geometric mean ratio of test to reference drugs were 94.79 - 103.33 % for AUClast and 99.86 - 108.02 % for Cmax . The test product is equivalent to the reference product in subjects under fasting and fed conditions within the Korean regulatory bioequivalence criteria . Both formulations were safe and well tolerated , and there were no noteworthy differences in the safety profiles between the test and reference drugs .
rewrite: This study aimed to evaluate the pharmacokinetic characteristics and relative bioavailability of two sustained-release formulations of isosorbide-5-mononitrate (5-ISMN) in healthy Korean participants under fasting and fed states. Sixty healthy volunteers were included (30 per fasting and fed group) and randomly assigned to treatment. Following a single dose of an investigational product, blood samples were taken at predetermined intervals from 0 to 36 hours. Plasma 5-ISMN levels were quantified using LC-MS/MS. Pharmacokinetic parameters were derived, and the 90% confidence intervals (CIs) for the geometric mean ratios (test/reference) of these parameters were determined through analysis of variance on log-transformed data. Under fasting conditions, the 90% CIs for the test/reference geometric mean ratios were 90.75–98.44% for AUClast and 92.28–98.33% for Cmax. In the fed state, the 90% CIs were 94.79–103.33% for AUClast and 99.86–108.02% for Cmax. The test formulation meets Korean regulatory bioequivalence standards compared to the reference under both fasting and fed conditions. Both products were safe and well tolerated, with no significant safety differences observed between the test and reference drugs.

text: To compare the use of the 810nm diode laser with conventional surgery in the management of soft tissue mucogingival problems associated with orthodontic treatment . Orthodontic patients requiring different soft tissue surgical procedures were randomly assigned to receive conventional surgery or soft tissue diode laser , ( wavelength 810 nm ) . Parameters documented include the type of anaesthesia used , intra and post operative pain , bleeding , the use of scalpel and sutures . The chi-squared test was used to test for significance at 95 % confidence level . Probability values ( p-values ) less than 0.05 were regarded as significant . Only 2 ( 16.7 % ) of the procedures carried out with the soft tissue laser required infiltration anaesthesia compared to 10 ( 90.9 % ) with conventional surgery and this was significant ( P < 0.001 ) . Post operative pain was significantly reduced in all cases treated with the diode laser ( P < 0.001 ) . There was also a significant difference ( P < 0.05 ) in post operative bleeding in all cases treated with the diode laser . No sutures were used in all soft tissue cases managed with the diode laser and this was significant ( P < 0.001 ) . There was no statistically significant difference in treatment time in the use of the laser compared with conventional surgery . Orthodontic patients treated with the diode laser required less infiltration anaesthesia , had reduced bleeding during and after surgery , rapid postoperative haemostasis , elimination of the need for sutures and an improved postoperative comfort and healing .
rewrite:
This study compared the use of an 810nm diode laser to conventional surgery for managing soft tissue mucogingival issues during orthodontic treatment. Orthodontic patients needing various soft tissue procedures were randomly assigned to receive either conventional surgery or diode laser treatment (810 nm wavelength). Recorded parameters included the type of anesthesia, intraoperative and postoperative pain, bleeding, and the use of scalpels and sutures. The chi-squared test assessed significance at a 95% confidence level, with p-values below 0.05 considered significant.

Only 2 procedures (16.7%) with the soft tissue laser required infiltration anesthesia, compared to 10 (90.9%) with conventional surgery, a significant difference (P < 0.001). Postoperative pain was significantly lower in all laser-treated cases (P < 0.001). A significant reduction in postoperative bleeding was also observed in all laser cases (P < 0.05). No sutures were used in any diode laser procedures, which was significant (P < 0.001). Treatment time showed no statistically significant difference between the two methods.

Orthodontic patients treated with the diode laser needed less infiltration anesthesia, experienced reduced intraoperative and postoperative bleeding, achieved rapid hemostasis, eliminated the need for sutures, and showed improved postoperative comfort and healing.

text: The purpose of this study was to compare once-daily tacrolimus with twice-daily tacrolimus in terms of safety , efficacy , and patient satisfaction . This prospective , randomized , open-label , multicenter study was conducted at three institutes . Patients in the investigational group were converted from tacrolimus twice daily to the same dose of extended-release tacrolimus once daily at 1 month post-transplantation , while patients in the control group were maintained on tacrolimus twice daily . The efficacies , safeties , and patient satisfaction for the two drugs at 6 months post-transplantation were compared . Sixty patients were enrolled and randomized to the investigational group ( 28 of 29 patients completed the study ) or the control group ( 26 of 31 patients completed the study ) . At 6 months post-transplantation , composite efficacy failure rates including the incidences of biopsy-confirmed acute rejection in the investigational and control groups were 0 % and 10.7 % , respectively ; patient survival was 100 % in each group . No difference in estimated glomerular filtration rate values were observed at 6 months post-transplantation ( p = 0.97 ) . The safety and satisfaction profile ( immunosuppressant therapy barrier scale ) of once-daily tacrolimus was comparable with that of twice-daily tacrolimus ( p = 0.35 ) . Conversion from twice-daily tacrolimus to once-daily tacrolimus one month after transplantation is safe and effective .
rewrite: This study aimed to evaluate the safety, efficacy, and patient satisfaction of once-daily versus twice-daily tacrolimus. In this prospective, randomized, open-label, multicenter trial conducted across three institutions, patients were assigned to either an investigational or control group. The investigational group switched from twice-daily tacrolimus to an equivalent once-daily extended-release formulation one month post-transplantation, while the control group continued with the twice-daily regimen. Outcomes including efficacy, safety, and patient satisfaction were assessed at six months post-transplantation. Of the 60 enrolled patients, 28 out of 29 in the investigational group and 26 out of 31 in the control group completed the study. At six months, composite efficacy failure rates, incorporating biopsy-confirmed acute rejection, were 0% in the investigational group and 10.7% in the control group, with 100% patient survival in both groups. Estimated glomerular filtration rates showed no significant difference at six months (p = 0.97). Safety and satisfaction profiles, measured by the immunosuppressant therapy barrier scale, were similar between the once-daily and twice-daily regimens (p = 0.35). Transitioning to once-daily tacrolimus one month after transplantation is both safe and effective.

text: It remains unclear whether analgesia from intraperitoneal local anesthetics is via local or central mechanisms . This double-blind clinical trial tests the hypothesis that intraperitoneal local anesthetic is superior to continuous IV infusion for pain management . Primary outcome was morphine consumption during 0 to 24 h. Informed consent was obtained from 60 patients , age 30 to 75 yr , American Society of Anesthesiologists physical status I to II , undergoing abdominal hysterectomy . A computer-generated program randomized patients in parallel arms to group IV : continuous infusion of lidocaine 50 mg/h ( 10 ml ) IV and saline 10 ml/h intermittently intraperitoneal ; group IP : injection of lidocaine 50 mg/h ( 10 ml ) once every hour intraperitoneally and continuous infusion of saline 10 ml/h intravenously ; and group P ( placebo ) : saline 10 ml/h both intravenously and intermittent intraperitoneal injection . Postoperative morphine consumption , pain intensity , recovery , home discharge , and lidocaine concentrations were measured . Morphine consumption during 0 to 24 h was lower in group IP versus group IV , mean difference -22.6 mg ( 95 % CI , 11.4 to 33.8 ; P < 0.01 ) . No difference was seen between group IV and group P. The total mean plasma concentration of lidocaine in group IP was significantly lower than group IV , 0 to 4.5 h postoperatively ( P = 0.03 ) with no evidence of systemic toxicity . Pain intensity and other recovery parameters were similar between the groups . The lower supplemental morphine consumption and plasma lidocaine concentration in group IP would confirm that the effects of local anesthetics are likely to be predominant via local intraperitoneal receptors or anti-inflammatory effects and not via central mechanisms alone .
rewrite: The mechanism of analgesia from intraperitoneal local anesthetics—whether local or central—remains uncertain. This double-blind trial tests the hypothesis that intraperitoneal local anesthetic provides better pain control than continuous IV infusion. The primary outcome was morphine use over 0–24 h. Sixty patients, aged 30–75 yr, ASA I–II, scheduled for abdominal hysterectomy, gave informed consent. A computer program randomized patients into parallel arms: group IV received continuous IV lidocaine (50 mg/h) plus intermittent intraperitoneal saline; group IP received hourly intraperitoneal lidocaine (50 mg) plus continuous IV saline; group P (placebo) received both IV and intraperitoneal saline. Postoperative morphine use, pain scores, recovery, discharge time, and lidocaine levels were recorded. Morphine consumption over 0–24 h was lower in group IP than group IV, mean difference –22.6 mg (95% CI 11.4–33.8; P<0.01). No difference was found between group IV and group P. Total mean plasma lidocaine concentration was significantly lower in group IP than group IV up to 4.5 h postoperatively (P=0.03), with no systemic toxicity. Pain intensity and recovery measures were similar across groups. Reduced morphine use and lower plasma lidocaine in group IP suggest that local anesthetic effects are likely mediated mainly by intraperitoneal receptors or anti-inflammatory actions, not solely by central mechanisms.

text: To evaluate the effect of scapular stabilization during horizontal adduction stretching ( cross-body ) on posterior shoulder tightness ( PST ) and passive internal rotation ( IR ) . Randomized controlled trial with single blinding . Athletic club . Asymptomatic volleyball players who are women with glenohumeral internal rotation deficit ( N = 60 ) . Subjects were randomly assigned to either horizontal adduction stretching with manual scapular stabilization ( n = 30 ) or horizontal adduction stretching without stabilization ( n = 30 ) . Passive stretching was performed for 3 - to 30-second holds in both groups . Range of motion measurements of PST and IR were performed on the athlete 's dominant shoulder prior to and immediately after the intervention . Baseline mean angular measurements of PST and IR for all athletes involved in the study were 6214 and 4010 , respectively , with no significant difference between groups ( P = .598 and P = .734 , respectively ) . Mean PST measurements were significantly different between groups after the horizontal adduction stretch , with a mean angle of 8317 among the scapular stabilization group and 6513 among the nonstabilization group ( P < .001 ) . Measurements of IR were also significantly different between groups , with a mean angle of 5114 among the scapular stabilization group and 439 among the nonstabilization group ( P = .006 ) . Horizontal adduction stretches performed with scapular stabilization produced significantly greater improvements in IR and PST than horizontal adduction stretching without scapular stabilization .
rewrite: To assess the impact of scapular stabilization during cross-body horizontal adduction stretching on posterior shoulder tightness (PST) and passive internal rotation (IR). A single-blinded randomized controlled trial was conducted. Setting: an athletic club. Participants: asymptomatic female volleyball players with glenohumeral internal rotation deficit (N=60). Participants were randomly allocated to either horizontal adduction stretching with manual scapular stabilization (n=30) or horizontal adduction stretching without stabilization (n=30). Both groups performed passive stretching with 3 to 30-second holds. PST and IR range of motion was measured on the dominant shoulder before and after the intervention. Baseline mean angular values for PST and IR across all athletes were 6214 and 4010, respectively, showing no significant intergroup differences (P=.598 and P=.734, respectively). Post-stretch mean PST differed significantly between groups, with 8317 in the scapular stabilization group and 6513 in the nonstabilization group (P<.001). IR measurements also showed a significant intergroup difference, with a mean angle of 5114 in the scapular stabilization group and 439 in the nonstabilization group (P=.006). Horizontal adduction stretching with scapular stabilization led to significantly greater enhancements in IR and PST compared to stretching without stabilization.

text: To evaluate the effectiveness of total laparoscopic hysterectomy compared with laparoscopic supracervical hysterectomy for alleviating dysmenorrhoea . Randomised blinded controlled trial . Norwegian university teaching hospital . Sixty-two women with dysmenorrhoea . Participants randomised to either total laparoscopic hysterectomy ( n = 31 ) or laparoscopic supracervical hysterectomy ( n = 31 ) . The primary outcome measure , measured 12 months after intervention , was reduction of cyclic pelvic pain ( visual analogue scale , 0-10 ) . Secondary outcome measures included patient satisfaction ( visual analogue scale , 0-10 ) and quality of life ( Short Form 36 , 0-100 ) . The groups were comparable at baseline . There was no difference in self-reported dysmenorrhoea at 12 months ( mean 0.8 [ SD 1.6 ] versus 0.8 [ SD 2.0 ] , P = 0.94 ) . There was no difference in patient satisfaction ( mean 9.3 [ SD 1.5 ] versus 9.1 [ SD 1.2 ] , P = 0.66 ) or quality of life ( mean 81.6 [ SD 17.8 ] versus 80.2 [ SD 18.0 ] , P = 0.69 ) . Improvement in dysmenorrhoea and quality of life as well as patient satisfaction were comparable in the medium term when comparing total laparoscopic hysterectomy with laparoscopic supracervical hysterectomy .
rewrite: To assess the efficacy of total laparoscopic hysterectomy versus laparoscopic supracervical hysterectomy in relieving dysmenorrhoea. Randomised blinded controlled trial. Norwegian university teaching hospital. Sixty-two women with dysmenorrhoea. Participants were randomised to either total laparoscopic hysterectomy (n = 31) or laparoscopic supracervical hysterectomy (n = 31). The primary outcome, measured 12 months post-intervention, was reduction in cyclic pelvic pain (visual analogue scale, 0-10). Secondary outcomes included patient satisfaction (visual analogue scale, 0-10) and quality of life (Short Form 36, 0-100). Baseline characteristics were similar between groups. No difference was found in self-reported dysmenorrhoea at 12 months (mean 0.8 [SD 1.6] versus 0.8 [SD 2.0], P = 0.94). No difference was observed in patient satisfaction (mean 9.3 [SD 1.5] versus 9.1 [SD 1.2], P = 0.66) or quality of life (mean 81.6 [SD 17.8] versus 80.2 [SD 18.0], P = 0.69). Improvements in dysmenorrhoea, quality of life, and patient satisfaction were comparable in the medium term between total laparoscopic hysterectomy and laparoscopic supracervical hysterectomy.

text: Nonadherence to treatment leads to suboptimal treatment outcomes and enormous costs to the economy . This is especially important in Parkinson 's disease ( PD ) . The progressive nature of the degenerative process , the complex treatment regimens and the high rates of comorbid conditions make treatment adherence in PD a challenge . Clinicians have limited face-to-face consultation time with PD patients , making it difficult to comprehensively address non-adherence . The rapid growth of digital technologies provides an opportunity to improve adherence and the quality of decision-making during consultation . The aim of this randomised controlled trial ( RCT ) is to evaluate the impact of using a smartphone and web applications to promote patient self-management as a tool to increase treatment adherence and working with the data collected to enhance the quality of clinical consultation . A 4-month multicentre RCT with 222 patients will be conducted to compare use of a smartphone - and internet-enabled Parkinson 's tracker smartphone app with treatment as usual for patients with PD and/or their carers . The study investigators will compare the two groups immediately after intervention . Seven centres across England ( 6 ) and Scotland ( 1 ) will be involved . The primary objective of this trial is to assess whether patients with PD who use the app show improved medication adherence compared to those receiving treatment as usual alone . The secondary objectives are to investigate whether patients who receive the app and those who receive treatment as usual differ in terms of quality of life , quality of clinical consultation , overall disease state and activities of daily living . We also aim to investigate the experience of those receiving the intervention by conducting qualitative interviews with a sample of participants and clinicians , which will be administered by independent researchers . ISRCTN45824264 ( registered 5 November 2013 ) .
rewrite: Failure to follow treatment plans results in poor health outcomes and significant economic burdens. This issue is particularly critical in Parkinson's disease (PD). The progressive degenerative nature, complex treatment schedules, and high prevalence of coexisting conditions make adherence difficult in PD. Clinicians have limited consultation time with PD patients, hindering thorough management of non-adherence. The swift advancement of digital technology offers a chance to enhance adherence and improve decision-making in consultations. This randomized controlled trial (RCT) aims to assess the effect of smartphone and web applications that support patient self-management, designed to boost treatment adherence and use collected data to improve consultation quality. A 4-month multicenter RCT involving 222 patients will compare a smartphone- and internet-based Parkinson’s tracker app with standard care for PD patients and/or their caregivers. Additionally, qualitative interviews with selected participants and clinicians, conducted by independent researchers, will explore the intervention experience. ISRCTN45824264 (registered 5 November 2013).

text: Higher-risk patients may not receive evidence-based therapy because of limited life expectancy , which is a composite measure that encompasses many patient factors , including age , frailty , and comorbidities . In this study , we evaluated the extent to which treatment care gaps can be explained by a difference in projected life expectancy . An observational cohort study was conducted on acute myocardial infarction patients hospitalized in Ontario , Canada . Projected life expectancy was estimated using actual survival data with extrapolation using proportional hazard models adjusting for important covariates . The relationship between projected life expectancy with statins and reperfusion therapy was examined using generalized linear models . Among the 7001 acute myocardial infarction patients , 84.3 % were prescribed statins and 72.9 % were treated with reperfusion therapy . When projected life expectancy was < 10 years , the likelihood of receiving either treatment declined progressively with reduction in life expectancy ( P < 0.001 ) . At the 25th percentile of projected life expectancies , the likelihood of receiving a statin decreased by 1.4 % ( 95 % confidence interval , 1.0-1 .8 % ) , and acute reperfusion therapy decreased by 2.6 % ( 95 % confidence interval , 1.8-3 .3 % ) for each year decline in projected life expectancy . Life expectancy of a patient strongly influences evidence-based treatment in acute myocardial infarction . It was seen not only among patients with limited life expectancies but also among those with many years to live . Treatment care gaps may reflect clinicians ' synthesis about frailty and life-expectancy gains .
rewrite: Patients at higher risk might not get evidence-based treatments due to shorter projected life spans, a measure that includes factors like age, frailty, and other health conditions. This study assessed how much differences in estimated life expectancy account for gaps in treatment. We performed an observational cohort analysis on acute myocardial infarction patients admitted to hospitals in Ontario, Canada. Projected life expectancy was calculated from actual survival data, extrapolated with proportional hazard models that adjusted for key covariates. Generalized linear models were used to analyze the link between projected life expectancy and the use of statins and reperfusion therapy. Of the 7001 acute myocardial infarction patients, 84.3% were given statins and 72.9% underwent reperfusion therapy. When projected life expectancy fell below 10 years, the chance of receiving either treatment dropped steadily as life expectancy decreased (P < 0.001). At the 25th percentile of projected life expectancies, each year of decline reduced the likelihood of statin prescription by 1.4% (95% CI, 1.0–1.8%) and of acute reperfusion therapy by 2.6% (95% CI, 1.8–3.3%). A patient’s life expectancy significantly affects evidence-based care in acute myocardial infarction. This pattern was observed not only in patients with limited life expectancies but also in those with many years remaining. Gaps in treatment may mirror clinicians’ overall judgment regarding frailty and potential gains in life expectancy.

text: Gemcitabine combined with carboplatin ( GC ) is a widely used regimen for advanced non-small cell lung cancer ( NSCLC ) , but clinical outcome is still hampered by its toxicity . We conducted a randomized phase II study of GC and compared biweekly versus standard schedules in patients with advanced NSCLC with respect to toxicity and outcome . Forty patients with stage IIIB or IV NSCLC were randomized to receive either a biweekly regimen of GC [ gemcitabine ( 1,000 mg/m ( 2 ) on days 1 and 14 ) and carboplatin ( area under the concentration-time curve , AUC = 3 on days 1 and 14 ) ] every 28 days or a standard regimen of GC [ gemcitabine ( 1,000 mg/m ( 2 ) on days 1 and 8 ) and carboplatin ( AUC = 5 on day 1 ) ] every 21 days . These cycles were repeated until disease progression . Response rates were 55 % for the biweekly regimen and 40 % for the standard regimen . Median overall and progression-free survival times were 19.7 and 6.2 months , respectively , for the biweekly regimen , and 11.8 and 2.8 months , respectively , for the standard GC regimen . Hematologic toxicity was prominent . However , the incidence of grade 1 or 2 thrombocytopenia was significantly lower in the biweekly than in the standard GC regimen ( p < 0.05 ) . Nonhematologic toxicity was mild . A biweekly GC regimen was better tolerated than a standard GC regimen in patients with advanced NSCLC .
rewrite: The combination of gemcitabine and carboplatin (GC) is a common treatment for advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), yet its effectiveness is often limited by toxicity. This randomized phase II trial evaluated biweekly versus standard GC schedules in advanced NSCLC patients, focusing on toxicity and outcomes. Forty stage IIIB or IV NSCLC patients were assigned to either a biweekly GC regimen [gemcitabine (1,000 mg/m² on days 1 and 14) plus carboplatin (AUC = 3 on days 1 and 14)] every 28 days, or a standard GC regimen [gemcitabine (1,000 mg/m² on days 1 and 8) with carboplatin (AUC = 5 on day 1)] every 21 days. Treatment continued until disease progression. Response rates were 55% for biweekly and 40% for standard therapy. Median overall and progression-free survival were 19.7 and 6.2 months, respectively, with biweekly dosing, versus 11.8 and 2.8 months with standard GC. Hematologic toxicity was notable, but grade 1 or 2 thrombocytopenia occurred less frequently with biweekly than standard GC (p < 0.05). Nonhematologic side effects were generally mild. The biweekly GC schedule demonstrated better tolerability in advanced NSCLC patients compared to the standard regimen.

text: The efficacy of topical ophthalmic corticosteroids depends upon small modifications in preparations , such as drug concentration.The aim of this study was to confirm that hydrocortisone acetate ( HC-ac ) ophthalmic ointments of 2.5 % and 1 % are more effective than a 0.5 % eye ointment . In this randomized , double-blind , placebo-controlled , parallel-group clinical study , the change of signs and symptoms of acute inflammation of the ocular surface and adnexa was evaluated in 411 subjects . Median time to clinically relevant response as estimated by 50 % reduction in clinical signs and symptoms ( CSS ) total score over the entire trial was similar for subjects treated with HC-ac 2.5 % ( 73.5 h ) and for subjects treated with HC-ac 1.0 % ( 67.7 h ) and was considerably and significantly longer for subjects treated with HC-ac 0.5 % ( 111.8 h ) [ p < 0.001 for both dosages ] . All trial medications were safe and well tolerated . Hydrocortisone acetate 2.5 % and Hydrocortisone acetate 1 % eye ointments are efficacious and safe treatments for acute inflammations of the ocular surface or adnexa , and showed significantly better efficacy than a control group treated with Hydrocortisone acetate 0.5 % therapy . Current Controlled Trials ISRCTN15464650 .
rewrite: The effectiveness of topical ophthalmic corticosteroids relies on minor adjustments in formulations, including drug concentration. This study aimed to verify that hydrocortisone acetate (HC-ac) ophthalmic ointments at 2.5% and 1% are superior to a 0.5% ointment. In this randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group clinical trial, changes in signs and symptoms of acute ocular surface and adnexa inflammation were assessed in 411 participants. Median time to clinically relevant response, defined as a 50% reduction in clinical signs and symptoms (CSS) total score throughout the trial, was comparable for subjects receiving HC-ac 2.5% (73.5 h) and HC-ac 1.0% (67.7 h), and was notably and significantly longer for those treated with HC-ac 0.5% (111.8 h) [p < 0.001 for both dosages]. Hydrocortisone acetate 2.5% and 1% eye ointments are effective and safe for acute inflammations of the ocular surface or adnexa, demonstrating significantly greater efficacy than a control group treated with Hydrocortisone acetate 0.5% therapy. Current Controlled Trials ISRCTN15464650.

text: To determine if motivational interviewing ( MI ) improves self-efficacy ( primary outcome ) , depressive symptoms ( secondary outcome ) , and stage-of-readiness-to-change ( secondary outcome ) among women in abusive relationships . Randomized controlled trial among women who experienced intimate partner violence in a current relationship over the past 12 months . Subjects were recruited from two family planning clinics ( December 2007 to May 2010 ) . The intervention included an initial face-to-face session and three telephone sessions administered 1 - , 2 - , and 4-months postenrollment , each using MI to identify personal goals . Controls were referred to community-based resources . Outcomes were measured by self-administered questionnaires before randomization and 6 months later . Modified intent-to-treat analyses of completed participants were conducted using multivariate analysis of variance for continuous outcomes and polytomous logistic regression for categorical outcomes . Three hundred six eligible women were enrolled ( recruitment rate = 64 % ) ; 204 completed the 6-month follow-up ( completion rate = 67 % ) . Depressive symptoms decreased to a greater extent in MI than referral women ( P = .07 ) . Self-efficacy and stage-of-readiness-to-change increased more in MI than referral women , but these differences were not statistically significant . With a lower than projected sample size , our findings did not achieve statistical significance at the 5 % level but suggest a beneficial effect of the MI intervention on reducing depressive symptoms .
rewrite: This study assessed whether motivational interviewing (MI) enhances self-efficacy (primary outcome), depressive symptoms (secondary outcome), and stage-of-readiness-to-change (secondary outcome) in women experiencing intimate partner violence. A randomized controlled trial was conducted with women who reported abuse in a current relationship within the past year. Participants were recruited from two family planning clinics between December 2007 and May 2010. The intervention consisted of an initial in-person session followed by three telephone sessions at 1, 2, and 4 months post-enrollment, each employing MI to help set personal goals. The control group received referrals to community resources. Outcomes were evaluated via self-administered questionnaires at baseline and 6 months later. Modified intent-to-treat analyses were performed using multivariate analysis of variance for continuous outcomes and polytomous logistic regression for categorical outcomes. Of 306 eligible women enrolled (recruitment rate = 64%), 204 completed the 6-month follow-up (completion rate = 67%). Depressive symptoms showed a greater reduction in the MI group compared to the referral group (P = .07). Self-efficacy and stage-of-readiness-to-change improved more with MI, though these differences were not statistically significant. With a smaller than planned sample size, the results did not reach statistical significance at the 5% level but indicate a potential benefit of MI in alleviating depressive symptoms.

text: Long-term management of chronic conditions , such as atrial fibrillation ( AF ) , require frequent interactions with the healthcare systems . The multinational EUropean Patient Survey in Atrial Fibrillation ( EUPS-AF ) was conducted to investigate patient satisfaction with AF management in different of five European healthcare systems at a time of changing treatment paradigms for stroke prophylaxis , prior to the advent of newer oral anticoagulants . Adults ( > 18 years ) were recruited at random from the total populations of France , Germany , Italy , Spain and the UK using a randomized telephone dialling system . At least 300 respondents per country reporting to have a diagnosis of AF or receiving oral anticoagulation therapy for suspected AF or to have a heart rhythm disturbance completed a structured telephone interview . Most respondents were satisfied with their treatment for AF over the previous 12 months , with 85.5 % ( n = 1289 ) rating their care as good or better . Suboptimal clinical practices , however , were identified in several key areas . Coordination of primary and secondary care and a lack of patient engagement and support were particular issues , especially for those patients likely to have extensive contact with their healthcare system . In the context of Europe-wide guidelines for management of AF , most patients with AF were satisfied with their care , but for a greater proportion of patients , some aspects are unsatisfactory . Patient-centred surveys , such as the EUPS-AF , are crucial for understanding the factors that contribute to patient satisfaction and compliance with long-term treatment for chronic conditions .
rewrite: Long-term management of chronic conditions like atrial fibrillation (AF) necessitates frequent interactions with healthcare systems. The multinational European Patient Survey in Atrial Fibrillation (EUPS-AF) aimed to assess patient satisfaction with AF management across five European healthcare systems, during a period of evolving treatment approaches for stroke prevention before newer oral anticoagulants became available. Adults (over 18 years) were randomly selected from the general populations of France, Germany, Italy, Spain, and the UK using a randomized telephone dialing system. At least 300 respondents per country, who reported a diagnosis of AF, were on oral anticoagulation for suspected AF, or had a heart rhythm disturbance, completed a structured telephone interview. Most respondents expressed satisfaction with their AF treatment over the past year, with 85.5% (n = 1289) rating their care as good or better. However, suboptimal clinical practices were noted in several key areas. Issues included coordination between primary and secondary care, along with insufficient patient engagement and support, particularly for those with extensive healthcare system contact. Despite Europe-wide AF management guidelines, while most AF patients were content with their care, a significant proportion found certain aspects lacking. Patient-focused surveys, such as the EUPS-AF, are vital for identifying factors that influence patient satisfaction and adherence to long-term treatment for chronic conditions.

text: Previous research has indicated positive effects of early developmental intervention ( EDI ) on the development of children in developing countries . Few studies , however , have examined longitudinally when differential treatment effects may be observed and whether differential outcomes are associated with exposure to different risk factors and country of implementation . Also , birth asphyxia as a risk condition has not been well studied . To address these limitations , we conducted a randomized controlled trial to test the hypothesis that there will be differential developmental trajectories favoring those who receive EDI versus a health education intervention in children in rural areas of India , Pakistan , and Zambia . Children with and without birth asphyxia were randomized to EDI or control intervention , which was implemented by parents who received training in biweekly home visits initiated before child age 1 month and continuing until 36 months . Development was assessed in 376 children at ages 12 , 24 , and 36 months using the Bayley Scales of Infant Development and Ages & Stages Questionnaire administered by evaluators blind to intervention assignment and risk condition . Longitudinal mixed model analysis indicated that EDI resulted in better development over 36 months in cognitive abilities , regardless of risk condition , maternal resources , child gender , or country . Psychomotor development and parent-reported general development showed similar trends as for cognitive abilities , but were not statistically different between intervention conditions . Developmental differences were observed first at 36 months of age . Early developmental intervention has promise for improving development in children across developing countries when exposed to various risk conditions . EDI should be one prominent approach used to begin to address long-term outcomes and intergenerational transmission of poverty .
rewrite: Earlier studies have shown beneficial impacts of early developmental intervention (EDI) on child development in developing nations. However, limited longitudinal research has explored when varying treatment effects might emerge and if divergent outcomes relate to differing risk factors or implementation country. Additionally, birth asphyxia as a risk factor has been insufficiently examined. To overcome these gaps, we performed a randomized controlled trial to evaluate the hypothesis that developmental trajectories will differ, favoring EDI over a health education intervention, among children in rural regions of India, Pakistan, and Zambia. Children with and without birth asphyxia were randomly assigned to EDI or a control intervention, delivered by parents trained through biweekly home visits starting before one month of age and lasting until 36 months. Development was evaluated in 376 children at 12, 24, and 36 months using the Bayley Scales of Infant Development and Ages & Stages Questionnaire, administered by assessors unaware of intervention group and risk status. Longitudinal mixed model analysis revealed that EDI led to enhanced development over 36 months in cognitive skills, irrespective of risk status, maternal resources, child sex, or country. Psychomotor development and parent-reported general development followed similar patterns as cognitive abilities but did not differ significantly between intervention groups. Developmental differences first appeared at 36 months. Early developmental intervention holds potential for enhancing development in children across developing countries facing diverse risk conditions. EDI should be a key strategy to help address long-term outcomes and the intergenerational cycle of poverty.

text: Patients with multiple sclerosis ( MS ) lose brain volume ( BV ) faster than healthy individuals . Our purpose , within the 12-month phase 3 TRANSFORMS study , was to examine the effect of treatment on BV loss in patient subgroups , establish correlations between baseline normalized BV ( NBV ) and baseline disease parameters , to identify variables predictive of baseline NBV and on-study percentage BV change ( PBVC ) , and to establish correlations between on-study PBVC and on-study efficacy outcomes . Patients received fingolimod 0.5 mg or 1.25 mg , or intramuscular ( IM ) interferon -1 a ( IFN-1a ) for 12 months . The effect of treatment on PBVC was examined in patient demographic , disease and magnetic resonance imaging ( MRI ) characteristic subgroups . Pearson 's correlation analyses and a stepwise linear regression model were used to identify variables predictive of NBV and PBVC . Fingolimod reduced BV loss over 12 months versus IFN-1a IM in all patient subgroups assessed , including individuals with or without gadolinium ( Gd ) - enhancing lesions at baseline . Baseline T1 hypointense lesion volume had the strongest correlation with baseline NBV . Baseline Gd-enhancing T1 lesion count was most predictive of change in PBVC over 12 months . Our results improve understanding of the contributions of different baseline demographic , clinical and MRI characteristics to NBV , including factors that may be predictive of future BV loss .
rewrite: Individuals with multiple sclerosis (MS) experience a more rapid decline in brain volume (BV) compared to healthy people. In the 12-month phase 3 TRANSFORMS trial, we aimed to assess treatment impact on BV loss across patient subgroups, correlate baseline normalized BV (NBV) with baseline disease measures, pinpoint predictors for baseline NBV and on-study percentage BV change (PBVC), and link on-study PBVC with efficacy outcomes. Participants were administered fingolimod 0.5 mg or 1.25 mg, or intramuscular (IM) interferon-1a (IFN-1a) for one year. Treatment effects on PBVC were analyzed within subgroups based on demographics, disease status, and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) features. Pearson’s correlation and stepwise linear regression identified predictors of NBV and PBVC. Fingolimod lessened BV loss over 12 months relative to IFN-1a IM in all evaluated subgroups, including those with or without gadolinium (Gd)-enhancing lesions at baseline. Baseline T1 hypointense lesion volume showed the strongest association with baseline NBV. Baseline Gd-enhancing T1 lesion count was the top predictor of PBVC change over 12 months. These findings enhance insight into how various baseline demographic, clinical, and MRI factors contribute to NBV, including elements that may forecast future BV loss.

text: Dietary nitrate , which is in green leafy vegetables and beetroot , decreases blood pressure through the enterosalivary nitrate-nitrite-nitric oxide pathway in healthy individuals . Whether similar effects would occur in individuals with treated hypertension and , therefore , at increased risk of cardiovascular disease is unclear . We assessed whether increased dietary nitrate intake by using beetroot juice for 1 wk lowers blood pressure in treated hypertensive men and women . Participants ( n = 27 ) were recruited to a randomized , placebo-controlled , double-blind crossover trial . The effect of 1-wk intake of nitrate-rich beetroot juice was compared with 1-wk intake of nitrate-depleted beetroot juice ( placebo ) . The primary outcome was blood pressure assessed by measuring home blood pressure during the intervention and 24-h ambulatory blood pressure on day 7 of the intervention . Other outcomes included nitrate metabolism assessed by measuring nitrate and nitrite in plasma , saliva , and urine . Relative to the placebo , 1-wk intake of nitrate-rich beetroot juice resulted in a 3-fold increase in plasma nitrite and nitrate , a 7-fold increase in salivary nitrite , an 8-fold higher salivary nitrate , and a 4-fold increase in both urinary nitrite and nitrate ( P < 0.001 ) . However , no differences in home blood pressure and 24-h ambulatory blood pressure were observed with 1-wk intake of nitrate-rich beetroot juice in comparison with the placebo . An increase in dietary nitrate intake may not be an effective short-term approach to further lower blood pressure in treated hypertensive subjects .
rewrite: Dietary nitrate, found in leafy greens and beetroot, reduces blood pressure via the enterosalivary nitrate-nitrite-nitric oxide pathway in healthy people. It remains uncertain whether comparable effects would happen in those with treated hypertension, who face higher cardiovascular risk. We evaluated if boosting dietary nitrate intake with beetroot juice over one week lowers blood pressure in treated hypertensive men and women. Participants (n=27) were enrolled in a randomized, placebo-controlled, double-blind crossover trial. One week of nitrate-rich beetroot juice was compared to one week of nitrate-depleted beetroot juice (placebo). The main outcome was blood pressure, measured through home monitoring during the intervention and 24-hour ambulatory monitoring on day 7. Additional outcomes involved nitrate metabolism, assessed by plasma, saliva, and urine levels of nitrate and nitrite. Compared to placebo, one week of nitrate-rich beetroot juice led to a 3-fold rise in plasma nitrite and nitrate, a 7-fold increase in salivary nitrite, an 8-fold higher salivary nitrate, and a 4-fold rise in both urinary nitrite and nitrate (P<0.001). Yet, no differences in home or 24-hour ambulatory blood pressure were seen with nitrate-rich beetroot juice versus placebo. Increasing dietary nitrate intake may not be a viable short-term strategy to further reduce blood pressure in treated hypertensive individuals.

text: Hospitalization for acute heart failure ( HF ) is associated with high rates of subsequent mortality and readmission . We assessed the influence of the time interval between previous HF hospitalization and randomization in the Candesartan in Heart failure : Reduction in Mortality and morbidity ( CHARM ) trials on clinical outcomes in patients with both reduced and preserved ejection fraction . CHARM enrolled 7599 patients with New York Heart Association class II to IV HF , of whom 5426 had a history of previous HF hospitalization . Cox proportional hazards regression models were used to assess the association between time from previous HF hospitalization and randomization and the primary outcome of cardiovascular death or unplanned admission to hospital for the management of worsening HF during a median of 36.6 months . For patients with HF and reduced or preserved ejection fraction , rates of cardiovascular mortality and HF hospitalization were higher among patients with previous HF hospitalization than those without . The risk for mortality and hospitalization varied inversely with the time interval between hospitalization and randomization . Rates were higher for patients with HF and reduced ejection fraction within each category . Event rates for those with HF with preserved ejection fraction and a HF hospitalization in the 6 months before randomization were comparable with the rate in patients with HF and reduced ejection fraction with no previous HF hospitalization . Rates of cardiovascular death or HF hospitalization are greatest in those who have been previously hospitalized for HF . Independent of EF , rates of death and readmission decline as time from HF hospitalization to trial enrollment increased . Recent HF hospitalization identifies a high-risk population for future clinical trials in HF and reduced ejection fraction and HF with preserved ejection fraction . http://www.clinicaltrials.gov . Unique identifier : NCT00634400 .
rewrite: Hospitalization for acute heart failure (HF) is linked to elevated subsequent mortality and readmission rates. We evaluated how the time from prior HF hospitalization to randomization in the Candesartan in Heart failure: Reduction in Mortality and morbidity (CHARM) trials affected outcomes in patients with reduced and preserved ejection fraction. CHARM included 7599 patients with New York Heart Association class II to IV HF, of which 5426 had a prior HF hospitalization. Cox proportional hazards models assessed the relationship between time from last HF hospitalization to randomization and the primary outcome of cardiovascular death or unplanned admission for worsening HF over a median of 36.6 months. For patients with HF and reduced or preserved ejection fraction, cardiovascular mortality and HF hospitalization rates were higher in those with prior HF hospitalization than without. Risk for mortality and hospitalization inversely correlated with the interval between hospitalization and randomization. Rates were higher for patients with HF and reduced ejection fraction across all intervals. Event rates for those with HF with preserved ejection fraction and a HF hospitalization within 6 months before randomization were similar to rates in patients with HF and reduced ejection fraction without prior HF hospitalization. Cardiovascular death or HF hospitalization rates are highest in those previously hospitalized for HF. Regardless of EF, death and readmission rates decrease as time from HF hospitalization to trial enrollment lengthens. Recent HF hospitalization defines a high-risk group for future trials in HF with reduced ejection fraction and HF with preserved ejection fraction. http://www.clinicaltrials.gov. Unique identifier: NCT00634400.

text: The aim of the current study is to compare the accuracy of the ultrasound ( US ) versus clinical assessment for determination of the spinal level , using X-ray as the Gold Standard for control . 200 patients were randomized into two equal groups . Patients in the Clinical Group were examined by landmarks to assess the Assumed Clinical Tuffier 's Line , and then by fluoroscopy to determine the True Clinical Tuffier 's Line . Patients in the Ultrasound Group were examined by the ultrasound to determine the Ultrasound Tuffier 's Line . The results of both groups were compared in relation to the plain X-ray , done for each patient , which determined the Radiological Tuffier 's Line . In the Clinical Group , the True Clinical Tuffier 's line met the Assumed Tuffier 's line in only 12 % of the patients . In the remaining patients , wrong leveling ranged from one space above in 80 % to 2 spaces above in 7 % and in 1 % of patients the line was at L2 . In the Ultrasound Group , wrong leveling occurred in 22 % of patients . The Ultrasound misidentification was less than one level in 17 % and one level in 5 % of patients . Ultrasound examination had a true limitation of 2 % of patients . Ultrasound examination of the spine is recommended in patients planned for spinal anesthesia , as it is superior to clinical assessment in identification of the interspinous levels . This will decrease the hazard of spinal cord trauma .
rewrite: This study aims to evaluate the accuracy of ultrasound (US) compared to clinical assessment in determining spinal level, using X-ray as the Gold Standard. 200 patients were equally randomized into two groups. The Clinical Group underwent landmark examination to identify the Assumed Clinical Tuffier's Line, followed by fluoroscopy to establish the True Clinical Tuffier's Line. The Ultrasound Group was assessed via ultrasound to locate the Ultrasound Tuffier's Line. Both groups' results were compared against plain X-rays performed for each patient, which defined the Radiological Tuffier's Line. In the Clinical Group, the True Clinical Tuffier's line aligned with the Assumed Tuffier's line in only 12% of patients. Among the rest, incorrect leveling ranged from one space above in 80% to two spaces above in 7%, with 1% of patients having the line at L2. In the Ultrasound Group, wrong leveling occurred in 22% of patients. Ultrasound misidentification was less than one level in 17% and one level in 5% of patients. Ultrasound examination had a true limitation in 2% of patients. Ultrasound examination of the spine is advised for patients scheduled for spinal anesthesia, as it outperforms clinical assessment in identifying interspinous levels, thereby reducing the risk of spinal cord trauma.

text: The effectiveness of extracorporeal shock wave therapy in the treatment of plantar fasciitis is controversial . The objective of the present study was to test whether focused extracorporeal shock wave therapy is effective in relieving chronic heel pain diagnosed as plantar fasciitis . Two hundred and fifty subjects were enrolled in a prospective , multicenter , double-blind , randomized , and placebo-controlled U.S. Food and Drug Administration trial . Subjects were randomized to focused extracorporeal shock wave therapy ( 0.25 mJ/mm ( 2 ) ) or placebo intervention , with three sessions of 2000 impulses in weekly intervals . Primary outcomes were both the percentage change of heel pain on the visual analog scale composite score ( pain during first steps in the morning , pain with daily activities , and pain with a force meter ) and the Roles and Maudsley score at twelve weeks after the last intervention compared with the scores at baseline . Two hundred and forty-six patients ( 98.4 % ) were available for intention-to-treat analysis at the twelve-week follow-up . With regard to the first primary end point , the visual analog scale composite score , there was a significant difference ( p = 0.0027 , one-sided ) in the reduction of heel pain in the extracorporeal shock wave therapy group ( 69.2 % ) compared with the placebo therapy group ( 34.5 % ) . Extracorporeal shock wave therapy was also significantly superior to the placebo therapy for the Roles and Maudsley score ( p = 0.0006 , one-sided ) . Temporary pain and swelling during and after treatment were the only device-related adverse events observed . The results of the present study provide proof of the clinically relevant effect size of focused extracorporeal shock wave therapy without local anesthesia in the treatment of recalcitrant plantar fasciitis , with success rates between 50 % and 65 % . Therapeutic Level I. See Instructions for Authors for a complete description of levels of evidence .
rewrite: The efficacy of extracorporeal shock wave therapy for plantar fasciitis remains debated. This study aimed to evaluate whether focused extracorporeal shock wave therapy alleviates chronic heel pain diagnosed as plantar fasciitis. In a prospective, multicenter, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled U.S. FDA trial, 250 subjects were enrolled. Participants were randomly assigned to receive focused extracorporeal shock wave therapy (0.25 mJ/mm²) or a placebo intervention, administered in three weekly sessions of 2000 impulses each. Primary outcomes included the percentage change in heel pain on a visual analog scale composite score (assessing morning first-step pain, daily activity pain, and force meter pain) and the Roles and Maudsley score at twelve weeks post-intervention compared to baseline. At the twelve-week follow-up, 246 patients (98.4%) were available for intention-to-treat analysis. For the first primary endpoint, the visual analog scale composite score, a significant difference (p = 0.0027, one-sided) was observed in heel pain reduction in the shock wave therapy group (69.2%) versus the placebo group (34.5%). Shock wave therapy also showed significant superiority over placebo for the Roles and Maudsley score (p = 0.0006, one-sided). Temporary pain and swelling during and after treatment were the only device-related adverse events noted. These findings demonstrate a clinically relevant effect size for focused extracorporeal shock wave therapy without local anesthesia in treating recalcitrant plantar fasciitis, with success rates ranging from 50% to 65%. Therapeutic Level I. Refer to Instructions for Authors for full details on evidence levels.

text: Pneumonia is the leading cause of childhood mortality globally . Respiratory syncytial virus ( RSV ) is the most important viral cause of pneumonia . Maternal serum antibody protects infants from RSV disease . The objective of our study was to characterize RSV antibody levels in mother-infant pairs . Serial serum samples were collected from mother-infant pairs in Bangladesh from the third trimester of pregnancy to 72 weeks postpartum and tested using an RSV antibody microneutralization assay . Serologic infection was defined as a 4-fold increase in antibody titer . Maternal antibody half-life was calculated using infant antibody titers from birth to 20 weeks . The ratio of infant cord blood to maternal serum RSV antibody titers in 149 mother-infant pairs was 1.01 ( 95 % confidence interval [ CI ] , .99 -1.03 ) . Maternal RSV antibody titers in the third trimester and at birth were strongly correlated ( R = 0.68 ) . Antibody half-life was 38 days ( 95 % CI , 36-42 days ) . Higher cord blood RSV antibody titers were associated with a lower risk of serologic infection ( P = .01 ) and maintenance of antibody titer above a potentially protective threshold ( P < .001 ) . Efficient transplacental transfer of RSV-specific antibody from mother to the fetus was documented in mother-infant pairs in Asia . Higher cord blood antibody titers were associated with protection from serologic infection .
rewrite: Pneumonia remains the primary cause of death among children worldwide. Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is the most significant viral agent responsible for pneumonia. Maternal antibodies in the blood safeguard infants against RSV illness. Our research aimed to analyze RSV antibody concentrations in mother-infant pairs. Sequential blood samples were gathered from mother-infant pairs in Bangladesh, spanning from the third trimester of pregnancy to 72 weeks after birth, and evaluated with an RSV antibody microneutralization test. A serologic infection was identified by a fourfold rise in antibody titer. The half-life of maternal antibodies was determined using infant antibody levels from birth to 20 weeks. In 149 mother-infant pairs, the ratio of RSV antibody titers between infant cord blood and maternal serum was 1.01 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.99–1.03). Maternal RSV antibody levels in the third trimester and at delivery showed a strong correlation (R = 0.68). The antibody half-life was 38 days (95% CI, 36–42 days). Elevated cord blood RSV antibody titers were linked to a reduced likelihood of serologic infection (P = .01) and sustained antibody levels above a potentially protective threshold (P < .001). Efficient transfer of RSV-specific antibodies across the placenta from mother to fetus was observed in Asian mother-infant pairs. Higher cord blood antibody titers were correlated with protection from serologic infection.

text: The purpose of this study was to investigate the usefulness of a hydrocolloid dressing containing ceramide for hand-foot skin reaction ( HFSR ) on the soles of the feet in metastatic renal cell carcinoma ( RCC ) patients treated with sorafenib . Patients with grade 1 HFSR on the soles of the feet were randomly assigned in to two groups . One group received a hydrocolloid dressing containing ceramide ( arm A ) and the other received 10 % urea cream ( arm B ) . Patients in both groups applied treatment to the affected sites on the soles of the feet , but not to the hands . The primary end point was the incidence of grade 2 or 3 HFSR on the soles of the feet in the first 4 weeks . Thirty-three patients were assessed ( 17 in arm A and 16 in arm B ) , and there were no significant differences in baseline characteristics between the two groups . During the observation period of this study , grade 2 or 3 HFSR on the soles of the feet was found in 29 % of patients in arm A and was significantly less than the 69 % in arm B ( P = 0.03 ) . The incidence of HFSR on the hands , however , was similar in both arms . The median time to grade 2 or 3 HFSR on the soles of the feet was also significantly longer in arm A than in arm B ( P = 0.03 ) . These results indicate that a hydrocolloid dressing containing ceramide prevented the worsening of HFSR caused by sorafenib in metastatic RCC patients . UMIN000002016 .
rewrite: This study aimed to evaluate the efficacy of a ceramide-containing hydrocolloid dressing for managing hand-foot skin reaction (HFSR) on the soles of metastatic renal cell carcinoma (RCC) patients undergoing sorafenib therapy. Participants with grade 1 HFSR on the soles were randomly divided into two groups: one receiving the ceramide hydrocolloid dressing (arm A) and the other using 10% urea cream (arm B). Treatments were applied only to the affected areas on the soles, not the hands. The primary outcome was the occurrence of grade 2 or 3 HFSR on the soles within the initial four weeks. Among the 33 patients evaluated (17 in arm A, 16 in arm B), baseline characteristics were comparable. During the study, grade 2 or 3 HFSR on the soles developed in 29% of arm A patients, significantly lower than the 69% in arm B (P = 0.03). HFSR incidence on the hands was similar between groups. The median time to grade 2 or 3 HFSR on the soles was also significantly longer in arm A compared to arm B (P = 0.03). These findings suggest that the ceramide hydrocolloid dressing helps prevent the progression of sorafenib-induced HFSR in metastatic RCC patients. UMIN000002016.

text: In patients with moderate-to-severe psoriasis , health-related quality of life ( HRQOL ) has been shown to improve in parallel with improvement in disease severity . To evaluate the role of pruritus ( itch ) in mediating the relationship between improvements in disease severity and HRQOL . Data from a phase 2 clinical trial , in which 142 patients with moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis received ixekizumab or placebo , were used for this posthoc analysis . Relationships between improvement in Psoriasis Area and Severity Index ( PASI ) , Itch Visual Analogue Scale ( VAS ) and Dermatology Life Quality Index ( DLQI ) , as well as in individual DLQI domains ( symptoms and feelings , treatment , work and school , daily activities , leisure , and personal relationships ) from baseline to week 16 were determined . Multiple hierarchical linear regressions and Sobel tests were conducted to evaluate the results . Improvement in PASI was highly correlated with pruritus improvement and improvements in DLQI total and domain scores at week 16 ( P < 001 ) . Multiple hierarchical linear regression analyses showed a statistically significant ( P < 001 ) association between improvement in pruritus and improvement in DLQI total score and each of the six DLQI domain scores after adjusting for improvement in PASI . Sobel tests indicated that pruritus had a significant mediation effect ( P < 005 ) on the association of PASI improvement with improvement in DLQI total score and all domains except the personal relationships score . Pruritus appears to be an important mediator of the association between improvements in disease severity and HRQOL in patients with moderate-to-severe psoriasis .
rewrite: In individuals with moderate-to-severe psoriasis, enhancements in health-related quality of life (HRQOL) have been observed to coincide with reductions in disease severity. This analysis aimed to assess the role of pruritus (itch) in mediating the link between disease severity improvements and HRQOL. Utilizing data from a phase 2 clinical trial involving 142 patients with moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis treated with ixekizumab or placebo, a posthoc analysis was performed. Changes from baseline to week 16 in the Psoriasis Area and Severity Index (PASI), Itch Visual Analogue Scale (VAS), and Dermatology Life Quality Index (DLQI), including its domains (symptoms and feelings, treatment, work and school, daily activities, leisure, and personal relationships), were examined. Multiple hierarchical linear regressions and Sobel tests were applied to analyze the data. PASI improvement was strongly correlated with reductions in pruritus and enhancements in DLQI total and domain scores at week 16 (P < 0.001). After adjusting for PASI improvement, multiple hierarchical linear regression analyses revealed a statistically significant (P < 0.001) association between pruritus improvement and improvements in the DLQI total score and all six DLQI domains. Sobel tests demonstrated that pruritus significantly mediated (P < 0.05) the relationship between PASI improvement and enhancements in the DLQI total score and all domains except personal relationships.
