ALICAT is a randomized, multi-centre phase two mixed-methods investigation comprising three parts: a randomized controlled trial, an embedded qualitative study, and a survey examining care pathways. The randomized controlled trial will assess continued low molecular weight heparin treatment for cancer-associated thrombosis against stopping at six months (current standard practice) in patients with locally advanced or metastatic cancer. The embedded qualitative study will involve clinician focus groups to explore recruitment attitudes and challenges in advancing to a full randomized controlled trial, along with semi-structured interviews with patients and relatives/carers to understand their perspectives on participation and identify potential barriers and concerns. Additionally, a UK-wide survey will be conducted to create a classification and enumeration system for cancer-associated thrombosis care models and pathways. Evidence is scarce regarding the optimal anticoagulation duration for cancer-associated thrombosis, leading to variability in treatment length. The ALICAT study will evaluate the feasibility of enrolling patients for a phase three trial. Current Controlled Trials ISRCTN37913976.

text: The ACOSOG ( American College of Surgeons Oncology Group ) Z9001 ( Alliance ) study , a randomized , placebo-controlled trial , demonstrated that 1 year of adjuvant imatinib prolonged recurrence-free survival ( RFS ) after resection of primary GI stromal tumor ( GIST ) . We sought to determine the pathologic and molecular factors associated with patient outcome . There were 328 patients assigned to the placebo arm and 317 to the imatinib arm . Median patient follow-up was 74 months . There were 645 tumor specimens available for mitotic rate or mutation analysis . RFS remained superior in the imatinib arm ( hazard ratio , 0.6 ; 95 % CI , 0.43 to 0.75 ; Cox model-adjusted P < .001 ) . On multivariable analysis of patients in the placebo arm , large tumor size , small bowel location , and high mitotic rate were associated with lower RFS , whereas tumor genotype was not significantly associated with RFS . Multivariable analysis of patients in the imatinib arm yielded similar findings . When comparing the two arms , imatinib therapy was associated with higher RFS in patients with a KIT exon 11 deletion of any type , but not a KIT exon 11 insertion or point mutation , KIT exon 9 mutation , PDGFRA mutation , or wild-type tumor , although some of these patient groups were small . Adjuvant imatinib did not seem to alter overall survival . Our findings show that tumor size , location , and mitotic rate , but not tumor genotype , are associated with the natural history of GIST . Patients with KIT exon 11 deletions assigned to 1 year of adjuvant imatinib had a longer RFS .
rewrite: The ACOSOG (American College of Surgeons Oncology Group) Z9001 (Alliance) trial, a randomized, placebo-controlled study, showed that one year of adjuvant imatinib improved recurrence-free survival (RFS) following resection of primary gastrointestinal stromal tumor (GIST). We aimed to identify pathologic and molecular factors linked to patient outcomes. The placebo arm included 328 patients, while 317 were in the imatinib arm. Median follow-up was 74 months. Mitotic rate or mutation analysis was performed on 645 tumor specimens. RFS continued to be better in the imatinib arm (hazard ratio, 0.6; 95% CI, 0.43 to 0.75; Cox model-adjusted P < .001). In multivariable analysis of placebo-arm patients, larger tumor size, small bowel site, and high mitotic rate correlated with reduced RFS, but tumor genotype did not significantly affect RFS. Multivariable analysis in the imatinib arm produced similar results. Comparing both arms, imatinib therapy was linked to higher RFS in patients with any KIT exon 11 deletion, but not in those with KIT exon 11 insertion or point mutation, KIT exon 9 mutation, PDGFRA mutation, or wild-type tumors, though some groups were small. Adjuvant imatinib did not appear to change overall survival. Our results indicate that tumor size, location, and mitotic rate, but not genotype, relate to the natural history of GIST. Patients with KIT exon 11 deletions assigned to one year of adjuvant imatinib experienced longer RFS.

text: To analyse late morbidity and mortality in pre and post-menopausal breast cancer patients treated with postmastectomy radiotherapy , with emphasis on side-effects from the heart , cerebrovascular and respiratory systems . Long term follow-up of two randomised , clinical trials with 1100 patients was carried out . Pre-menopausal women were allocated to radiotherapy ( RT ) , RT + oral cyclophosphamide ( RT+C ) or cyclophosphamide only ( C ) . Post-menopausal women were allocated to RT , RT+T amoxifen for one year ( RT+T am ) or tamoxifen only ( Tam ) . Information on admission to hospital , mortality and causes of death was obtained from national registers . After 25 years , adding RT to cyclophosphamide in pre-menopausal women raised the mortality from heart disease from zero to 0.8 % ( p = 0.04 ) . In post-menopausal women , adding RT to Tam raised the mortality from heart disease from 10.5 % to 18.4 % ( p = 0.005 ) . In post-menopausal women mortality due to cerebrovascular disease increased from 3.4 % to 8.7 % by adding RT to Tam ( p = 0.015 ) . The differences were not evident until in the second decade of follow-up . In spite of differences in specific causes of death , there were no significant differences between the treatment arms concerning morbidity or overall mortality . Postmastectomy radiotherapy to the chest wall and loco-regional lymph nodes including the parasternal lymph nodes as delivered in the end of the seventies did not reduce overall mortality , but gave a significantly increased risk of death from heart and cerebrovascular disease , which appeared during the second decade after radiotherapy .
rewrite: This study examines long-term morbidity and mortality in pre- and post-menopausal breast cancer patients following postmastectomy radiotherapy, focusing on cardiac, cerebrovascular, and respiratory side effects. Two randomized trials involving 1100 patients were followed long-term. Pre-menopausal patients received radiotherapy (RT), RT plus oral cyclophosphamide (RT+C), or cyclophosphamide alone (C). Post-menopausal patients received RT, RT plus one year of tamoxifen (RT+Tam), or tamoxifen alone (Tam). Hospital admissions, mortality, and causes of death were sourced from national registries. After 25 years, adding RT to cyclophosphamide in pre-menopausal women increased heart disease mortality from 0% to 0.8% (p=0.04). In post-menopausal women, adding RT to Tam raised heart disease mortality from 10.5% to 18.4% (p=0.005) and cerebrovascular mortality from 3.4% to 8.7% (p=0.015). These differences emerged only in the second follow-up decade. Despite variations in specific causes, no significant differences in overall morbidity or mortality were found between treatment groups. Postmastectomy radiotherapy targeting the chest wall and loco-regional lymph nodes, including parasternal nodes as administered in the late 1970s, did not lower overall mortality but significantly increased the risk of fatal heart and cerebrovascular disease, which became apparent during the second decade after treatment.

text: We previously reported that compared to standard glycemic control [ blood glucose ( BG ) : 70-180 mg/dL ] , patients randomized to intensive glycemic control ( BG : 70-110 mg/dL ) were at increased risk of graft rejection in renal transplantation . However , the underlying mechanisms that associate the effect of intensive glycemic control with renal transplant outcomes have not been identified . A secondary data analysis of 93 participants ( n = 44 intensive , n = 49 control ) was conducted using data from a previous randomized controlled clinical trial . We examined inflammatory biomarkers , glycemic variability , hypoglycemia , and hyperglycemia as potential contributing etiologies by assessing the effect of intensive glycemic control on these characteristics , and evaluate the association of these variables with graft rejection . Intensive glycemic control had no appreciable effect on highly sensitive C-reactive protein , interleukin ( IL ) -6 , tumor necrosis factor alpha , IL-1 , or IL-10 levels at all time points after transplantation . Moreover , neither inflammatory biomarkers nor increased glycemic variability were associated with graft rejection . However , intensive treatment increased the risk of hypoglycemia ( BG < 70 mg/dL , 84 % vs. 25 % , P < 0.001 ) . In sub-analysis , compared to non-rejecters , rejecters demonstrated higher rates of blood glucose below 70 mg/dL ( 90 % vs. 49 % , P = 0.02 ) . Inflammatory biomarkers and increased glycemic variability lack correlation with clinical outcomes in renal transplant , but importantly , increased perioperative hypoglycemic episodes ( BG < 70mg/dL ) may be a salient etiology that contributed to the increased risk for acute allograft rejection related to intensive glycemic control . Further research is needed to confirm a causal association .
rewrite: Our earlier findings indicated that patients assigned to intensive glycemic control (blood glucose: 70-110 mg/dL) faced a higher risk of graft rejection after kidney transplantation compared to those under standard control (BG: 70-180 mg/dL). Yet, the mechanisms linking intensive glucose management to transplant results remain unclear. A secondary analysis of 93 subjects (44 intensive, 49 control) from a prior randomized trial was performed. We investigated inflammatory markers, glycemic variability, hypoglycemia, and hyperglycemia as possible factors, analyzing how intensive control influenced these traits and their relationship with rejection. Intensive control showed no significant impact on levels of high-sensitivity C-reactive protein, interleukin-6, tumor necrosis factor alpha, IL-1, or IL-10 at any post-transplant time. Additionally, neither inflammatory markers nor greater glycemic variability were linked to rejection. However, intensive therapy raised hypoglycemia risk (BG < 70 mg/dL, 84% vs. 25%, P < 0.001). In subgroup analysis, rejecters had more frequent glucose levels below 70 mg/dL than non-rejecters (90% vs. 49%, P = 0.02). Inflammatory biomarkers and heightened glycemic variability do not correlate with outcomes in renal transplantation, but notably, more perioperative hypoglycemic events (BG < 70 mg/dL) may be a key factor driving the elevated acute rejection risk tied to intensive glycemic control. Further studies are required to establish causality.

text: Infants with acute lymphoblastic leukemia ( ALL ) present with aggressive disease and a poor prognosis . Early relapse within 6-9 months of diagnosis is common . Approximately 75 % of infants have MLL-rearranged ( MLL-R ) ALL with event free survival ( EFS ) ranging from 20 % to 30 % . Children 's Oncology Group ( COG ) P9407 used shortened ( 46 weeks ) , intensified therapy to address early relapse and poor EFS . P9407 therapy was modified three times for induction toxicity resulting in three cohorts of therapy . One hundred forty-seven infants were enrolled in the third cohort . We report an overall 5-year EFS and OS of 42.36 % and 52.96.5 % respectively . Poor prognostic factors included age 90 days at diagnosis , MLL-R ALL and white cell count 50,000 / l. For infants 90 days of age , the 5-year EFS was 15.510.1 % and 48.56.7 % for those > 90 days ( P < 0.0001 ) . Among infants > 90 days of age , 5-year EFS rates were 43.88 % for MLL-R versus 69.113.6 % for MLL-germline ALL ( P < 0.0001 ) . Age 90 days at diagnosis was the most important prognostic factor . Despite shortened therapy with early intensification , EFS remained less than 50 % overall in MLL-R ALL .
rewrite: Infants diagnosed with acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) often exhibit aggressive disease and face a poor prognosis. Early relapse, typically within 6-9 months after diagnosis, is frequent. Around 75% of infants have MLL-rearranged (MLL-R) ALL, with event-free survival (EFS) rates between 20% and 30%. The Children's Oncology Group (COG) P9407 trial employed a shortened (46-week), intensified therapy to combat early relapse and low EFS. Due to induction toxicity, the P9407 regimen was modified three times, creating three treatment cohorts. The third cohort enrolled 147 infants. We report overall 5-year EFS and OS rates of 42.36% and 52.96.5%, respectively. Poor prognostic factors included age ≤90 days at diagnosis, MLL-R ALL, and white cell count ≥50,000/µl. For infants ≤90 days old, the 5-year EFS was 15.510.1%, compared to 48.56.7% for those >90 days (P < 0.0001). Among infants >90 days, 5-year EFS rates were 43.88% for MLL-R versus 69.113.6% for MLL-germline ALL (P < 0.0001). Age ≤90 days at diagnosis was the most significant prognostic factor. Despite using shortened therapy with early intensification, overall EFS in MLL-R ALL remained below 50%.

text: The rising number of children in daycare nurseries increases opportunities for the transmission of infectious diseases . Pathogens may be transmitted directly from child to child via sneezing , coughing and touching , or indirectly via the environment . Toys are among the fomites with the highest pathogen load , but their role in disease transmission is unknown . To determine if washing and disinfection of toys can reduce sickness absence and microbial pathogen load in the nursery environment . Twelve nurseries ( caring for 587 children ) were randomized to intervention and control groups . The intervention consisted of washing and disinfection of toys and linen every two weeks for three months by a commercial cleaning company . The extent and causes of sickness absence among the children were recorded in both groups before and after introduction of the intervention . Ten sampling points in each nursery were examined for bacteria and respiratory viruses . The presence of respiratory virus DNA/RNA was widespread , but very few pathogenic bacteria were found in the environment . The intervention reduced the presence of adenovirus [ odds ratio ( OR ) 2.4 , 95 % confidence interval ( CI ) 1.1-5 .0 ] , rhinovirus ( OR 5.3 , 95 % CI 2.3-12 .4 ) and respiratory syncytial virus ( OR 4.1 , 95 % CI 1.5-11 .2 ) compared with the control group , but the intervention had no effect on sickness absence or disease patterns in the nurseries . Although cleaning and disinfection of toys every two weeks can decrease the microbial load in nurseries , it does not appear to reduce sickness absence among nursery children .
rewrite: The increasing prevalence of children attending daycare centers heightens the risk for spreading infectious illnesses. Germs can spread directly between children through sneezing, coughing, and physical contact, or indirectly via contaminated surroundings. Toys rank among the fomites carrying the highest pathogen levels, yet their specific role in spreading disease remains unclear. This study aimed to assess whether washing and disinfecting toys could lower illness-related absences and reduce microbial contamination in nurseries. Twelve facilities (caring for 587 children) were randomly assigned to intervention and control groups. The intervention involved a commercial cleaning service washing and disinfecting toys and linens every two weeks over three months. Sickness absence rates and causes among the children were documented in both groups before and after the intervention. Ten sampling sites in each nursery were tested for bacteria and respiratory viruses. Respiratory virus genetic material was commonly detected, but few pathogenic bacteria were found in the environment. Compared to the control group, the intervention reduced the presence of adenovirus [odds ratio (OR) 2.4, 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.1–5.0], rhinovirus (OR 5.3, 95% CI 2.3–12.4), and respiratory syncytial virus (OR 4.1, 95% CI 1.5–11.2). However, the intervention did not affect sickness absence rates or illness patterns in the nurseries. While biweekly toy cleaning and disinfection can reduce microbial loads in these settings, it does not seem to decrease sickness absences among daycare children.

text: Concern about pain during placement of an intrauterine device ( IUD ) represents a barrier to use , especially among nulliparous women . We hypothesized that nitroglycerin gel applied vaginally 30 min prior to IUD placement would reduce insertion-related pain . We designed a randomized , double-blinded , placebo-controlled pilot study to evaluate the efficacy and tolerability of 0.5-mg nitroglycerin gel ( 1 mL ) or identical placebo gel applied vaginally in nulliparous women 30 min prior to IUD placement . The study was limited to women who opted for the levonorgestrel-releasing intrauterine system . Subjects completed a series of 100-mm visual analogue scales at several time points . The primary outcome was subject-reported pain with passage of the IUD through the cervix . Secondary outcomes included subject-reported pain at other time points , provider-reported ease of insertion , side effects , adverse events and need for additional dilation . A total of 24 women were randomized . Baseline characteristics were similar between groups . The mean pain score with IUD deployment was 55.0 mm [ standard deviation ( SD ) = 29.7 mm ] in the placebo group and 57.4 mm ( SD 22.1 mm ) in the nitroglycerin group ( p = .82 ) . There was no difference in ease of insertion reported by providers . Two subjects required dilation , one in each group . Vaginal administration of 0.5-mg nitroglycerin gel 30 min prior to IUD placement does not appear to decrease patient-reported procedural pain among nulliparous women or ease of insertion for providers .
rewrite: Fear of pain during intrauterine device (IUD) insertion acts as a deterrent, particularly for nulliparous women. We proposed that vaginally applied nitroglycerin gel 30 minutes before IUD placement might lessen insertion-related pain. A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled pilot study was conducted to assess the effectiveness and tolerability of 0.5-mg nitroglycerin gel (1 mL) versus an identical placebo gel applied vaginally in nulliparous women 30 minutes prior to IUD insertion. The study included only women choosing the levonorgestrel-releasing intrauterine system. Participants rated their pain on 100-mm visual analogue scales at multiple intervals. The main outcome measured was patient-reported pain as the IUD passed through the cervix. Secondary measures included pain at other times, provider-rated insertion ease, side effects, adverse events, and the need for additional cervical dilation. Twenty-four women were randomized, with similar baseline characteristics across groups. The average pain score during IUD deployment was 55.0 mm [standard deviation (SD) = 29.7 mm] for the placebo group and 57.4 mm (SD 22.1 mm) for the nitroglycerin group (p = .82). Providers reported no difference in insertion ease. Dilation was required for two subjects, one from each group. Vaginally administering 0.5-mg nitroglycerin gel 30 minutes before IUD placement does not seem to reduce patient-reported procedural pain in nulliparous women or improve insertion ease for providers.

text: To compare 4 analgesic protocols in dogs undergoing stifle joint surgery . Randomized , blinded , prospective clinical trial . Animals-48 client-owned dogs that underwent stifle joint surgery . Dogs undergoing tibial plateau leveling osteotomy were randomly assigned to receive a constant rate infusion of a combination of morphine , lidocaine , and ketamine ; a lumbosacral epidural with morphine and ropivacaine ; both treatments ( ie , constant rate infusion and lumbosacral epidural ) ; or only IM premedication with morphine . Indices of cardiorespiratory function and isoflurane requirement were recorded at 5-minute intervals during anesthesia . A validated sedation scoring system and the modified Glasgow composite measure pain score were used to assess comfort and sedation after surgery and anesthesia once the swallowing reflex returned and a body temperature of 36.7 C ( 98.1 F ) was attained . Pain and sedation scores were acquired at 60-minute intervals for 4 hours , then at 4-hour intervals for 24 hours . Dogs with a postoperative pain score > 5 of 24 were given morphine as rescue analgesia . No differences in heart rate , respiratory rate , systolic arterial blood pressure , end-tidal Pco2 , end-tidal isoflurane concentration , and vaporizer setting were detected among groups . No differences in pain score , sedation score , rescue analgesia requirement , or time to first rescue analgesia after surgery were detected . Pain scores were similar among groups , and all 4 groups had similar rescue analgesia requirements and similar times to first administration of rescue analgesia . All 4 analgesic protocols provided acceptable analgesia for 24 hours after stifle joint surgery .
rewrite: To evaluate four analgesic regimens in dogs following stifle joint surgery. A randomized, blinded, prospective clinical trial. Subjects—48 client-owned dogs undergoing stifle joint surgery. Dogs receiving tibial plateau leveling osteotomy were randomly allocated to one of four groups: a constant-rate infusion combining morphine, lidocaine, and ketamine; a lumbosacral epidural with morphine and ropivacaine; both treatments (i.e., constant-rate infusion and lumbosacral epidural); or only intramuscular premedication with morphine. Cardiorespiratory parameters and isoflurane requirements were recorded every 5 minutes during anesthesia. Postoperative comfort and sedation were assessed using a validated sedation scale and the modified Glasgow composite pain score, once swallowing reflex returned and body temperature reached 36.7°C (98.1°F). Pain and sedation scores were collected hourly for 4 hours, then every 4 hours for 24 hours. Dogs with a postoperative pain score exceeding 5 out of 24 received morphine as rescue analgesia. No significant differences were observed among groups in heart rate, respiratory rate, systolic arterial pressure, end-tidal PCO₂, end-tidal isoflurane concentration, or vaporizer settings. Similarly, no differences were found in pain scores, sedation scores, need for rescue analgesia, or time to first rescue analgesia after surgery. Pain scores were comparable across groups, and all four groups showed similar rescue analgesia requirements and times to first rescue administration. All four analgesic protocols delivered adequate analgesia over 24 hours following stifle joint surgery.

text: Peritoneal implantation metastasis of gastric cancer is the major reason for cancer recurrence after radical operations . As a new chemotherapeutic agent , raltitrexed has been widely used in intravenous chemotherapy for many kinds of cancers . However , no study has reported the efficacy and safety of raltitrexed in intraperitoneal chemotherapy . This study aimed to explore the safety of intraperitoneal chemotherapy with raltitrexed during gastric cancer operation compared to normal saline ( NS ) rinsing of the abdominal cavity . In this prospective study , 91 gastric cancer patients undergoing surgery and reconstruction were consecutively enrolled and randomly assigned into two groups . Raltitrexed in NS ( 500 ml ) was injected into the abdominopelvic cavity for the patients in the RT group ( n = 48 ) , while for the patients in the group NS ( n = 43 ) , only NS ( 500 ml ) was injected . The postoperative complications , gas passage time , and adverse effects , according to NCI-CTCAE v3 .0 , were compared between the two groups . There were no significant differences in age , sex , cancer pathological type , clinical stage or operation method between the two groups ( all P > 0.05 ) . No significant difference was observed in adverse effects and postoperative complications between the two groups ( all P > 0.05 ) . No significant change was found in the levels of red blood cells , white blood cells , platelets , lactate dehydrogenase , blood urea nitrogen , and alanine aminotransferase before and after the operation for both groups ( all P > 0.05 ) . All adverse events were mild or moderate by NCI-CTCAE v3 .0 ( National Cancer Institute common terminology criteria for adverse events ) grade . The findings of the present study demonstrate that intraperitoneal chemotherapy with raltitrexed after gastric cancer operation is safe and could be used for patients .
rewrite: Peritoneal metastasis from gastric cancer is a primary cause of recurrence following curative surgery. Raltitrexed, a newer chemotherapeutic agent, is commonly administered intravenously for various cancers. Yet, its effectiveness and safety in intraperitoneal chemotherapy remain unreported. This research assessed the safety of intraperitoneal raltitrexed during gastric cancer surgery versus abdominal rinsing with normal saline (NS). In this prospective trial, 91 surgical gastric cancer patients were consecutively recruited and randomly divided into two groups. The RT group (n=48) received raltitrexed in NS (500 ml) injected into the abdominopelvic cavity, while the NS group (n=43) received only NS (500 ml). Postoperative complications, time to gas passage, and adverse effects per NCI-CTCAE v3.0 were compared. No significant differences existed between groups in age, sex, pathological type, clinical stage, or surgical method (all P>0.05). Adverse effects and postoperative complications showed no significant differences (all P>0.05). Levels of red blood cells, white blood cells, platelets, lactate dehydrogenase, blood urea nitrogen, and alanine aminotransferase remained unchanged pre- and post-operation in both groups (all P>0.05). All adverse events were mild to moderate per NCI-CTCAE v3.0. These results indicate that intraperitoneal chemotherapy with raltitrexed after gastric cancer surgery is safe and applicable for patients.

text: To examine whether transcutaneous electric nerve stimulation at acupoints ( Acu-TENS ) improved the biochemical and physical indices of patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus ( T2DM ) . Ninety subjects with T2DM were divided randomly into a control group ( n = 30 ) , aerobic exercise group ( n = 30 ) , or Acu-TENS group ( n = 30 ) . In addition to conventional diabetes drug treatment , patients in the Acu-TENS group received acupoint stimulation , the aerobic exercise group engaged in walking exercises , and the control group was given sham electrical stimulation . All groups were treated for 30 min for each session and five times a week for 2 months . The indices of glycosylated hemoglobin , 2 h postprandial glucose , fasting serum insulin , triglyceride , total cholesterol , and body mass index were assessed at pre-treatment , post-treatment , and follow-up , which was 2 months after treatment . The indices of the control group were not changed ( P > 0.05 ) at the three time points . At the pre-treatment measurement , there were significant differences ( P > 0.05 ) in indices among the three groups . At post-treatment , each index of the two groups was lower than that of the control group ( P < 0.05 ) , and improved in comparison with the pre-treatment measurement ( P < 0.05 ) . In follow-up , each index of the aerobic exercise group and Acu-TENS group increased , but was still decreased compared with the pre-treatment value ( P < 0.05 ) , excluding body mass index . Acu-TENS could improve the state of patients with T2DM and be used as a therapy in clinical application .
rewrite: This study investigated whether transcutaneous electrical nerve stimulation at acupoints (Acu-TENS) enhances biochemical and physical markers in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). Ninety T2DM participants were randomly assigned to a control group (n=30), an aerobic exercise group (n=30), or an Acu-TENS group (n=30). Alongside standard medication, the Acu-TENS group received acupoint stimulation, the aerobic group performed walking exercises, and the control group received sham stimulation. All groups underwent 30-minute sessions, five times weekly for two months. Glycosylated hemoglobin, 2-hour postprandial glucose, fasting serum insulin, triglycerides, total cholesterol, and body mass index were measured before treatment, after treatment, and at a two-month follow-up. The control group showed no significant changes (P>0.05) across time points. Baseline measurements indicated no significant differences (P>0.05) among groups. Post-treatment, both intervention groups exhibited lower values than the control (P<0.05) and showed improvement from baseline (P<0.05). At follow-up, markers in the aerobic and Acu-TENS groups had risen but remained below pre-treatment levels (P<0.05), except for body mass index. Acu-TENS may improve T2DM patient outcomes and holds potential for clinical use.

text: Prospective trials specifically designed for elderly patients with advanced non-small-cell lung cancer demonstrating the benefit of platinum-based therapies are still lacking . This trial was designed to clarify whether the addition of cisplatin to monotherapy could improve survival for elderly patients . Elderly patients ( age 70 years , ECOG performance Status 0-1 ) with advanced non-small-cell lung cancer were randomized to receive docetaxel 20 mg/m ( 2 ) plus cisplatin 25 mg/m ( 2 ) on Day 1 , 8 and 15 ( docetaxel plus cisplatin ) or docetaxel 25 mg/m ( 2 ) on the same schedule ( docetaxel ) . Both regimens were repeated every 4 weeks until disease progression . One hundred and twenty-six patients were enrolled . Sixty-three were randomly assigned docetaxel plus cisplatin and 63 docetaxel monotherapy . Median age was 76 years ( range 70-88 ) . The second planned interim analysis was performed on 112 assessable patients ( docetaxel/docetaxel plus cisplatin : 56/56 ) . Although the formal criterion for stopping the trial was not met , the Data and Safety Monitoring Committee recommended study termination on ethical grounds based on the interaction ( two-sided P = 0.077 , hazard ratios for 74/75 : 0.23 / 0.72 ) between age and subgroup and treatment arm , which suggested that docetaxel may not represent an adequate control arm regimen for the age subgroup of 70-74 years . The interpretation of study results is limited due to early stopping . Further study is needed to confirm survival benefit of platinum-based chemotherapy for elderly non-small-cell lung cancer [ UMIN-CTR ( www.umin.ac.jp/ctr/ ) ID : C000000146 ] .
rewrite: Prospective studies specifically targeting elderly patients with advanced non-small-cell lung cancer that demonstrate the advantages of platinum-based treatments remain scarce. This trial aimed to determine if adding cisplatin to single-agent therapy could enhance survival in this population. Elderly patients (aged 70 years, ECOG performance status 0-1) with advanced non-small-cell lung cancer were randomly assigned to receive docetaxel 20 mg/m² plus cisplatin 25 mg/m² on Days 1, 8, and 15 (docetaxel plus cisplatin) or docetaxel 25 mg/m² on the same schedule (docetaxel alone). Both treatment plans were repeated every four weeks until disease progression. A total of 126 patients were enrolled, with 63 allocated to docetaxel plus cisplatin and 63 to docetaxel monotherapy. The median age was 76 years (range 70-88). The second planned interim analysis included 112 evaluable patients (docetaxel/docetaxel plus cisplatin: 56/56). Although the formal stopping criterion was not fulfilled, the Data and Safety Monitoring Committee advised ending the study on ethical grounds, based on the interaction (two-sided P = 0.077, hazard ratios for ages 74/75: 0.23/0.72) between age subgroup and treatment arm, indicating docetaxel might not be a suitable control regimen for the 70-74 age subgroup. Early termination limits the interpretation of the findings. Additional research is required to verify the survival benefit of platinum-based chemotherapy for elderly non-small-cell lung cancer patients [UMIN-CTR (www.umin.ac.jp/ctr/) ID: C000000146].

text: Depressive disorders are one of the leading components of the global burden of disease with a prevalence of up to 14 % in the general population . Numerous studies have demonstrated that pharmacotherapy combined with non-pharmacological measures offer the best treatment approach . Psycho-education as an intervention has been studied mostly in disorders such as schizophrenia and dementia , less so in depressive disorders . The present study aimed to assess the impact of psycho-education of patients and their caregivers on the outcome of depression . A total of 80 eligible depressed subjects were recruited and randomised into 2 groups . The study group involved an eligible family member and all were offered individual structured psycho-educational modules . Another group ( controls ) received routine counselling . The subjects in both groups also received routine pharmacotherapy and counselling from the treating clinician and were assessed at baseline , 2 , 4 , 8 , and 12 weeks using the Hamilton Depression Rating Scale ( HDRS ) , Global Assessment of Functioning ( GAF ) , and Psychological General Well-Being Index ( PGWBI ) . Results from both groups were compared using statistical methods including Chi-square test , Fisher 's exact test , Student 's t test , Pearson 's correlation coefficient , as well as univariate and multiple regression analyses . Baseline socio-demographic and assessment measures were similar in both groups . The study group had consistent improvement in terms of outcome measures with HDRS , GAF , and PGWBI scores showing respective mean change of -15.08 , 22 , and 60 over 12 weeks . The comparable respective changes in the controls were -8.77 , 18.1 , and 43.25 . Structured psycho-education combined with pharmacotherapy is an effective intervention for people with depressive disorders . Psycho-education optimises the pharmacological treatment of depression in terms of faster recovery , reduction in severity of depression , and improvement in subjective wellbeing and social functioning .
rewrite: Depressive disorders represent a major contributor to the global disease burden, affecting up to 14% of the general population. Extensive research indicates that combining pharmacotherapy with non-drug interventions yields the most effective treatment strategy. While psycho-education has been widely examined for conditions like schizophrenia and dementia, its application in depressive disorders is less explored. This study evaluated the effect of psycho-education for patients and their caregivers on depression outcomes. Eighty qualified depressed participants were enrolled and randomly assigned to two groups. The study group included an eligible family member, with all receiving individual, structured psycho-educational sessions. The control group was provided routine counselling instead. Both groups also obtained standard pharmacotherapy and clinician counselling, with assessments conducted at baseline, 2, 4, 8, and 12 weeks using the Hamilton Depression Rating Scale (HDRS), Global Assessment of Functioning (GAF), and Psychological General Well-Being Index (PGWBI). Outcomes were compared statistically via Chi-square test, Fisher's exact test, Student's t-test, Pearson's correlation coefficient, and univariate and multiple regression analyses. Baseline socio-demographic and clinical measures were comparable between groups. The study group demonstrated consistent improvement across all measures, with mean score changes over 12 weeks of -15.08 for HDRS, 22 for GAF, and 60 for PGWBI. Corresponding changes in the control group were -8.77, 18.1, and 43.25. Structured psycho-education combined with pharmacotherapy proves an effective intervention for depressive disorders. It enhances pharmacological treatment by accelerating recovery, reducing depression severity, and improving subjective wellbeing and social functioning.

text: Recent evidence suggests thyroidectomy ( Tx ) followed by radioiodine remnant ablation to be beneficial to Graves ' orbitopathy ( GO ) patients . The aim of the study was to evaluate the effect of ( 131 ) I thyroid ablation after recombinant human TSH stimulation in patients with moderate-to-severe GO . The study was prospective , randomized , and single-blind , and it included 40 consecutive patients with moderate-to-severe GO randomized into : 1 ) a Tx-radioactive iodine ( RAI ) group ( 20 subjects who underwent total-Tx and ( 131 ) I ablation after recombinant human TSH stimulation ) ; and 2 ) a Tx group ( 20 subjects who underwent total-Tx alone ) . The overall GO outcome 12 months after Tx/radioiodine ablation was the main measure . GO evaluation at the end of iv glucocorticoids showed eye disease to be improved in 65 % of the Tx-RAI group and 60 % of the Tx group patients . At 6 and 12 months , no further changes in the GO outcome could be observed in the Tx-RAI group . Conversely , five patients from the Tx group exhibited a deterioration in GO . At 12 months , GO was found to be improved in 70 % of the Tx-RAI and 20 % of the Tx group patients , the latter being found to be stable ( 55 % ) or worse ( 25 % ) than at baseline evaluation . At 12 months , GO was found to be inactive in a significantly higher percentage of patients in the Tx-RAI than in the Tx group ( 75 vs 30 % ; P < .01 ) . Postoperative radioiodine ablation proved more effective than Tx alone in inducing earlier and steadier GO improvement in patients with moderate-to-severe GO treated with iv glucocorticoids over a 24-month follow-up period .
rewrite: Recent findings indicate that thyroidectomy (Tx) combined with radioiodine remnant ablation benefits patients with Graves' orbitopathy (GO). This study aimed to assess the impact of (131)I thyroid ablation after recombinant human TSH stimulation in moderate-to-severe GO cases. Designed as prospective, randomized, and single-blind, it involved 40 consecutive patients randomly assigned to: 1) a Tx-radioactive iodine (RAI) group (20 subjects receiving total Tx and (131)I ablation post recombinant human TSH stimulation); and 2) a Tx group (20 subjects undergoing total Tx only). The primary outcome was overall GO status 12 months after Tx/radioiodine ablation. Following intravenous glucocorticoids, GO improved in 65% of the Tx-RAI group and 60% of the Tx group. At 6 and 12 months, no additional changes occurred in the Tx-RAI group, whereas five Tx group patients experienced GO worsening. By 12 months, GO improvement was seen in 70% of Tx-RAI patients versus 20% in the Tx group, with the latter stable (55%) or worse (25%) compared to baseline. Inactive GO was significantly more common in the Tx-RAI group than the Tx group at 12 months (75% vs 30%; P < .01). Postoperative radioiodine ablation was more effective than Tx alone in promoting earlier and more consistent GO improvement over a 24-month follow-up in moderate-to-severe GO patients treated with intravenous glucocorticoids.

text: The aim of our study was to investigate the relationship between nasal irrigation techniques ( NIT ) and the survival rate and the quality of life ( QOL ) in patients with nasal sinusitis ( NS ) . We studied data from 1134 patients with nasopharyngeal carcinoma ( NPC ) who received radical radiotherapy , which were randomly divided into three groups ( A , B and C ) . Group A used nasal irrigator ; Group B used homemade nasal irrigation ( NI ) connector combined with enemator ; and Group C used nasal sprayer . The clinical effects , 5-year overall survival ( OS ) and progression-free survival ( PFS ) were observed . Furthermore , the QOL in patients with NS was evaluated using the Sino-Nasal Outcome Test 20 . The median follow-up time was 69 months . The 5-year OS and PFS were 80.5 % and 73.2 % , respectively , for all patients . There was no significant difference in OS , PFS , xerostomia and neck skin toxicity grade 3 and greater among groups . There was no difference among groups . The incidence of NS was the highest in group C. The symptoms of NS seriously affected the QOL period of 1 year . Group C showed no improvement during the follow-up period , which for A and B , by contrast , had after 1 year . Although the exact mechanism remains to be explored in NIT , our findings suggest that patients with NPC should nasal irrigate for 2 years after radiotherapy . Our study shows that a nasal irrigator is necessary for patients with NPC for a high QOL in terms of NS .
rewrite: This study aimed to examine the association between nasal irrigation techniques (NIT) and both survival rates and quality of life (QOL) in patients with nasal sinusitis (NS). Data from 1134 nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC) patients treated with radical radiotherapy were analyzed. Participants were randomly assigned to three groups (A, B, and C). Group A utilized a nasal irrigator; Group B employed a homemade nasal irrigation (NI) connector with an enemator; and Group C used a nasal sprayer. Clinical outcomes, 5-year overall survival (OS), and progression-free survival (PFS) were assessed. Additionally, QOL in NS patients was measured using the Sino-Nasal Outcome Test 20. The median follow-up duration was 69 months. For all patients, the 5-year OS and PFS rates were 80.5% and 73.2%, respectively. No significant differences were observed among groups regarding OS, PFS, xerostomia, or grade 3 and higher neck skin toxicity. The incidence of NS was highest in Group C. NS symptoms significantly impaired QOL over a 1-year period. While Group C showed no improvement during follow-up, Groups A and B demonstrated improvement after 1 year. Although the precise mechanism of NIT requires further investigation, our results indicate that NPC patients should perform nasal irrigation for 2 years post-radiotherapy. This study concludes that a nasal irrigator is essential for NPC patients to achieve a high QOL related to NS.

text: Cross-match-compatible platelets are used to support thrombocytopenic patients who are refractory to randomly selected platelets . However , few studies have addressed the efficacy of using this strategy for patients requiring intensive platelet transfusion therapy . The aim of this study was to determine the effectiveness of cross-match-compatible platelets in an unselected group of patients refractory to platelets from random donors . A total of 406 cross-match-compatible platelet components were administered to 40 evaluable patients who were refractory to random-donor platelets . A solid-phase red cell adherence method was used for platelet cross-matching . The corrected count increment was used to monitor the effectiveness of each platelet transfusion . Multivariate analysis was performed to detect whether any variables could predict the response to transfusion . Statistically significant improvements were found in the mean corrected count increment when comparing cross-match-compatible platelets with randomly selected and incompatible platelets ( p < 0.001 for each ) . Compatible platelet transfusions were associated with a good response in 72.9 % of cases while incompatible platelets were associated with a poor response in 66.7 % of transfusion events ( p < 0.001 ) . In the presence of clinical factors or alloimmunisation , compatible platelets were associated with good responses in 67.9 % and 28.0 % respectively vs 100 % and 93.3 % in their absence ( p = 0.009 , p < 0.001 ) . Multivariate analysis revealed that cross-matching and alloimmunisation were the strongest predictors of transfusion response at 1 hour , while ABO compatibility , type of units received , followed by alloimmunisation then clinical factors were predictors at 24 hours . Platelet cross-matching using the solid-phase red cell adherence technique is an effective and rapid first-line approach for the management of patients refractory to platelet transfusions .
rewrite: Cross-match-compatible platelets are employed for thrombocytopenic patients unresponsive to randomly chosen platelets. Yet, limited research has explored their efficacy in those needing intensive platelet transfusion therapy. This study aimed to assess the effectiveness of cross-match-compatible platelets in a general cohort of patients refractory to random-donor platelets. We administered 406 cross-match-compatible platelet units to 40 evaluable patients refractory to random-donor platelets, using a solid-phase red cell adherence method for cross-matching. The corrected count increment monitored each transfusion's effectiveness, and multivariate analysis identified predictors of response. Statistically significant improvements in mean corrected count increment were observed with cross-match-compatible versus randomly selected and incompatible platelets (p < 0.001 each). Compatible transfusions yielded good responses in 72.9% of cases, whereas incompatible ones led to poor responses in 66.7% (p < 0.001). With clinical factors or alloimmunisation present, compatible platelets showed good responses in 67.9% and 28.0%, respectively, versus 100% and 93.3% in their absence (p = 0.009, p < 0.001). Multivariate analysis indicated cross-matching and alloimmunisation as key predictors at 1 hour, while ABO compatibility, unit type, alloimmunisation, and clinical factors predicted outcomes at 24 hours. Platelet cross-matching via solid-phase red cell adherence is an effective, rapid first-line strategy for managing platelet transfusion-refractory patients.

text: To determine the degree of dietary adherence or change in eating patterns , and demographic , psychosocial and study characteristics associated with adherence , in the Comparing Healthy Options in Cooking and Eating ( CHOICE ) Study . Randomized controlled trial where women were randomized to one of three eating patterns : ( i ) Whole Foods , plant-based , macrobiotic-style ( n 22 ) ; and Moderate Fat with ( ii ) , and without ( iii ) , 10 g of ground flaxseed added daily , which were combined ( n 49 ) . A year-long intervention based on social cognitive theory , consisting of twenty-four class sessions involving hands-on cooking classes and behavioural sessions . Monthly 24 h food recalls were obtained and a psychosocial questionnaire was administered at baseline , 6 and 12 months . Healthy , free-living , postmenopausal women . A non-adherence score measuring all food servings out-of-compliance with eating pattern recommendations was specifically designed for the present study . Non-adherence scores decreased significantly ( P < 005 ) in both groups to about 65 % during the adoption phase ( first 4 months ) and remained so during the 8-month maintenance period . Class attendance of the Moderate Fat group showed a trend towards significance as a predictor of adherence ( P = 0063 ) . None of the other predictors ( e.g. demographic and psychosocial factors ) in a longitudinal regression model were significant . Postmenopausal women were able to adopt and maintain significant changes in their eating patterns , including those on a demanding , near-vegetarian eating plan , suggesting that behavioural interventions with a healthy free-living population can be effective . The non-adherence score developed for the study provides an example of a means for evaluating eating pattern adherence to a dietary intervention .
rewrite: To assess dietary adherence or shifts in eating habits, along with demographic, psychosocial, and study factors linked to adherence, in the Comparing Healthy Options in Cooking and Eating (CHOICE) Study. A randomized controlled trial assigned women to one of three eating patterns: (i) Whole Foods, plant-based, macrobiotic-style (n=22); and Moderate Fat with (ii), and without (iii), 10 g of daily ground flaxseed, which were combined (n=49). A year-long intervention grounded in social cognitive theory, featuring twenty-four class sessions with hands-on cooking and behavioral components. Monthly 24-hour food recalls were collected, and a psychosocial questionnaire was given at baseline, 6, and 12 months. Participants were healthy, free-living, postmenopausal women. A non-adherence score, quantifying all food servings deviating from eating pattern guidelines, was created for this study. Non-adherence scores dropped significantly (P<0.05) in both groups to around 65% during the adoption phase (first 4 months) and stayed stable over the 8-month maintenance period. Class attendance in the Moderate Fat group showed a near-significant trend as a predictor of adherence (P=0.063). No other predictors (e.g., demographic and psychosocial variables) in a longitudinal regression model were significant. Postmenopausal women successfully adopted and sustained notable changes in their eating patterns, even on a rigorous, near-vegetarian plan, indicating that behavioral interventions can work in a healthy free-living population. The study's non-adherence score offers an example of a method for assessing eating pattern compliance in dietary interventions.

text: To compare bipolar with standard monopolar transurethral resection of the prostate ( TURP ) . A prospectively randomized study was conducted between January 2010 and September 2011 . Primary end points studied were efficacy ( maximum flow rate [ Qmax ] , International Prostate Symptom Score ) and safety ( adverse events , decline in postoperative serum sodium [ Na + ] and haemoglobin [ Hb ] levels ) . Secondary end points were operation time and duration of irrigation , catheterization , and hospitalization . Sixty consecutive patients were randomized and completed the study , with 29 patients in the monopolar TURP group and 31 in the TURIS group . At baseline , the two groups were comparable in age , prostate volume , mean prostate-specific antigen value , International Prostate Symptom Score , and they had at least 12 months of follow-up . Declines in the mean postoperative serum Na + for bipolar and monopolar TURP groups were 1.2 and 8.7 mmol/L , respectively . However , there was no statistical difference in the decline in postoperative Hb between the two groups . The mean catheterization time was 26.6 and 52 hours in the bipolar and standard groups , respectively . This difference was statistically significant as was the difference in the time to hospital discharge . The IPSS and Qmax improvements were comparable between the two groups at 12 months of follow-up . No clinically relevant differences in short-term efficacy are existed between the two techniques , but bipolar TURP is preferable due to a more favorable safety profile and shorter catheterization duration .
rewrite: This study aimed to compare bipolar and standard monopolar transurethral resection of the prostate (TURP). A prospective randomized trial was performed from January 2010 to September 2011. Primary outcomes assessed were efficacy (maximum flow rate [Qmax], International Prostate Symptom Score) and safety (adverse events, postoperative decreases in serum sodium [Na+] and hemoglobin [Hb]). Secondary outcomes included operation time and the durations of irrigation, catheterization, and hospitalization. Sixty consecutive patients were randomized and completed the study: 29 in the monopolar TURP group and 31 in the bipolar TURIS group. Baseline characteristics, including age, prostate volume, mean prostate-specific antigen, and International Prostate Symptom Score, were similar between groups, with at least 12 months of follow-up. The mean postoperative serum Na+ decrease was 1.2 mmol/L for bipolar TURP and 8.7 mmol/L for monopolar TURP. However, the postoperative Hb decline showed no statistical difference between groups. Mean catheterization times were 26.6 hours for bipolar and 52 hours for standard TURP. This difference was statistically significant, as was the time to hospital discharge. Improvements in IPSS and Qmax were comparable between groups at the 12-month follow-up. While no clinically significant differences in short-term efficacy were found, bipolar TURP is favored for its superior safety profile and reduced catheterization time.

text: Low back pain affects approximately 80 % of people at some stage in their lives . Exercise therapy is the most widely used nonsurgical intervention for low back pain in practice guidelines . Whole body vibration exercise is becoming increasingly popular for relieving musculoskeletal pain and improving health-related quality of life . However , the efficacy of whole body vibration exercise for low back pain is not without dispute . This study aims to estimate the effect of whole body vibration exercise for chronic low back pain . We will conduct a prospective , single-blind , randomized controlled trial of 120 patients with chronic low back pain . Patients will be randomly assigned into an intervention group and a control group . The intervention group will participate in whole body vibration exercise twice a week for 3 months . The control group will receive general exercise twice a week for 3 months . Primary outcome measures will be the visual analog scale for pain , the Oswestry Disability Index and adverse events . The secondary outcome measures will include muscle strength and endurance of spine , trunk proprioception , transversus abdominis activation capacity , and quality of life . We will conduct intention-to-treat analysis if any participants withdraw from the trial . Important features of this study include the randomization procedures , single-blind , large sample size , and a standardized protocol for whole body vibration in chronic low back pain . This study aims to determine whether whole body vibration exercise produces more beneficial effects than general exercise for chronic low back pain . Therefore , our results will be useful for patients with chronic low back pain as well as for medical staff and health-care decision makers . Chinese Clinical Trial Registry : ChiCTR-TRC-13003708 .
rewrite: Low back pain impacts around 80% of individuals at some point in life. Exercise therapy is the most common nonsurgical treatment recommended in guidelines for low back pain. Whole body vibration exercise is gaining popularity for alleviating musculoskeletal pain and enhancing health-related quality of life. Yet, its effectiveness for low back pain remains debated. This study seeks to evaluate the effect of whole body vibration exercise on chronic low back pain. We will perform a prospective, single-blind, randomized controlled trial involving 120 patients with chronic low back pain. Participants will be randomly allocated to an intervention group or a control group. The intervention group will undergo whole body vibration exercise twice weekly for three months. The control group will perform general exercise twice weekly for three months. Primary outcomes will include the visual analog scale for pain, the Oswestry Disability Index, and adverse events. Secondary outcomes will encompass spine muscle strength and endurance, trunk proprioception, transversus abdominis activation capacity, and quality of life. Intention-to-treat analysis will be used if any participants drop out. Key aspects of this study are the randomization, single-blind design, large sample size, and a standardized whole body vibration protocol for chronic low back pain. This research aims to establish if whole body vibration exercise offers greater benefits than general exercise for chronic low back pain. Thus, our findings will be valuable for patients with chronic low back pain, as well as for healthcare providers and policymakers. Chinese Clinical Trial Registry: ChiCTR-TRC-13003708.

text: To evaluate the effects of a non-pharmacologic electro-acupuncture method at different acupoints on labor pain management . Nulliparous women under the maternity care of the Department of Obstetrics and Gynecology of Sir Run Run Shaw Hospital were recruited and allocated into two experimental groups ( EX-B2 group and SP6 group ) and one control group , each with 60 eligible participants . Visual analog scale ( VAS ) was used to assess the pain during active phase of labor before and 30 , 60 , 120 min after intervention . The duration of active phase , the duration of second stage of labor , the duration of third stage of labor , use of oxytocin , neonatal birth weight , neonatal Apgar score at 1 and 5 min were considered as secondary outcomes of this study . After 30 min intervention , the mean VAS scores of both EX-B2 group and SP6 group were significantly decreased compared with the control group ( P < 0.01 ) ; however , no significant difference was observed between the two experimental groups ( P > 0.05 ) . After 60 and 120 min intervention , the mean VAS scores of EX-B2 group were significantly lower than SP-6 group ( P < 0.05 ) . Both EX-B2 group and SP6 group had significant lower VAS scores after interventions and shorter time used in active phase of labor than the control group ( P < 0.05 ) . The study revealed that the application of electro-acupuncture at EX-B2 and SP6 acupoints could be used as a non-pharmacologic method to reduce labor pain and shorten the duration of active phase of labor .
rewrite: This study assessed the impact of non-pharmacological electro-acupuncture applied to specific acupoints on managing labor pain. Nulliparous women receiving maternity care at Sir Run Run Shaw Hospital's Department of Obstetrics and Gynecology were enrolled and divided into two experimental groups (EX-B2 and SP6) and one control group, each containing 60 eligible subjects. Pain during the active phase of labor was measured using a visual analog scale (VAS) before the intervention and at 30, 60, and 120 minutes afterward. Secondary outcomes included the duration of the active phase, the second stage, and the third stage of labor, along with oxytocin use, neonatal birth weight, and Apgar scores at 1 and 5 minutes. At 30 minutes post-intervention, mean VAS scores in both the EX-B2 and SP6 groups were significantly reduced compared to the control group (P < 0.01), but no significant difference was found between the two experimental groups (P > 0.05). At 60 and 120 minutes, the EX-B2 group showed significantly lower mean VAS scores than the SP6 group (P < 0.05). Both intervention groups had significantly lower VAS scores after treatment and a shorter active phase duration compared to the control group (P < 0.05). The findings indicate that electro-acupuncture at EX-B2 and SP6 acupoints can serve as a non-pharmacological approach to alleviate labor pain and reduce the length of the active labor phase.

text: Most men diagnosed with prostate cancer become long-term survivors , but are at risk for medical late-effects that can affect their long-term health . Mailed surveys are well suited to study late-effects in this population , but low response rates can compromise survey validity . This study investigated whether an unconditional $ 5.00 gift certificate incentive or Priority Mail delivery increased prostate cancer survivors ' response to mailed surveys . 976 participants ( mean age = 66.8 years ) , 2-8 years post-diagnosis , were randomized to one of four groups : Incentive ; Priority Mail ; Incentive & Priority Mail ; or Control . After an introductory letter , initial study packets were mailed based on randomization ; 46 days later , a second study packet was mailed to all non-responders by First-Class Mail . The first mailing yielded a significant variation in response rates across groups ( ( 2 ) = 9.34 ; p = 0.025 ) . Priority Mail ( 64.7 % ; p = 0.008 ) and Incentive & Priority Mail ( 63.6 % ; p = 0.016 ) groups had significantly higher response rates than Controls ( 52.9 % ) . After the second mailing , the overall response rate increased significantly from 59.6 % to 71.4 % ( p < 0.001 ) ; however , response rates no longer differed across groups ( range , 69.3 % [ Incentive group ] to 73.9 % [ Priority Mail group ] ) . Long-term prostate cancer survivors ' response rates to mailed surveys increased with the use of Priority Mail and a repeat survey mailing , but the unconditional gift certificate incentive was not supported in this population . By identifying and applying specialized survey methods , studies targeting survivors of prostate cancer and other geriatric cancers may improve response rates , thus limiting a source of potential bias .
rewrite: Most men with prostate cancer survive long-term, yet face risks from medical late-effects impacting their health. Mailed surveys are effective for studying these late-effects, but low response rates can undermine validity. This research examined whether a $5.00 gift certificate incentive or Priority Mail delivery improved response rates among prostate cancer survivors. 976 participants (average age 66.8 years), 2–8 years post-diagnosis, were assigned to one of four groups: Incentive; Priority Mail; Incentive & Priority Mail; or Control. Following an introductory letter, initial study packets were mailed according to randomization; 46 days later, a second packet was sent via First-Class Mail to all non-responders. The first mailing showed significant differences in response rates across groups (χ²=9.34; p=0.025). Priority Mail (64.7%; p=0.008) and Incentive & Priority Mail (63.6%; p=0.016) groups had notably higher rates than Controls (52.9%). After the second mailing, the overall response rate rose significantly from 59.6% to 71.4% (p<0.001); however, group differences disappeared (range: 69.3% [Incentive] to 73.9% [Priority Mail]). Response rates for long-term prostate cancer survivors improved with Priority Mail and a repeat mailing, but the unconditional gift certificate incentive was ineffective in this group. By adopting tailored survey methods, studies on prostate cancer and other geriatric cancers can boost response rates, reducing potential bias.

text: Collateral artery growth ( arteriogenesis ) is an important adaptive response to hampered arterial perfusion . It is unknown whether preventive physical exercise before limb ischemia can improve arteriogenesis and modulate mononuclear cell function . This study aimed at investigating the effects of endurance exercise before arterial occlusion on MNC function and collateral artery growth . After 3 weeks of voluntary treadmill exercise , ligation of the right femoral artery was performed in mice . Hindlimb perfusion immediately after surgery did not differ from sedentary mice . However , previous exercise improved perfusion restoration 7 days after femoral artery ligation , also when exercise was stopped at ligation . This was accompanied by an accumulation of peri-collateral macrophages and increased expression of endothelial nitric oxide synthase and inducible nitric oxide synthase ( iNOS ) in hindlimb collateral and in MNC of blood and spleen . Systemic monocyte and macrophage depletion by liposomal clodronate but not splenectomy attenuated exercise-induced perfusion restoration , collateral artery growth , peri-collateral macrophage accumulation , and upregulation of iNOS . iNOS-deficient mice did not show exercise-induced perfusion restoration . Transplantation of bone marrow-derived MNC from iNOS-deficient mice into wild-type animals inhibited exercise-induced collateral artery growth . In contrast to sedentary controls , thrice weekly aerobic exercise training for 6 months in humans increased peripheral blood MNC iNOS expression . Circulating mononuclear cell-derived inducible nitric oxide is an important mediator of exercise-induced collateral artery growth .
rewrite: Collateral artery growth (arteriogenesis) serves as a key adaptive mechanism to reduced arterial blood flow. It remains unclear if preventive physical activity prior to limb ischemia can enhance arteriogenesis and influence mononuclear cell function. This research sought to examine the impact of endurance training before arterial occlusion on MNC activity and collateral artery development. Following three weeks of voluntary treadmill running, the right femoral artery was ligated in mice. Post-surgery hindlimb perfusion was similar to that in sedentary mice. Yet, prior exercise promoted perfusion recovery seven days after femoral artery ligation, even when exercise ceased at ligation. This improvement correlated with a buildup of peri-collateral macrophages and elevated expression of endothelial nitric oxide synthase and inducible nitric oxide synthase (iNOS) in hindlimb collaterals and in blood and spleen MNCs. Systemic depletion of monocytes and macrophages via liposomal clodronate, but not splenectomy, reduced exercise-induced perfusion recovery, collateral artery growth, peri-collateral macrophage accumulation, and iNOS upregulation. Mice lacking iNOS did not exhibit exercise-induced perfusion restoration. Transplanting bone marrow-derived MNCs from iNOS-deficient mice into wild-type animals blocked exercise-induced collateral artery growth. Unlike sedentary controls, humans engaging in thrice-weekly aerobic exercise for six months showed increased iNOS expression in peripheral blood MNCs. Inducible nitric oxide from circulating mononuclear cells is a significant mediator of exercise-induced collateral artery growth.

text: To evaluate the effect of 8-week moderate intensity aerobic ( heart-rate reserve 40-60 % ) exercise on neuropathy quality of life in type 2 diabetes . A single blind , parallel-group , randomized controlled trial was carried out in a tertiary setting . People with type 2 diabetes were eligible for the study if they had clinical neuropathy which was defined by a minimum score of seven on the Michigan diabetic neuropathy score . Following which , the patients were randomly assigned to an 8-week program by a computer-generated random number tables to intervention or control group . Repeated measure analysis of variance was used for data analysis ( p < 0.05 was considered significant ) . There were 47 participants in the control group and 40 participants in the study group after randomization but 37 from the control group and 29 from the intervention group completed the final analysis . The two groups had a significant difference , pre-post intervention in scores of pain ( F = 7 , p = 0.01 ) , sensory symptoms ( F = 4.60 , p = 0.04 ) , restricted activities of daily living ( F = 4.97 , p = 0.03 ) , disruptions in social relationships ( F = 5.43 , p = 0.02 ) , specific impact on quality of life ( F = 9.28 , p < 0.001 ) overall quality of life ( F = 28.72 , p < 0.001 ) , and total score ( F = 31.10 , p < 0.001 ) . Degrees of freedom for all the components were 1 , 62 . Moderate intensity aerobic exercise is cornerstone in improving the quality of life of individuals with peripheral neuropathy in type 2 diabetes .
rewrite: This study assessed how an 8-week moderate-intensity aerobic exercise program (40-60% heart-rate reserve) affects neuropathy-related quality of life in type 2 diabetes. A single-blind, parallel-group, randomized controlled trial was conducted in a tertiary care setting. Eligibility required a clinical diagnosis of neuropathy, defined as a Michigan Diabetic Neuropathy Score of at least seven. Participants were then randomly allocated via computer-generated tables to either an intervention or control group for the 8-week program. Data were analyzed using repeated measures ANOVA, with significance set at p < 0.05. Initially, 47 participants were in the control group and 40 in the study group; final analysis included 37 from the control and 29 from the intervention group. Significant pre-post intervention differences were found between groups for pain (F=7, p=0.01), sensory symptoms (F=4.60, p=0.04), restrictions in daily activities (F=4.97, p=0.03), disruptions in social relationships (F=5.43, p=0.02), specific quality of life impact (F=9.28, p<0.001), overall quality of life (F=28.72, p<0.001), and total score (F=31.10, p<0.001), all with 1,62 degrees of freedom. Moderate-intensity aerobic exercise is fundamental for enhancing quality of life in type 2 diabetes patients with peripheral neuropathy.

text: To compare 28-day mortality rates and clinical outcomes in ICU patients with ventilator-associated pneumonia according to the diagnostic strategy used . This was a prospective randomized clinical trial . Of the 73 patients included in the study , 36 and 37 were randomized to undergo BAL or endotracheal aspiration ( EA ) , respectively . Antibiotic therapy was based on guidelines and was adjusted according to the results of quantitative cultures . The 28-day mortality rate was similar in the BAL and EA groups ( 25.0 % and 37.8 % , respectively ; p = 0.353 ) . There were no differences between the groups regarding the duration of mechanical ventilation , antibiotic therapy , secondary complications , VAP recurrence , or length of ICU and hospital stay . Initial antibiotic therapy was deemed appropriate in 28 ( 77.8 % ) and 30 ( 83.3 % ) of the patients in the BAL and EA groups , respectively ( p = 0.551 ) . The 28-day mortality rate was not associated with the appropriateness of initial therapy in the BAL and EA groups ( appropriate therapy : 35.7 % vs. 43.3 % ; p = 0.553 ; and inappropriate therapy : 62.5 % vs. 50.0 % ; p = 1.000 ) . Previous use of antibiotics did not affect the culture yield in the EA or BAL group ( p = 0.130 and p = 0.484 , respectively ) . In the context of this study , the management of VAP patients , based on the results of quantitative endotracheal aspirate cultures , led to similar clinical outcomes to those obtained with the results of quantitative BAL fluid cultures . ( Brazilian Registry of Clinical Trials -- ReBEC ; identification number RBR-86DCDX [ http://www.ensaiosclinicos.gov.br] ) .
rewrite: This prospective randomized clinical trial compared 28-day mortality and clinical outcomes in ICU patients with ventilator-associated pneumonia based on diagnostic strategy. Among 73 enrolled patients, 36 were assigned to bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) and 37 to endotracheal aspiration (EA). Antibiotic therapy followed guidelines and was adjusted per quantitative culture results. The 28-day mortality was comparable between BAL and EA groups (25.0% vs. 37.8%; p=0.353). No significant differences were observed in mechanical ventilation duration, antibiotic therapy length, secondary complications, VAP recurrence, or ICU and hospital stay. Initial antibiotic therapy was appropriate in 77.8% of BAL patients and 83.3% of EA patients (p=0.551). Mortality at 28 days was not linked to initial therapy appropriateness in either group (appropriate: 35.7% vs. 43.3%, p=0.553; inappropriate: 62.5% vs. 50.0%, p=1.000). Prior antibiotic use did not significantly impact culture yield in EA (p=0.130) or BAL (p=0.484) groups. In this study, managing VAP using quantitative endotracheal aspirate cultures yielded clinical outcomes similar to those based on quantitative BAL fluid cultures. (Brazilian Registry of Clinical Trials—ReBEC; identifier: RBR-86DCDX [http://www.ensaiosclinicos.gov.br]).

text: To evaluate the presence of spinal inflammation with and without sacroiliac ( SI ) joint inflammation on magnetic resonance imaging ( MRI ) in patients with active nonradiographic axial spondyloarthritis ( SpA ) , and to compare the disease characteristics of these subgroups . ABILITY-1 is a multicenter , randomized , controlled trial of adalimumab versus placebo in patients with nonradiographic axial SpA classified using the Assessment of SpondyloArthritis international Society axial SpA criteria . Baseline MRIs were centrally scored independently by 2 readers using the Spondyloarthritis Research Consortium of Canada ( SPARCC ) method for the SI joints and the SPARCC 6-discovertebral unit method for the spine . Positive evidence of inflammation on MRI was defined as a SPARCC score of 2 for either the SI joints or the spine . Among patients with baseline SPARCC scores , 40 % had an SI joint score of 2 and 52 % had a spine score of 2 . Forty-nine percent of patients with baseline SI joint scores of < 2 , and 58 % of those with baseline SI joint scores of 2 , had a spine score of 2 . Comparison of baseline disease characteristics by baseline SI joint and spine scores showed that a greater proportion of patients in the subgroup with a baseline SPARCC score of 2 for both SI joints and spine were male , and patients with spine and SI joint scores of < 2 were younger and had shorter symptom duration . SPARCC spine scores correlated with baseline symptom duration , and SI joint scores correlated negatively with the baseline Bath Ankylosing Spondylitis Disease Activity Index , but neither correlated with the baseline Ankylosing Spondylitis Disease Activity Score , total back pain , the patient 's global assessment of disease activity , the Bath Ankylosing Spondylitis Functional Index , morning stiffness , nocturnal pain , or C-reactive protein level . Assessment by experienced readers showed that spinal inflammation on MRI might be observed in half of patients with nonradiographic axial SpA without SI joint inflammation .
rewrite: This study assessed spinal inflammation with and without sacroiliac (SI) joint involvement on MRI in patients with active nonradiographic axial spondyloarthritis (SpA), comparing disease characteristics between subgroups. ABILITY-1 was a multicenter, randomized, controlled trial of adalimumab versus placebo in patients meeting ASAS criteria for nonradiographic axial SpA. Baseline MRIs were centrally and independently scored by two readers using the SPARCC method for SI joints and the SPARCC 6-discovertebral unit method for the spine. MRI inflammation was defined as a SPARCC score of ≥2 for SI joints or spine. Of patients with baseline scores, 40% had an SI joint score ≥2 and 52% had a spine score ≥2. Among those with baseline SI joint scores <2, 49% had a spine score ≥2, compared to 58% of those with SI joint scores ≥2. Comparing baseline characteristics by SI joint and spine scores revealed a higher proportion of males in the subgroup with scores ≥2 for both sites, while patients with scores <2 for both were younger and had shorter symptom duration. SPARCC spine scores correlated with baseline symptom duration, and SI joint scores inversely correlated with baseline BASDAI, but neither correlated with ASDAS, total back pain, patient global assessment, BASFI, morning stiffness, nocturnal pain, or CRP. Expert assessment indicated spinal inflammation on MRI may be present in half of nonradiographic axial SpA patients without SI joint inflammation.

text: To investigate the effect of endotracheal intubation ( TT ) or the laryngeal mask airway ( LMA ) on the incidence of perioperative respiratory adverse events in children with upper respiratory tract infection undergo general anesthesia . From November , 2006 to October , 2012 in the Zhuji People 's Hospital , 76 children with upper respiratory tract infection approved by hospital ethic committee were randomly divided into 2 groups : group I ( n = 36 ) , children were applied with endotracheal intubation during general anesthesia ( TT group ) , while groupII ( n = 40 ) , laryngeal mask airway were used ( LMA group ) . Intraoperative mean arterial pressure ( MAP ) , hear rate ( HR ) , pulse oximetry ( SPO2 ) , and end-tidal carbon dioxide partial pressure ( P ETCO2 ) were recorded during the surgery . The incidence of adverse events such as hypoxemia , fidgety , sore throat , and laryngospasm were evaluated in resuscitation room.We also assessed the pre - and postoperative symptoms of respiratory tract infection . There was no significant difference in upper respiratory tract infection symptoms between two groups , and the children in both groups have good tolerance to TT or LMA.However , the hemodynamics status in LMA group were more stable than those in TT group after the LMA insertion or removing ( P < 0.05 ) . The incidence of hypoxemia , fidgety , sore throat , and laryngospasm were significant lower in LMA group compared with those in TT group ( P < 0.05 ) . LMA could decrease the incidence of perioperative respiratory adverse events and can be safely used in children with upper respiratory tract infection undergo general anesthesia .
rewrite: To examine the impact of endotracheal intubation (TT) versus laryngeal mask airway (LMA) on perioperative respiratory adverse events in children with upper respiratory tract infections under general anesthesia. From November 2006 to October 2012 at Zhuji People's Hospital, 76 children with upper respiratory tract infections, approved by the hospital ethics committee, were randomly assigned to two groups: group I (n=36) received endotracheal intubation during general anesthesia (TT group), while group II (n=40) received a laryngeal mask airway (LMA group). Intraoperative mean arterial pressure (MAP), heart rate (HR), pulse oximetry (SPO2), and end-tidal carbon dioxide partial pressure (PETCO2) were monitored. The occurrence of adverse events like hypoxemia, agitation, sore throat, and laryngospasm was evaluated in the recovery room. Pre- and postoperative respiratory infection symptoms were also assessed. No significant difference in upper respiratory tract infection symptoms was found between the groups, and both groups tolerated TT or LMA well. However, hemodynamics were more stable in the LMA group after insertion and removal compared to the TT group (P<0.05). The incidence of hypoxemia, agitation, sore throat, and laryngospasm was significantly lower in the LMA group than in the TT group (P<0.05). LMA reduces the incidence of perioperative respiratory adverse events and is safe for use in children with upper respiratory tract infections undergoing general anesthesia.

text: We aimed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of fully covered esophageal stent placement for preventing esophageal strictures after endoscopic submucosal dissection ( ESD ) . Twenty-two patients with a mucosal defects that exceeded 75 % of the circumference of the esophagus after ESD treatment for superficial esophageal squamous cell carcinomas were grouped according to the type of mucosal defect and randomized to undergo fully covered esophageal stent placement post-ESD ( group A , n = 11 ) or no stent placement ( group B , n = 11 ) . In group A , the esophageal stents were removed 8 weeks post-ESD . Endoscopy was performed when patients reported dysphagia symptoms and at 12 weeks post-ESD in patients without symptoms . Savary-Gilliard dilators were used for bougie dilation in patients experiencing esophageal stricture in both groups , and we compared the rates of post-ESD strictures and the need for bougie dilation procedures . The proportion of patients who developed a stricture was significantly lower in group A ( 18.2 % , n = 2 ) than in group B ( 72.7 % , n = 8 ) ( P < 0.05 ) . Moreover , the number of bougie dilation procedures was significantly lower in group A ( mean 0.45 , range 0-3 ) than in group B ( mean 3.9 , range 0-17 ) ( P < 0.05 ) . The two patients in group A who experienced stricture also had stent displacement . Esophageal stents are a safe and effective method of preventing esophageal strictures in cases where > 75 % of the circumference of the esophagus has mucosal defects after ESD treatment for early esophageal cancer .
rewrite: This study assessed the effectiveness and safety of fully covered esophageal stents in preventing strictures following endoscopic submucosal dissection (ESD). Twenty-two patients with mucosal defects covering over 75% of the esophageal circumference after ESD for superficial esophageal squamous cell carcinoma were categorized by defect type and randomly assigned to receive a fully covered esophageal stent after ESD (group A, n=11) or no stent (group B, n=11).
