This trial offers initial evidence that antisense oligonucleotides could serve as a treatment for neuroimmunological conditions. It provides Class I evidence that ATL1102 decreases new active brain MRI lesions in RRMS patients.

text: The purpose of this study was to investigate the efficacy of a 1440-nm neodymium : yttrium-aluminum-garnet ( Nd : YAG ) laser on relieving pain in relation to the levels of inflammatory cytokine and neuropeptides in the root canal exudates of teeth with persistent symptomatic apical periodontitis . Forty teeth with persistent symptomatic apical periodontitis were randomly assigned to treatment groups : group L , intracanal irradiation of 1440-nm Nd : YAG laser with a 300-m-diameter fiberoptic tip in addition to conventional root canal retreatment , and group C , conventional root canal re-treatment . The degrees of both spontaneous pain and the pain on percussion before and after treatment were recorded , and root canal exudate samples were collected to quantify the associated levels of substance P , calcitonin gene-related peptide ( CGRP ) , and matrix metalloproteinase ( MMP ) -8 by immunoassay . All of the measured parameters were significantly reduced in group L ( P < .05 ) , whereas the level of pain on percussion , CGRP , and MMP-8 were significantly reduced in group C ( P < .05 ) . The 1440-nm Nd : YAG laser had significantly better effect on the relief of pain on percussion and the reduction of substance P , CGRP , and MMP-8 levels . The visual analog scale scores of perceived pain correlated with pain-related neuropeptides and inflammatory cytokine levels in root canal exudates . The 1440-nm Nd : YAG laser irradiation via fiberoptic tip to the teeth with persistent apical periodontitis provided promising consequences of pain and inflammation modulation .
rewrite: This study aimed to assess the effectiveness of a 1440-nm neodymium:yttrium-aluminum-garnet (Nd:YAG) laser in alleviating pain by examining inflammatory cytokine and neuropeptide levels in root canal exudates from teeth with persistent symptomatic apical periodontitis. Forty affected teeth were randomly divided into two treatment groups: group L received intracanal irradiation using a 1440-nm Nd:YAG laser with a 300-µm fiberoptic tip alongside conventional root canal retreatment, while group C underwent conventional retreatment alone. Spontaneous pain and percussion pain were evaluated before and after treatment, and exudate samples were analyzed via immunoassay for substance P, calcitonin gene-related peptide (CGRP), and matrix metalloproteinase (MMP)-8. All measured parameters decreased significantly in group L (P < .05), whereas group C showed significant reductions only in percussion pain, CGRP, and MMP-8 (P < .05). The 1440-nm Nd:YAG laser demonstrated superior efficacy in reducing percussion pain and lowering substance P, CGRP, and MMP-8 levels. Visual analog scale pain scores correlated with neuropeptide and inflammatory cytokine concentrations in the exudates. Fiberoptic tip irradiation with the 1440-nm Nd:YAG laser in teeth with persistent apical periodontitis yielded promising outcomes for modulating pain and inflammation.

text: This research compared the effects of real versus hyper-real images on anxiety , disgust , and physiological arousal during internet-delivered exposure in high spider-fearfuls . Hyper-real images were digitally altered to highlight fearful aspects . A further aim was to examine self-reported and behavioural therapeutic outcomes and exposure-related predictors of these outcomes . Twenty-eight females were randomised to real ( n = 14 ) or hyper-real ( n = 14 ) treatment groups and nine participants were subsequently allocated to a wait-list control group . Treatment groups viewed an 8-stage exposure hierarchy of real or hyper-real spider images . Subjective anxiety and disgust ratings were taken during each stage ( 0 , 60 , 120 , 180s ) with heart rate and skin conductance recorded throughout . Anxiety , disgust and physiological arousal habituated within each exposure stage , with no differential effect of real compared to hyper-real images . Both treatment groups but not controls demonstrated significant reductions in behavioural avoidance and self-reported phobic symptoms from pre-treatment to post-treatment with large effect sizes noted . The change in within-stage habituation of anxiety , disgust and heart rate , between the first and last stage , predicted improvement in behavioural avoidance at post-treatment . This suggests that generalisation of habituation to multiple images is an important predictor of improvement . While findings in relation to therapeutic outcome should be considered preliminary , clear relationships were found between exposure-related variables and outcome among those who undertook treatment . Findings provide evidence in support of the efficacy of online image-based exposure and have implications for informing further research into the underlying mechanisms of image-based exposure treatment .
rewrite: This study examined the impact of real and hyper-real images on anxiety, disgust, and physiological arousal during online exposure therapy for individuals with high spider fear. Hyper-real images were digitally enhanced to emphasize fear-inducing features. An additional objective was to assess self-reported and behavioral treatment outcomes, along with exposure-related predictors. Twenty-eight female participants were assigned to either real (n=14) or hyper-real (n=14) treatment conditions, with nine later placed in a wait-list control group. Treatment groups completed an 8-step exposure hierarchy using either real or hyper-real spider images. Subjective anxiety and disgust were rated at intervals (0, 60, 120, 180s), while heart rate and skin conductance were continuously monitored. Anxiety, disgust, and physiological arousal habituated within each exposure stage, with no significant difference between real and hyper-real images. Both treatment groups, but not controls, showed substantial reductions in behavioral avoidance and self-reported phobic symptoms from pre- to post-treatment, with large effect sizes. The change in within-stage habituation of anxiety, disgust, and heart rate between the first and last stages predicted improvements in behavioral avoidance post-treatment. This indicates that generalization of habituation across multiple images is a key predictor of progress. Although therapeutic outcome findings are preliminary, clear associations were observed between exposure-related variables and outcomes among treated participants. The results support the effectiveness of online image-based exposure and highlight directions for further research into its underlying mechanisms.

text: whole-body vibration training may improve neuromuscular function , falls risk and bone density , but previous studies have had conflicting findings . this study aimed to evaluate the influence of vertical vibration ( VV ) and side-alternating vibration ( SV ) on musculoskeletal health in older people at risk of falls . single-blind , randomised , controlled trial comparing vibration training to sham vibration ( Sham ) in addition to usual care . participants were 61 older people ( 37 women and 24 men ) , aged 80.2 + 6.5 years , referred to an outpatient falls prevention service . participants were randomly assigned to VV , SV or Sham in addition to the usual falls prevention programme . Participants were requested to attend three vibration sessions per week for 12 weeks , with sessions increasing to six , 1 min bouts of vibration . Falls risk factors and neuromuscular tests were assessed , and blood samples collected for determination of bone turnover , at baseline and following the intervention . chair stand time , timed-up-and-go time , fear of falling , NEADL index and postural sway with eyes open improved in the Sham group . There were significantly greater gains in leg power in the VV than in the Sham group and in bone formation in SV and VV compared with the Sham group . Conversely , body sway improved less in the VV than in the Sham group . Changes in falls risk factors did not differ between the groups . whole-body vibration increased leg power and bone formation , but it did not provide any additional benefits to balance or fall risk factors beyond a falls prevention programme in older people at risk of falls .
rewrite: Whole-body vibration training could enhance neuromuscular function, reduce fall risk, and increase bone density, though earlier research has shown inconsistent results. This investigation sought to assess the effects of vertical vibration (VV) and side-alternating vibration (SV) on musculoskeletal health in older adults at risk of falling. A single-blind, randomized, controlled trial compared vibration training to sham vibration (Sham) alongside standard care. Participants included 61 older individuals (37 women, 24 men), average age 80.2 ± 6.5 years, recruited from an outpatient falls prevention service. They were randomly allocated to VV, SV, or Sham groups in addition to the usual falls prevention program. Participants attended three vibration sessions weekly for 12 weeks, with sessions gradually increasing to six one-minute bouts of vibration. Fall risk factors and neuromuscular tests were evaluated, and blood samples were taken to measure bone turnover at baseline and after the intervention. Improvements in chair stand time, timed-up-and-go time, fear of falling, NEADL index, and postural sway with eyes open were observed in the Sham group. Significantly greater improvements in leg power were noted in the VV group compared to Sham, and in bone formation for both SV and VV groups relative to Sham. In contrast, body sway improved less in the VV group than in Sham. Changes in fall risk factors did not vary significantly between groups. Whole-body vibration boosted leg power and bone formation but offered no extra advantages for balance or fall risk factors beyond a standard falls prevention program in older adults at risk of falls.

text: Transcranial direct current stimulation ( tDCS ) is a non-invasive technique used for modulating cortical excitability in vivo in humans . Here we evaluated the effect of tDCS on behavioral and electrophysiological aspects of physiological sucking and swallowing . Twelve healthy subjects underwent three tDCS sessions ( anodal , cathodal and sham stimulation ) on separate days in a double-blind randomized order . The active electrode was placed over the right swallowing motor cortex . Repeated sucking and swallowing acts were performed at baseline and at 15 and 60 min after each tDCS session and the mean liquid bolus volume ingested at each time point was measured . We also calculated average values of the following electrophysiological parameters : 1 ) area and 2 ) duration of the rectified EMG signal from the suprahyoid/submental muscles related to the sucking and swallowing phases ; 3 ) EMG peak amplitude for the sucking and swallowing phases ; 4 ) area and peak amplitude of the laryngeal-pharyngeal mechanogram ; 5 ) oropharyngeal delay . The volume of the ingested bolus significantly increased ( by an average of about 30 % compared with the baseline value ) both at 15 and at 60 min after the end of anodal tDCS . The electrophysiological evaluation after anodal tDCS showed a significant increase in area and duration of the sucking phase-related EMG signal . Anodal tDCS leads to stronger sucking of a liquid bolus in healthy subjects , likely by increasing recruitment of cortical areas of the swallowing network . This finding might open up interesting perspectives for the treatment of patients suffering from dysphagia due to various pathological conditions .
rewrite: Transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) is a non-invasive method for modulating cortical excitability in humans. This study assessed the impact of tDCS on behavioral and electrophysiological features of natural sucking and swallowing. Twelve healthy participants completed three tDCS sessions (anodal, cathodal, and sham stimulation) on different days in a randomized, double-blind design. The active electrode was positioned over the right swallowing motor cortex. Repeated sucking and swallowing actions were carried out at baseline, 15 minutes, and 60 minutes after each tDCS session, with the mean liquid bolus volume consumed at each interval recorded. We also computed average values for these electrophysiological measures: 1) area and 2) duration of the rectified EMG signal from suprahyoid/submental muscles during sucking and swallowing phases; 3) EMG peak amplitude for both phases; 4) area and peak amplitude of the laryngeal-pharyngeal mechanogram; 5) oropharyngeal delay. The ingested bolus volume rose significantly (by roughly 30% on average relative to baseline) at 15 and 60 minutes following anodal tDCS. Electrophysiological analysis after anodal tDCS revealed a notable increase in area and duration of the EMG signal linked to the sucking phase. Anodal tDCS enhances liquid bolus sucking in healthy individuals, probably by boosting recruitment in cortical regions of the swallowing network. This result could offer promising avenues for treating dysphagia in patients with various pathological conditions.

text: Declining cognition is a risk factor for falls among older adults . The extent to which impaired judgment in performance of daily activities increases fall risk is unclear . The aim of this study was to determine whether engagement in mobility activities in a risky manner explains the association between declining cognition and rate of falls . This study was a secondary analysis of baseline and prospective data from older adults enrolled in the intervention arm of a randomized clinical trial . Two hundred forty-five community-dwelling older adults ( 79 % female ; mean age = 79 years , SD = 8.0 ) who were at risk for falls received physical , cognitive , and functional evaluations . Cognition was assessed with the Short Portable Mental Status Questionnaire ( SPMSQ ) . Using interview and in-home assessment data , physical therapists determined whether participants were at risk for falls when performing mobility-related activities of daily living ( ADL ) and instrumental ADL ( IADL ) . Falls were measured prospectively for 1 year using monthly falls diaries . Declining cognition was associated with increased number of mobility activities designated as risky ( 1.5 % of mobility activities performed in a risky manner per SPMSQ point ) and with increased rate of falls ( rate ratio = 1.16 for each unit change in SPMSQ score ) . Risky performance of mobility activities mediated the relationship between cognition and rate of falls . Risk assessment was based on the clinical judgment of experienced physical therapists . Cognition was measured with a relatively insensitive instrument , and only selected mobility activities were evaluated . Engagement in mobility ADL and IADL tasks in a risky manner emerged as a link between declining cognition and increased number of falls , suggesting a mechanism through which the rate of falls may increase . Specifically , declining cognition is associated with performance of mobility activities in an unsafe manner , thereby increasing the risk for falls .
rewrite: Cognitive decline is a risk factor for falls in older adults. It remains uncertain how impaired judgment in daily activities elevates fall risk. This study aimed to assess whether engaging in mobility activities unsafely mediates the link between cognitive decline and fall rates. A secondary analysis was conducted using baseline and prospective data from older adults in the intervention group of a randomized clinical trial. Participants included 245 community-dwelling older adults (79% female; mean age = 79 years, SD = 8.0) at risk for falls, who underwent physical, cognitive, and functional assessments. Cognition was evaluated with the Short Portable Mental Status Questionnaire (SPMSQ). Based on interview and in-home assessment data, physical therapists identified whether participants performed mobility-related activities of daily living (ADL) and instrumental ADL (IADL) unsafely. Falls were tracked prospectively for one year via monthly diaries. Cognitive decline correlated with a higher number of mobility activities deemed risky (1.5% of mobility activities performed unsafely per SPMSQ point) and with an increased fall rate (rate ratio = 1.16 per unit change in SPMSQ score). Risky performance of mobility activities mediated the cognition-fall rate relationship. Risk assessment relied on the clinical judgment of experienced physical therapists. Cognition was measured with a relatively insensitive tool, and only specific mobility activities were examined. Engaging unsafely in mobility ADL and IADL tasks emerged as a connection between cognitive decline and more falls, indicating a potential mechanism for increased fall rates. In essence, cognitive decline is linked to unsafe performance of mobility activities, thus raising fall risk.

text: To investigate the effect of central venous blood oxygen saturation ( ScvO2 ) and venous-arterial PCO2 ( P ( cv-a ) CO2 ) guided fluid therapy on tissue perfusion , gastrointestinal function recovering and outcome of the patients who undergoing open gastrointestinal surgery . Forty patients undergoing open gastrointestinal surgery were randomly divided into 2 groups ( n = 20 each ) : ScvO2 guided fluid therapy ( group S ) and P ( cv-a ) CO2 guided fluid therapy ( group P ) . All the patients were infused 10 ml/kg lactated Ringer 's ( LR ) solution before anesthesia induction , they were all also given a continuous lactated Ringer 's ( LR ) solution 's infusion at the speed of 2 mlkg ( -1 ) h ( -1 ) during the operation . While , 6 % HES 130/0 .4 ( free flex 6 % HES 130/0 .4 , Fresenius Kabi ) infusion was different between the 2 groups , when the patients of group S 's central venous blood oxygen saturation < 75 % or venous-arterial PCO2 in the patients of P group 6 mm Hg , then infused 6 % HES 130/0 .4 . Arterial and central venous blood gas analyses were performed every 20 minutes after skin incision , measure the venous and arterial lactate value , and record the anal exhaust time after surgery , postoperative complications and mortality in 28 days . Compared with group S , the arterial lactate value in T4 ( after operation began 80 min ) were significantly decreased in group P ( P = 0.013 ) , and venous lactate value in T5 ( after operation began 100 min ) were also lower ( P = 0.044 ) , other lactate value were not different ( P > 0.05 ) . The anal exhaust time was not different between the two groups ( P = 0.673 ) . All the patients were survival , and there were no obvious postoperative complications . Compared to group S , there was a transient improvement in tissue perfusion in group P , but there were no difference in complications and mortality .
rewrite: To examine the impact of fluid therapy guided by central venous oxygen saturation (ScvO2) and venous-arterial PCO2 (P(cv-a)CO2) on tissue perfusion, gastrointestinal function recovery, and outcomes in patients undergoing open gastrointestinal surgery. Forty patients scheduled for open gastrointestinal surgery were randomly assigned to two groups (n=20 each): ScvO2-guided fluid therapy (group S) and P(cv-a)CO2-guided fluid therapy (group P). All patients received a 10 ml/kg lactated Ringer's (LR) solution infusion before anesthesia induction, along with a continuous LR infusion at 2 ml·kg⁻¹·h⁻¹ during surgery. However, the administration of 6% HES 130/0.4 (free flex 6% HES 130/0.4, Fresenius Kabi) differed between groups: it was infused when ScvO2 fell below 75% in group S or when P(cv-a)CO2 exceeded 6 mm Hg in group P. Arterial and central venous blood gas analyses were conducted every 20 minutes post-skin incision, measuring venous and arterial lactate levels, with postoperative anal exhaust time, complications, and 28-day mortality recorded. Compared to group S, group P showed significantly lower arterial lactate at T4 (80 minutes after surgery start; P=0.013) and venous lactate at T5 (100 minutes after surgery start; P=0.044), with no differences in other lactate values (P>0.05). Anal exhaust time did not differ between groups (P=0.673). All patients survived without significant postoperative complications. Relative to group S, group P demonstrated a transient improvement in tissue perfusion, but no differences in complications or mortality were observed.

text: This study sought to investigate the effect of a multiple micronutrient supplement on left ventricular ejection fraction ( LVEF ) in patients with heart failure . Observational studies suggest that patients with heart failure have reduced intake and lower concentrations of a number of micronutrients . However , there have been very few intervention studies investigating the effect of micronutrient supplementation in patients with heart failure . This was a randomized , double-blind , placebo-controlled , parallel-group study involving 74 patients with chronic stable heart failure that compared multiple micronutrient supplementation taken once daily versus placebo for 12 months . The primary endpoint was LVEF assessed by cardiovascular magnetic resonance imaging or 3-dimensional echocardiography . Secondary endpoints were Minnesota Living With Heart Failure Questionnaire score , 6-min walk test distance , blood concentrations of N-terminal prohormone of brain natriuretic peptide , C-reactive protein , tumor necrosis factor alpha , interleukin-6 , interleukin-10 , and urinary levels of 8-iso-prostaglandin F2 alpha . Blood concentrations of a number of micronutrients increased significantly in the micronutrient supplement group , indicating excellent compliance with the intervention . There was no significant difference in mean LVEF at 12 months between treatment groups after adjusting for baseline ( mean difference : 1.6 % , 95 % confidence interval : -2.6 to 5.8 , p = 0.441 ) . There was also no significant difference in any of the secondary endpoints at 12 months between treatment groups . This study provides no evidence to support the routine treatment of patients with chronic stable heart failure with a multiple micronutrient supplement . ( Micronutrient Supplementation in Patients With Heart Failure [ MINT-HF ] ; NCT01005303 ) .
rewrite: This research aimed to examine the impact of a multiple micronutrient supplement on left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) in heart failure patients. Observational data indicate that heart failure patients often have diminished intake and lower levels of various micronutrients. Yet, intervention studies exploring micronutrient supplementation in this population are scarce. In this randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group trial, 74 patients with chronic stable heart failure received either a daily multiple micronutrient supplement or a placebo for 12 months. The primary outcome was LVEF measured via cardiovascular magnetic resonance imaging or 3-dimensional echocardiography. Secondary outcomes included the Minnesota Living With Heart Failure Questionnaire score, 6-minute walk test distance, and blood levels of N-terminal prohormone of brain natriuretic peptide, C-reactive protein, tumor necrosis factor alpha, interleukin-6, interleukin-10, as well as urinary 8-iso-prostaglandin F2 alpha. Blood micronutrient concentrations rose significantly in the supplement group, reflecting high adherence. After adjusting for baseline, no significant difference in mean LVEF was observed at 12 months between groups (mean difference: 1.6%, 95% CI: -2.6 to 5.8, p = 0.441). Similarly, none of the secondary endpoints showed significant differences at 12 months. These findings offer no support for the routine use of multiple micronutrient supplements in patients with chronic stable heart failure. (Micronutrient Supplementation in Patients With Heart Failure [MINT-HF]; NCT01005303).

text: Four-factor prothrombin complex concentrates ( PCCs ) , which contain factorII , FVII , FIX , and FX , have shown the potential to reverse the anticoagulant effect of rivaroxaban in healthy volunteers . The purpose of this study was to determine whether a three-factor PCC , which contains little FVII , has a similar effect . We performed an open-label , single-center , parallel-group study comparing the effect of a three-factor PCC ( ProfilnineSD ) with that of a four-factor PCC ( BeriplexP/N ) on the pharmacodynamics of rivaroxaban in 35 healthy volunteers . After receiving 4days of rivaroxaban 20mg twice daily to obtain supratherapeutic steady-state concentrations , volunteers were randomized to receive a single 50IUkg ( -1 ) bolus dose of four-factor PCC , three-factor PCC or saline 4h after the morning dose of rivaroxaban on day5 , and the effects of these interventions on prothrombin time and thrombin generation were determined . Within 30min , four-factor PCC reduced mean prothrombin time by 2.5-3 .5 s , whereas three-factor PCC produced only a 0.6-1 .0 - s reduction . In contrast , three-factor PCC reversed rivaroxaban-induced changes in thrombin generation more than four-factor PCC . This study demonstrates the potential of both three-factor and four-factor PCCs to at least partially reverse the anticoagulant effects of rivaroxaban in healthy adults . The discrepant effects of the PCC preparations may reflect differences in the procoagulant components present in each .
rewrite: Four-factor prothrombin complex concentrates (PCCs), containing factors II, VII, IX, and X, have demonstrated potential to counteract rivaroxaban's anticoagulant effect in healthy subjects. This study aimed to assess whether a three-factor PCC, with minimal factor VII, exerts a comparable effect. We conducted an open-label, single-center, parallel-group trial comparing the impact of a three-factor PCC (ProfilnineSD) and a four-factor PCC (BeriplexP/N) on rivaroxaban's pharmacodynamics in 35 healthy volunteers. Following 4 days of rivaroxaban 20 mg twice daily to achieve supratherapeutic steady-state levels, participants were randomized to receive a single 50 IU/kg bolus of four-factor PCC, three-factor PCC, or saline 4 hours after the morning rivaroxaban dose on day 5. The interventions' effects on prothrombin time and thrombin generation were evaluated. Within 30 minutes, four-factor PCC shortened mean prothrombin time by 2.5–3.5 s, while three-factor PCC reduced it by only 0.6–1.0 s. Conversely, three-factor PCC more effectively reversed rivaroxaban-induced alterations in thrombin generation than four-factor PCC. This research indicates that both three-factor and four-factor PCCs can at least partially reverse rivaroxaban's anticoagulant effects in healthy adults. The differing effects of the PCC formulations may arise from variations in their procoagulant constituents.

text: Chinese Americans are at increased risk for hepatitis B virus ( HBV ) infection . To reduce or eliminate disparities in HBV-related infection rates , participation in scientific investigations of HBV risk and treatment , including biospecimen sampling , is important . However , Asian Americans have low rates of participation in biospecimen research , and little is known about how educational interventions affect knowledge and participation in HBV-related biospecimen research . Eight Chinese community-based organizations participated in a quasi-experimental , two-group design with education assessments at pre - and postworkshop and a 3-month follow-up . Four sites were randomly assigned to receive the intervention ( n = 175 ) and four sites to receive general health education ( control ; n = 240 ) . Participant knowledge about biospecimen research increased from pre - to posteducation in the intervention but not in the control condition . Of intervention participants , 83.4 % ( 146/175 ) donated one tube of blood for future HBV biospecimen research , and 50.9 % ( 89/175 ) donated another tube of blood for HBV testing . In contrast , only 1.1 % of participants in the control condition reported donating a blood sample at follow-up assessment . The intervention program significantly increased knowledge of and participation in HBV biospecimen research among Chinese Americans . Community-based participatory research ( CBPR ) methods featured active support by community leaders , a culturally specific curriculum , and convenient , immediate access to blood sampling , which resulted in high donation rates . HBV-related morbidity and mortality is an urgent problem faced by Chinese Americans . CBPR provides a model for engaging communities in early detection , vaccination , and treatment that can reduce this health threat .
rewrite: Chinese Americans face a heightened risk of hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection. Addressing disparities in HBV infection rates requires involvement in scientific studies on HBV risk and treatment, including biospecimen collection. Yet, Asian Americans show low engagement in biospecimen studies, and the impact of educational efforts on their knowledge and participation in HBV-related biospecimen research is poorly understood. Eight Chinese community organizations took part in a quasi-experimental, two-group study with evaluations before and after workshops and at a 3-month follow-up. Four sites were randomly chosen for the intervention (n = 175), while four received general health education (control; n = 240). Knowledge about biospecimen research rose from pre- to post-education in the intervention group but not in the control group. Among intervention participants, 83.4% (146/175) gave one blood tube for future HBV biospecimen research, and 50.9% (89/175) donated an additional tube for HBV testing. In comparison, only 1.1% of control participants reported donating blood at follow-up. The intervention notably boosted knowledge and participation in HBV biospecimen research among Chinese Americans. Community-based participatory research (CBPR) approaches, which included strong community leader backing, a culturally tailored curriculum, and easy, on-site blood collection, led to high donation rates. HBV-related illness and death pose a pressing challenge for Chinese Americans. CBPR offers a framework to involve communities in early detection, vaccination, and treatment, helping to mitigate this health risk.

text: Very little is known about the relationship between non-sickle cell anemia and stroke . The purpose of this study is to evaluate the association of iron-deficiency anemia ( IDA ) with stroke based on a nationwide coverage database in Taiwan . The case-control study subjects were obtained from the Taiwanese Longitudinal Health Insurance Database 2000 . We included 51,093 subjects with stroke as cases and randomly selected 153,279 controls ( 3 controls per case ) in this study.Separate conditional logistic regression analyses were used to calculate the odds ratio ( OR ) for having been previously diagnosed with IDA between cases and controls.We further analyzed the association between stroke and IDA by stroke subtype . Results showed that 3,685 study subjects ( 1.81 % ) had been diagnosed with IDA prior to the index date ; of those subjects , 1,268 ( 2.48 % ) were cases and 2,417 ( 1.58 % ) were controls ( p < 0.001 ) . Conditional logistic regression shows that the OR of having previously received an IDA diagnosis among cases was 1.49 ( 95 % CI : 1.39 ~ 1.60 ; p < 0.01 ) that of controls after adjusting for monthly income , geographic region , hypertension , diabetes , coronary heart disease , atrial fibrillation , heart failure , hyperlipidemia , tobacco use disorder , and alcohol abuse/alcohol dependency syndrome . Furthermore , the adjusted OR of prior IDA for cases with ischemic stroke was found to be 1.45 ( 95 % CI : 1.34 ~ 1.58 ) compared to controls . However , we did not find any significant relationship between IDA and subarachnoid/intracerebral hemorrhage even adjusting for other confounding factors ( OR = 1.17 , 95 % CI = 0.97 ~ 1.40 ) . There is a significant association between prior IDA and ischemic stroke .
rewrite: The connection between non-sickle cell anemia and stroke remains poorly understood. This study aims to assess the link between iron-deficiency anemia (IDA) and stroke using a comprehensive national database in Taiwan. Data were drawn from the Taiwanese Longitudinal Health Insurance Database 2000. The analysis included 51,093 stroke patients as cases and 153,279 randomly selected controls (3 per case). Conditional logistic regression was employed to compute the odds ratio (OR) for a prior IDA diagnosis in cases versus controls, with further analysis by stroke subtype. Findings indicated that 3,685 subjects (1.81%) had an IDA diagnosis before the index date; among these, 1,268 (2.48%) were cases and 2,417 (1.58%) were controls (p < 0.001). After adjusting for income, region, hypertension, diabetes, coronary heart disease, atrial fibrillation, heart failure, hyperlipidemia, tobacco use disorder, and alcohol abuse/dependency, the OR for prior IDA in cases was 1.49 (95% CI: 1.39–1.60; p < 0.01). For ischemic stroke specifically, the adjusted OR was 1.45 (95% CI: 1.34–1.58). However, no significant association was found between IDA and subarachnoid/intracerebral hemorrhage after adjusting for confounders (OR = 1.17, 95% CI: 0.97–1.40). A significant relationship exists between prior IDA and ischemic stroke.

text: There have been several studies of atrial fibrillation ( AF ) over the past decades ; however , data from Chinese patients are scarce . The aim of the study was therefore to describe the patient characteristics , risk profile and management strategies for Chinese AF patients presenting to emergency department ( ED ) . We conducted a prospective , multicentre registry of patients with AF or atrial flutter ( AFL ) in China . Participants were enrolled at 20 EDs , then data regarding baseline characteristics and treatment in EDs were collected . Of the 2016 Chinese patients , 1104 ( 54.8 % ) were female . Six hundred eighteen ( 30.7 % ) had paroxysmal AF , 452 ( 22.4 % ) had persistent AF and 945 ( 46.9 % ) had permanent AF . The most common comorbidity was hypertension ( 55.5 % ) , followed by coronary artery disease ( 41.8 % ) and heart failure ( HF , 37.4 % ) . The prevalence of concomitant cardiovascular risk factors , such as HF and valvular heart disease , increased as AF progressed . Among the patients with non-valvular AF , 110 ( 12.7 % ) of those with CHADS2 ( congestive HF , hypertension , age of 75 years and greater , diabetes mellitus and history of stroke ) 2 were prescribed oral anticoagulants ( OAC ) , while 119 ( 15.6 % ) of those with CHADS2 < 2 received such agents . Among the 324 patients with valvular AF , 134 ( 41.4 % ) actually were treated with OAC . The international normalised ratio value was within the target range ( 2.0-3 .0 ) in 96 patients only ( 26.4 % ) . Moreover , a total of 16.2 % of the patients received 1 anti-arrhythmic agents , whereas rate control agents were used more frequently ( 68.4 % ) . According to the present study , the risk profile and management of Chinese patients with AF/AFL differed from that observed in previous studies . The use of OAC inadequately deviate from current guidelines .
rewrite: Over recent decades, multiple studies have examined atrial fibrillation (AF), yet data from Chinese populations remain limited. This study aimed to characterize patient profiles, risk factors, and management approaches for Chinese AF patients in emergency departments (EDs). We performed a prospective, multicenter registry of AF or atrial flutter (AFL) patients across China. Enrollment occurred at 20 EDs, with collection of baseline characteristics and ED treatments. Among 2016 patients, 1104 (54.8%) were female. Paroxysmal AF was present in 618 (30.7%), persistent AF in 452 (22.4%), and permanent AF in 945 (46.9%). Hypertension was the most frequent comorbidity (55.5%), followed by coronary artery disease (41.8%) and heart failure (HF, 37.4%). Accompanying cardiovascular risks, like HF and valvular heart disease, rose with AF progression. In non-valvular AF patients, 110 (12.7%) with CHADS2 (congestive HF, hypertension, age ≥75, diabetes, stroke history) ≥2 received oral anticoagulants (OAC), versus 119 (15.6%) with CHADS2 <2. Among 324 valvular AF patients, 134 (41.4%) were treated with OAC. Only 96 patients (26.4%) had international normalized ratio values within the target range (2.0–3.0). Additionally, 16.2% of patients received anti-arrhythmic drugs, while rate control agents were more common (68.4%). This study indicates that risk profiles and management for Chinese AF/AFL patients differ from prior research, with OAC use often not aligning with current guidelines.

text: Cryptococcal meningitis is the most common cause of adult meningitis in sub-Saharan Africa . Raised intracranial pressure ( ICP ) is common in cryptococcosis . Prior studies suggest elevated ICP is associated with mortality , and guidelines recommend frequent lumbar punctures ( LPs ) to control ICP . However , the magnitude of the impact of LPs on cryptococcal-related mortality is unknown . In sum , 248 individuals with human immunodeficiency virus ( HIV ) - associated cryptococcal meningitis , screened for the Cryptococcal Optimal ART Timing ( COAT ) trial in Uganda and South Africa , were observed . Individuals received an LP to diagnose meningitis , and subsequent therapeutic LPs were recommended for elevated ICP ( > 250 mmH2O ) or new symptoms . We compared survival , through 11 days , between individuals receiving at least 1 therapeutic LP with individuals not receiving therapeutic LPs . The COAT trial randomized subjects at 7-11 days ; thus , follow-up stopped at time of death , randomization , or 11 days . Seventy-five ( 30 % ) individuals had at least 1 therapeutic LP . Individuals receiving therapeutic LPs had higher cerebrospinal fluid ( CSF ) opening pressures , higher CSF fungal burdens , and were more likely to have altered mental status at baseline than those with no therapeutic LPs . Thirty-one deaths ( 18 % ) occurred among 173 individuals without a therapeutic LP and 5 deaths ( 7 % ) among 75 with at least 1 therapeutic LP . The adjusted relative risk of mortality was 0.31 ( 95 % confidence interval : .12 -.82 ) . The association was observed regardless of opening pressure at baseline . Therapeutic LPs were associated with a 69 % relative improvement in survival , regardless of initial intracranial pressure . The role of therapeutic LPs should be reevaluated .
rewrite: Cryptococcal meningitis represents the leading cause of adult meningitis in sub-Saharan Africa. Elevated intracranial pressure (ICP) frequently occurs in cryptococcosis. Previous research indicates that high ICP is linked to mortality, and guidelines advise regular lumbar punctures (LPs) to manage ICP. Yet, the extent to which LPs affect cryptococcal-related mortality remains unclear. In total, 248 participants with human immunodeficiency virus (HIV)-associated cryptococcal meningitis, screened for the Cryptococcal Optimal ART Timing (COAT) trial in Uganda and South Africa, were monitored. All underwent an LP for meningitis diagnosis, with additional therapeutic LPs advised for high ICP (>250 mmH2O) or new symptoms. Survival up to 11 days was compared between those receiving at least one therapeutic LP and those receiving none. The COAT trial randomized participants at 7-11 days; therefore, follow-up ended at death, randomization, or 11 days. Seventy-five (30%) participants had at least one therapeutic LP. Those receiving therapeutic LPs exhibited higher cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) opening pressures, greater CSF fungal burdens, and were more prone to altered mental status at baseline compared to those without therapeutic LPs. Among 173 individuals without a therapeutic LP, 31 deaths (18%) occurred, while among 75 with at least one therapeutic LP, 5 deaths (7%) occurred. The adjusted relative risk of mortality was 0.31 (95% confidence interval: .12–.82). This association was noted irrespective of baseline opening pressure. Therapeutic LPs were linked to a 69% relative improvement in survival, independent of initial intracranial pressure. The function of therapeutic LPs warrants reevaluation.

text: To measure the feasibility , safety , and efficacy of the cranial cup device in a sample of hospitalized infants at risk for deformational plagiocephaly ( DP ) . A multisite , stratified , and randomized single-blinded study . Neonatal intensive care units ( NICU ) from three urban and one suburban hospital participated . Subjects included 62 infants with lengths of stay 14 days . Nurses caring for infants in study group 1 used the moldable positioner . In study group 2 , nurses rotated the moldable positioner and cranial cup devices using the cranial cup for a target goal of 12 hours/day . Both study groups received routine position changes . Outcome measures included hours of device use ( feasibility ) , cardiorespiratory and emesis events ( safety ) , and cranial measurements obtained at discharge ( efficacy ) by one of four , licensed orthotists who were blinded to the study . A total of 35 infants were randomized to study group 1 ( moldable positioner ) and 27 infants to study group 2 ( moldable positioner and cranial cup ) . The median hours per day on the cranial cup was 10.7 ( range 4.5-15 .3 ) . Emesis and cardiorespiratory events were equally distributed for the moldable positioner and cranial cup devices in study group 2 . At discharge , more infants in study group 1 ( 46 % , n = 16 ) exhibited abnormal cranial measurements than those in study group 2 ( 19 % , n = 5 ) ( p = .03 ) . Rotating the cranial cup with the moldable positioner provides a feasible , safe , and potentially efficacious therapy for prevention of DP .
rewrite: To assess the feasibility, safety, and efficacy of the cranial cup device among hospitalized infants at risk for deformational plagiocephaly (DP). A multisite, stratified, randomized single-blinded study was conducted. Neonatal intensive care units (NICUs) from three urban and one suburban hospital participated. Subjects comprised 62 infants with stays of 14 days. Nurses for study group 1 used the moldable positioner. In study group 2, nurses alternated between the moldable positioner and cranial cup devices, targeting 12 hours/day of cup use. Both groups received routine repositioning. Outcomes measured were hours of device use (feasibility), cardiorespiratory and emesis events (safety), and cranial measurements at discharge (efficacy), assessed by one of four licensed orthotists blinded to the study. A total of 35 infants were assigned to study group 1 (moldable positioner) and 27 to study group 2 (moldable positioner and cranial cup). Median daily cranial cup use was 10.7 hours (range 4.5–15.3). Emesis and cardiorespiratory events were similarly distributed for both devices in study group 2. At discharge, more infants in study group 1 (46%, n = 16) showed abnormal cranial measurements compared to study group 2 (19%, n = 5) (p = .03). Alternating the cranial cup with the moldable positioner offers a feasible, safe, and potentially effective therapy for DP prevention.

text: Sequential bacillus Calmette-Guerin ( BCG ) and electromotive mitomycin ( sequential therapy ) have been shown in a randomized prospective trial to be superior to therapy with BCG alone in patients with high-risk non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer . The objective of the current study was to compare the costs and benefits of these 2 treatment strategies by performing a 5-year and 10-year cost-effectiveness study . A Markov model was developed to estimate the incremental cost-effectiveness ratio over a 5-year and 10-year period . Estimates of disease progression , death , and treatment efficacy were obtained from what to the authors ' knowledge is the only randomized trial comparing the 2 therapies . Costs included : 1 ) medical costs ( physician fees ) ; 2 ) drug costs ( preparation and instillation ) ; and 3 ) hospital costs ( procedure fees , admission fees , and tests and procedures done during surveillance ) . Patients were allowed a second course of induction therapy . Sequential therapy was found to be associated with a higher initial material cost for induction and maintenance . The average effectiveness for the patients treated with therapy with BCG alone was 4.39 years with a mean cost of $ 9236 ( 95 % confidence interval , $ 9118 - $ 9345 ) per patient . The sequential group resulted in an average effectiveness of 4.65 years , with a mean cost of $ 16,468 ( 95 % confidence interval , $ 16,371 - $ 16,527 ) . The 5-year incremental cost-effectiveness ratio of sequential versus BCG-alone therapy was $ 27,815 per life-year gained . The corresponding figure over a 10-year period was $ 8618 per life-year gained . The results of the current study suggest that sequential therapy is a cost-effective treatment for patients with high-risk non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer .
rewrite: A randomized prospective trial demonstrated that sequential bacillus Calmette-Guerin (BCG) and electromotive mitomycin (sequential therapy) offers superior outcomes compared to BCG alone for high-risk non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer. This study aimed to evaluate the costs and benefits of these two strategies through 5-year and 10-year cost-effectiveness analyses. A Markov model was constructed to calculate the incremental cost-effectiveness ratio over both timeframes. Data on disease progression, mortality, and treatment efficacy were sourced from what the authors believe is the sole randomized trial comparing the two approaches. Costs encompassed: 1) medical expenses (physician fees); 2) drug costs (preparation and administration); and 3) hospital charges (procedure fees, admission fees, and surveillance tests and procedures). Patients could receive a second induction therapy course. Sequential therapy incurred higher initial material costs for induction and maintenance. For BCG-alone therapy, average effectiveness was 4.39 years at a mean cost of $9,236 per patient (95% CI: $9,118–$9,345). The sequential group achieved an average effectiveness of 4.65 years, with a mean cost of $16,468 (95% CI: $16,371–$16,527). The 5-year incremental cost-effectiveness ratio for sequential versus BCG-alone therapy was $27,815 per life-year gained, decreasing to $8,618 per life-year gained over 10 years. These findings indicate that sequential therapy is a cost-effective option for patients with high-risk non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer.

text: To observe the clinical efficacy of transcutaneous acupoint electrical stimulation ( TAES ) combined intravenous injection and/or Neiguan ( P6 ) injection with droperidol in preventing and treating post-operative nausea and vomiting ( PONV ) after thyroid tumor surgery . Recruited were 120 female patients who underwent selective thyroid tumor surgery were randomly assigned to the control group , the TAES group , the IV group ( intravenous injection of droperidol ) , and the P6 group [ Neiguan point ( P6 ) injection of droperidol ] , respectively , 30 cases in each group . Thirty min before anesthesia induction , 2 mL 0.9 % normal saline injection was intravenously injected to those in the control group . Patients in the TAES group received TEAS at bilateral P6 points . 2.5 mg ( 1 mL ) droperidol added in 1 mL 0.9 normal saline was intravenously injected to those in the IV group and injected at bilateral P6 points of those in the P6 group . The occurrence and severity of PONV were observed within 0 - 6 h and within 6 - 24 h after operation in each group . Compared with the control group , the incidence and the severity of PONV within 0 - 6 h and within 6 - 24 h after thyroid surgery were significantly reduced in the three treatment groups ( P < 0.05 ) . There was no statistical difference in the incidence or the severity of PONV among the TAES , IV and P6 groups ( P > 0.05 ) . TEAS at P6 could dramatically reduce the occurrence and the severity of PONV after thyroid tumor surgery . Besides , it got equivalent effect to that by intravenous injecting droperidol or by injecting droperidol at P6 .
rewrite: This study evaluated the clinical efficacy of transcutaneous acupoint electrical stimulation (TAES) combined with intravenous or Neiguan (P6) point injection of droperidol for preventing post-operative nausea and vomiting (PONV) after thyroid tumor surgery. One hundred twenty female patients undergoing elective thyroid tumor surgery were randomly divided into four groups: control, TAES, IV (intravenous droperidol), and P6 (Neiguan point injection of droperidol), with 30 patients per group. Thirty minutes before anesthesia induction, the control group received 2 mL of 0.9% normal saline intravenously. The TAES group received TEAS at bilateral P6 points. The IV group received 2.5 mg (1 mL) droperidol diluted in 1 mL 0.9% saline intravenously, while the P6 group received the same dose injected at bilateral P6 points. PONV occurrence and severity were recorded at 0–6 h and 6–24 h post-operation. Compared to the control group, all three treatment groups showed significantly reduced PONV incidence and severity in both time periods (P < 0.05). No significant differences in PONV incidence or severity were observed among the TAES, IV, and P6 groups (P > 0.05). TEAS at P6 significantly decreased the occurrence and severity of PONV following thyroid tumor surgery and demonstrated comparable effectiveness to intravenous or P6 point injection of droperidol.

text: 1 ) To investigate the impact of acetazolamide , a drug commonly prescribed for altitude sickness , on cortical oscillations in patients with obstructive sleep apnea syndrome ( OSAS ) . 2 ) To examine alterations in the sleep EEG after short-term discontinuation of continuous positive airway pressure ( CPAP ) therapy . Data from two double-blind , placebo-controlled randomized cross-over design studies were analyzed . Polysomnographic recordings in sleep laboratory at 490 m and at moderate altitudes in the Swiss Alps : 1630 or 1860 m and 2590 m. Study 1 : 39 OSAS patients . Study 2 : 41 OSAS patients . Study 1 : OSAS patients withdrawn from treatment with CPAP . Study 2 : OSAS patients treated with autoCPAP . Treatment with acetazolamide ( 500-750 mg ) or placebo at moderate altitudes . An evening dose of 500 mg acetazolamide reduced slow-wave activity ( SWA ; approximately 10 % ) and increased spindle activity ( approximately 10 % ) during non-REM sleep . In addition , alpha activity during wake after lights out was increased . An evening dose of 250 mg did not affect these cortical oscillations . Discontinuation of CPAP therapy revealed a reduction in SWA ( 5-10 % ) and increase in beta activity ( approximately 25 % ) . The higher evening dose of 500 mg acetazolamide showed the `` spectral fingerprint '' of Benzodiazepines , while 250 mg acetazolamide had no impact on cortical oscillations . However , both doses had beneficial effects on oxygen saturation and sleep quality .
rewrite: 1) To assess the effects of acetazolamide, a medication often used for altitude sickness, on cortical oscillations in individuals with obstructive sleep apnea syndrome (OSAS). 2) To evaluate changes in the sleep EEG following brief cessation of continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) treatment. Analyses were based on two double-blind, placebo-controlled randomized cross-over trials. Polysomnographic data were collected in a sleep lab at 490 m and at moderate elevations in the Swiss Alps: 1630 or 1860 m and 2590 m. Study 1 included 39 OSAS patients. Study 2 involved 41 OSAS patients. Study 1: OSAS patients taken off CPAP therapy. Study 2: OSAS patients using autoCPAP. Administration of acetazolamide (500-750 mg) or placebo at moderate altitudes. An evening dose of 500 mg acetazolamide decreased slow-wave activity (SWA; about 10%) and raised spindle activity (around 10%) during non-REM sleep. Additionally, alpha activity during wakefulness after lights out was elevated. A 250 mg evening dose did not alter these cortical oscillations. Stopping CPAP therapy led to a decrease in SWA (5-10%) and an increase in beta activity (approximately 25%). The higher 500 mg evening dose of acetazolamide produced a "spectral fingerprint" similar to Benzodiazepines, whereas 250 mg acetazolamide had no effect on cortical oscillations. Nevertheless, both doses improved oxygen saturation and sleep quality.

text: Fresh red cells may improve outcomes in critically ill patients by enhancing oxygen delivery while minimizing the risks of toxic effects from cellular changes and the accumulation of bioactive materials in blood components during prolonged storage . In this multicenter , randomized , blinded trial , we assigned critically ill adults to receive either red cells that had been stored for less than 8 days or standard-issue red cells ( the oldest compatible units available in the blood bank ) . The primary outcome measure was 90-day mortality . Between March 2009 and May 2014 , at 64 centers in Canada and Europe , 1211 patients were assigned to receive fresh red cells ( fresh-blood group ) and 1219 patients were assigned to receive standard-issue red cells ( standard-blood group ) . Red cells were stored a mean ( SD ) of 6.14.9 days in the fresh-blood group as compared with 22.08.4 days in the standard-blood group ( P < 0.001 ) . At 90 days , 448 patients ( 37.0 % ) in the fresh-blood group and 430 patients ( 35.3 % ) in the standard-blood group had died ( absolute risk difference , 1.7 percentage points ; 95 % confidence interval [ CI ] , -2.1 to 5.5 ) . In the survival analysis , the hazard ratio for death in the fresh-blood group , as compared with the standard-blood group , was 1.1 ( 95 % CI , 0.9 to 1.2 ; P = 0.38 ) . There were no significant between-group differences in any of the secondary outcomes ( major illnesses ; duration of respiratory , hemodynamic , or renal support ; length of stay in the hospital ; and transfusion reactions ) or in the subgroup analyses . Transfusion of fresh red cells , as compared with standard-issue red cells , did not decrease the 90-day mortality among critically ill adults . ( Funded by the Canadian Institutes of Health Research and others ; Current Controlled Trials number , ISRCTN44878718 . )
rewrite: Fresh red blood cells could potentially benefit critically ill patients by boosting oxygen delivery and reducing risks from cellular degradation and bioactive substance accumulation in longer-stored blood. In this multicenter, randomized, blinded study, critically ill adults were allocated to receive either red cells stored for under 8 days or standard-issue units (the oldest compatible ones from the blood bank). The primary endpoint was 90-day mortality. From March 2009 to May 2014, across 64 centers in Canada and Europe, 1211 patients were assigned to the fresh-blood group and 1219 to the standard-blood group. Mean storage times were 6.1±4.9 days for fresh blood versus 22.0±8.4 days for standard blood (P<0.001). By 90 days, 448 patients (37.0%) in the fresh group and 430 (35.3%) in the standard group had died (absolute risk difference, 1.7 percentage points; 95% CI, -2.1 to 5.5). Survival analysis showed a hazard ratio for death of 1.1 (95% CI, 0.9 to 1.2; P=0.38) for fresh versus standard blood. No significant differences were observed in secondary outcomes (major illnesses; duration of respiratory, hemodynamic, or renal support; hospital length of stay; transfusion reactions) or subgroup analyses. Transfusing fresh red cells did not lower 90-day mortality in critically ill adults compared to standard-issue cells. (Funded by the Canadian Institutes of Health Research et al.; Current Controlled Trials number, ISRCTN44878718.)

text: Detoxification with psychosocial counseling remains a standard opioid-use disorder treatment practice but is associated with poor outcomes . This study tested the efficacy of a newly developed psychosocial intervention , Community Reinforcement Approach and Family Training for Treatment Retention ( CRAFT-T ) , relative to psychosocial treatment as usual ( TAU ) , for improving treatment outcomes . A randomized , 14-week trial with follow-up visits at 6 and 9 months post-randomization conducted at two substance use disorder ( SUD ) treatment programs . Opioid-dependent adults ( i.e. , identified patient - IP ) enrolled in a residential buprenorphine-detoxification program and their identified concerned significant other ( CSO ) was randomized to CRAFT-T ( n = 28 dyads ) or TAU ( n = 24 dyads ) . CRAFT-T consisted of two sessions with the IP and CSO together and 10 with the CSO alone , over 14 weeks . TAU for the CSOs was primarily educational and referral to self-help . All IPs received treatment as usually provided by the SUD program in which they were enrolled . The primary outcome was time to first IP drop from treatment lasting 30 days or more . Opioid and other drug use were key secondary outcomes . CRAFT-T resulted in a moderate but non-significant effect on treatment retention ( p = 0.058 , hazard ratio = 0.57 ) . When the CSO was parental family , CRAFT-T had a large and significant effect on treatment retention ( p < 0.01 , hazard ratio = .040 ) . CRAFT-T had a significant positive effect on IP opioid and other drug use ( p < 0.0001 ) . CRAFT-T is a promising treatment for opioid use disorder but replication is needed to confirm these results .
rewrite: Psychosocial counseling during detoxification continues to be a standard practice for opioid-use disorder, yet it is linked to unfavorable outcomes. This research evaluated the effectiveness of a novel psychosocial intervention, the Community Reinforcement Approach and Family Training for Treatment Retention (CRAFT-T), compared to usual psychosocial care (TAU), in enhancing treatment results. A randomized, 14-week trial with follow-ups at 6 and 9 months post-randomization was carried out at two substance use disorder (SUD) treatment facilities. Opioid-dependent adults (the identified patient, IP) in a residential buprenorphine-detoxification program and their concerned significant other (CSO) were assigned to CRAFT-T (28 dyads) or TAU (24 dyads). CRAFT-T included two joint sessions with the IP and CSO and 10 sessions with the CSO alone over 14 weeks. TAU for CSOs mainly involved education and self-help referrals. All IPs received standard treatment from their SUD program. The main outcome measured was time to first IP treatment dropout lasting 30 days or longer, with opioid and other drug use as key secondary outcomes. CRAFT-T showed a moderate, non-significant effect on treatment retention (p = 0.058, hazard ratio = 0.57). When the CSO was a parent, CRAFT-T had a large, significant impact on retention (p < 0.01, hazard ratio = 0.40). CRAFT-T also significantly reduced IP opioid and other drug use (p < 0.0001). CRAFT-T appears to be a promising approach for opioid use disorder, though further replication is required to verify these findings.

text: Twenty vertically HIV-infected children , 6-16 years of age , with stable viral load control and CD4 + values above 400 cells/mm ( 3 ) . Ten subjects continued their ongoing antiretroviral treatment ( ART , Group A ) and 10 were immunized with a HIV-DNA vaccine in addition to their previous therapy ( ART and vaccine , Group B ) . The genetic vaccine represented HIV-1 subtypes A , B and C , encoded Env , Rev , Gag and RT and had no additional adjuvant . Immunizations took place at weeks 0 , 4 and 12 , with a boosting dose at week 36 . Monitoring was performed until week 60 and extended to week 96 . Safety data showed good tolerance of the vaccine . Adherence to ART remained high and persistent during the study and did not differ significantly between controls and vaccinees . Neither group experienced either virological failure or a decline of CD4 + counts from baseline . Higher HIV-specific cellular immune responses were noted transiently to Gag but not to other components of the vaccine . Lymphoproliferative responses to a virion antigen HIV-1 MN were higher in the vaccinees than in the controls ( p = 0.047 ) , whereas differences in reactivity to clade-specific Gag p24 , RT or Env did not reach significance . Compared to baseline , the percentage of HIV-specific CD8 + lymphocytes releasing perforin in the Group B was higher after the vaccination schedule had been completed ( p = 0.031 ) . No increased CD8 + perforin levels were observed in control Group A. The present study demonstrates the feasibility , safety and moderate immunogenicity of genetic vaccination in vertically HIV-infected children , paving the way for amplified immunotherapeutic approaches in the pediatric population . clinicaltrialsregister.eu _ 2007-002359-18IT .
rewrite: Twenty children with vertical HIV infection, aged 6–16 years, maintained stable viral loads and CD4+ counts exceeding 400 cells/mm³. text: The purpose of this study was to evaluate the effectiveness of mandibular advancement devices ( MADs ) for treatment of obstructive sleep apnea syndrome ( OSAS ) compared with the results obtained with a placebo device in accordance with the following indicators : apnea hypopnea index ( AHI ) per hour of sleep , apnea index ( AI ) per hour of sleep , mean oxyhemoglobin saturation , sleep efficiency , and percentage of rapid eye movement ( REM ) sleep . This is a controlled , prospective longitudinal study with a follow-up time of 10.5 months . Nineteen patients ( 8 females and 11 males ) with mean age 48.6 years ( SD 9.6 ) were selected for the study . The sample was randomized in terms of device use , and the evaluation design was double blind . A total of 57 polysomnography tests were studied ( at baseline , after the use of a MAD , and after the use of placebo ) . The following variables were assessed : AHI , AI , mean oxyhemoglobin saturation , percentage of REM sleep , and sleep efficiency . Wilcoxon and Mann-Whitney tests were used for evaluating data ( p < 0.05 ) . Reductions from 16.3 to 11.7 in AHI and from 5.7 to 3.8 in AI were observed after MAD use . During the use of placebo , AHI increased from 16.3 to 19.6 , and AI from 5.7 to 7.5 . The other indexes showed no statistically significant differences . Treatment with oral appliances , i.e. , MADs , can be an effective alternative for mild and medium-to-moderate OSAS , but requires strict monitoring due to differences in individual response to this therapy .
rewrite: This study aimed to assess the efficacy of mandibular advancement devices (MADs) in treating obstructive sleep apnea syndrome (OSAS) versus a placebo device, using these metrics: apnea hypopnea index (AHI) per sleep hour, apnea index (AI) per sleep hour, mean oxyhemoglobin saturation, sleep efficiency, and rapid eye movement (REM) sleep percentage. It is a controlled, prospective longitudinal investigation with a 10.5-month follow-up. Nineteen participants (8 women, 11 men), averaging 48.6 years old (SD 9.6), were enrolled. The sample was randomized for device application, and the assessment design was double-blind. Fifty-seven polysomnography tests were analyzed (at baseline, post-MAD use, and post-placebo use). The evaluated variables included AHI, AI, mean oxyhemoglobin saturation, REM sleep percentage, and sleep efficiency. Data were analyzed using Wilcoxon and Mann-Whitney tests (p < 0.05). Following MAD use, AHI decreased from 16.3 to 11.7 and AI from 5.7 to 3.8. With placebo, AHI rose from 16.3 to 19.6 and AI from 5.7 to 7.5. Other indices showed no statistically significant changes. Oral appliance therapy, specifically MADs, can serve as an effective option for mild to moderate OSAS, though strict monitoring is necessary due to variability in individual therapeutic responses.

text: No highly effective interventions to prevent delirium have been identified . To examine whether ramelteon , a melatonin agonist , is effective for the prevention of delirium . A multicenter , rater-blinded , randomized placebo-controlled trial was performed in intensive care units and regular acute wards of 4 university hospitals and 1 general hospital . Eligible patients were 65 to 89 years old , newly admitted due to serious medical problems , and able to take medicine orally . Patients were excluded from the study if they had an expected stay or life expectancy of less than 48 hours . Sixty-seven patients were randomly assigned using the sealed envelope method to receive ramelteon ( 8 mg/d ; 33 patients ) or placebo ( 34 patients ) every night for 7 days . Incidence of delirium , as defined by the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders ( Fourth Edition ) . Ramelteon was associated with a lower risk of delirium ( 3 % vs 32 % ; P = .003 ) , with a relative risk of 0.09 ( 95 % CI , 0.01-0 .69 ) . Even after risk factors were controlled for , ramelteon was still associated with a lower incidence of delirium ( P = .01 ; odds ratio , 0.07 [ 95 % CI , 0.008-0 .54 ] ) . The Kaplan-Meier estimates of time to development of delirium were 6.94 ( 95 % CI , 6.82-7 .06 ) days for ramelteon and 5.74 ( 5.05-6 .42 ) days for placebo . Comparison by log-rank test showed that the frequency of delirium was significantly lower in patients taking ramelteon than in those taking placebo ( ( 2 ) = 9.83 ; P = .002 ) . Ramelteon administered nightly to elderly patients admitted for acute care may provide protection against delirium . This finding supports a possible pathogenic role of melatonin neurotransmission in delirium . University Hospital Medical Information Network Clinical Trials Registry Identifier : UMIN000005591 .
rewrite: No highly effective interventions for preventing delirium have been established. This study investigated whether ramelteon, a melatonin agonist, is effective in preventing delirium. A multicenter, rater-blinded, randomized placebo-controlled trial was conducted in intensive care units and acute wards across four university hospitals and one general hospital. Delirium incidence was assessed using DSM-IV criteria. Ramelteon was linked to a reduced risk of delirium (3% vs. 32%; P = .003), with a relative risk of 0.09 (95% CI, 0.01–0.69).
