text: To evaluate the effectiveness of specialized physiotherapy methods measured by the BODE index in patients with COPD during hospitalization . The study was conducted on a group of 30 patients diagnosed with COPD , all under treatment at the clinical hospital in Wroclaw due to the exacerbation of their symptoms . All patients were undergoing standard pharmacological treatment along with basic physiotherapy . The subjects of the study were randomly divided between an experimental group of 20 persons and a control group of 10 persons . Patients in the experimental group underwent a series of 6 additional massage treatments performed over a period of a few days , aimed at reshaping the following muscles : the sterno-cleidomastoid , pectoralis major , pectoralis minor , trapezius , levator scapulae , rhomboids and serratus anterior . Each massage lasted for 30 minutes and consisted of stroking , grinding , vibration and kneading techniques . Before and after therapy the patients were assessed based on the BODE index . First , the patient 's BMI was calculated ( B ) . Airflow obstruction ( O ) was determined by the percentage value of FEV1 while the MRC scale was used to evaluate a patient 's dyspnea ( D ) . Exercise capacity ( E ) was measured by the distance a patient could cover in a 6-minute walk test . Each variable of the BODE index was ranked on a scale from 0 to 3 points except the BMI , for which was given either 0 or 1 point . Analysis of the results showed a significant improvement of the BODE index in the experimental group while in the control group this ratio changed slightly . The FEV1 and MRC parameters changed significantly only in the experimental group . After a week of therapy the BODE index improved in both groups , but in the experimental group there was a significantly higher difference . In the experimental group all BODE components except BMI improved highly significantly , whereas in the control group only exercise capacity was significantly improved .
rewrite: This study assessed the effectiveness of specialized physiotherapy, measured by the BODE index, in hospitalized COPD patients. Thirty patients with COPD, all hospitalized in Wroclaw for symptom exacerbation, participated. All received standard pharmacological treatment and basic physiotherapy. Participants were randomly assigned to an experimental group (20 persons) or a control group (10 persons). The experimental group received six additional massage sessions over several days, targeting the sternocleidomastoid, pectoralis major, pectoralis minor, trapezius, levator scapulae, rhomboids, and serratus anterior muscles. Each 30-minute session included stroking, grinding, vibration, and kneading techniques. Patients were evaluated using the BODE index before and after therapy. The index components were: BMI (B), airflow obstruction (O) via FEV1 percentage, dyspnea (D) via the MRC scale, and exercise capacity (E) via the 6-minute walk distance. Each variable was scored from 0 to 3 points, except BMI, scored as 0 or 1. Results indicated a significant BODE index improvement in the experimental group, with only a slight change in the control group. FEV1 and MRC parameters improved significantly only in the experimental group. After one week, the BODE index improved in both groups, but the improvement was significantly greater in the experimental group. In the experimental group, all BODE components except BMI improved highly significantly, while in the control group, only exercise capacity showed significant improvement.

text: The aim of the present randomized study was to evaluate the efficacy of intermaxillary fixation screw ( IMFS ) versus eyelet interdental wiring for intermaxillary fixation ( IMF ) in minimally displaced mandibular fractures . A total of 50 patients with a minimally displaced mandibular fracture were enrolled , with 25 patients randomly selected for each group . In group I ( study group , n = 25 ) , the patients were treated using IMFS , and in group II ( control group , n = 25 ) , they received eyelet interdental wiring . Both techniques were assessed for the following parameters : time required for placement and removal of each type of IMF technique , time required for placement of IMF wires , postoperative occlusion , stability of the IMF wire , local anesthesia requirement during removal of each fixation type , oral hygiene status , glove perforation rate , and complications associated with both techniques . The collected data were analyzed using Student 's unpaired t test or 2 test . P < .05 was considered significant and the Statistical Package for Social Sciences software , version 10 , was used for analysis . The average time required for placement in groups I and II was 17.56 and 35.08 minutes , respectively ( P = .000 ) . The time required for placement of the IMF wire in group I was 2.1 minutes and in group II was 6 minutes . The oral hygiene status was assessed , and the mean plaque index score for groups I and II was 1.44 and 2.12 , respectively ( P = .00 ) . The glove perforation rate was much less in group I than in group II . Finally , the most common complication in both groups was mucosal growth . The results established the supremacy of IMFS compared with eyelet interdental wiring . Thus , we have concluded that IMFS , in the present scenario , is a safe and time-saving technique . IMFS is a cost-effective , straightforward , and viable alternative to cumbersome eyelet interdental and other wiring techniques for providing IMF , with satisfactory occlusion during closed reduction or intraoperative open reduction internal fixation of fractures . In addition , oral hygiene can be maintained , and the glove perforation rate was very low using IMFS . The relatively small sample size and limited follow-up period were the study limitations .
rewrite:
This randomized study assessed the efficacy of intermaxillary fixation screws (IMFS) versus eyelet interdental wiring for intermaxillary fixation (IMF) in minimally displaced mandibular fractures. Fifty patients with such fractures were enrolled, randomly assigned to two groups of 25 each. Group I (study group) received IMFS, while Group II (control group) underwent eyelet interdental wiring. Both methods were evaluated based on placement and removal times, time for IMF wire placement, postoperative occlusion, IMF stability, local anesthesia needs during removal, oral hygiene, glove perforation rates, and complications. Data analysis employed Student’s unpaired t-test or chi-square test, with significance set at P < .05 using SPSS version 10.

Average placement times were 17.56 minutes for Group I and 35.08 minutes for Group II (P = .000). IMF wire placement took 2.1 minutes in Group I and 6 minutes in Group II. Oral hygiene, measured by plaque index, showed mean scores of 1.44 for Group I and 2.12 for Group II (P = .00). Glove perforation rates were significantly lower in Group I. The most frequent complication in both groups was mucosal growth.

Results demonstrated the superiority of IMFS over eyelet interdental wiring. IMFS proved to be a safe, time-efficient, cost-effective, and straightforward alternative for IMF, ensuring satisfactory occlusion during closed reduction or intraoperative open reduction internal fixation. It also facilitated better oral hygiene maintenance and reduced glove perforation. Study limitations included a relatively small sample size and short follow-up period.

text: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of intravitreal bevacizumab ( IVB ) in eyes with neovascular glaucoma ( NVG ) undergoing Ahmed glaucoma valve ( AGV ) implantation . This was a multicentre , prospective , randomized clinical trial that enrolled 40 patients with uncontrolled neovascular glaucoma that had undergone panretinal photocoagulation and required glaucoma drainage device implantation . Patients were randomized to receive IVB ( 1.25 mg ) or not during Ahmed valve implant surgery . Injections were administered intra-operatively , and 4 and 8 weeks after surgery . After a mean follow-up of 2.25 0.67 years ( range 1.5-3 years ) , both groups showed a significant decrease in IOP ( p < 0.05 ) . There was no difference in IOP between groups except at the 18-month interval , when IOP in IVB group was significantly lower ( 14.57 1.72 mmHg vs. 18.37 1.06 mmHg - p = 0.0002 ) . There was no difference in survival success rates between groups . At 24 months , there was a trend to patients treated with IVB using less antiglaucoma medications than the control group ( p = 0.0648 ) . Complete regression of rubeosis iridis was significantly more frequent in the IVB group ( 80 % ) than in the control group ( 25 % ) ( p = 0.0015 ) . Intravitreal bevacizumab may lead to regression of new vessels both in the iris and in the anterior chamber angle in patients with neovascular glaucoma undergoing Ahmed glaucoma valve implantation . There is a trend to slightly lower IOPs and number of medications with IVB use during AGV implantation for neovascular glaucoma .

text: To establish the prevalence of anthelmintic resistance in ovine gastrointestinal nematodes in southern Queensland . An observational parasitological study using the faecal egg count reduction test . Sheep farms ( n = 20 ) enrolled in this study met the twin criteria of using worm testing for drench decisions and having concerns about anthelmintic efficacy . On each farm , 105 sheep were randomly allocated to one of six treatment groups or an untreated control group . Faecal samples were collected on day 0 and days 10-14 for worm egg counts and larval differentiation . Single - and multi-combination anthelmintics , persistent and non-persistent , oral liquid or capsule , pour-on and injectable formulations were tested . Monepantel was not tested . Farmers also responded to a questionnaire on drenching practices . Haemonchus contortus was the predominant species . Efficacy < 95 % was recorded on 85 % of farms for one or more anthelmintics and on 10 % of farms for six anthelmintics . No resistance was identified on three farms . The 4-way combination product was efficacious ( n = 4 farms ) . Napthalophos resistance was detected on one farm only . Resistance to levamisole ( 42 % of farms ) , moxidectin injection ( 50 % of farms ) and the closantel/abamectin combination ( 67 % of farms ) was identified . Moxidectin oral was efficacious against Trichostrongylus colubriformis , which was predominant on only one farm . Of the farms tested , 55 % ran meat breeds , 60 % dosed more than the recommended dose rate and 70 % always , mostly or when possible practised a ` drench and move ' strategy . This level of anthelmintic resistance in southern Queensland will severely compromise worm control and force increased use of monepantel .
rewrite: To determine the prevalence of anthelmintic resistance in gastrointestinal nematodes of sheep in southern Queensland, an observational parasitological study employing the faecal egg count reduction test was conducted. Twenty sheep farms were selected based on their use of worm testing for drench decisions and concerns regarding anthelmintic efficacy. On each farm, 105 sheep were randomly assigned to one of six treatment groups or an untreated control. Faecal samples were taken on day 0 and between days 10–14 for egg counts and larval differentiation. Various anthelmintics were evaluated, including single and multi-combination products, persistent and non-persistent formulations, oral liquids or capsules, pour-ons, and injectables, though monepantel was excluded. Farmers completed a questionnaire on drenching practices. Haemonchus contortus was the dominant species. Efficacy below 95% was observed on 85% of farms for at least one anthelmintic and on 10% of farms for six anthelmintics. Three farms showed no resistance. The 4-way combination product was effective (tested on four farms). Napthalophos resistance was found on only one farm. Resistance to levamisole (42% of farms), moxidectin injection (50% of farms), and the closantel/abamectin combination (67% of farms) was detected. Oral moxidectin was effective against Trichostrongylus colubriformis, which was predominant on just one farm. Among the farms, 55% raised meat breeds, 60% administered doses above the recommended rate, and 70% consistently or often used a 'drench and move' strategy. This extent of anthelmintic resistance in southern Queensland will critically undermine worm control and necessitate greater reliance on monepantel.

text: Despite all the technological advances in orthodontics , orthodontic treatment still seems to involve some degree of discomfort and/or pain . Pain control during orthodontic therapy is of great concern to both orthodontists and patients . However , there has been limited research into controlling such pain . The purpose of this work was to assess patient-perceived pain following fixed orthodontic treatment and to evaluate the comparative analgesic efficacy of non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs for controlling pain . A total of 45patients about to undergo fixed appliance orthodontic treatment were enrolled in this double-blind prospective study . Patients were evenly and randomly distributed in a blinded manner to one of three groups as follows : paracetamol/acetaminophen 500mg thrice daily ; placebo in the form of empty capsules ; and etoricoxib 60mg once daily . Drug administration began 1h before initiating the bonding procedure and archwire placement , and given until the day3 . The pain perceived was recorded by the patients on a linear and graded Visual Analogue Scale at time intervals of 2h after insertion of the appliance ; 6h thereafter and again at nighttime of the same day of the appointment ; 24h later and on the 2nd day at nighttime ; 48h after the appointment and on day3 at nighttime . Our results revealed that moderately intense pain is associated with routine orthodontic treatment , and that the amount of pain individuals perceive varies widely . We observed statistically significant differences in the pain control among the three groups , and that etoricoxib 60mg proved most efficient . Etoricoxib 60mg is highly efficacious for controlling pain during fixed orthodontic appliance therapy .
rewrite: Even with the progress in orthodontic technology, patients often experience some level of discomfort or pain during treatment. Managing this pain is a key concern for both orthodontists and those undergoing care, yet studies on effective pain control remain limited. This study aimed to measure patient-reported pain after fixed orthodontic procedures and compare the pain-relieving effectiveness of non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs. In this double-blind prospective trial, 45 patients scheduled for fixed appliance treatment were included. They were randomly and evenly assigned in a blinded fashion to one of three groups: paracetamol/acetaminophen 500mg three times daily; placebo as empty capsules; or etoricoxib 60mg once daily. Medication started one hour before bonding and archwire placement and continued until day three. Patients recorded their pain using a linear, graded Visual Analogue Scale at intervals: 2 hours after appliance insertion; 6 hours later and that night; 24 hours later and the next night; and 48 hours after the appointment and on the third night. Findings indicated that routine orthodontic treatment involves moderately intense pain, with considerable variation in individual pain perception. Statistically significant differences in pain management were noted among the groups, with etoricoxib 60mg showing the highest efficacy. Etoricoxib 60mg is highly effective for pain control in fixed orthodontic therapy.

text: The use of a video-assisted laryngoscope ( VL ) has been shown to reduce the time to achieve intubation with a double-lumen endobronchial tube ( DLT ) . As the blade of the VL is curved differently to a standard laryngoscope , the DLT must be angled into a hockey stick shape to fit properly . We conducted a study to establish which direction of angulation was best to facilitate correct positioning of the DLT when using a VL . We enrolled patients scheduled for thoracic surgery who required intubation with a DLT . They were prospectively randomized into one of two groups : those intubated with a DLT angled to conceal the tracheal orifice ( the tracheal orifice-covered , TOC ) group or the tracheal orifice-exposed ( TOE ) group . The composite primary outcome measures were time taken to intubate and the frequency of first-time success . The time taken to intubate was divided into : T1 , the time from mouth opening to visualization of the vocal cords with the VL ; and T2 , the time taken to advance the DLT through the cords until its tip lay within the trachea and three carbon dioxide waveforms had been detected by capnography . The hemodynamic responses to intubation and intubation-related adverse events were also recorded . Sixty-six patients completed the study , with 33 in each group . Total intubation time was significantly shorter in the TOC group ( mean 30.6 standard deviation 2.7 seconds versus 38.73.3 seconds , p < 0.0001 ) . T2 was also significantly shorter in the TOC group than the TOE group ( 27.22.5 seconds versus 34.93.0 seconds , p < 0.0001 ) . The severity of hoarseness on the first postoperative day and sore throat on the fourth postoperative day were significantly lower in the TOC group than the TOE group ( p = 0.02 and < 0.0001 , respectively ) . The hemodynamic responses to intubation were broadly similar between the groups . When placing a left-sided DLT using a VL , angling the bronchial lumen to a hockey stick shape that conceals the tracheal lumen saves time and ameliorates the severity of post-intubation complications . ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier : NCT01605591 .
rewrite: Video-assisted laryngoscopy (VL) shortens the time needed for double-lumen endobronchial tube (DLT) intubation. Because the VL blade has a distinct curvature compared to standard laryngoscopes, the DLT must be bent into a hockey-stick shape for proper placement. This study aimed to determine which angulation direction best facilitates correct DLT positioning with a VL. We included patients undergoing thoracic surgery who required DLT intubation. Participants were prospectively randomized into two groups: the tracheal orifice-covered (TOC) group, where the DLT was angled to hide the tracheal orifice, or the tracheal orifice-exposed (TOE) group. The primary outcomes were intubation duration and first-attempt success rate. Intubation time was split into T1 (mouth opening to vocal cord visualization with VL) and T2 (advancing the DLT through the cords until tracheal placement with three capnography waveforms). Hemodynamic responses and adverse events were also noted. Sixty-six patients finished the study, with 33 per group. Total intubation time was notably shorter in the TOC group (mean 30.6 ± 2.7 seconds vs. 38.7 ± 3.3 seconds, p < 0.0001). T2 was also significantly reduced in the TOC group compared to the TOE group (27.2 ± 2.5 seconds vs. 34.9 ± 3.0 seconds, p < 0.0001). Hoarseness severity on postoperative day one and sore throat on day four were lower in the TOC group (p = 0.02 and < 0.0001, respectively). Hemodynamic responses were largely similar between groups. When inserting a left-sided DLT using a VL, angling the bronchial lumen into a hockey-stick shape that covers the tracheal lumen reduces time and lessens post-intubation complication severity. ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT01605591.

text: Episodes of patient deterioration on hospital units are expected to increasingly contribute to morbidity and healthcare costs . To determine if real-time alerts sent to the rapid response team ( RRT ) improved patient care . Randomized , controlled trial . Eight medicine units ( Barnes-Jewish Hospital ) . Five hundred seventy-one patients . Real-time alerts generated by a validated deterioration algorithm were sent real-time to the RRT ( intervention ) or hidden ( control ) . Intensive care unit ( ICU ) transfer , hospital mortality , hospital duration . ICU transfer ( 17.8 % vs 18.2 % ; odds ratio : 0.972 ; 95 % confidence interval [ CI ] : 0.635-1 .490 ) and hospital mortality ( 7.3 % vs 7.7 % ; odds ratio : 0.947 ; 95 % CI : 0.509-1 .764 ) were similar for the intervention and control groups . The number of patients requiring transfer to a nursing home or long-term acute care hospital was similar for patients in the intervention and control groups ( 26.9 % vs 26.3 % ; odds ratio : 1.032 ; 95 % CI : 0.712-1 .495 ) . Hospital duration ( 8.49.5 days vs 9.411.1 days ; P = 0.038 ) was statistically shorter for the intervention group . The number of RRT calls initiated by the primary care team was similar for the intervention and control groups ( 19.9 % vs 16.5 % ; odds ratio : 1.260 ; 95 % CI : 0.823-1 .931 ) . Real-time alerts sent to the RRT did not reduce ICU transfers , hospital mortality , or the need for subsequent long term care . However , hospital length of stay was modestly reduced .
rewrite: Patient deterioration events in hospital settings are anticipated to increasingly impact morbidity and healthcare expenses. This study assessed whether real-time notifications to the rapid response team (RRT) enhanced patient outcomes. A randomized, controlled trial was conducted across eight medical units at Barnes-Jewish Hospital, involving 571 patients. Real-time alerts from a validated deterioration algorithm were either sent to the RRT (intervention) or concealed (control). Outcomes measured included ICU transfer, hospital mortality, and length of stay. ICU transfer rates (17.8% vs. 18.2%; odds ratio: 0.972; 95% CI: 0.635–1.490) and hospital mortality (7.3% vs. 7.7%; odds ratio: 0.947; 95% CI: 0.509–1.764) did not differ significantly between intervention and control groups. Similarly, transfers to nursing homes or long-term acute care hospitals were comparable (26.9% vs. 26.3%; odds ratio: 1.032; 95% CI: 0.712–1.495). Hospital stay was statistically shorter for the intervention group (8.49.5 days vs. 9.411.1 days; P = 0.038). RRT calls initiated by the primary care team were also similar between groups (19.9% vs. 16.5%; odds ratio: 1.260; 95% CI: 0.823–1.931). Real-time alerts to the RRT did not decrease ICU transfers, hospital mortality, or long-term care needs, but they modestly reduced hospital length of stay.

text: Caudal block ( CB ) has some disadvantages , one of which is its short duration of action after a single injection . For hypospadias repair , pudendal nerve block ( PNB ) might be a suitable alternative since it has been successfully used for analgesia for circumcision . We evaluated PNB compared with CB as measured by total analgesic consumption 24 hours postoperatively . In this prospective , double-blinded study , patients were randomized into 2 groups , either receiving CB or nerve stimulator-guided PNB . In the PNB group , patients were injected with 0.3 mL/kg 0.25 % bupivacaine and 1 g/kg clonidine . In the CB group , patients were injected with 1 mL/kg 0.25 % bupivacaine and 1 g/kg clonidine . Analgesic consumption was assessed during the first 24 hours postoperatively . The `` objective pain scale '' developed by Hannalah and Broadman was used to assess postoperative pain . Eighty patients participated in the study , 40 in each group . The mean age in the PNB group was 3.1 ( 1.1 ) years and in the CB group was 3.2 ( 1.1 ) years . The mean weights in the PNB and CB groups were 15.3 ( 2.8 ) kg and 15.3 ( 2.2 ) kg , respectively . The percentage of patients who received analgesics during the first 24 hours were significantly higher in the CB ( 70 % ) compared with the PNB group ( 20 % , P < 0.0001 ) . The average amount of analgesics consumed per patient within 24 hours postoperatively was higher in the CB group ( paracetamol P < 0.0001 , Tramal P = 0.003 ) . Patients who received PNB had reduced analgesic consumption and pain within the first 24 hours postoperatively compared with CB .
rewrite: Caudal block (CB) has certain drawbacks, including a limited duration of action following a single injection. For hypospadias repair, pudendal nerve block (PNB) may serve as an appropriate alternative, as it has proven effective for analgesia in circumcision. We compared PNB with CB based on total analgesic use within 24 hours after surgery. In this prospective, double-blind trial, patients were randomly assigned to two groups, receiving either CB or nerve stimulator-guided PNB. The PNB group received 0.3 mL/kg of 0.25% bupivacaine and 1 µg/kg clonidine, while the CB group received 1 mL/kg of 0.25% bupivacaine and 1 µg/kg clonidine. Analgesic consumption was evaluated over the initial 24 postoperative hours. Postoperative pain was measured using the "objective pain scale" by Hannalah and Broadman. Eighty patients took part, with 40 in each group. The mean age was 3.1 (1.1) years in the PNB group and 3.2 (1.1) years in the CB group. Mean weights were 15.3 (2.8) kg for PNB and 15.3 (2.2) kg for CB. The proportion of patients requiring analgesics in the first 24 hours was significantly greater in the CB group (70%) than in the PNB group (20%, P < 0.0001). The average analgesic dose per patient within 24 hours postoperatively was higher in the CB group (paracetamol P < 0.0001, Tramal P = 0.003). Patients undergoing PNB showed lower analgesic use and reduced pain in the first 24 hours after surgery compared to those receiving CB.

text: Acetaminophen ( APAP ) by oral or intravenous ( iv ) routes is used for mild to moderate pain but may take time to be effective . When fast relief is required and/or oral or iv routes are not available because of the patient 's condition , the transmucosal route may be an alternative . A new transmucosal/buccal ( b ) pharmaceutical form of APAP dissolved in 50 % wt alcohol is compared with other routes of administration . Two consecutive randomized , crossover , double-blind clinical trials ( CT1 : NCT00982215 and CT2 : NCT01206985 ) included 16 healthy volunteers . CT1 compared the pharmacology of 250 mg bAPAP with 1 g iv APAP . CT2 compared the pharmacodynamics of 125 mg bAPAP with 1 g iv and 125 mg sublingual ( s ) APAP . Mechanical pain thresholds are recorded in response to mechanical stimuli applied on the forearm several times during 120 minutes . The objective is to compare the time of onset of antinociception and the antinociception ( area under the curve ) between the routes of administration with analysis of variance ( significance P < 0.05 ) . bAPAP has a faster time of antinociception onset ( 15 minutes , P < 0.01 ) and greater antinociception at 50 minutes ( P < 0.01 , CT1 ) and 30 minutes ( P < 0.01 , CT2 ) than ivAPAP and sAPAP . All routes are similar after 50 minutes . bAPAP has a faster antinociceptive action in healthy volunteers . This attractive alternative to other routes would be useful in situations where oral or iv routes are not available . This finding must now be confirmed in patients suffering from acute pain of mild and moderate intensity .
rewrite: Acetaminophen (APAP) administered orally or intravenously (iv) is employed for mild to moderate pain, though its effects may be delayed. When rapid relief is needed or oral/iv routes are inaccessible due to the patient's condition, the transmucosal route offers a potential alternative. A novel transmucosal/buccal (b) formulation of APAP, dissolved in 50% wt alcohol, is evaluated against other administration methods. Two sequential randomized, crossover, double-blind clinical trials (CT1: NCT00982215 and CT2: NCT01206985) involved 16 healthy participants. CT1 assessed the pharmacology of 250 mg bAPAP versus 1 g iv APAP. CT2 examined the pharmacodynamics of 125 mg bAPAP compared to 1 g iv and 125 mg sublingual (s) APAP. Mechanical pain thresholds were measured in response to forearm stimuli multiple times over 120 minutes. The aim was to compare the onset time of antinociception and its extent (area under the curve) across routes using analysis of variance (significance P < 0.05). bAPAP demonstrated a quicker onset of antinociception (15 minutes, P < 0.01) and greater antinociception at 50 minutes (P < 0.01, CT1) and 30 minutes (P < 0.01, CT2) than ivAPAP and sAPAP. All routes showed similar effects after 50 minutes. bAPAP acts faster in healthy volunteers. This appealing alternative could be beneficial when oral or iv administration is not feasible. These results require confirmation in patients experiencing mild to moderate acute pain.

text: Sedation using intranasal dexmedetomidine is a convenient and well-tolerated technique . This study evaluated the sedative efficacy of intranasal dexmedetomidine in combination with patient-controlled sedation ( PCS ) for upper gastrointestinal endoscopy . In this double-blind , randomised , controlled trial , 50 patients received either intranasal dexmedetomidine 1.5 g/kg ( dexmedetomidine group ) or intranasal saline ( placebo group ) 1h before the procedure . PCS with propofol and alfentanil was provided for rescue sedation . Additional sedative consumption , perioperative sedation scores using Observer 's Assessment of Alertness/Sedation ( OAA/S ) scale , recovery , vital signs , adverse events and patient satisfaction were assessed . Total consumption of PCS propofol and alfentanil was significantly less in the dexmedetomidine than placebo group with a mean difference of -13.8 mg propofol ( 95 % confidence interval -27.3 to -0.3 ) and -34.5 g alfentanil ( 95 % confidence interval -68.2 to -0.7 ) at the completion of the procedure ( P = 0.044 ) . Weighted areas under the curve ( AUCw ) of OAA/S scores were significantly lower in the dexmedetomidine group before , during and after procedures ( P < 0.001 , P = 0.024 and P = 0.041 respectively ) . AUCw of heart rate and systolic blood pressure were also significantly lower during the procedure ( P = 0.007 and P = 0.022 respectively ) with dexmedetomidine . There was no difference in recovery , side effects or satisfaction . Intranasal dexmedetomidine with PCS propofol and alfentanil confers deeper perioperative clinical sedation with significantly less use of additional sedatives during upper gastrointestinal endoscopy .
rewrite: Intranasal dexmedetomidine provides a convenient and well-tolerated sedation method. This investigation assessed its sedative effect combined with patient-controlled sedation (PCS) during upper gastrointestinal endoscopy. In this double-blind, randomized, controlled trial, 50 patients were given either intranasal dexmedetomidine 1.5 µg/kg (dexmedetomidine group) or intranasal saline (placebo group) one hour before the procedure. PCS using propofol and alfentanil was available for rescue sedation. Measurements included additional sedative use, perioperative sedation levels via the Observer's Assessment of Alertness/Sedation (OAA/S) scale, recovery, vital signs, adverse events, and patient satisfaction. Total PCS propofol and alfentanil consumption was notably lower in the dexmedetomidine group, with mean reductions of -13.8 mg propofol (95% CI -27.3 to -0.3) and -34.5 µg alfentanil (95% CI -68.2 to -0.7) by procedure end (P = 0.044). Weighted areas under the curve (AUCw) for OAA/S scores were significantly reduced in the dexmedetomidine group before, during, and after procedures (P < 0.001, P = 0.024, and P = 0.041, respectively). AUCw for heart rate and systolic blood pressure were also significantly lower during the procedure (P = 0.007 and P = 0.022, respectively) with dexmedetomidine. No differences were observed in recovery, side effects, or satisfaction. Intranasal dexmedetomidine combined with PCS propofol and alfentanil yields deeper clinical sedation perioperatively while substantially reducing supplemental sedative requirements during upper gastrointestinal endoscopy.

text: Cardiovascular diseases ( CVD ) and metabolic alterations are among the majors public health concern that have been reported in people living with HIV infections . Factors contributing to cardio metabolic syndrome in HIV include body fat distribution , dyslipidemia , insulin resistance , cardiovascular dysfunction and inflammation . The aim of the study was to determine the effect of Spirulina platensis ( Cyanobacteriaceae ) supplementation versus local diet on lipid profile in HIV-infected antiretroviral-naive patients . A prospective single-blind , randomized , multicentre study was conducted from February 2010 to December 2012 . A total of 320 HIV antiretroviral-nave patients were screened and 169 were recruited in this study . Patients were randomized and received either Spirulina supplementation combined with local diet ( n = 82 ) or local diet only ( n = 87 ) . Age , weight , body mass index ( BMI ) , lipid profile , CD4 count , and local food intake variables were assessed on three separate occasions ( three , six and twelve months ) . An average age of the patients was 35.69 years . The majority of participants were female 67.1 % . Regarding the lipid profile , there is a significant increase in HDL-cholesterol and a significant decrease in total cholesterol , LDL-cholesterol and triglycerides in the group of patients who consumed Spirulina platensis . A change in the atherogenic index defined by the ratio CT/HDL-C substitutable by LDL-C/HDL-C and the TC/HDL decreased significantly from 10.83 at baseline to 2.22 after 12 months ( p = 0.21 and p < 0.0001 ) in the patients taking Spirulina . Nutritional supplementation with Spirulina combined with a quantitative and qualitative balanced diet for at least six months can retard an exposition to lipid abnormalities in HIV-infected antiretroviral-naive patients . Further studies are recommended on a large group of people not infected with HIV and exposed to cardiovascular risk factors .
rewrite: Cardiovascular diseases (CVD) and metabolic disorders are major public health issues observed in individuals with HIV infection. Contributing factors to cardiometabolic syndrome in HIV include altered body fat distribution, dyslipidemia, insulin resistance, cardiovascular impairment, and inflammation. This study aimed to evaluate the impact of Spirulina platensis (Cyanobacteriaceae) supplementation compared to a local diet on lipid profiles in antiretroviral-naive HIV patients. A prospective, single-blind, randomized, multicenter trial was conducted from February 2010 to December 2012. Out of 320 screened antiretroviral-naive HIV patients, 169 were enrolled. Participants were randomized to receive either Spirulina supplementation alongside the local diet (n = 82) or the local diet alone (n = 87). Age, weight, body mass index (BMI), lipid profile, CD4 count, and local dietary intake were evaluated at three, six, and twelve months. The average patient age was 35.69 years, with 67.1% being female. In terms of lipid profile, the Spirulina group showed a significant rise in HDL-cholesterol and notable reductions in total cholesterol, LDL-cholesterol, and triglycerides. The atherogenic index, measured by ratios such as CT/HDL-C (or LDL-C/HDL-C) and TC/HDL, decreased significantly from 10.83 at baseline to 2.22 after 12 months (p = 0.21 and p < 0.0001) in Spirulina recipients. Nutritional supplementation with Spirulina, combined with a balanced diet in both quantity and quality for at least six months, can help mitigate lipid abnormalities in antiretroviral-naive HIV patients. Additional research is advised involving larger cohorts of HIV-negative individuals with cardiovascular risk factors.

text: Proton-pump inhibitors are known to be effective in the treatment and prevention of ulcers related to low-dose aspirin ( LDA ) , but few reports address H2 - receptor antagonists ( H2RAs ) and gastroprotective agents ( GPs ) . This study was intended to compare the therapeutic effects of an H2RA and a GP against gastroduodenal mucosal injuries in patients taking LDA . The subjects consisted of patients requiring continuous LDA treatment , in whom no peptic ulcer was found on endoscopy at enrollment . The patients were randomized to either famotidine 20mg/day ( group F ) or teprenone 150mg/day ( group T ) . The study medication was administered for 12 weeks . The patients underwent endoscopy after administration of the study medication in order to obtain a Lanza score . A total of 66 patients ( 38 in group F , 28 in group T ) were included in the efficacy analysis population . The Lanza score changed as follows : in group F , it improved significantly , from 0.891.03 ( meanstandard deviation ) before medication to 0.390.75 after medication ( P = 0.006 ) ; in group T , no significant difference was observed : 0.750.93 before medication and 0.680.82 after medication . Famotidine is better than teprenone in terms of reducing the number of the erosions under use of LDA .
rewrite: Proton-pump inhibitors are recognized as effective for treating and preventing ulcers associated with low-dose aspirin (LDA), yet data on H2-receptor antagonists (H2RAs) and gastroprotective agents (GPs) are limited. This study aimed to compare the efficacy of an H2RA and a GP in managing gastroduodenal mucosal injuries in LDA users. Participants were patients needing ongoing LDA therapy, with no peptic ulcer detected at baseline endoscopy. They were randomly assigned to receive either famotidine 20mg/day (group F) or teprenone 150mg/day (group T) for 12 weeks. Post-treatment endoscopy was performed to assess Lanza scores. The efficacy analysis included 66 patients (38 in group F, 28 in group T). Lanza scores showed significant improvement in group F, decreasing from 0.89±1.03 (mean±SD) pre-medication to 0.39±0.75 post-medication (P=0.006). In group T, no significant change occurred: 0.75±0.93 before and 0.68±0.82 after medication. Famotidine is superior to teprenone in reducing erosion count during LDA therapy.

text: We aimed to compare the effect of repaglinide and metformin monotherapy as an initial therapy in Chinese patients with newly diagnosed type 2 diabetes mellitus ( T2DM ) . In this 15-week , open-labelled , parallel-controlled , randomised study , 60 Chinese drug-naive patients with newly diagnosed T2DM were randomised ( 2:1 ) to receive repaglinide or metformin monotherapy . Primary endpoint was change in HbA1c from baseline to the end of the trial . Secondary endpoints included changes in glycaemic variability , insulin sensitivity and - cell function . Patients in both repaglinide and metformin groups achieved significant reductions in HbA1c ( -1.8 1.5 vs -1.6 1.5 % ) , FPG ( fasting blood glucose ) ( -1.7 1.7 vs -2.1 1.7 mmol/l ) and 2-hPPG ( post-prandial glucose ) ( -3.8 3.1 vs -3.8 3.6 mmol/l ) , with no statistical differences between the groups . Glycaemic variability , glucose infusion rate and - cell function were all significantly improved from baseline in the two groups ( all P < 0.05 ) , without any statistical differences in the improvement between the groups . Repaglinide and metformin achieved comparable efficacy in improving glycaemic control , reducing glycaemic variability , enhancing insulin sensitivity and ameliorating - cell function . Therefore , repaglinide is an optional agent for initial therapy in Chinese patients with newly diagnosed T2DM .
rewrite: This study compared repaglinide and metformin monotherapy as initial treatments for Chinese patients with newly diagnosed type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). In this 15-week, open-label, parallel-controlled, randomized trial, 60 drug-naive Chinese patients were assigned (2:1) to receive either repaglinide or metformin. The primary endpoint was the change in HbA1c from baseline to week 15. Secondary endpoints included changes in glycemic variability, insulin sensitivity, and β-cell function. Both groups showed significant reductions in HbA1c (-1.8 ± 1.5% vs -1.6 ± 1.5%), FPG (-1.7 ± 1.7 vs -2.1 ± 1.7 mmol/L), and 2-h PPG (-3.8 ± 3.1 vs -3.8 ± 3.6 mmol/L), with no significant intergroup differences. Glycemic variability, glucose infusion rate, and β-cell function improved significantly from baseline in both groups (all P < 0.05), with no statistical differences between treatments. Repaglinide and metformin demonstrated comparable efficacy in glycemic control, reducing glycemic variability, improving insulin sensitivity, and enhancing β-cell function. Thus, repaglinide is a viable option for initial therapy in Chinese patients with newly diagnosed T2DM.

text: We examined the impact of a prenatal exercise intervention on physical activity in 260 women at risk for gestational diabetes mellitus . We randomized participants in the Behaviors Affecting Baby and You ( BABY ) Study , which took place from 2007 to 2012 , to either a 12-week individually tailored , motivationally matched exercise intervention ( n = 132 ) or to a comparison health and wellness intervention ( n = 128 ) . We assessed physical activity with the Pregnancy Physical Activity Questionnaire . We used linear mixed models to evaluate the impact of the interventions on change in physical activity according to intensity and type , total walking , and sedentary behavior . Compared with the health and wellness arm , the exercise arm had significantly greater increases in sports or exercise activity ( 0.3 vs 5.3 metabolic equivalent of task [ MET ] hours/week ; P < .001 ) , and smaller declines in total activity ( -42.7 vs -2.1 MET hours/week ; P = .02 ) and activities of moderate to vigorous intensity ( -30.6 vs -10.6 MET hours/week ; P = .05 ) , and was more likely to achieve recommended guidelines for physical activity ( odds ratio = 2.12 ; 95 % confidence interval = 1.45 , 3.10 ) . These findings extend the previous literature by demonstrating the benefits of a clinically feasible exercise intervention in an ethnically and socio-economically diverse population . Given the increased risk of adverse maternal health outcomes in ethnic minority groups , these findings may have important implications for reducing health disparities .
rewrite: We investigated the effects of a prenatal exercise program on physical activity among 260 women at elevated risk for gestational diabetes. Participants in the Behaviors Affecting Baby and You (BABY) Study (2007–2012) were randomly assigned to either a 12-week, individually tailored and motivationally matched exercise intervention (n=132) or to a comparison health and wellness program (n=128). Physical activity was measured using the Pregnancy Physical Activity Questionnaire. Linear mixed models assessed intervention effects on changes in activity by intensity and type, total walking, and sedentary behavior. Compared to the health and wellness group, the exercise group showed significantly larger increases in sports/exercise (0.3 vs. 5.3 MET-hours/week; P<.001), smaller reductions in total activity (-42.7 vs. -2.1 MET-hours/week; P=.02) and in moderate-to-vigorous activity (-30.6 vs. -10.6 MET-hours/week; P=.05), and was more likely to meet recommended physical activity guidelines (OR=2.12; 95% CI=1.45, 3.10). These results extend prior research by showing the advantages of a clinically practical exercise intervention in an ethnically and socioeconomically diverse sample. Considering the higher risk of adverse maternal outcomes among ethnic minorities, these findings could help inform strategies to lessen health disparities.

text: To evaluate the impact of 10-14-day intravenous administration of meldonium as part of combination therapy in patients with chronic heart failure in the early post-infarction period on the recovery period , structural and functional parameters , and heart rate variability ( HRV ) . The investigation enrolled 60 patients ( men and women ) aged 45 to 75 years at weeks 3-4 after post-myocardial infarction with symptoms of Functional Class II-III heart failure . All the patients underwent 24-hour electrochocardiography monitoring , cardiac echocardiography , and HRV study . After dividing the patients into 2 groups , Group 1 ( a study group ) ( n = 30 ) was given intravenous meldonium ( idrinol ) 1000 mg/day in addition to the basic therapy of coronary heart disease . The patients in the study and control ( Group 2 ; n = 30 ) groups were at baseline matched for age , gender , disease severity , and basic therapy pattern . Following 10-14 days of treatment , both groups showed clinical improvement and the favorable changes in cardiac structural and functional parameters and HRV values , which were more pronounced in the patients receiving meldonium . The patients with CHF using meldonium as part of combination therapy in the early post-infarction period were observed to have clinical improvement , a significant reduction in the rate of angina attacks and in the need for nitrates , a decrease in the number of arrhythmic and ischemic episodes , and favorable changes in cardiac structural and functional parameters and HRV values .
rewrite: This study assessed the effects of a 10-14-day intravenous meldonium course within combination therapy for patients with chronic heart failure in the early post-infarction phase, focusing on recovery, structural/functional cardiac parameters, and heart rate variability (HRV). Sixty patients (men and women) aged 45-75 years at 3-4 weeks post-myocardial infarction, with Functional Class II-III heart failure symptoms, were enrolled. All participants underwent 24-hour electrocardiography monitoring, echocardiography, and HRV analysis. Patients were divided into two groups. Group 1 (study group, n=30) received intravenous meldonium (idrinol) 1000 mg/day alongside standard coronary heart disease therapy. Both the study and control groups (Group 2, n=30) were comparable at baseline regarding age, gender, disease severity, and core treatment. After 10-14 days of treatment, clinical improvement and beneficial changes in cardiac structure, function, and HRV were noted in both groups, with these effects being more marked in the meldonium recipients. Incorporating meldonium into combination therapy for CHF in the early post-infarction period was associated with clinical improvement, a notable reduction in angina attack frequency and nitrate use, fewer arrhythmic and ischemic episodes, and positive alterations in cardiac structural/functional measures and HRV.

text: To determine changes in Canine Brief Pain Inventory scores for dogs with osteoarthritis after administration of a monoclonal antibody ( mAb ) against nerve growth factor ( NGF ) that was modified by use of a proprietary process for administration to dogs . 11 adult dogs . Dogs received the anti-NGF mAb ( 0.2 mg/kg , IV ) at various evaluation times during the study period ; at other evaluation times , dogs received an equivalent volume of PBS solution IV . Owners determined Canine Brief Pain Inventory pain severity ( PS ) and pain interference ( PI ) scores immediately before ( baseline ) and 2 , 4 , and 6 weeks after administration of the anti-NGF mAb ; owners were unaware of the evaluation time at which the mAb had been administered . Compared with baseline PS scores ( median , 4.75 ; range , 0.75 to 8.5 ) , dogs had significantly lower PS scores 2 weeks ( median , 3 ; range , 1 to 5.5 ) and 4 weeks ( median , 2.25 ; range , 0.25 to 7.25 ) after administration of anti-NGF mAb . Compared with baseline PI scores ( median , 5.33 ; range , 1.17 to 9.33 ) , dogs had significantly lower PI scores 2 weeks ( median , 3 ; range , 0.67 to 6.83 ) and 4 weeks ( median , 3.33 ; range , 0.67 to 6.67 ) after administration of anti-NGF mAb . The PS and PI scores 6 weeks after mAb administration were lower than baseline scores , although values were not significantly different . Results of this study suggested the evaluated anti-NGF mAb decreased PS and PI scores for 4 weeks after administration . This treatment may be effective for alleviation of signs of pain in dogs with osteoarthritis for up to 4 weeks .
rewrite: To assess alterations in Canine Brief Pain Inventory scores for dogs with osteoarthritis following treatment with a proprietary-process-modified monoclonal antibody (mAb) targeting nerve growth factor (NGF). Eleven adult dogs were included. Dogs were administered the anti-NGF mAb (0.2 mg/kg, IV) at specific evaluation points during the study; at other times, they received an equal volume of PBS solution IV. Owners recorded Canine Brief Pain Inventory pain severity (PS) and pain interference (PI) scores just before (baseline) and at 2, 4, and 6 weeks post-administration of the anti-NGF mAb, with owners blinded to the timing of mAb administration. Relative to baseline PS scores (median, 4.75; range, 0.75 to 8.5), dogs exhibited significantly reduced PS scores at 2 weeks (median, 3; range, 1 to 5.5) and 4 weeks (median, 2.25; range, 0.25 to 7.25) after anti-NGF mAb administration. Compared to baseline PI scores (median, 5.33; range, 1.17 to 9.33), dogs showed significantly lower PI scores at 2 weeks (median, 3; range, 0.67 to 6.83) and 4 weeks (median, 3.33; range, 0.67 to 6.67) post-administration. PS and PI scores at 6 weeks after mAb administration were below baseline levels, though not statistically significant. Findings indicated that the tested anti-NGF mAb reduced PS and PI scores for up to 4 weeks after administration. This therapy may be effective in mitigating pain symptoms in dogs with osteoarthritis for as long as 4 weeks.

text: To prevent salivary dysfunction in thyroid cancer patients who have undergone radioiodine ablation , massaging the parotid gland ( PG ) is presumed to be helpful for the removal of radioiodine . The purpose of this study was to evaluate the effect of PG massage in the removal of radioiodine from the PG . Forty-four patients ( female , 38 ; 49.1 11.0 years ) who underwent total thyroidectomy followed by I-131 ablation were included in this prospective study . Three serial salivary gland scans were performed 2h after administration of I-123 in thyroid hormone withdrawal status . The patients were divided into two groups . There was a 1-min ( or 2-min ) interval between the first and second scans for control , followed by the performance of PG massage for 1 min ( or 2 min ) between the second and third scans . Changes in uptakes were calculated between the first and second scans ( control ) and between the second and third scans ( massage ) . The mean change in uptake at the 1-min massage was 0.97 11.27 % , whereas that at the 1-min control was 11.54 5.59 % ( P < 0.001 ) . The mean change in uptake at the 2-min massage was also significantly lower than that at the 2-min control ( 11.11 6.97 vs. -0.85 9.78 % , P < 0.001 ) . However , no statistical difference was observed between the mean changes in uptake after 1 - and 2-min massages ( P = 0.573 ) . PG massage reduced the radioiodine uptake in the PG , and the effect of PG massage for 1 min was comparable with that of PG massage for 2 min . PG massage can be applied to thyroid cancer patients who receive radioiodine therapy to reduce PG dysfunction .
rewrite: Massaging the parotid gland (PG) is thought to aid in clearing radioiodine, potentially preventing salivary dysfunction in thyroid cancer patients after radioiodine ablation. This study aimed to assess the impact of PG massage on radioiodine removal from the gland. Forty-four patients (38 female; mean age 49.1 ± 11.0 years) who had total thyroidectomy followed by I-131 ablation were enrolled prospectively. Three sequential salivary gland scans were conducted 2 hours after I-123 administration during thyroid hormone withdrawal. Patients were split into two groups. A 1-minute (or 2-minute) interval between the first and second scans served as a control, followed by 1 minute (or 2 minutes) of PG massage between the second and third scans. Uptake changes were computed between the first and second scans (control) and between the second and third scans (massage). The mean uptake change with 1-minute massage was 0.97 ± 11.27%, compared to 11.54 ± 5.59% for the 1-minute control (P < 0.001). Similarly, the mean uptake change with 2-minute massage was significantly lower than with the 2-minute control (11.11 ± 6.97% vs. -0.85 ± 9.78%, P < 0.001). However, no statistical difference was found between the mean uptake changes after 1- and 2-minute massages (P = 0.573). PG massage decreased radioiodine uptake in the gland, with 1-minute massage showing comparable effectiveness to 2-minute massage. PG massage can be used for thyroid cancer patients undergoing radioiodine therapy to mitigate PG dysfunction.

text: The present study examined the impact of BP from childhood to mid-adulthood on retinal microvascular architecture . The Cardiovascular Risk in Young Finns Study included children aged 3-18 years , from five Finnish University cities , with participants chosen randomly from the national population registrar from those areas . The age of participants included in the current analyses in childhood ( 1980 ) ranged from three to nine years and in mid-adulthood ( 2011 ) ranged from 34 to 40 years ( complete data n = 657 ) . Measures of retinal microvasculature architecture measured in adulthood included diameters , tortuosity , lengths , and LDR . Regression analysis showed a strong negative association between childhood systolic BP and adult arteriolar diameter ( standardized regression coefficient [ ] -0.300 ; p < 0.001 ) and with change in systolic BP from childhood to adulthood ( = -0.249 ; p < 0.001 ) . For arteriolar tortuosity , there was a strong positive association between childhood systolic BP and adult arteriolar tortuosity ( = 0.154 ; p < 0.001 ) and no association with change in systolic BP from childhood to adulthood ( = 0.072 ; p = 0.110 ) . High BP in childhood and increased BP from childhood to adulthood impacts on retinal microvascular architecture in mid-adulthood .
rewrite: This study investigated the influence of blood pressure (BP) from childhood through mid-adulthood on retinal microvascular structure. The Cardiovascular Risk in Young Finns Study enrolled children aged 3-18 years, randomly selected from the national population register across five Finnish university cities. For the current analyses, participants were aged three to nine years in childhood (1980) and 34 to 40 years in mid-adulthood (2011) (complete data n = 657). Adult retinal microvascular architecture was assessed via diameters, tortuosity, lengths, and length-diameter ratio (LDR). Regression analysis revealed a significant negative association between childhood systolic BP and adult arteriolar diameter (standardized coefficient β = -0.300; p < 0.001), as well as with the change in systolic BP from childhood to adulthood (β = -0.249; p < 0.001). For arteriolar tortuosity, a significant positive association was found with childhood systolic BP (β = 0.154; p < 0.001), but no association with the change in systolic BP over time (β = 0.072; p = 0.110). Elevated BP in childhood and a rise in BP from childhood to adulthood affect retinal microvascular architecture in mid-adulthood.

text: Sickness absence due to poor mental health is a common problem in many Western countries . To facilitate return to work , it may be important to identify individuals on sick leave and at risk of having a mental disorder and subsequently to offer appropriate treatment . Psychoeducation alone has not previously been used as a return to work intervention , but may be a promising tool to facilitate return to work . Therefore , the aim of the study is to evaluate the effectiveness of psychoeducation designed specifically to facilitate return to work for individuals on sick leave and at risk of having a mental disorder . The psychoeducation was a supplement to the various standard offers provided by the job centres . The study is a randomised controlled trial , in which individuals on sick leave either receive psychoeducation and standard case management or standard case management alone . Participants were individuals with mental health symptoms , who had been on sick leave from part-time or full-time work or unemployment for about 4-8 weeks . The psychoeducational intervention was group-based and the course consisted of 2 hour sessions once a week for 6 weeks . The course was given by psychiatric nurses , a psychologist , a social worker , a physiotherapist and a person who had previously been on sick leave due to mental health problems . The sessions focused on stress and work life , and the purpose was to provide individuals on sick leave the skills to understand and improve their mental functioning.The primary outcome is the duration of sickness absence measured by register data . Secondary outcomes include psychological symptoms , mental health-related quality of life , and locus of control . These outcomes are measured by questionnaires at the start of the intervention and at 3 and 6 months follow-up . On the basis of this trial , the effect of psychoeducation for individuals on sick leave and at risk of having a mental disorder will be studied . The results will contribute to the continuing research on sickness absence and mental health . It will primarily show whether psychoeducation can lead to faster and sustainable return to work . Clinical Trial.gov NCT01637363 . Registered 6 July 2012 .
rewrite: Sickness absence linked to poor mental health is a widespread issue in numerous Western nations. To support return to work, identifying individuals on sick leave who are at risk of a mental disorder and providing suitable treatment could be crucial. While psychoeducation has not been applied before as a return-to-work intervention, it might serve as a promising approach to aid this process. Consequently, this study aims to assess the effectiveness of psychoeducation specifically designed to help individuals on sick leave and at risk of a mental disorder return to work. The psychoeducation supplemented the standard services offered by job centres. This randomised controlled trial compares participants receiving psychoeducation plus standard case management with those receiving standard case management only. Participants included individuals with mental health symptoms, on sick leave from part-time or full-time employment or unemployment for approximately 4-8 weeks. The psychoeducational intervention was delivered in groups, with weekly 2-hour sessions over 6 weeks. The course was led by psychiatric nurses, a psychologist, a social worker, a physiotherapist, and a peer with prior experience of sick leave due to mental health issues.
