text: Hip fracture ( HF ) in frail elderly patients is associated with poor physical recovery and death . There is often postoperative blood loss and the hemoglobin ( Hb ) threshold for red blood cell ( RBC ) transfusions in these patients is unknown . We investigated whether RBC transfusion strategies were associated with the degree of physical recovery or with reduced mortality after HF surgery . We enrolled 284 consecutive post-surgical HF patients ( aged 65 years ) with Hb levels < 11.3 g/dL ( 7 mmol/L ) who had been admitted from nursing homes or sheltered housing . Allocation was stratified by residence . The patients were randomly assigned to either restrictive ( Hb < 9.7 g/dL ; < 6 mmol/L ) or liberal ( Hb < 11.3 g/dL ; < 7 mmol/L ) RBC transfusions given within the first 30 days postoperatively . Follow-up was at 90 days . No statistically significant differences were found in repeated measures of daily living activities or in 90-day mortality rate between the restrictive group ( where 27 % died ) and the liberal group ( where 21 % died ) . Per-protocol 30-day mortality was higher with the restrictive strategy ( hazard ratio ( HR ) = 2.4 , 95 % CI : 1.1-5 .2 ; p = 0.03 ) . The 90-day mortality rate was higher for nursing home residents in the restrictive transfusion group ( 36 % ) than for those in the liberal group ( 20 % ) ( HR = 2.0 , 95 % CI : 1.1-3 .6 ; p = 0.01 ) . According to our Hb thresholds , recovery from physical disabilities in frail elderly hip fracture patients was similar after a restrictive RBC transfusion strategy and after a liberal strategy . Implementation of a liberal RBC transfusion strategy in nursing home residents has the potential to increase survival .
rewrite: Hip fractures (HF) in frail elderly individuals are linked to limited physical recovery and mortality. Postoperative blood loss is common, and the optimal hemoglobin (Hb) threshold for red blood cell (RBC) transfusions in this group remains unclear. We examined whether RBC transfusion approaches were related to physical recovery levels or lower mortality following HF surgery. A total of 284 consecutive post-surgical HF patients (aged 65 years) with Hb levels below 11.3 g/dL (7 mmol/L), admitted from nursing homes or sheltered housing, were enrolled. Allocation was based on residence. Patients were randomly assigned to either restrictive (Hb < 9.7 g/dL; <6 mmol/L) or liberal (Hb < 11.3 g/dL; <7 mmol/L) RBC transfusions within the initial 30 days after surgery. Follow-up occurred at 90 days. No statistically significant differences were observed in repeated measures of daily living activities or in 90-day mortality between the restrictive group (27% died) and the liberal group (21% died). Per-protocol 30-day mortality was higher with the restrictive strategy (hazard ratio [HR] = 2.4, 95% CI: 1.1–5.2; p = 0.03). The 90-day mortality rate was greater for nursing home residents in the restrictive transfusion group (36%) compared to those in the liberal group (20%) (HR = 2.0, 95% CI: 1.1–3.6; p = 0.01). Based on our Hb thresholds, recovery from physical disabilities in frail elderly hip fracture patients was similar with both restrictive and liberal RBC transfusion strategies. Adopting a liberal RBC transfusion strategy in nursing home residents may improve survival.

text: To evaluate the safety of the concurrent combination of bevacizumab with adjuvant radiotherapy ( B-RT ) in breast cancer ( BC ) . Multicentre , prospective study , of the toxicity of adjuvant radiotherapy ( RT ) alone or B-RT in patients with non-metastatic BC enrolled in randomized Phase 3 BEATRICE trial . Early and late toxicities were assessed by the Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events v. 3.0 during and 12 months after the completion of RT. . From 2007 to 2012 , 39 females received adjuvant B-RT and 45 received adjuvant RT alone . Median follow-up was 21.5 months . All patients had triple-negative non-metastatic BC and received adjuvant chemotherapy followed by RT. 90 % of the 39 females treated by concurrent B-RT received whole breast irradiation ( WBI ) with a boost and 4 ( 10 % ) received post-mastectomy RT. . Lymph node RT was delivered in 49 % of the females with internal mammary chain irradiation . The mean duration of bevacizumab was 11.7 months . 38 ( 84 % ) females treated by RT alone received WBI with a boost and 16 % of the females received post-mastectomy RT. . Lymph node RT was delivered in 47 % of the females with internal mammary chain RT in 31 % . Grade 3 acute dermatitis was observed in 9 % of patients receiving B-RT and 5 % of patients receiving RT alone with no significant difference . 1 year after the completion of RT , the most common late grade 1-2 toxicities in the B-RT group were pain ( 18 % ) , fibrosis ( 8 % ) and telangiectasia ( 5 % ) . The concurrent bevacizumab with locoregional RT is associated with acceptable early and late 1-year toxicities in patients with BC . The largest series of this association .
rewrite: To assess the safety of combining bevacizumab concurrently with adjuvant radiotherapy (B-RT) in breast cancer (BC). A multicentre, prospective study evaluated the toxicity of adjuvant radiotherapy (RT) alone versus B-RT in patients with non-metastatic BC from the randomized Phase 3 BEATRICE trial. Early and late toxicities were graded using the Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events v. 3.0 during and 12 months post-RT. Between 2007 and 2012, 39 women received adjuvant B-RT and 45 received adjuvant RT alone. Median follow-up was 21.5 months. All patients had triple-negative non-metastatic BC and underwent adjuvant chemotherapy followed by RT. Among the 39 women treated with concurrent B-RT, 90% received whole breast irradiation (WBI) with a boost, while 4 (10%) had post-mastectomy RT. Lymph node RT was administered to 49% of women, including internal mammary chain irradiation. The mean duration of bevacizumab treatment was 11.7 months. In the RT-alone group, 38 (84%) women received WBI with a boost, and 16% underwent post-mastectomy RT. Lymph node RT was given to 47% of women, with internal mammary chain RT in 31%. Grade 3 acute dermatitis occurred in 9% of B-RT patients and 5% of RT-alone patients, showing no significant difference. One year after RT completion, the most frequent late grade 1-2 toxicities in the B-RT group were pain (18%), fibrosis (8%), and telangiectasia (5%). Concurrent bevacizumab with locoregional RT is linked to acceptable early and late 1-year toxicities in BC patients. This represents the largest series on this combination.

text: To assess the potential therapeutic effect of intratendinous injection of platelet-rich plasma ( PRP ) under ultrasound ( US ) guidance to treat tendon tears and tendinosis in a pilot study with long-term follow-up . The study included 408 consecutive patients referred for treatment by PRP injection of tendinopathy in the upper ( medial and lateral epicondylar tendons ) and the lower ( patellar , Achilles , hamstring and adductor longus , and peroneal tendons ) limb who received a single intratendinous injection of PRP under US guidance . Clinical and US data were retrospectively collected for each anatomic compartment for upper and lower limbs before treatment ( baseline ) and 6 weeks after treatment . Late clinical data without US were collected until 32 months after the procedure ( mean , 20.2 months ) . The McNemar test and regression model were used to compare clinical and US data . QuickDASH score , Western Ontario and McMaster Universities Osteoarthritis Index ( WOMAC ) score , and residual US size of lesions were significantly lower after intratendinous injection of PRP under US guidance at 6 weeks and during long-term follow-up compared with baseline ( P < .001 in upper and lower limb ) independent of age , gender , and type of tendinopathy ( P > .29 ) . No clinical complication was reported during follow-up . Intratendinous injection of PRP under US guidance appears to allow rapid tendon healing and is well tolerated .
rewrite: To evaluate the therapeutic potential of ultrasound-guided intratendinous platelet-rich plasma (PRP) injection for tendon tears and tendinosis in a pilot study with extended follow-up. The research involved 408 consecutive patients referred for PRP injection treatment of tendinopathy in the upper limb (medial and lateral epicondylar tendons) and lower limb (patellar, Achilles, hamstring, adductor longus, and peroneal tendons), each receiving a single US-guided intratendinous PRP injection. Clinical and ultrasound data were retrospectively gathered for each anatomic region in the upper and lower limbs before treatment (baseline) and at 6 weeks post-treatment. Additional clinical data without ultrasound were collected up to 32 months after the procedure (mean, 20.2 months). The McNemar test and regression model were applied to compare clinical and US findings. QuickDASH score, WOMAC score, and residual ultrasound lesion size were significantly reduced following US-guided intratendinous PRP injection at 6 weeks and over long-term follow-up compared to baseline (P < .001 for both upper and lower limbs), regardless of age, gender, or tendinopathy type (P > .29). No clinical complications were reported during follow-up. Ultrasound-guided intratendinous PRP injection seems to promote rapid tendon healing and is well tolerated.

text: In this paper , we review the results of existing statistical models of the long-term persistence of hepatitis A vaccine-induced antibodies in light of recently available immunogenicity data from 2 clinical trials ( up to 17 years of follow-up ) . Healthy adult volunteers monitored annually for 17 years after the administration of the first vaccine dose in 2 double-blind , randomized clinical trials were included in this analysis . Vaccination in these studies was administered according to a 2-dose vaccination schedule : 0 , 12 months in study A and 0 , 6 months in study B ( NCT00289757/NCT00291876 ) . Antibodies were measured using an in-house ELISA during the first 11 years of follow-up ; a commercially available ELISA was then used up to Year 17 of follow-up . Long-term antibody persistence from studies A and B was estimated using statistical models for longitudinal data . Data from studies A and B were modeled separately . A total of 173 participants in study A and 108 participants in study B were included in the analysis . A linear mixed model with 2 changepoints allowed all available results to be accounted for . Predictions based on this model indicated that 98 % ( 95 % CI : 94-100 % ) of participants in study A and 97 % ( 95 % CI : 94-100 % ) of participants in study B will remain seropositive 25 years after receiving the first vaccine dose . Other models using part of the data provided consistent results : 95 % of the participants was projected to remain seropositive for 25 years . This analysis , using previously used and newly selected model structures , was consistent with former estimates of seropositivity rates 95 % for at least 25 years .
rewrite: This paper reviews existing statistical models for the long-term persistence of hepatitis A vaccine-induced antibodies, incorporating recent immunogenicity data from two clinical trials with follow-up periods extending up to 17 years. The analysis included healthy adult volunteers from two double-blind, randomized clinical trials, who were monitored annually for 17 years following their initial vaccine dose. Vaccination in these trials followed a two-dose schedule: 0 and 12 months in study A, and 0 and 6 months in study B (NCT00289757/NCT00291876). Antibody levels were assessed with an in-house ELISA for the first 11 years of follow-up, and a commercial ELISA was employed thereafter up to year 17. Longitudinal statistical models were applied to estimate long-term antibody persistence from studies A and B, with each study's data modeled independently. The analysis encompassed 173 participants from study A and 108 from study B. A linear mixed model incorporating two changepoints accommodated all available data. Model predictions suggest that 98% (95% CI: 94–100%) of participants in study A and 97% (95% CI: 94–100%) in study B will maintain seropositivity 25 years after the first vaccine dose. Alternative models using subsets of the data yielded consistent projections, indicating 95% of participants would remain seropositive for 25 years. This analysis, utilizing both established and newly chosen model frameworks, aligns with prior estimates of seropositivity rates of 95% for at least 25 years.

text: To evaluate the effects of a 12-week balance training programme on self-assessed function and disability in healthy community-dwelling older adults with self-perceived balance deficits and fear of falling . A prospective , randomized controlled trial . Stockholm County , Sweden . A total of 59 community-dwelling older adults ( 42 women and 17 men ) aged 67-93 were randomized to either an intervention group ( n = 38 ) or to serve as controls ( n = 21 ) after baseline testing . The intervention was a 12-week , three times per week , progressive , specific and individually adjusted group balance-training programme . Self-perceived function and disability measured with Late Life Function and Disability Instrument . The intervention group reported improvement in overall function ( p = 0.016 ) , as well as in basic ( p = 0.044 ) and advanced lower extremity function ( p = 0.025 ) compared with the control group . The study showed no improvement in overall disability or upper extremity function . This group balance training programme improves self-assessed function in community-dwelling older adults with balance deficits and fear of falling .
rewrite: To assess the impact of a 12-week balance training program on self-reported function and disability in healthy, community-dwelling older adults experiencing self-perceived balance deficits and fear of falling. A prospective, randomized controlled trial was conducted in Stockholm County, Sweden. Fifty-nine community-dwelling older adults (42 women, 17 men), aged 67-93, were randomized after baseline testing into an intervention group (n=38) or a control group (n=21). The intervention consisted of a 12-week, progressive, specific, and individually adjusted group balance-training program, conducted three times per week. Self-perceived function and disability were measured using the Late Life Function and Disability Instrument. Compared to the control group, the intervention group reported improvements in overall function (p=0.016), as well as in basic (p=0.044) and advanced lower extremity function (p=0.025). No improvement was observed in overall disability or upper extremity function. This group balance training program enhances self-assessed function in community-dwelling older adults with balance deficits and fear of falling.

text: Current parameters for assessing the efficacy of actinic keratosis ( AK ) treatments compare clinical lesions at the start and end of a study . However , the sun-exposed field also contains subclinical lesions which may become detectable during treatment . Lmax , the maximum lesion count during treatment , is a new concept to better assess the efficacy of field-directed AK therapies . Measuring efficacy using the reduction in lesions from Lmax includes for the first time the clearance of both subclinical and clinical lesions . To evaluate the reduction of lesions from Lmax to study end and compare the results with traditional efficacy endpoints using imiquimod 3.75 % ( IQ3 .75 % ) as an example of field-directed AK therapy . Pooled analysis of data from two 14-week , vehicle-controlled , double-blind studies of IQ3 .75 % . With IQ3 .75 % , the median number of lesions increased from 10 at baseline to an Lmax of 22 . The median absolute reduction in lesions to study end was 18 from Lmax versus 7 from baseline . The median percentage reduction in AK lesions to study end was 92.2 % from Lmax compared with 81.8 % from baseline . The reduction in lesion count from Lmax is a novel efficacy parameter that should become the new way of evaluating field-directed AK therapies since it enables their efficacy against both clinical and subclinical lesions to be accurately determined . Together , the Lmax concept and IQ3 .75 % represent a new approach for the management of AK across a large sun-exposed field .
rewrite: Current methods for evaluating actinic keratosis (AK) treatment effectiveness typically compare visible lesions at the beginning and end of a study. Yet, sun-exposed areas also contain subclinical lesions that may become apparent during therapy. Lmax, the highest lesion count observed during treatment, is a novel concept designed to better gauge the efficacy of field-directed AK treatments. Assessing efficacy by the reduction from Lmax to study end incorporates, for the first time, the clearance of both subclinical and clinical lesions. This analysis evaluates lesion reduction from Lmax to study conclusion and compares these outcomes with traditional efficacy endpoints, using imiquimod 3.75% (IQ3.75%) as an example of field-directed AK therapy. Data from two 14-week, vehicle-controlled, double-blind studies of IQ3.75% were pooled. With IQ3.75%, the median lesion count rose from 10 at baseline to an Lmax of 22. The median absolute reduction in lesions to study end was 18 from Lmax, versus 7 from baseline. The median percentage reduction in AK lesions to study end was 92.2% from Lmax, compared to 81.8% from baseline. The reduction in lesion count from Lmax is a new efficacy measure that should become the standard for evaluating field-directed AK therapies, as it allows precise determination of their effectiveness against both clinical and subclinical lesions. Collectively, the Lmax concept and IQ3.75% offer a fresh strategy for managing AK across extensive sun-exposed areas.

text: Women with primary ovarian insufficiency ( POI ) display low androgen levels , which could contribute to mood and behavioral symptoms observed in this condition . We examined the effects of physiologic testosterone therapy added to standard estrogen/progestin therapy on quality of life , self-esteem , and mood in women with POI . One hundred twenty-eight women with 46 , XX spontaneous POI participated in a 12-month randomized , placebo-controlled , parallel-design investigation of the efficacy of testosterone augmentation of estrogen/progestin therapy . Quality of life , self-esteem , and mood symptoms were evaluated with standardized rating scales and a structured clinical interview . Differences in outcome measures between the testosterone and placebo treatments were analyzed by Wilcoxon rank sum tests . No differences in baseline characteristics , including serum hormone levels ( P > 0.05 ) , were found . Baseline mean ( SD ) Center for Epidemiologic Studies Depression Scale scores were 10.7 ( 8.6 ) and 9.2 ( 7.8 ) for testosterone and placebo , respectively ( P = 0.35 ) . After 12 months of treatment , measures of quality of life , self-esteem , and mood symptoms did not differ between treatment groups . Serum testosterone levels achieved physiologic levels in the testosterone group and were significantly higher compared with placebo ( P < 0.001 ) . Baseline testosterone levels were not associated with either adverse or beneficial clinical effects . A 150-g testosterone patch achieves physiologic hormone levels in women with POI . Our findings suggest that augmentation of standard estrogen/progestin therapy with physiologic testosterone therapy in young women with POI neither aggravates nor improves baseline reports of quality of life or self-esteem and had minimal effects on mood . Other mechanisms might play a role in the altered mood accompanying this disorder .
rewrite: Women with primary ovarian insufficiency (POI) have reduced androgen levels, which may influence the mood and behavioral symptoms associated with this condition. We investigated whether adding physiologic testosterone therapy to standard estrogen/progestin treatment affects quality of life, self-esteem, and mood in women with POI. In a 12-month randomized, placebo-controlled, parallel-design study, 128 women with 46,XX spontaneous POI were enrolled to assess the efficacy of testosterone augmentation of estrogen/progestin therapy. Standardized rating scales and a structured clinical interview were used to evaluate quality of life, self-esteem, and mood symptoms. Outcome differences between testosterone and placebo treatments were analyzed using Wilcoxon rank sum tests. Baseline characteristics, including serum hormone levels (P > 0.05), showed no significant differences. Mean (SD) baseline Center for Epidemiologic Studies Depression Scale scores were 10.7 (8.6) for the testosterone group and 9.2 (7.8) for placebo (P = 0.35). After 12 months of treatment, no differences in quality of life, self-esteem, or mood symptoms were observed between the groups. Serum testosterone levels reached physiologic ranges in the testosterone group and were significantly higher than in the placebo group (P < 0.001). Baseline testosterone levels were not linked to either adverse or beneficial clinical effects. A 150-μg testosterone patch achieves physiologic hormone levels in women with POI. Our results indicate that augmenting standard estrogen/progestin therapy with physiologic testosterone in young women with POI neither worsens nor enhances baseline reports of quality of life or self-esteem and has minimal impact on mood. Other mechanisms may contribute to the mood changes seen in this disorder.

text: This double-blind sham-controlled crossover study investigated the interactions between primary sensory and motor cortex after stroke and their response to Theta Burst Stimulation ( TBS ) . Thirteen chronic subcortical stroke patients with upper limb impairment performed standardised dexterity training primed with ipsilesional M1 intermittent TBS ( iTBSiM1 ) , contralesional M1 continuous TBS ( cTBScM1 ) or sham TBS . The effects on sensorimotor integration , corticomotor excitability , sensation and grip-lift kinetics were examined . After iTBSiM1 , improvements in paretic grip-lift performance were accompanied by an immediate facilitation of ipsilesional M1 excitability and a subsequent increase in ipsilesional short latency afferent inhibition ( SAI ) during training . Precision grip-lift performance improved after cTBScM1 and training , alongside increased ipsilesional M1 excitability with no effect on ipsilesional SAI . There were no effects on sensory performance . Primary motor cortex iTBS not only modulates M1 corticospinal excitability but also increases M1 receptiveness to sensory input . Priming with iTBSiM1 may enhance ipsilesional sensorimotor integration and facilitate better quality sensorimotor training after subcortical stroke .
rewrite: This double-blind sham-controlled crossover study examined the interactions between primary sensory and motor cortex following stroke and their response to Theta Burst Stimulation (TBS). Thirteen chronic subcortical stroke patients with upper limb impairment underwent standardized dexterity training primed with ipsilesional M1 intermittent TBS (iTBSiM1), contralesional M1 continuous TBS (cTBScM1), or sham TBS. The effects on sensorimotor integration, corticomotor excitability, sensation, and grip-lift kinetics were assessed. After iTBSiM1, enhancements in paretic grip-lift performance were associated with an immediate facilitation of ipsilesional M1 excitability and a later increase in ipsilesional short latency afferent inhibition (SAI) during training. Precision grip-lift performance improved following cTBScM1 and training, along with increased ipsilesional M1 excitability but no change in ipsilesional SAI. Sensory performance was unaffected. Primary motor cortex iTBS not only modulates M1 corticospinal excitability but also boosts M1 receptivity to sensory input. Priming with iTBSiM1 may improve ipsilesional sensorimotor integration and promote higher-quality sensorimotor training after subcortical stroke.

text: To determine the association of body mass index ( BMI ) on complications , recurrence , and survival in GOG LAP2 , a randomized comparison of laparoscopic versus open staging in clinically early stage uterine cancer ( EC ) . An ancillary data analysis of GOG LAP2 was performed . Categorical variables were compared using Pearson chi-square test and continuous variables using the Wilcoxon-Mann-Whitney and Kruskal-Wallis tests by BMI group . Survival was estimated using the Kaplan-Meier method . Cox proportional hazards model was used to evaluate independent prognostic factors on survival . Statistical tests were two-tailed with = 0.05 , except where noted . Statistical analyses utilized R programming language . 2596 women were included . BMI ( kg/m ( 2 ) ) groups were < 25 ( 29.5 % ) , 25-30 ( 28.2 % ) , 30-35 ( 21 % ) , 35-40 ( 10.9 % ) , and 40 ( 10.4 % ) . Stage ( p = 0.021 ) , grade ( p < 0.001 ) , and histology ( p = 0.005 ) differed by BMI . Obese women were less likely to have high risk ( HR ) disease ( + lymph nodes/ovaries/cytology ) or tumor features that met GOG99 high intermediate risk ( HIR ) criteria ( p < 0.001 ) . Adjuvant therapy ( p = 0.151 ) and recurrence ( p = 0.46 ) did not vary by BMI . Hospitalization > 2days , antibiotic use , wound infection , and venous thrombophlebitis were higher with BMI 40 . BMI ( p = 0.016 ) , age ( p < 0.0001 ) , race ( p = 0.033 ) , and risk group ( p < 0.0001 ) predicted all-cause mortality . BMI was not predictive of disease-specific survival ( p = 0.79 ) , but age ( p = 0.032 ) and risk group ( p < 0.0001 ) were significant factors . Obese women have greater surgical risk and lower risk of metastatic disease . BMI is associated with all-cause but not disease-specific mortality , emphasizing the detrimental effect of obesity ( independent of EC ) , which deserves particular attention .
rewrite: This study examined the impact of body mass index (BMI) on complications, recurrence, and survival in GOG LAP2, a trial comparing laparoscopic versus open surgical staging for clinically early-stage uterine cancer (EC). An ancillary analysis of GOG LAP2 data was conducted. Categorical variables were compared with the Pearson chi-square test, and continuous variables with the Wilcoxon-Mann-Whitney and Kruskal-Wallis tests, stratified by BMI. Survival was estimated via the Kaplan-Meier method. Independent prognostic factors for survival were assessed using a Cox proportional hazards model. Statistical tests were two-tailed with α=0.05, unless specified. Analyses were performed using the R programming language. The cohort included 2596 women. BMI (kg/m²) groups were: <25 (29.5%), 25–30 (28.2%), 30–35 (21%), 35–40 (10.9%), and ≥40 (10.4%). Stage (p=0.021), grade (p<0.001), and histology (p=0.005) varied significantly by BMI. Hospitalizations exceeding two days, antibiotic use, wound infections, and venous thrombophlebitis were more frequent with BMI ≥40. BMI (p=0.016), age (p<0.0001), race (p=0.033), and risk group (p<0.0001) were predictors of all-cause mortality. BMI did not predict disease-specific survival (p=0.79), whereas age (p=0.032) and risk group (p<0.0001) were significant factors. Obese women face higher surgical risks but a lower likelihood of metastatic disease. BMI is linked to all-cause, but not disease-specific, mortality, highlighting the adverse effects of obesity independent of EC, which warrant specific focus.

text: To evaluate the effects of 0.5 % levobupivacaine at 37 C preheated from room temperature , on sensorial block , motor block , and haemodynamics in patients undergoing transurethral prostate resection ( TUR-P ) . The patients were randomly allocated to two groups : Group I patients were injected with 3 mL 0.5 % levobupivacaine solution which had been kept at room temperature for at least 24 hours and Group II patients were injected with 3 mL 0.5 % levobupivacaine solution which had been kept at 37 C for at least 24 hours . The patients were examined in terms of sensorial block , motor block , haemodynamic profile , and incidence of side effects . No significant difference was found between the groups in terms of demographic data . The time to reach T 10 sensory block and the time of starting motor block were found to be significantly shorter in Group II . The duration of sensory block over T 10 and T 6 , the duration of L 1 regression , the duration of the sensory block , and the regression time of the motor blocks from 3 to 2 were found to be longer in Group II . The use of 0.5 % levobupivacaine spinal anaesthesia heated to 37 C accelerated the start of sensory and motor block .
rewrite: This study assessed the impact of using 0.5% levobupivacaine preheated to 37°C, compared to room temperature, on sensory block, motor block, and hemodynamics in patients undergoing transurethral resection of the prostate (TUR-P). Patients were randomly divided into two groups: Group I received 3 mL of 0.5% levobupivacaine maintained at room temperature for at least 24 hours, while Group II received the same volume preheated to 37°C for at least 24 hours. Evaluations included sensory block, motor block, hemodynamic parameters, and side effects. Demographic characteristics were similar between groups. The time to achieve T10 sensory block and the onset of motor block were significantly shorter in Group II. Additionally, the duration of sensory block above T10 and T6, the time for L1 regression, the overall sensory block duration, and the regression time of motor block from grade 3 to 2 were all longer in Group II. Spinal anesthesia with 0.5% levobupivacaine warmed to 37°C thus accelerated the onset of both sensory and motor blockade.

text: To assess which is the optimal protocol in terms of endometrial preparation prior to frozen-thawed embryo transfer ( FET ) in women with polycystic ovarian syndrome ( PCOS ) and to explore the effect in stimulated cycle with the addition of vaginal 17 - oestradiol . Five hundred and seventy-six patients with PCOS were prepared for FET using artificial cycle induced with oestradiol and progesterone supplementation ( n = 291 ) and stimulated cycle induced by human menopausal gonadotrophin ( HMG ) within or without the addition of vaginal 17 - oestradiol ( n = 285 ) . Then the FET was performed in a receptive endometrium . Endometrial thickness was similar ( 9.03 1.65 vs. 9.12 1.58 , P > 0.05 ) in artificial and stimulated cycle . The two protocols resulted in clinical pregnancy rate ( 41.0 % vs. 41.6 % , P > 0.05 ) , ongoing pregnancy rate ( 36.6 % vs. 34.7 % , P > 0.05 ) , live birth rate ( 30.0 % vs. 31.7 % , P > 0.05 ) , which were not statistically different . Nevertheless , the cancelled cycle rate made a significant difference ( 2.2 % vs. 5.4 % , P < 0.05 ) . There is no significant difference in the clinical pregnancy rate in HMG , HMG added with vaginal oestradiol and HMG switch to vaginal oestradiol group ( 42.6 % , 41.1 % , and 33.3 % , respectively ) . The mean endometrial thickness , clinical pregnancy rate , ongoing pregnancy rate , live birth rate and implantation rate were similar in artificial and stimulated cycle for endometrial preparation prior to FET in PCOS . It was fine to add vaginal 17 - oestradiol to stimulated cycle when necessary . However , stimulated cycles had a significantly higher cancelled cycle rate . We should follow the principles of individualization , securitization and optimization in endometrial preparation of the FET in patients with PCOS .
rewrite: To evaluate the optimal endometrial preparation protocol for frozen-thawed embryo transfer (FET) in women with polycystic ovarian syndrome (PCOS) and to examine the impact of adding vaginal 17-oestradiol in a stimulated cycle. A total of 576 PCOS patients underwent FET preparation using either an artificial cycle with oestradiol and progesterone support (n = 291) or a stimulated cycle induced by human menopausal gonadotrophin (HMG) with or without vaginal 17-oestradiol (n = 285). FET was conducted once the endometrium was receptive. Endometrial thickness did not differ significantly (9.03 ± 1.65 vs. 9.12 ± 1.58, P > 0.05) between the artificial and stimulated cycles. Both protocols yielded comparable clinical pregnancy rates (41.0% vs. 41.6%, P > 0.05), ongoing pregnancy rates (36.6% vs. 34.7%, P > 0.05), and live birth rates (30.0% vs. 31.7%, P > 0.05), with no statistical differences. However, the cancelled cycle rate was significantly higher in the stimulated cycle (2.2% vs. 5.4%, P < 0.05). Among HMG-based groups, clinical pregnancy rates were similar for HMG alone, HMG with vaginal oestradiol, and HMG switched to vaginal oestradiol (42.6%, 41.1%, and 33.3%, respectively). Mean endometrial thickness, clinical pregnancy rate, ongoing pregnancy rate, live birth rate, and implantation rate were comparable between artificial and stimulated cycles for FET preparation in PCOS. Adding vaginal 17-oestradiol to a stimulated cycle is acceptable when needed. Nevertheless, stimulated cycles showed a notably higher cancelled cycle rate. Individualization, safety, and optimization should guide endometrial preparation for FET in PCOS patients.

text: It has been suggested that weight reduction decreases the frequency of urinary incontinence ( UI ) episodes . However , it is not known if this improvement is associated with anatomical changes in the pelvis . The aim of this study was to investigate the effects of weight loss on UI episodes and pelvic floor anatomy . Three hundred seventy-eight overweight/obese women were randomly allocated either to behavioral weight loss or to structured education programs . The patients were evaluated by voiding diary , Pelvic Floor Distress Inventory ( PFDI ) , and Pelvic Organ Prolapse Quantification ( POP-Q ) system at baseline and after 6months . The women in the intervention group had a mean weight loss of 9.4 % , whereas the weight in the control group remained almost the same ( P < 0.001 ) . While there were no change in stress and urge incontinence episodes in the control group , the mean number of stress incontinence episodes per 3-day diary dropped from 7.96 episodes to 3.11 , and the mean number of urge incontinence episodes per 3-day diary dropped from 2.85 episodes to 1.08 in the study group ( P < 0.05 ) . Regarding the POP-Q system , only genital hiatus , perineal body , and Ap measurements were significantly lower in the weight loss group than in the control group after 6months . Weight reduction provides improvement in episodes of UI , decreases the incidence of drops of urine leakage , and increases quality of life related to pelvic floor symptoms . However , there are little to no changes in the parameters of the POP-Q system with weight reduction .
rewrite: It has been proposed that weight loss reduces urinary incontinence (UI) episode frequency. Yet, whether this improvement relates to pelvic anatomical changes remains unclear. This study aimed to examine the impact of weight reduction on UI episodes and pelvic floor anatomy. Three hundred seventy-eight overweight/obese women were randomly assigned to either a behavioral weight loss program or structured education. Participants were assessed using voiding diaries, the Pelvic Floor Distress Inventory (PFDI), and the Pelvic Organ Prolapse Quantification (POP-Q) system at baseline and six months. The intervention group achieved a mean weight loss of 9.4%, while the control group’s weight remained nearly unchanged (P < 0.001). In the control group, stress and urge incontinence episodes showed no change. In contrast, the study group’s mean stress incontinence episodes per 3-day diary fell from 7.96 to 3.11, and urge incontinence episodes dropped from 2.85 to 1.08 (P < 0.05). For the POP-Q system, only genital hiatus, perineal body, and Ap measurements were significantly lower in the weight loss group compared to controls after six months. Weight loss leads to fewer UI episodes, reduced urine leakage incidents, and better quality of life regarding pelvic floor symptoms. However, POP-Q system parameters show minimal to no change with weight reduction.

text: Behavioral interventions for obesity are commonly delivered in groups , although the effect of group size on weight loss has not been empirically evaluated . This behavioral weight loss trial compared the 6 - and 12-month weight changes associated with interventions delivered in a large group ( LG ) or small groups ( SG ) . Obese adults ( N = 66 ; mean age = 50 years ; mean BMI = 36.5 kg/m2 ; 47 % African American ; 86 % women ) recruited from a health maintenance organization were randomly assigned to : ( 1 ) LG treatment ( 30 members/group ) , or ( 2 ) SG treatment ( 12 members/group ) . Conditions were comparable in frequency and duration of treatment , which included 24 weekly group sessions ( months 1-6 ) followed by six monthly extended care contacts ( months 7-12 ) . A mixed effects model with unstructured covariance matrix was applied to analyze the primary outcome of weight change while accounting for baseline weight and dependence among participants ' measurements over time . SG participants lost significantly more weight than LG participants at Month 6 ( -6.5 vs. -3.2 kg ; p = 0.03 ) and Month 12 ( -7.0 vs. -1.7 kg ; p < 0.002 ) . SG participants reported better treatment engagement and self-monitoring adherence at Months 6 and 12 , ps < 0.04 , with adherence fully mediating the relationship between group size and weight loss . Receiving obesity treatment in smaller groups may promote greater weight loss and weight loss maintenance . This effect may be due to improved adherence facilitated by SG interactions . These novel findings suggest that the perceived efficiency of delivering behavioral weight loss treatment to LGs should be balanced against the potentially better outcomes achieved by a SG approach .
rewrite: Behavioral obesity interventions are often conducted in groups, yet the impact of group size on weight loss lacks empirical assessment. This trial compared weight changes at 6 and 12 months for interventions delivered in large groups (LG) versus small groups (SG). Obese adults (N=66; mean age=50 years; mean BMI=36.5 kg/m²; 47% African American; 86% women) from a health maintenance organization were randomly assigned to: (1) LG treatment (30 members/group), or (2) SG treatment (12 members/group). Both conditions matched in treatment frequency and duration, involving 24 weekly group sessions (months 1-6) and six monthly extended care contacts (months 7-12). A mixed effects model with an unstructured covariance matrix was used to analyze weight change, adjusting for baseline weight and repeated measurements. SG participants achieved significantly greater weight loss than LG participants at Month 6 (-6.5 vs. -3.2 kg; p=0.03) and Month 12 (-7.0 vs. -1.7 kg; p<0.002). SG participants also showed better treatment engagement and self-monitoring adherence at Months 6 and 12 (ps<0.04), with adherence fully mediating the group size and weight loss relationship. Obesity treatment in smaller groups may enhance weight loss and maintenance, possibly due to improved adherence fostered by SG dynamics. These new findings indicate that the perceived efficiency of LG delivery should be weighed against the potentially superior outcomes of an SG approach.

text: Many risks of death in childhood bacterial meningitis are well-identified , but factors influencing survival time have received less attention . Better understanding of this issue could help explain why adjuvant medications have performed unevenly in different trials . In a post hoc analysis of prospectively collected data from a large bacterial meningitis treatment trial in Luanda , Angola , we compared time to death after initiation of antimicrobial treatment among 206 children with etiology and other patient characteristics . The risks of dying very quickly ( 0-4 hours ) , quickly ( 4-8 hours ) or after longer periods were analyzed by logistic regression . Median time to death was 18.5 hours , half the time in Streptococcus pneumoniae ( 11.8 hours ) compared with Haemophilus influenzae ( 26.8 hours ) meningitis . Of all deaths caused by pneumococcal or H.influenzae meningitis , 42 % versus 16 % , respectively , occurred within the first 8 hours . In addition , patients who succumbed within 8 hours , unlike those dying later , had a short disease history , shock , hypoglycemia and poor cerebrospinal fluid white cell response . Time to death in Angola is so short that hardly anything , except perhaps modern intensive care , is likely to improve outcome in a patient with meningitis , especially the pneumococcal disease .
rewrite: Numerous mortality risks in pediatric bacterial meningitis are well-documented, yet determinants of survival duration have been less thoroughly examined. Enhanced insight into this matter might clarify why adjunctive therapies have shown variable efficacy across clinical studies. Using a post hoc analysis of prospectively gathered data from a major bacterial meningitis treatment trial in Luanda, Angola, we assessed time to death following antimicrobial treatment initiation in 206 children, considering etiology and other patient traits. Logistic regression was employed to analyze risks of death within very short (0–4 hours), short (4–8 hours), or extended periods. The median time to death was 18.5 hours, with Streptococcus pneumoniae cases (11.8 hours) showing half the duration of Haemophilus influenzae cases (26.8 hours). Among fatalities due to pneumococcal or H. influenzae meningitis, 42% versus 16%, respectively, happened within the initial 8 hours. Moreover, patients who died within 8 hours, in contrast to later deaths, presented with brief illness duration, shock, hypoglycemia, and a weak cerebrospinal fluid white cell response. In Angola, the interval to death is so brief that little, aside from possibly advanced intensive care, is apt to enhance outcomes for meningitis patients, particularly those with pneumococcal disease.

text: To evaluate the effects of continuous paravertebral nerve block after nephrectomy . 60 cases receiving simple nephrectomy , American Society of Anesthesiologists ( ASA ) grading status I or II , aged from 30 to 65 years , weighing from 45 to 80 kg , male or female , were randomly divided into 2 groups : control group ( CEA group ) and continuous paravertebral nerve block group ( PVB group ) , 30 patients in each one . Both groups were performed with 0.2 % ropivacaine 250 ml in continuous infusion , assisted with intravenous morphine patient-controlled analgesia . The blood gas was examined in 6 , 12 , 24 and 48 h postoperatively , and the VAS scores of quiet state and motion state were assessed.In 48 h postoperation , the total amount of morphine was calculated and the complications cases were recorded . Compared with the CEA group , PaO2 in PVB group increased and PaCO2 declined significantly . There was no difference of VAS score under quiet state , but under the motion state the VAS scores declined significantly , the total amount of morphine reduced [ ( 5.2 1.2 ) vs ( 13.9 1.6 ) mg ) ] , the cases of nausea , vomiting , pruritus , orthostatic hypotension decreased and the postoperative first anal exhaust time interval shortened ( P < 0.05 ) . Compared with CEA , postoperative administration of PVB for open nephrectomy results in lowering morphine dose as well as side effect related with the use of morphine .
rewrite: To assess the impact of continuous paravertebral nerve block following nephrectomy, 60 patients undergoing simple nephrectomy, classified as ASA I or II, aged 30–65 years, weighing 45–80 kg, and of either gender, were randomly assigned to two groups: a control group (CEA group) and a continuous paravertebral nerve block group (PVB group), with 30 patients each. Both groups received continuous infusion of 0.2% ropivacaine 250 ml, supplemented by intravenous morphine patient-controlled analgesia. Blood gas analysis was conducted at 6, 12, 24, and 48 hours postoperatively, and VAS scores were evaluated at rest and during movement. At 48 hours after surgery, total morphine consumption was tallied and complications were documented. Relative to the CEA group, the PVB group showed increased PaO2 and significantly decreased PaCO2. While VAS scores at rest were similar, scores during movement were notably lower in the PVB group, with reduced total morphine use [(5.2 ± 1.2) vs (13.9 ± 1.6) mg], fewer instances of nausea, vomiting, pruritus, and orthostatic hypotension, and a shorter time to first postoperative anal exhaust (P < 0.05). Compared to CEA, PVB after open nephrectomy leads to decreased morphine requirements and fewer morphine-related side effects.

text: To evaluate the initial safety and effectiveness of the intrauterine ball ( IUB ) , a copper intrauterine device that , upon insertion in the uterus , takes a three-dimensional spherical form . Fifteen women were followed for 1 year , with follow-up visits at 1 , 3 , 6 , 9 and 12 months . The physician reported that all devices were very easy to insert . One subject discontinued before the 6-month visit ( at 119 days after insertion ) for a reason not related to the device . There were no perforations , expulsions , malpositions or complications , or pregnancies . No safety or efficacy concerns were raised . Due to its form and deployment process the IUB is expected to ease insertion and reduce perforation , malposition and expulsion rates and may also reduce dysmenorrhea and menorrhagia .
rewrite: To assess the initial safety and efficacy of the intrauterine ball (IUB), a copper intrauterine device that assumes a three-dimensional spherical shape once placed in the uterus. Fifteen women were monitored over one year, with check-ups at 1, 3, 6, 9, and 12 months. The physician noted that all insertions were very straightforward. One participant withdrew prior to the 6-month visit (at 119 days post-insertion) for reasons unrelated to the device. No perforations, expulsions, malpositions, complications, or pregnancies occurred. No issues regarding safety or effectiveness were identified. Owing to its design and insertion method, the IUB is anticipated to facilitate easier placement, lower rates of perforation, malposition, and expulsion, and potentially alleviate dysmenorrhea and menorrhagia.

text: Testing the ability to program IVF GnRH-antagonist cycles to avoid weekend oocyte retrieval . Preliminary randomized clinical trial . Patients presenting an indication for IVF or IVF-ICSI were assigned into either the Treatment Group - GnRH antagonist protocol , programmed to start stimulatory agents on a Friday , with oral 2mg estradiol valerate twice a day from the 2nd day of cycle until the first Friday to follow , or to the Control Group - long luteal GnRH agonist protocol . The performance of 27 Treatment Group patients and 24 Control Group patients was analyzed . Cycle dynamics were not clinically or statistically different except for a significant difference in the number of follicles measuring 18 mm on hCG administration day . There were no differences in the number of aspirated ova , fertilization rates , embryo quality or number of embryos to be transferred . Pregnancy rate was 41.7 % in the Treatment Group and 50 % in the Control Group ( P > 0.5 ) . Only one patient assigned to the Treatment Group had a weekend retrieval . Preliminary results demonstrate no compromise related to follicular estrogen programming in a GnRH antagonist protocol and provide reassurance regarding the ability to achieve programming goals .
rewrite: Evaluating the feasibility of scheduling IVF GnRH-antagonist cycles to prevent weekend oocyte retrievals. Initial randomized clinical trial. Patients indicated for IVF or IVF-ICSI were allocated to either the Treatment Group—using a GnRH antagonist protocol with stimulation initiated on a Friday, plus oral 2mg estradiol valerate twice daily from cycle day 2 until the subsequent Friday—or the Control Group, employing a long luteal GnRH agonist protocol. Outcomes from 27 Treatment Group and 24 Control Group patients were assessed. Cycle parameters showed no clinically or statistically significant variations, aside from a notable difference in follicles reaching 18 mm on the day of hCG administration. No disparities were observed in oocytes retrieved, fertilization rates, embryo quality, or embryos available for transfer. Pregnancy rates were 41.7% in the Treatment Group and 50% in the Control Group (P > 0.5). Just one patient in the Treatment Group required a weekend retrieval. Initial findings indicate no detriment from follicular estrogen programming within a GnRH antagonist protocol and support the potential to meet scheduling objectives.

text: This study examines the importance of work in life of people with disability and then focuses on employer attitudes towards these people . In the light of Stone and Colella 's model , the study examines the employer attitudes and the role of variables such as type of disability , employer experience in the hiring of persons with disabilities , the description of hypothetical hirees with disabilities , the ways in which employers evaluate work performance and social acceptability , and the work tasks that they consider appropriate for workers with disability . Eighty employers were randomly assigned to standard condition ( candidates with disability were presented by referring to the disability they presented ) or positive condition ( candidates were presented with reference to their strengths ) . It was found that the type of disability and its presentation influence employer attitudes . In addition , realistic and conventional tasks were considered appropriate for hirees with disabilities . Implications were discussed .
rewrite: This research investigates the significance of employment for individuals with disabilities, concentrating on employer perceptions toward this group. Using Stone and Colella's framework, the study analyzes employer attitudes and the impact of factors including disability type, employer experience in hiring persons with disabilities, descriptions of hypothetical disabled candidates, methods for assessing work performance and social acceptability, and job tasks deemed suitable for workers with disabilities. Eighty employers were randomly assigned to a standard condition (candidates were described by their disability) or a positive condition (candidates were described emphasizing their strengths). Findings indicate that both disability type and its presentation affect employer attitudes. Moreover, realistic and conventional tasks were viewed as appropriate for employees with disabilities. Implications are discussed.

text: Inactivity is a primary factor related to childhood obesity , yet aerobic exercise has been shown to prevent weight gain and improve fitness in adolescents . Moreover , children become less active during their summer break from school . This study compared the effects of 4 and 8 weeks of supervised summer activity versus an unsupervised summer break on metabolic function and fitness in adolescents . Twenty-two adolescents were divided into 4-week ( n = 6 , weight 48.114.9 kg , body fat 27.48.4 % ) and 8-week exercise groups ( n = 6 , weight 43.410.9 kg , body fat 28.512.8 % ) , that performed supervised , play-based physical activity , versus an age-matched 8 week control group that maintained their typical summer break ( n = 10 , weight 41.710.0 kg , body fat 23.78.0 % ) . Anthropometrics , resting energy expenditure ( REE ) , resting heart rate ( RHR ) and peak aerobic capacity ( VO ( 2peak ) ) were evaluated before and after the intervention ( 4 or 8 weeks ) . REE showed group differences in posttraining conditions ( the 4-week group vs. the control group , 1220169 vs. 1067144 kcal/die , and the 8-week group vs. the control group , 1202151 vs. 1067144 kcal/die , P = 0.047 ) , but RHR decreased ( pre-program vs. post program : 9722 vs. 808 beat/min , P = 0.001 ) and VO ( 2peak ) significantly increased ( pre-program vs. post program : 27.87.8 vs. 34.86.5 mL/kg/min , P = 0.001 ) in the 8-week group compared to the control group . Eight weeks of supervised play-based activity increased REE and VO ( 2peak ) in adolescents with concomitant decreases in RHR . These data suggest that this novel model of exercise prescription could be considered world-wide by clinicians to improve fitness base in adolescents and help to combat the growing epidemic of childhood obesity .
rewrite: Inactivity is a key contributor to childhood obesity, while aerobic exercise has been demonstrated to prevent weight gain and enhance fitness in adolescents. Additionally, children tend to be less active during summer vacation. This research examined the impacts of 4 and 8 weeks of supervised summer activity compared to an unsupervised summer break on metabolic function and fitness in adolescents. Twenty-two adolescents were assigned to 4-week (n=6, weight 48.1±14.9 kg, body fat 27.4±8.4%) and 8-week exercise groups (n=6, weight 43.4±10.9 kg, body fat 28.5±12.8%), engaging in supervised, play-based physical activity, versus an age-matched 8-week control group continuing their usual summer break (n=10, weight 41.7±10.0 kg, body fat 23.7±8.0%). Anthropometrics, resting energy expenditure (REE), resting heart rate (RHR), and peak aerobic capacity (VO2peak) were assessed before and after the intervention (4 or 8 weeks). REE exhibited group differences post-training (4-week vs. control: 1220±169 vs. 1067±144 kcal/day; 8-week vs. control: 1202±151 vs. 1067±144 kcal/day, P=0.047), but RHR declined (pre- vs. post-program: 97±22 vs. 80±8 beats/min, P=0.001) and VO2peak significantly rose (pre- vs. post-program: 27.8±7.8 vs. 34.8±6.5 mL/kg/min, P=0.001) in the 8-week group relative to controls. Eight weeks of supervised play-based activity elevated REE and VO2peak in adolescents alongside reductions in RHR. These findings indicate that this innovative exercise model could be adopted globally by clinicians to boost fitness in adolescents and aid in addressing the escalating childhood obesity epidemic.

text: Angina pectoris is common in patients with heart failure and reduced ejection fraction ( HF-REF ) but its relationship with outcomes has not been well defined . This relationship was investigated further in a retrospective analysis of the Controlled Rosuvastatin Multinational Trial in Heart Failure ( CORONA ) . Four thousand , eight hundred and seventy-eight patients were divided into three categories : no history of angina and no chest pain at baseline ( Group A ; n = 1240 ) , past history of angina but no chest pain at baseline ( Group B ; n = 1353 ) and both a history of angina and chest pain at baseline ( Group C ; n = 2285 ) . Outcomes were examined using Kaplan-Meier and Cox regression survival analysis . Compared with Group A , Group C had a higher risk of non-fatal myocardial infarction or unstable angina ( HR : 2.36 , 1.54-3 .61 ; P < 0.001 ) , this composite plus coronary revascularization ( HR : 2.54 , 1.76-3 .68 ; P < 0.001 ) , as well as HF hospitalization ( HR : 1.35 , 1.13-1 .63 ; P = 0.001 ) , over a median follow-up period of 33 months . There was no difference in cardiovascular or all-cause mortality . Group B had a smaller increase in risk of coronary events but not of heart failure hospitalization . Patients with HF-REF and ongoing angina are at an increased risk of acute coronary syndrome and HF hospitalization . Whether these patients would benefit from more aggressive medical therapy or percutaneous revascularization is not known and merits further investigation .
rewrite: Angina pectoris frequently occurs in individuals with heart failure and reduced ejection fraction (HF-REF), yet its association with clinical outcomes remains insufficiently characterized. This association was explored in a retrospective review of the Controlled Rosuvastatin Multinational Trial in Heart Failure (CORONA). A total of 4,878 participants were classified into three groups: no prior angina and no baseline chest pain (Group A; n=1240), previous angina history without baseline chest pain (Group B; n=1353), and both a history of angina and baseline chest pain (Group C; n=2285). Outcomes were assessed via Kaplan-Meier and Cox regression survival analyses. Relative to Group A, Group C exhibited a greater risk of non-fatal myocardial infarction or unstable angina (HR: 2.36, 1.54–3.61; P<0.001), this composite plus coronary revascularization (HR: 2.54, 1.76–3.68; P<0.001), and HF hospitalization (HR: 1.35, 1.13–1.63; P=0.001) over a median follow-up of 33 months. No differences were observed in cardiovascular or all-cause mortality. Group B showed a modestly elevated risk for coronary events but not for heart failure hospitalization. Patients with HF-REF and active angina face heightened risks of acute coronary syndrome and HF hospitalization. Whether more intensive medical treatment or percutaneous revascularization would benefit these patients is unclear and warrants additional study.

text: To evaluate the effect of wearing a dorsiflexion assist orthosis ( DAO ) on walking distance , physiological cost , fatigue , and strength and balance measures after a modified 6-minute walk test ( 6MWT ) in people with multiple sclerosis ( MS ) . Randomized crossover trial . Hospital Movement Laboratory . People with moderate MS and Expanded Disability Status Scale score of 3.70.7 ( N = 34 ; 26 women ) . Modified 6MWT with and without a DAO worn on the weaker leg . Distance walked , perceived fatigue , and the physiological cost of walking were compared between walking conditions . Pre - and postwalk changes in knee extensor and ankle dorsiflexor isometric strength and standing postural sway with eyes open and closed were compared between walking conditions . There were no differences in distance walked or perceived fatigue between the 2 walking conditions . However , there was a reduced physiological cost of walking ( P < .05 ) , a smaller reduction in knee extensor strength ( P < .05 ) , and a smaller increase in standing postural sway with eyes open ( P < .01 ) after walking while wearing the DAO compared with walking without wearing the DAO . Despite not increasing walking distance or reducing perceived fatigue , the DAO reduced the physiological cost of walking and maintained knee strength and standing balance , which may have important implications for physical rehabilitation in people with MS. Further trials are required to determine whether the beneficial effects of wearing a DAO found here are maintained for longer periods .
rewrite: To assess the impact of using a dorsiflexion assist orthosis (DAO) on walking distance, physiological cost, fatigue, and measures of strength and balance following a modified 6-minute walk test (6MWT) in individuals with multiple sclerosis (MS). Randomized crossover design. Conducted in a Hospital Movement Laboratory. Participants had moderate MS with an Expanded Disability Status Scale score of 3.70.7 (N=34; 26 female). A modified 6MWT was performed both with and without a DAO on the weaker leg. Distance covered, perceived fatigue, and walking physiological cost were compared across conditions. Changes in knee extensor and ankle dorsiflexor isometric strength, along with standing postural sway with eyes open and closed before and after walking, were also compared between conditions. No differences were found in walking distance or perceived fatigue between the two conditions. However, wearing the DAO resulted in a lower physiological cost of walking (P<.05), a lesser decline in knee extensor strength (P<.05), and a smaller increase in standing postural sway with eyes open (P<.01) compared to walking without the DAO. Although the DAO did not enhance walking distance or lessen perceived fatigue, it decreased the physiological cost of walking and preserved knee strength and standing balance, which could be significant for physical rehabilitation in MS patients. Additional trials are needed to confirm if these beneficial effects of the DAO persist over longer durations.

text: Robotic guidance has been shown to facilitate motor skill acquisition , through altered sensorimotor control , in neurologically impaired and healthy populations . To determine if robot-guided practice and online visual feedback availability primarily influences movement planning or online control mechanisms . In this two-experiment study , participants first performed a pre-test involving reaches with or without vision , to obtain baseline measures . In both experiments , participants then underwent an acquisition phase where they either actively followed robot-guided trajectories or trained unassisted . Only in the second experiment , robot-guided or unassisted acquisition was performed either with or without online vision . Following acquisition , all participants completed a post-test that was the same as the pre-test . Planning and online control mechanisms were assessed through endpoint error and kinematic analyses . The robot-guided and unassisted groups generally exhibited comparable changes in endpoint accuracy and precision . Kinematic analyses revealed that only participants who practiced with the robot exhibited significantly reduced the proportion of movement time spent during the limb deceleration phase ( i.e. , time after peak velocity ) . This was true regardless of online visual feedback availability during training . The influence of robot-assisted motor skill acquisition is best explained by improved motor planning processes .
rewrite: Robotic guidance has been demonstrated to aid motor skill learning by modifying sensorimotor control in both neurologically impaired and healthy individuals. This study aimed to identify whether robot-guided practice and the presence of online visual feedback primarily affect movement planning or online control mechanisms. In this two-experiment design, participants initially completed a pre-test with and without vision to establish baseline performance. During the acquisition phase, participants either actively followed robot-guided trajectories or practiced without assistance. In the second experiment only, robot-guided and unassisted training were conducted with or without online vision. After acquisition, all participants performed a post-test identical to the pre-test. Endpoint error and kinematic analyses were used to evaluate planning and online control. Both robot-guided and unassisted groups showed similar improvements in endpoint accuracy and precision. Kinematic analysis indicated that only those who practiced with the robot significantly decreased the proportion of movement time spent in the deceleration phase (i.e., after peak velocity). This effect occurred irrespective of online visual feedback during training. The benefits of robot-assisted motor skill acquisition are most consistent with enhancements in motor planning processes.

text: To investigate the effectivity of pentoxifylline ( PTX ) and immunoglobulin M ( IgM ) - enriched intravenous immunoglobulin ( IVIG ) therapy in the treatment of neonatal sepsis ( NS ) , alone or in combination . This was a prospective , double-blind , controlled study . Newborns with suspicion of sepsis were enrolled in the study . The patients were separated into four groups according to treatment protocol : Group 1 = placebo , Group 2 = pentoxifylline , Group 3 = IgM-enriched IVIG , and Group 4 = pentoxifylline + IgM-enriched IVIG . Blood samples were taken for C-reactive protein , interleukin-6 , neutrophil CD64 expression , and tumor necrosis factor-alfa measurements immediately before treatment ( 1st day ) , and measurements were repeated on the 2nd and 4th days of the therapy . A total of 204 patients , 51 in each group , were recruited into the study . There were no significant differences for symptoms of sepsis among groups , except lethargy . No significant differences were observed among the groups according to laboratory data . Overall mortality rate was 8.8 % . The rates of morbidities and mortality among study groups were similar . PTX and IgM-enriched IVIG therapies , either alone or in combination , did not reduce the rates of morbidities and mortality in NS .
rewrite: This study aimed to evaluate the efficacy of pentoxifylline (PTX) and IgM-enriched intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG) therapy, used individually or together, for treating neonatal sepsis (NS). It was conducted as a prospective, double-blind, controlled trial. Newborns suspected of having sepsis were included and divided into four treatment groups: Group 1 received a placebo, Group 2 received pentoxifylline, Group 3 received IgM-enriched IVIG, and Group 4 received both pentoxifylline and IgM-enriched IVIG. Blood samples were collected to measure C-reactive protein, interleukin-6, neutrophil CD64 expression, and tumor necrosis factor-alpha before treatment (day 1) and again on days 2 and 4 of therapy. The study enrolled 204 patients, with 51 in each group. Sepsis symptoms were largely similar across groups, with lethargy being the only exception. Laboratory findings also showed no significant differences between the groups. The overall mortality rate was 8.8%. Rates of morbidity and mortality did not differ significantly among the study groups. Neither PTX nor IgM-enriched IVIG therapy, alone or combined, reduced morbidity or mortality in NS.

text: To report the long-term results of the ARO 95-06 randomized trial comparing hyperfractionated accelerated chemoradiation with mitomycin C/5-fluorouracil ( C-HART ) with hyperfractionated accelerated radiation therapy ( HART ) alone in locally advanced head and neck cancer . The primary endpoint was locoregional control ( LRC ) . Three hundred eighty-four patients with stage III ( 6 % ) and IV ( 94 % ) oropharyngeal ( 59.4 % ) , hypopharyngeal ( 32.3 % ) , and oral cavity ( 8.3 % ) cancer were randomly assigned to 30Gy/2Gy daily followed by twice-daily 1.4 Gy to a total of 70.6 Gy concurrently with mitomycin C/5-FU ( C-HART ) or 16Gy/2Gy daily followed by twice-daily 1.4 Gy to a total dose of 77.6 Gy alone ( HART ) . Statistical analyses were done with the log-rank test and univariate and multivariate Cox regression analyses . The median follow-up time was 8.7 years ( 95 % confidence interval [ CI ] : 7.8-9 .7 years ) . At 10years , the LRC rates were 38.0 % ( C-HART ) versus 26.0 % ( HART , P = .002 ) . The cancer-specific survival and overall survival rates were 39 % and 10 % ( C-HART ) versus 30.0 % and 9 % ( HART , P = .042 and P = .049 ) , respectively . According to multivariate Cox regression analysis , the combined treatment was associated with improved LRC ( hazard ratio [ HR ] : 0.6 [ 95 % CI : 0.5-0 .8 ; P = .002 ] ) . The association between combined treatment arm and increased LRC appeared to be limited to oropharyngeal cancer ( P = .003 ) as compared with hypopharyngeal or oral cavity cancer ( P = .264 ) . C-HART remains superior to HART in terms of LRC . However , this effect may be limited to oropharyngeal cancer patients .
rewrite: This study reports the long-term outcomes of the ARO 95-06 trial, which compared hyperfractionated accelerated chemoradiation using mitomycin C/5-fluorouracil (C-HART) to hyperfractionated accelerated radiation therapy (HART) alone for locally advanced head and neck cancer. The primary endpoint was locoregional control (LRC). A total of 384 patients with stage III (6%) or IV (94%) cancers of the oropharynx (59.4%), hypopharynx (32.3%), and oral cavity (8.3%) were randomized. They received either 30 Gy/2 Gy daily followed by twice-daily 1.4 Gy to 70.6 Gy with concurrent chemotherapy (C-HART) or 16 Gy/2 Gy daily followed by twice-daily 1.4 Gy to 77.6 Gy alone (HART). Analyses used the log-rank test and Cox regression. With a median follow-up of 8.7 years (95% CI: 7.8–9.7 years), the 10-year LRC rates were 38.0% for C-HART versus 26.0% for HART (P=.002). Cancer-specific survival and overall survival rates were 39% and 10% (C-HART) versus 30.0% and 9% (HART; P=.042 and P=.049), respectively. Multivariate analysis showed combined treatment improved LRC (HR: 0.6 [95% CI: 0.5–0.8; P=.002]). This benefit appeared confined to oropharyngeal cancer (P=.003), not hypopharyngeal or oral cavity cancers (P=.264). C-HART remains superior to HART for LRC, though the effect may be specific to oropharyngeal cancer patients.

text: A limited amount of data exists regarding the effect of lipoic acid ( LA ) , an oral antioxidant supplement , on cytokine profiles among multiple sclerosis ( MS ) patients . We aimed to assess the effect of daily consumption of LA on the cytokine profiles in MS patients . In this double-blind , placebo-controlled , randomized clinical trial , 52 relapsing-remitting MS patients with an age range of 18-50 years were recruited into 2 groups : LA consumption ( 1,200 mg/day ) or placebo . Patients followed their prescribed supplements for 12 weeks . Fasting blood samples for cytokine profile measurement were collected at baseline and after the intervention . Anthropometric parameters were measured based on the standard guidelines . INF - , ICAM-1 , TGF - and IL-4 were significantly reduced in the LA group compared to the placebo group [ ( INF - : 0.82 0.2 vs. 0.2 0.2 pg/ml , p < 0.0001 ) , ( ICAM-1 : 20.2 9.4 vs. 8 10 ng/ml , p = 0.0001 ) , ( TGF - : 103.1 20.2 vs. 54.9 26 ng/ml , p < 0.0001 ) and ( IL-4 : 0.1 0.1 vs. 1.02 1.7 ng/ml , p = 0.0112 ) ] . No significant changes in TNF - , IL-6 , EDSS and MMP-9 were found between the LA and placebo groups ( p = 0.6 , p = 0.8 , p = 0.09 and p = 0.8 , respectively ) . The results suggested that consumption of 1,200 mg LA per day beneficially affects several inflammatory cytokines including INF - , ICAM-1 TGF - and IL-4 . Further investigations are needed to verify the beneficial role of LA on other cytokine profiles among MS patients .
rewrite: There is limited data on the impact of lipoic acid (LA), an oral antioxidant supplement, on cytokine profiles in multiple sclerosis (MS) patients. This study aimed to evaluate the effect of daily LA intake on cytokine profiles in MS patients. In a double-blind, placebo-controlled, randomized clinical trial, 52 relapsing-remitting MS patients aged 18–50 years were assigned to two groups: LA (1,200 mg/day) or placebo. Participants took their assigned supplements for 12 weeks. Fasting blood samples for cytokine profiling were collected at baseline and post-intervention. Anthropometric parameters were assessed following standard guidelines. INF-γ, ICAM-1, TGF-β, and IL-4 were significantly lower in the LA group compared to the placebo group [(INF-γ: 0.82 ± 0.2 vs. 0.2 ± 0.2 pg/ml, p < 0.0001), (ICAM-1: 20.2 ± 9.4 vs. 8 ± 10 ng/ml, p = 0.0001), (TGF-β: 103.1 ± 20.2 vs. 54.9 ± 26 ng/ml, p < 0.0001), and (IL-4: 0.1 ± 0.1 vs. 1.02 ± 1.7 ng/ml, p = 0.0112)]. No significant differences in TNF-α, IL-6, EDSS, and MMP-9 were observed between the LA and placebo groups (p = 0.6, p = 0.8, p = 0.09, and p = 0.8, respectively). The findings indicate that daily intake of 1,200 mg LA beneficially influences several inflammatory cytokines, such as INF-γ, ICAM-1, TGF-β, and IL-4. Additional research is required to confirm the beneficial effects of LA on other cytokine profiles in MS patients.

text: To investigate the postoperative analgesic effects of preemptive dexketoprofen trometamol in dogs subjected to ovariohysterectomy ( OHE ) . Seventeen adult bitches of various breeds were used in this study . The dogs were randomly allocated into of two groups . Subjects in the dexketoprofen trometamol ( DEX ) group ( n = 10 ) , received intravenous ( i.v. ) dexketoprofen trometamol , 1 mg/kg , 15 minutes before premedication , while those assigned to the control ( C ) group ( n = 7 ) were given no analgesics prior to premedication . Pain level was assessed by two researchers before the administration of anaesthesia ( 15 minutes before start ) and 0 , 1 , 2 , 4 and 6 hours after surgery . A modified University of Melbourne Pain Scale ( UMPS ) was used to evaluate pain in both groups . Serum cortisol level changed from 0 to 1 h and from 0 to 1 to 4 h were compared between the groups ; the increase in the C group was statistically significant . The modified UMPS was applied to both groups at baseline and postoperative 1 , 2 , 4 and 6 h. According to this test , the values for DEX were significantly lower than controls at 4 and 6 h ( p < 0.001 ) . Stable vital signs with unchanged biochemical parameters on dexketoprofen administration are a promising finding . The clinical advantage shown by the pain scale difference and the low serum cortisol levels should qualify dexketoprofen for preemptive pain management in dogs ( Tab . 5 , Fig. 2 , Ref . 30 ) .
rewrite: This study examined the preemptive analgesic efficacy of dexketoprofen trometamol in dogs undergoing ovariohysterectomy (OHE). Seventeen adult bitches of various breeds were randomly divided into two groups. The dexketoprofen trometamol (DEX) group (n=10) received intravenous dexketoprofen trometamol (1 mg/kg) 15 minutes before premedication, while the control (C) group (n=7) received no preemptive analgesia. Serum cortisol changes from 0 to 1 hour and from 0 to 4 hours were compared; the increase in the C group was statistically significant. text: Unexplained fatigue is often left untreated or treated with antidepressants . This randomized , placebo-controlled , single-blinded study evaluated the efficacy and tolerability of single-dose intravenous ferric carboxymaltose ( FCM ) in iron-deficient , premenopausal women with symptomatic , unexplained fatigue . Fatigued women ( Piper Fatigue Scale [ PFS ] score 5 ) with iron deficiency ( ferritin < 50 g/L and transferrin saturation < 20 % , or ferritin < 15 g/L ) and normal or borderline hemoglobin ( 115 g/L ) were enrolled in 21 sites in Austria , Germany , Sweden and Switzerland , blinded to the study drug and randomized ( computer-generated randomization sequence ) to a single FCM ( 1000 mg iron ) or saline ( placebo ) infusion . Primary endpoint was the proportion of patients with reduced fatigue ( 1 point decrease in PFS score from baseline to Day 56 ) . The full analysis included 290 women ( FCM 144 , placebo 146 ) . Fatigue was reduced in 65.3 % ( FCM ) and 52.7 % ( placebo ) of patients ( OR 1.68 , 95 % CI 1.05-2 .70 ; p = 0.03 ) . A 50 % reduction of PFS score was achieved in 33.3 % FCM - vs. 16.4 % placebo-treated patients ( p < 0.001 ) . At Day 56 , all FCM-treated patients had hemoglobin levels 120 g/L ( vs. 87 % at baseline ) ; with placebo , the proportion decreased from 86 % to 81 % . Mental quality-of-life ( SF-12 ) and the cognitive function scores improved better with FCM . ` Power of attention ' improved better in FCM-treated patients with ferritin < 15 g/L . Treatment-emergent adverse events ( placebo 114 , FCM 209 ; most frequently headache , nasopharyngitis , pyrexia and nausea ) were mainly mild or moderate . A single infusion of FCM improved fatigue , mental quality-of-life , cognitive function and erythropoiesis in iron-deficient women with normal or borderline hemoglobin . Although more side effects were reported compared to placebo , FCM can be an effective alternative in patients who can not tolerate or use oral iron , the common treatment of iron deficiency . Overall , the results support the hypothesis that iron deficiency can affect women 's health , and a normal iron status should be maintained independent of hemoglobin levels . ClinicalTrials.gov NCT01110356 .

text: We evaluated chr6q25 .3 organic cation transporter gene ( SLC22A1 , SLC22A2 , SLC22A3 ) variation and response to smoking cessation therapies . The corresponding proteins are low-affinity transporters of choline , acetylcholine and monoamines , and smoking cessation pharmacotherapies expressed in multiple tissues . We selected 7 common polymorphisms for mega-regression analysis . We assessed additive model association of polymorphisms with 7-day point prevalence abstinence overall and by assigned pharmacotherapy at end of treatment and at 6 months among European-ancestry participants of 7 randomized controlled trials adjusted for demographic , population genetic , and trial covariates . Initial results were obtained in 6 trials with 1,839 participants . Nominally statistically significant associations of 2 SLC22A2 polymorphisms were observed : ( 1 ) with rs316019 at 6 months , overall ( [ c. 808T > G ; p.Ser270Ala ] , OR = 1.306 , 95 % CI = 1.034-1 .649 , p = .025 ) , and among those randomized to nicotine replacement therapy ( NRT ) ( OR = 1.784 , 95 % CI = 1.072-2 .970 , p = .026 ) ; and ( 2 ) with rs316006 ( c.1502-529A > T ) among those randomized to varenicline ( OR = 1.420 , 95 % CI = 1.038-1 .944 , p = .028 , OR = 1.362 , 95 % CI = 1.001-1 .853 , p = .04 ) at end of treatment and 6 months . Individuals randomized to NRT from a seventh trial were genotyped for rs316019 ; rs316019 was associated with a nominally statistically significant effect on abstinence overall at 6 months among 2,233 participants ( OR = 1.249 , 95 % CI = 1.007-1 .550 , p = .043 ) . The functional OCT2 Ser270Ala polymorphism is nominally statistically significantly associated with abstinence among European-ancestry treatment-seeking smokers after adjustments for pharmacotherapy , demographics , population genetics , and without adjustment for multiple testing of 7 SNPs . Replication of these preliminary findings in additional randomized controlled trials of smoking cessation therapies and from multiple continental populations would describe another pharmacogenetic role for SLC22A2/OCT2 .

text: Primary cardiovascular prevention may be achieved by lifestyle/nutrition improvements and specific drugs , although a relevant role is now emerging for specific functional foods and nutraceuticals . The aim of this study was to evaluate the usefulness of a nutraceutical multitarget approach in subjects with moderate cardiovascular risk and to compare it with pravastatin treatment . Thirty patients with moderate dyslipidemia and metabolic syndrome ( according to the Third Report of the National Cholesterol Education Program Expert Panel on Detection , Evaluation , and Treatment of High Blood Cholesterol in Adults ) were included in an 8-week randomized , double-blind crossover study and took either placebo or a nutraceutical combination that contained red yeast rice extract , berberine , policosanol , astaxanthin , coenzyme Q10 , and folic acid ( Armolipid Plus ) . Subsequently , they were subjected to another 8-week treatment with pravastatin 10 mg/d . This dosage was selected on the basis of its expected -20 % efficacy in reducing low-density lipoprotein-cholesterol . Treatment with Armolipid Plus led to a significant reduction of total cholesterol ( -12.8 % ) and low-density lipoprotein-cholesterol ( -21.1 % ) , similar to pravastatin ( -16 % and -22.6 % , respectively ) , and an increase of high-density lipoprotein-cholesterol ( 4.8 % ) . Armolipid Plus improved the leptin-to-adiponectin ratio , whereas adiponectin levels were unchanged . These results indicate that this nutraceutical approach shows a lipid-lowering activity comparable to pravastatin treatment . Hence , it may be a safe and useful option , especially in conditions of moderate cardiovascular risk , in which a pharmacologic intervention may not be appropriate .
