text: Our objective was to assess the safety , feasibility , and effects of the standardized 8-week mindfulness-based stress reduction ( MBSR ) course in adults with migraines . Stress is a well-known trigger for headaches . Research supports the general benefits of mind/body interventions for migraines , but there are few rigorous studies supporting the use of specific standardized interventions . MBSR is a standardized 8-week mind/body intervention that teaches mindfulness meditation/yoga . Preliminary research has shown MBSR to be effective for chronic pain syndromes , but it has not been evaluated for migraines . We conducted a randomized controlled trial with 19 episodic migraineurs randomized to either MBSR ( n = 10 ) or usual care ( n = 9 ) . Our primary outcome was change in migraine frequency from baseline to initial follow-up . Secondary outcomes included change in headache severity , duration , self-efficacy , perceived stress , migraine-related disability/impact , anxiety , depression , mindfulness , and quality of life from baseline to initial follow-up . MBSR was safe ( no adverse events ) , with 0 % dropout and excellent adherence ( daily meditation average : 3411 minutes , range 16-50 minutes/day ) . Median class attendance from 9 classes ( including retreat day ) was 8 ( range [ 3 , 9 ] ) ; average class attendance was 6.7 2.5 . MBSR participants had 1.4 fewer migraines/month ( MBSR : 3.5 to 1.0 vs control : 1.2 to 0 migraines/month , 95 % confidence interval CI [ -4.6 , 1.8 ] , P = .38 ) , an effect that did not reach statistical significance in this pilot sample . Headaches were less severe , although not significantly so ( -1.3 points/headache on 0-10 scale , [ -2.3 , 0.09 ] , P = .053 ) and shorter ( -2.9 hours/headache , [ -4.6 , -0.02 ] , P = .043 ) vs control . Migraine Disability Assessment and Headache Impact Test-6 dropped in MBSR vs control ( -12.6 , [ -22.0 , -1.0 ] , P = .017 and -4.8 , [ -11.0 , -1.0 ] , P = .043 , respectively ) . Self-efficacy and mindfulness improved in MBSR vs control ( 13.2 [ 1.0 , 30.0 ] , P = .035 and 13.1 [ 3.0 , 26.0 ] , P = .035 respectively ) . MBSR is safe and feasible for adults with migraines . Although the small sample size of this pilot trial did not provide power to detect statistically significant changes in migraine frequency or severity , secondary outcomes demonstrated this intervention had a beneficial effect on headache duration , disability , self-efficacy , and mindfulness . Future studies with larger sample sizes are warranted to further evaluate this intervention for adults with migraines . This study was prospectively registered ( ClinicalTrials.gov identifier NCT01545466 ) .
rewrite: This study aimed to evaluate the safety, feasibility, and impact of the standardized 8-week mindfulness-based stress reduction (MBSR) program in adults suffering from migraines. Stress is a recognized headache trigger. While mind/body approaches are broadly beneficial for migraines, rigorous evidence for specific standardized programs is limited. MBSR is a structured 8-week intervention teaching mindfulness meditation and yoga. Prior studies indicate MBSR's efficacy for chronic pain, but its application to migraines remains untested. We performed a randomized controlled trial involving 19 episodic migraine patients, assigned to MBSR (n=10) or usual care (n=9). The primary outcome was the change in migraine frequency from baseline to initial follow-up. Secondary outcomes encompassed changes in headache severity, duration, self-efficacy, perceived stress, migraine-related disability/impact, anxiety, depression, mindfulness, and quality of life. MBSR proved safe (no adverse events), with no dropouts and high adherence (average daily meditation: 34±11 minutes, range 16-50 minutes/day). Median class attendance was 8 out of 9 sessions (range 3-9); average attendance was 6.7±2.5. MBSR participants experienced 1.4 fewer migraines per month (MBSR: 3.5 to 1.0 vs control: 1.2 to 0, 95% CI [-4.6, 1.8], P=.38), a non-significant reduction in this pilot. Headaches were less severe (-1.3 points on a 0-10 scale, [-2.3, 0.09], P=.053) and shorter in duration (-2.9 hours/headache, [-4.6, -0.02], P=.043) compared to controls. Migraine Disability Assessment and Headache Impact Test-6 scores decreased more in the MBSR group (-12.6, [-22.0, -1.0], P=.017 and -4.8, [-11.0, -1.0], P=.043, respectively). Self-efficacy and mindfulness improved versus controls (13.2 [1.0, 30.0], P=.035 and 13.1 [3.0, 26.0], P=.035, respectively). MBSR is safe and feasible for migraine patients. Although this pilot's small sample limited power to detect significant changes in frequency or severity, secondary outcomes indicated benefits for headache duration, disability, self-efficacy, and mindfulness. Larger studies are needed to further assess this intervention for adults with migraines. The trial was prospectively registered (ClinicalTrials.gov identifier NCT01545466).

text: Chronic kidney disease ( CKD ) is highly prevalent in patients with diabetes or hypertension in primary care . A shared care model could improve quality of care in these patients To assess the effect of a shared care model in managing patients with CKD who also have diabetes or hypertension . Design and setting A cluster randomised controlled trial in nine general practices in The Netherlands . Five practices were allocated to the shared care model and four practices to usual care for 1 year . Primary outcome was the achievement of blood pressure targets ( 130/80 mmHg ) and lowering of blood pressure in patients with diabetes mellitus or hypertension and an estimated glomerular filtration rate ( eGFR ) < 60 ml/min/1 .73 m ( 2 ) . Data of 90 intervention and 74 control patients could be analysed . Blood pressure in the intervention group decreased with 8.1 ( 95 % CI = 4.8 to 11.3 ) / 1.1 ( 95 % CI = -1.0 to 3.2 ) compared to -0.2 ( 95 % CI = -3.8 to 3.3 ) / -0.5 ( 95 % CI = -2.9 to 1.8 ) in the control group . Use of lipid-lowering drugs , angiotensin-system inhibitors and vitamin D was higher in the intervention group than in the control group ( 73 % versus 51 % , 81 % versus 64 % , and 15 % versus 1 % , respectively , [ P = 0.004 , P = 0.01 , and P = 0.002 ] ) . A shared care model between GP , nurse practitioner and nephrologist is beneficial in reducing systolic blood pressure in patients with CKD in primary care .
rewrite: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is common among patients with diabetes or hypertension in primary care settings. A shared care model may enhance care quality for these individuals. This study evaluated the impact of such a model on managing CKD patients with diabetes or hypertension. Design and setting: A cluster randomised controlled trial across nine general practices in The Netherlands. Five practices implemented the shared care model, while four continued usual care for one year. The primary outcome was meeting blood pressure targets (130/80 mmHg) and reducing blood pressure in patients with diabetes or hypertension and an estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) < 60 ml/min/1.73 m². Data from 90 intervention and 74 control patients were analysed. Blood pressure in the intervention group decreased by 8.1 (95% CI = 4.8 to 11.3)/1.1 (95% CI = -1.0 to 3.2), compared to -0.2 (95% CI = -3.8 to 3.3)/-0.5 (95% CI = -2.9 to 1.8) in the control group. Use of lipid-lowering drugs, angiotensin-system inhibitors, and vitamin D was higher in the intervention group than in controls (73% vs. 51%, 81% vs. 64%, and 15% vs. 1%, respectively; [P = 0.004, P = 0.01, and P = 0.002]). A shared care model involving GPs, nurse practitioners, and nephrologists effectively reduces systolic blood pressure in primary care CKD patients.

text: This paper attempts to describe the patterns of exercise and the perceived benefits and barriers to exercise in an urban south Indian population . Study participants were recruited from the baseline survey of the D-CLIP ( Diabetes Community Lifestyle Improvement Program ) . Frequency , duration , type and location of exercise were assessed using a questionnaire , while a Likert type scale was used to assess perceived benefits of and barriers to exercise . Quality of life was measured using the EQ-5D . Out of 1281 participants ( 63.7 % males ) , 24.1 % reported doing 150min of exercise/week ( `` exercisers '' ) compared to 75.9 % `` non-exercisers '' . Exercisers were significantly older ( 47 vs. 43 years ) , better educated ( 68.8 % vs. 60 % ) , had a higher monthly income ( 41 % vs. 29.2 % ) , consumed more fruits ( 38.2 % vs. 25.6 % ) and vegetables ( 84.1 % vs. 77.7 % ) and had better perceived state of health ( 81.1 % vs. 76.8 % ) , compared to non-exercisers . Exercisers had significantly lower HOMA-IR , higher Matsuda index and lower prevalence of low HDL cholesterol compared to non-exercisers . However , there were no significant differences in cardio-metabolic risk factors like diabetes , hypertension and obesity between the two groups . Walking was the most common type of exercise . Both exercisers and non-exercisers perceived the benefits of exercising , but barriers weighed more heavily on exercise behaviour . Urgent steps are needed to improve overall exercise levels in India by addressing barriers and improving the quality of exercise performed so as to enhance overall metabolic health .
rewrite: This study aims to outline exercise patterns and the perceived advantages and obstacles to physical activity in an urban south Indian community. Participants were enrolled from the D-CLIP (Diabetes Community Lifestyle Improvement Program) baseline survey. A questionnaire evaluated exercise frequency, duration, type, and location, with a Likert scale used to gauge perceived benefits and barriers. Quality of life was assessed via the EQ-5D. Among 1281 participants (63.7% male), 24.1% reported achieving 150 minutes of exercise weekly ("exercisers") versus 75.9% "non-exercisers." Exercisers were notably older (47 vs. 43 years), more educated (68.8% vs. 60%), had greater monthly income (41% vs. 29.2%), consumed more fruits (38.2% vs. 25.6%) and vegetables (84.1% vs. 77.7%), and reported better perceived health (81.1% vs. 76.8%) compared to non-exercisers. Exercisers also showed significantly lower HOMA-IR, higher Matsuda index, and reduced prevalence of low HDL cholesterol. However, no significant differences were found in cardio-metabolic risk factors such as diabetes, hypertension, and obesity between groups. Walking was the most frequent exercise type. Both groups recognized the benefits of exercise, but barriers had a stronger influence on exercise behavior. Immediate actions are required to boost overall exercise levels in India by tackling barriers and enhancing exercise quality to improve metabolic health.

text: To study the predictive value of biphasic ST-events for interventions for suspected fetal distress and adverse neonatal outcome , when using ST-analysis of the fetal electrocardiogram ( FECG ) for intrapartum fetal monitoring . Prospective cohort study . Three academic hospitals in Sweden . Women in labor with a high-risk singleton fetus in cephalic position beyond 36weeks of gestation . In women in labor who were monitored with conventional cardiotocography , ST-waveform analysis was recorded and concealed . Traces with biphasic ST-events of the FECG ( index ) were compared with traces without biphasic events of the FECG . The ability of biphasic events to predict interventions for suspected fetal distress and adverse outcome was assessed using univariable and multivariable logistic regression analyses . Interventions for suspected fetal distress and adverse outcome ( defined as presence of metabolic acidosis ( i.e. umbilical cord pH < 7.05 and base deficit in extracellular fluid > 12mmol ) , umbilical cord pH < 7.00 , 5-min Apgar score < 7 , admittance to neonatal intensive care unit or perinatal death ) . Although the presence of biphasic events of the FECG was associated with more interventions for fetal distress and an increased risk of adverse outcome compared with cases with no biphasic events , the presence of significant ( i.e. intervention advised according to cardiotocography interpretation ) biphasic events showed no independent association with interventions for fetal distress [ odds ratio ( OR ) 1.71 , 95 % confidence interval ( CI ) 0.65-4 .50 ] or adverse outcome ( OR 1.96 , 95 % CI 0.74-5 .24 ) . The presence of significant biphasic events did not discriminate in the prediction of interventions for fetal distress or adverse outcome . Therefore , biphasic events in relation to ST-analysis monitoring during birth should be omitted if future studies confirm our findings .
rewrite: To examine the predictive role of biphasic ST-events for interventions due to suspected fetal distress and adverse neonatal outcomes, when employing ST-analysis of the fetal electrocardiogram (FECG) for intrapartum monitoring. Prospective cohort design. Three academic hospitals in Sweden. Laboring women with a high-risk singleton fetus in cephalic position beyond 36 weeks gestation. In women monitored with conventional cardiotocography, ST-waveform analysis was recorded and concealed. Traces with biphasic ST-events of the FECG (index) were compared to traces without such events. The predictive ability of biphasic events for interventions for suspected fetal distress and adverse outcomes was evaluated using univariable and multivariable logistic regression. Outcomes included interventions for suspected fetal distress and adverse neonatal outcome (defined as metabolic acidosis [umbilical cord pH < 7.05 and base deficit in extracellular fluid > 12 mmol], umbilical cord pH < 7.00, 5-minute Apgar score < 7, admission to neonatal intensive care, or perinatal death). While biphasic FECG events were linked to more interventions for fetal distress and a higher risk of adverse outcome compared to cases without such events, significant biphasic events (i.e., those prompting intervention advice based on cardiotocography) showed no independent association with interventions for fetal distress [odds ratio (OR) 1.71, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.65–4.50] or adverse outcome (OR 1.96, 95% CI 0.74–5.24). Significant biphasic events did not aid in predicting interventions for fetal distress or adverse outcome. Consequently, biphasic events in ST-analysis monitoring during labor should be disregarded if future studies corroborate these findings.

text: It is often assumed that animations ( i.e. , videos ) will lead to higher learning compared to static media ( i.e. , pictures ) because they provide a more realistic demonstration of the learning task . To investigate whether learning basic life support ( BLS ) and cardiopulmonary resuscitation ( CPR ) from video produce higher learning outcomes compared to pictures in reciprocal learning . A randomized controlled trial . A total of 128 students ( mean age : 17 years ) constituting eight intact classes from a secondary school learned BLS in reciprocal roles of doer and helper with tablet PCs . Student pairs in each class were randomized over a Picture and a Video group . In the Picture group , students learned BLS by means of pictures combined with written instructions . In the Video group , BLS was learned through videos with on-screen instructions . Informational equivalence was assured since instructions in both groups comprised exactly the same words . BLS assessment occurred unannounced , three weeks following intervention . Analysis of variance demonstrated no significant differences in chest compression depths between the Picture group ( M = 42 mm , 95 % CI = 40-45 ) and the Video group ( M = 39 mm , 95 % CI = 36-42 ) . In the Picture group significantly higher percentages of chest compressions with correct hand placement were achieved ( M = 67 % , CI = 58-77 ) compared to the Video group ( M = 53 % , CI = 43-63 ) , P = .03 , ( p ) ( 2 ) = .03 . No other significant differences were found . Results do not support the assumption that videos are superior to pictures for learning BLS and CPR in reciprocal learning .
rewrite: It is commonly believed that animations (i.e., videos) enhance learning more than static media (i.e., pictures) by offering a more lifelike representation of the task. This study examined whether learning basic life support (BLS) and cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) from videos yields better outcomes than pictures in reciprocal learning. A randomized controlled trial was conducted with 128 secondary school students (mean age: 17 years) from eight intact classes, learning BLS in reciprocal doer-helper roles using tablet PCs. Student pairs in each class were randomly assigned to either a Picture or Video group. The Picture group learned BLS via pictures with written instructions, while the Video group used videos with on-screen instructions. Informational equivalence was maintained, as both groups received identical wording. BLS skills were assessed unexpectedly three weeks after the intervention. Analysis of variance showed no significant differences in chest compression depths between the Picture group (M = 42 mm, 95% CI = 40–45) and the Video group (M = 39 mm, 95% CI = 36–42). However, the Picture group achieved significantly higher percentages of correct hand placement during compressions (M = 67%, CI = 58–77) compared to the Video group (M = 53%, CI = 43–63), P = .03, η² = .03. No other significant differences were observed. These findings do not support the assumption that videos are superior to pictures for learning BLS and CPR in reciprocal learning.

text: To detect a difference in ( 1 ) intubation success and ( 2 ) successful intubation times between novice physicians using a Macintosh-style or video-assisted laryngoscope on a difficult airway manikin . Prospective randomized trial . Academic , tertiary medical center . Forty first-year residents across a variety of disciplines with fewer than 5 total live intubations were recruited for the study . Testing took place during orientation prior to commencement of clinical duties . The entire group was provided training by faculty otolaryngologists and anesthesiologists using both laryngoscope types on a manikin airway simulator in a standard intubating scenario . Subjects were then randomized into 2 testing groups , using either a Macintosh laryngoscope or video-assisted laryngoscope in a difficult intubation scenario . The difficult airway simulation entailed oral cavity/oropharyngeal obstruction using inflation of the tongue , as well as cervical spine immobilization with a rigid collar preventing extension and elevation of the head and limiting oral cavity opening . Success was defined as a confirmed endotracheal intubation by the testing instructor in 120 seconds or less . The Macintosh laryngoscope group ( n = 19 ) had an intubation success rate of 47.4 % with a mean intubation time of 69.0 seconds ( 95 % confidence interval [ CI ] : 52.7 , 85.2 ) . The video-assisted group ( n = 21 ) demonstrated a significantly higher success rate of 100 % ( P < .0001 ) and a decreased mean intubation time of 23.1 seconds ( 95 % CI : 18.4 , 27.8 ; P < .0001 ) . The mean difference in success rate between groups was 52.6 % ( 95 % CI : 30.0 % , 75.3 % ) . Novice physicians with little to no prior intubation experience showed significantly higher intubation success with lower intubation times using a video-assisted laryngoscope in a difficult airway manikin simulator .
rewrite: This study aimed to compare (1) intubation success rates and (2) intubation times between novice physicians using a Macintosh laryngoscope versus a video-assisted laryngoscope on a difficult airway manikin. A prospective randomized trial was conducted at an academic, tertiary medical center. Participants included 40 first-year residents from various disciplines, each with fewer than five prior live intubations. Testing occurred during orientation before clinical duties began. All participants received training from otolaryngology and anesthesiology faculty using both laryngoscope types on a manikin in a standard scenario. They were then randomized into two groups for a difficult intubation scenario, using either the Macintosh or video-assisted laryngoscope. The difficult airway simulation involved oral cavity/oropharyngeal obstruction via tongue inflation and cervical spine immobilization with a rigid collar, restricting head extension/elevation and limiting mouth opening. Success was defined as confirmed endotracheal intubation by the instructor within 120 seconds. The Macintosh group (n=19) achieved a 47.4% success rate with a mean time of 69.0 seconds (95% CI: 52.7, 85.2). The video-assisted group (n=21) had a significantly higher success rate of 100% (P<.0001) and a shorter mean time of 23.1 seconds (95% CI: 18.4, 27.8; P<.0001). The mean difference in success rates was 52.6% (95% CI: 30.0%, 75.3%). Novice physicians with minimal prior experience demonstrated significantly better intubation success and faster times using the video-assisted laryngoscope in a difficult airway manikin simulation.

text: We assessed the efficacy and tolerability of onabotulinumtoxinA 200 U vs placebo to treat lower urinary tract symptoms/benign prostatic hyperplasia inmen previously treated with oral benign prostatic hyperplasia medication in a24-week phase 2 , multicenter , double-blind , randomized , placebo controlled , parallel group trial . Patients with I-PSS ( International Prostate Symptom Score ) 14 or greater , peak urinary flow rate 4 to 15 ml per second and total prostate volume 30 to 80 ml were randomized 1:1 to a single intraprostatic treatment of onabotulinumtoxinA 200 U or placebo . A single-blind sham procedure followed by a 4-week run-in was included to attempt to minimize any potential placebo effect . Patients who still met eligibility criteria after the run-in entered the double-blind active treatment period . The primary end point was the change from baseline in total I-PSS at week 12 . Other end points assessed at weeks 6 , 12and 24 included the change from baseline in total I-PSS , peak urinary flow rate , total prostate volume and post-void residual urine volume . Of 427 patients enrolled 315 were randomized and treated . Decreases from baseline in I-PSS were observed in the onabotulinumtoxinA and placebo groups ( -6.3 vs -5.6 points , p < 0.001 ) with no difference between the groups overall or in subgroups . Improvement was observed in the peak urinary flow rate , which was significant only at week 6 compared to placebo . Improvement was significant at all time points in a patient subgroup on stable concurrent - blockers or 5-reductase inhibitors during the study . Adverse events were similar in the 2 treatment groups . OnabotulinumtoxinA 200 U and placebo improved I-PSS and were well tolerated but no between group difference in efficacy was observed .
rewrite: We evaluated the effectiveness and safety of onabotulinumtoxinA 200 U compared to placebo for managing lower urinary tract symptoms/benign prostatic hyperplasia in men who had prior oral medication for benign prostatic hyperplasia, through a 24-week phase 2, multicenter, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled, parallel-group study. Participants with an International Prostate Symptom Score (I-PSS) of 14 or higher, peak urinary flow rate between 4 and 15 ml per second, and total prostate volume of 30 to 80 ml were assigned 1:1 to receive a single intraprostatic injection of onabotulinumtoxinA 200 U or placebo. A single-blind sham procedure with a 4-week run-in phase was implemented to reduce potential placebo effects. Those who continued to meet the criteria after the run-in proceeded to the double-blind active treatment phase. The primary outcome was the change from baseline in total I-PSS at week 12. Secondary outcomes measured at weeks 6, 12, and 24 included changes from baseline in total I-PSS, peak urinary flow rate, total prostate volume, and post-void residual urine volume. Out of 427 enrolled patients, 315 were randomized and received treatment. Reductions in I-PSS from baseline were noted in both the onabotulinumtoxinA and placebo groups (-6.3 vs -5.6 points, p < 0.001), with no overall or subgroup differences between the groups. Peak urinary flow rate improved, showing significance only at week 6 versus placebo. In a subgroup of patients on stable concurrent α-blockers or 5α-reductase inhibitors during the trial, improvement was significant at all time points. Adverse events were comparable between the two treatment groups. OnabotulinumtoxinA 200 U and placebo both enhanced I-PSS and were well tolerated, but no efficacy difference was observed between the groups.

text: Complex regional pain syndrome type I ( CPRS I ) , is a complex of symptoms characterized by diffuse pain usually with associated swelling , vasomotor instability , and severe functional impairment of the affected extremity in stroke patients . Pain is a prominent feature and is often refractory to variety of treatment . To investigate the clinical , functional , and psychosocial effects of upper extremity aerobic exercise ( UEAE ) and compare the effect of aerobic exercise with that of conventional physiotherapy in patients with CPRS type I following stroke as a randomized controlled assesor blinded 4 week-study . A total of 52 inpatients with stroke [ mean age : 65.95 8.7 ( min . = 53 , max . = 80 ) years , and the mean age of the control group was 67.5011.2 years ] , all within 6 months post-stroke and diagnosed with CPRS I. The UEAE program consisted of an arm crank ergometer ( 10 W/min ) , in addition to a conventional physiotherapy ( whirlpool , TENS , retrograd massage ) . Primary outcome measures were CPRS clinical determinants ( pain , hyperalgesia , allodynia , and autonomic abnormalities ) secondary outcome measures were functional independence measure ( FIM ) , Nottingham Health Profile ( NHP ) , and Beck Depression Scale scores that were performed at 0 month ( baseline ) and 4 weeks ( post-treatment ) . In UEAE group , patients reported significant pain relief ( 89.9 % ) and significant decline in CRPS signs and symptoms . The mean change in pain at shoulder , pain at the hand as well as and NHP and BDS scores between groups were statistically significant ( P < 0.05 ) . UEAE made an excellent improvement in the symptoms and signs of CRPS I. Combined treatment of conventional physiotherapy and aerobic exercises may be an excellent synthesis for this syndrome in these patients .
rewrite: Complex regional pain syndrome type I (CRPS I) is a symptom complex marked by diffuse pain, typically accompanied by swelling, vasomotor instability, and significant functional impairment of the affected limb in stroke patients. Pain is a dominant symptom and often resistant to various treatments. This randomized controlled assessor-blinded 4-week study aimed to examine the clinical, functional, and psychosocial impacts of upper extremity aerobic exercise (UEAE) and compare its effects with conventional physiotherapy in post-stroke CRPS I patients. Fifty-two inpatients with stroke [mean age: 65.95 ± 8.7 years (range 53–80); control group mean age: 67.50 ± 11.2 years], all within 6 months post-stroke and diagnosed with CRPS I, were included. The UEAE program involved arm crank ergometry (10 W/min) alongside conventional physiotherapy (whirlpool, TENS, retrograde massage). Primary outcomes were CRPS clinical determinants (pain, hyperalgesia, allodynia, autonomic abnormalities); secondary outcomes included Functional Independence Measure (FIM), Nottingham Health Profile (NHP), and Beck Depression Scale scores, assessed at baseline (0 months) and post-treatment (4 weeks). The UEAE group showed significant pain reduction (89.9%) and a notable decrease in CRPS signs and symptoms. Mean changes in shoulder pain, hand pain, NHP, and BDS scores between groups were statistically significant (P < 0.05). UEAE led to substantial improvement in CRPS I symptoms and signs. Combining conventional physiotherapy with aerobic exercise may offer an effective integrated approach for this syndrome in such patients.

text: It has frequently been speculated that pruritus and skin lesions develop after topical exposure to aeroallergens in sensitized patients with atopic dermatitis ( AD ) . We sought to study cutaneous reactions to grass pollen in adult patients with AD with accompanying clear IgE sensitization to grass allergen in an environmental challenge chamber using a monocenter , double-blind , placebo-controlled study design . Subjects were challenged on 2 consecutive days with either 4000 pollen grains/m ( 3 ) of Dactylis glomerata pollen or clean air . The severity of AD was assessed at each study visit up to 5 days after challenge by ( objective ) scoring of AD ( SCORAD ) . Additionally , air-exposed and non-air-exposed skin areas were each scored using local SCORAD scoring and investigator global assessments . Levels of a series of serum cytokines and chemokines were determined by using a Luminex-based immunoassay . The primary end point of the study was the change in objective SCORAD scores between prechallenge and postchallenge values . Exposure to grass pollen induced a significant worsening of AD . A pronounced eczema flare-up of air-exposed rather than covered skin areas occurred . In grass pollen-exposed subjects a significantly higher increase in CCL17 , CCL22 , and IL-4 serum levels was observed . This study demonstrates that controlled exposure to airborne allergens of patients with a so-called extrinsic IgE-mediated form of AD induced a worsening of cutaneous symptoms .
rewrite: It is often hypothesized that pruritus and skin lesions arise following topical contact with aeroallergens in sensitized atopic dermatitis (AD) patients. We aimed to examine cutaneous responses to grass pollen in adult AD patients with confirmed IgE sensitization to grass allergen within an environmental challenge chamber, employing a monocenter, double-blind, placebo-controlled design. Participants underwent challenge on two consecutive days with either 4000 pollen grains/m³ of Dactylis glomerata pollen or clean air. AD severity was evaluated at each visit up to 5 days post-challenge via objective SCORAD scoring. Additionally, both air-exposed and covered skin areas were assessed using local SCORAD and investigator global assessments. Serum levels of various cytokines and chemokines were measured with a Luminex-based immunoassay. The primary endpoint was the change in objective SCORAD scores from pre- to post-challenge. Grass pollen exposure led to a significant exacerbation of AD. A marked eczema flare occurred more on air-exposed than on covered skin areas. In subjects exposed to grass pollen, significantly greater increases in CCL17, CCL22, and IL-4 serum levels were noted. This study shows that controlled airborne allergen exposure in patients with an extrinsic IgE-mediated form of AD triggers a worsening of skin symptoms.

text: To study compliance to treatment and effectiveness of therapy in patients with axial spondyloarthritis ( ax-SpA ) in different observational regimes . 168 patients without TNF - therapy and BASDAI 4 were randomized into 3 groups . 96 of them were observed in a traditional manner , 26 visited a rheumatologist every 12 weeks , and 46 were counseled by phone once in 4 weeks . In all these cases , rheumatologists collected data on the activity of the disease ( BASDAI , ASDAS , PASS , etc. ) and the effectiveness of therapy . BASDAI in group 1 was 5.32 3.2 initially and 5.17 2.16 one year after onset of the study , ASDAS 3.45 2.1 and 3.1 1.1 respectively ( p > 0.05 ) . In group 2 , BASDAI values were 5.21 3.0 and 4.77 2.2 ; ASDAS 3.42 2.9 and 2.79 2.6 respectively . In group 3 , BASDAI values were 5.32 3.2 and 3.17 2.12 ; ASDAS 3.44 3.1 and 2.6 1.8 ; p < 0.05 for the differences between initial and subsequent values in groups 2 and 3 and final values for all groups . Positive PASS was reached in 15 patients ( 57.69 % , n = 26 ) of group 3 , in 4 ones ( 20 % , n = 20 ) of group 2 , and in 0 ( 0 % ) patients of group 1 . Five ( 19.23 % ) , 15 ( 75 % ) and 93 ( 96.87 % ) patients in groups 1 , 2 and 3 respectively wilfully ceased to take NSAID . 96 ( 100 % ) , 19 ( 95 % ) and 3 ( 11.5 % ) patients of these groups stated that they needed hospitalization . Telephone monitoring of ax-SpA activity once in every 4 weeks revealed a better compliance with the treatment and results of therapy than active observation every 12 weeks or arbitrary monitoring .
rewrite: This study assessed treatment adherence and therapeutic outcomes in axial spondyloarthritis (ax-SpA) patients under various observational approaches. A total of 168 patients, not on TNF therapy and with a BASDAI ≥4, were randomized into three groups. Traditional observation was used for 96 patients, 26 were seen by a rheumatologist every 12 weeks, and 46 received telephone counseling every 4 weeks. Rheumatologists recorded disease activity measures (BASDAI, ASDAS, PASS, etc.) and therapy effectiveness in all cases. In group 1, BASDAI was 5.32±3.2 at baseline and 5.17±2.16 after one year; ASDAS was 3.45±2.1 and 3.1±1.1, respectively (p>0.05). For group 2, BASDAI values were 5.21±3.0 and 4.77±2.2; ASDAS was 3.42±2.9 and 2.79±2.6. In group 3, BASDAI was 5.32±3.2 and 3.17±2.12; ASDAS was 3.44±3.1 and 2.6±1.8; p<0.05 for differences between initial and follow-up values in groups 2 and 3, and for final values across all groups. A positive PASS was achieved by 15 patients (57.69%, n=26) in group 3, 4 patients (20%, n=20) in group 2, and 0 patients (0%) in group 1. NSAID use was voluntarily discontinued by 5 (19.23%), 15 (75%), and 93 (96.87%) patients in groups 1, 2, and 3, respectively. Hospitalization was reported as necessary by 96 (100%), 19 (95%), and 3 (11.5%) patients in these groups. Telephone monitoring of ax-SpA activity every 4 weeks demonstrated superior treatment compliance and therapy results compared to active observation every 12 weeks or irregular monitoring.

text: The mechanisms by which a ` Mediterranean diet ' reduces cardiovascular disease ( CVD ) burden remain poorly understood . Lycopene is a potent antioxidant found in such diets with evidence suggesting beneficial effects . We wished to investigate the effects of lycopene on the vasculature in CVD patients and separately , in healthy volunteers ( HV ) . We randomised 36 statin treated CVD patients and 36 healthy volunteers in a 21 treatment allocation ratio to either 7 mg lycopene or placebo daily for 2 months in a double-blind trial . Forearm responses to intra-arterial infusions of acetylcholine ( endothelium-dependent vasodilatation ; EDV ) , sodium nitroprusside ( endothelium-independent vasodilatation ; EIDV ) , and NG-monomethyl-L-arginine ( basal nitric oxide ( NO ) synthase activity ) were measured using venous plethysmography . A range of vascular and biochemical secondary endpoints were also explored . EDV in CVD patients post-lycopene improved by 53 % ( 95 % CI : +9 % to +93 % , P = 0.03 vs. placebo ) without changes to EIDV , or basal NO responses . HVs did not show changes in EDV after lycopene treatment . Blood pressure , arterial stiffness , lipids and hsCRP levels were unchanged for lycopene vs. placebo treatment groups in the CVD arm as well as the HV arm . At baseline , CVD patients had impaired EDV compared with HV ( 30 % lower ; 95 % CI : -45 % to -10 % , P = 0.008 ) , despite lower LDL cholesterol ( 1.2 mmol/L lower , 95 % CI : -1.6 to -0.9 mmol/L , P < 0.001 ) . Post-therapy EDV responses for lycopene-treated CVD patients were similar to HVs at baseline ( 2 % lower , 95 % CI : -30 % to +30 % , P = 0.85 ) , also suggesting lycopene improved endothelial function . Lycopene supplementation improves endothelial function in CVD patients on optimal secondary prevention , but not in HVs . ClinicalTrials.gov NCT01100385 .
rewrite: The mechanisms through which a 'Mediterranean diet' lowers cardiovascular disease (CVD) burden are still not fully clear. Lycopene, a strong antioxidant present in such diets, shows evidence of beneficial impacts. We aimed to examine lycopene's effects on the vasculature in CVD patients and, separately, in healthy volunteers (HV). In a double-blind trial, we randomized 36 statin-treated CVD patients and 36 healthy volunteers in a 2:1 allocation to receive either 7 mg lycopene or placebo daily for two months. Using venous plethysmography, we measured forearm responses to intra-arterial infusions of acetylcholine (endothelium-dependent vasodilation; EDV), sodium nitroprusside (endothelium-independent vasodilation; EIDV), and NG-monomethyl-L-arginine (basal nitric oxide synthase activity). Various vascular and biochemical secondary endpoints were also assessed. In CVD patients, EDV improved by 53% after lycopene (95% CI: +9% to +93%, P=0.03 vs. placebo), with no changes in EIDV or basal NO responses. HVs showed no EDV changes following lycopene treatment. Blood pressure, arterial stiffness, lipids, and hsCRP levels remained unchanged for lycopene versus placebo in both the CVD and HV groups. At baseline, CVD patients had impaired EDV compared to HVs (30% lower; 95% CI: -45% to -10%, P=0.008), despite lower LDL cholesterol (1.2 mmol/L lower, 95% CI: -1.6 to -0.9 mmol/L, P<0.001). Post-therapy EDV responses in lycopene-treated CVD patients were comparable to HVs at baseline (2% lower, 95% CI: -30% to +30%, P=0.85), further indicating lycopene enhanced endothelial function. Lycopene supplementation improves endothelial function in CVD patients on optimal secondary prevention, but not in HVs. ClinicalTrials.gov NCT01100385.

text: The first description of the simplified acute physiology score ( SAPS ) II dates back to 1993 , but little is known about its accuracy in daily practice . Our purpose was to evaluate the accuracy of scoring and the factors that affect it in a nationwide survey . Twenty clinical scenarios , covering a broad range of illness severities , were randomly assigned to a convenience sample of physicians or nurses in Swiss adult intensive care units ( ICUs ) , who were asked to assess the SAPS II score for a single scenario . These data were compared to a reference that was defined by five experienced researchers . The results were cross-matched with demographic characteristics and data on the training and quality control for the scoring , structural and organisational properties of each participating ICU . A total of 345 caregivers from 53 adult ICU providers completed the SAPS II evaluation of one clinical scenario . The mean SAPS II scoring was 42.6 23.4 , with a bias of +5.74 ( 95 % CI 2.0-9 .5 ) compared to the reference score . There was no evidence of bias variation according to the case severity , ICU size , linguistic area , profession ( physician vs. nurse ) , experience , initial SAPS II training , or presence of a quality control system . This nationwide survey revealed substantial variability in the SAPS II scoring results . On average , SAPS II scoring was overestimated by more than 13 % , irrespective of the profession or experience of the scorer or of the structural characteristics of the ICUs .
rewrite: The initial documentation of the simplified acute physiology score (SAPS) II originated in 1993, yet its precision in routine clinical use remains poorly understood. This study aimed to assess scoring accuracy and influencing factors through a national survey. Twenty clinical scenarios, representing a wide spectrum of illness severity, were randomly allocated to a convenience sample of physicians or nurses in Swiss adult intensive care units (ICUs). Each participant evaluated the SAPS II score for one assigned scenario. These assessments were then compared against a reference standard established by five expert researchers. Findings were analyzed alongside demographic details, training and quality control data for scoring, and the structural and organizational features of each participating ICU. In total, 345 caregivers from 53 adult ICU providers completed a SAPS II evaluation for one clinical scenario. The mean SAPS II score recorded was 42.6 ± 23.4, showing a bias of +5.74 (95% CI 2.0–9.5) relative to the reference. No significant variation in bias was observed based on case severity, ICU size, language region, profession (physician versus nurse), experience, initial SAPS II training, or the existence of a quality control system. This national survey demonstrated considerable variability in SAPS II scoring outcomes. On average, SAPS II scores were overestimated by over 13%, regardless of the scorer's profession or experience or the ICU's structural attributes.

text: The purpose of this study was to compare secondary intention healing of oral soft tissues after laser surgery with and without the use of a compound containing amino acids and sodium hyaluronate . Sodium hyaluronate has been successfully used in medicine to promote healing . It has not been studied in the healing of laser-produced wounds . Excisional biopsy was performed in oral soft tissues with a potassium-titanyl-phosphate ( KTP ) laser ( 532 nm , SmartLite , DEKA , Florence , Italy ) in 49 patients divided into two groups . In the study group ( SG ) , 31 patients received a compound gel containing four amino acids and sodium hyaluronate ( Aminogam ( ) , Errekappa , Italy ) after laser surgery ; in the control group ( CG ) , 18 subjects received no treatment involving a drug or gel . Numeric rating scale ( NRS ) was used to evaluate pain experienced after surgery [ pain index ( PI ) ] . Using a grid as a benchmark and computer software , the lesion area was measured after surgery ( T0 ) and after 7 days ( T1 ) . A percentage healing index ( PHI ) was calculated indicating healing extension in 7 days . SG cases showed an average PHI of 64.3826.50 , whereas the average PHI in the CG was 47.88 % 27.84 . Mean PI was 2.670.96 for SG and 2.750.86 for CG . A statistically significant difference was detected between the groups for PHI ( p = 0.0447 ) , whereas no difference was detectable for PI ( p = 0.77 ) . The use of a gel containing amino acids and sodium hyaluronate can promote faster healing via secondary intention in laser-induced wounds , although it does not seem to affect pain perception .
rewrite: This study aimed to evaluate secondary intention healing in oral soft tissues following laser surgery, comparing outcomes with and without a gel containing amino acids and sodium hyaluronate. Sodium hyaluronate is known to aid healing in medical applications but had not been assessed for laser-induced wounds. Excisional biopsies were conducted using a KTP laser (532 nm, SmartLite, DEKA, Italy) on 49 patients split into two groups. In the study group (SG) of 31 patients, the amino acid and sodium hyaluronate gel (Aminogam, Errekappa, Italy) was applied post-surgery; the control group (CG) of 18 subjects received no topical treatment. Pain was assessed using a numeric rating scale [pain index (PI)]. Lesion areas were measured immediately after surgery (T0) and at 7 days (T1) via a grid and software, with a percentage healing index (PHI) computed to show healing progression. The SG had an average PHI of 64.38% ± 26.50, compared to 47.88% ± 27.84 in the CG. Mean PI was 2.67 ± 0.96 for SG and 2.75 ± 0.86 for CG. A statistically significant difference in PHI was found between groups (p = 0.0447), but no difference was observed for PI (p = 0.77). The gel containing amino acids and sodium hyaluronate appears to accelerate secondary intention healing in laser wounds, though it does not significantly influence pain perception.

text: To determine the impact of adjunctive Buchang Naoxintong Capsule ( , NXT ) on dual antiplatelet therapy in patients with cytochrome P450 2C19 * 2 ( CYP2C19 * 2 ) polymorphism undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention ( PCI ) . Ninety patients with CYP2C19 * 2 polymorphism were enrolled , and their genotypes were confirmed by polymerase chain reaction ( PCR ) . The patients were randomly assigned to receive either adjunctive NXT ( triple group , 45 cases ) or dual antiplatelet therapy ( dual group , 45 cases ) using a computer-generated randomization sequence and sealed envelopes . Platelet function was assessed at baseline and 7 days after treatment with conventional aggregometry . Subsequent major adverse cardiovascular events ( MACE , including sudden cardiac arrest and acute coronary syndrome ) were recorded during a 12-month follow-up . Baseline platelet function measurements were similar in both groups . After 7 days , percent inhibitions of maximum platelet aggregation and late platelet aggregation were significantly greater in the triple versus dual group ( 42.3 % 16.0 % vs. 20.8 % 15.2 % , P < 0.01 , and 54.7 % 18.3 % vs. 21.5 % 29.2 % , P < 0.01 , respectively ) . During the 12-month follow-up , the rate of subsequent MACE ( 6/45 ) was significantly lower in the triple group compared with the dual group ( 14/45 ; P < 0.05 ) . Adjunctive NXT to maintenance dose clopidogrel ( 75 g ) could enhance the antiplatelet effect and decrease subsequent MACE in patients with the CYP2C19 * 2 polymorphism undergoing PCI .
rewrite: This study evaluated the effect of adding Buchang Naoxintong Capsule (NXT) to dual antiplatelet therapy in PCI patients with the CYP2C19*2 polymorphism. Ninety patients with confirmed CYP2C19*2 genotypes via PCR were randomized using a computer-generated sequence and sealed envelopes into two groups: a triple therapy group (45 cases) receiving adjunctive NXT, and a dual therapy group (45 cases). Platelet function was measured by conventional aggregometry at baseline and after 7 days of treatment. Major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), including sudden cardiac arrest and acute coronary syndrome, were recorded over a 12-month follow-up. Baseline platelet function was comparable between groups. At day 7, the triple group showed significantly greater percent inhibition of maximum platelet aggregation (42.3% ± 16.0% vs. 20.8% ± 15.2%, P < 0.01) and late platelet aggregation (54.7% ± 18.3% vs. 21.5% ± 29.2%, P < 0.01) compared to the dual group. Over 12 months, the triple group had a significantly lower MACE rate (6/45) than the dual group (14/45; P < 0.05). Adding NXT to maintenance-dose clopidogrel (75 mg) enhanced antiplatelet effects and reduced subsequent MACE in CYP2C19*2 polymorphism patients undergoing PCI.

text: To explore the effect of single-dose dexmedetomidine on recovery period after sevoflurane anesthesia with spontaneous respiration in pediatric patients undergoing cleft lip and palate repair . A total of 60 American Society of Anesthesiologists ( ASA ) I-II pediatric patients undergoing cleft lip and palate repair from October to December 2013 were randomly divided into groups D and C ( n = 30 each ) . Dexmedetomidine 0.5 g/kg ( group D ) or an equal volume of normal saline ( group C ) was ad ministered intravenously over a period of 10 min at 30 min before the end of surgery . Anesthesia was induced and maintained with sevoflurane under spontaneous ventilation . Heart rate , mean arterial pressure ( MAP ) , hemoglobin oxygen saturation ( SpO2 ) , respiratory rate , tidal volume ( VT ) and pressure of end-tidal carbon dioxide ( PETCO2 ) were recorded at the time before induction ( T0 ) , 30 min before the end of surgery ( T1 ) , 20 min before the end of surgery ( T2 ) , 15 min before the end of surgery ( T3 ) , 10 min before the end of surgery ( T4 ) , the end of surgery ( T5 ) , extubation ( T6 ) , 5 min after transferal into post-anesthesia care unit ( PACU ) ( T7 ) , 1 h after surgery ( T8 ) , extubation time , length of PACU stay , fentanyl consumption and adverse events were all recorded . The incidence and severity of coughing and emergence agitation were assessed . Compared to T0 , MAP and heart rate at T1 to T5 all decreased in two groups ( P < 0.05 ) . MAP and heart rate at T6 both increased in two groups and group C was higher than group D ( P < 0.05 ) . No inter-group differences existed in SpO2 , respiratory rate , VT or PETCO2 . The incidence of coughing and emergence agitation ( 30 % and 13.3 % ) , fentanyl consumption of group D ( 0.8 2.1 g ) were all significantly lower than that of group C [ ( 66.7 % vs 56.7 % ) and ( 4.9 6.50 ) g , P < 0.05 ] . Length of PACU stay in group D was shorter than that in group C [ ( 15 6 ) vs ( 23 19 ) min , P < 0.05 ] . No inter-group difference existed in extubation time or adverse events . A single intravenous dose of dexmedetomidine is effective in reducing emergence agitation and coughing , shortening length of PACU stay and improving the quality of recovery period after sevoflurane anesthesia in pediatric patients undergoing cleft lip and palate repair .
rewrite: This study investigated the impact of a single dose of dexmedetomidine on recovery quality following sevoflurane anesthesia with spontaneous breathing in children undergoing cleft lip and palate surgery. Sixty ASA I-II pediatric patients scheduled for this repair between October and December 2013 were randomly assigned to either group D or group C (30 per group). At 30 minutes before surgery concluded, group D received intravenous dexmedetomidine (0.5 µg/kg) over 10 minutes, while group C received an equivalent volume of saline. Anesthesia was induced and maintained using sevoflurane under spontaneous ventilation. Measurements of heart rate, mean arterial pressure (MAP), hemoglobin oxygen saturation (SpO₂), respiratory rate, tidal volume (VT), and end-tidal carbon dioxide pressure (PETCO₂) were taken at multiple time points: before induction (T0), 30 min (T1), 20 min (T2), 15 min (T3), and 10 min (T4) before surgery end, at surgery end (T5), at extubation (T6), 5 min after PACU arrival (T7), and 1 hour post-surgery (T8). Extubation time, PACU stay duration, fentanyl use, and adverse events were also documented. Coughing and emergence agitation incidence and severity were evaluated. Relative to T0, MAP and heart rate from T1 to T5 decreased in both groups (P < 0.05). At T6, MAP and heart rate increased in both groups, with higher values in group C versus group D (P < 0.05). No significant differences were observed between groups for SpO₂, respiratory rate, VT, or PETCO₂. Group D exhibited significantly lower rates of coughing and emergence agitation (30% and 13.3%), along with reduced fentanyl consumption (0.8 ± 2.1 µg), compared to group C (66.7%, 56.7%, and 4.9 ± 6.50 µg, respectively; P < 0.05). PACU stay was shorter for group D (15 ± 6 min) than for group C (23 ± 19 min) (P < 0.05). Extubation time and adverse event rates showed no significant inter-group differences. A single intravenous dose of dexmedetomidine effectively reduces emergence agitation and coughing, shortens PACU stay, and enhances recovery quality after sevoflurane anesthesia in pediatric cleft lip and palate repair patients.

text: The metabolism of alcohol and cognitive functions can vary during the menstrual cycle . Also , both alcohol ingestion and hormonal variations during menstruation have been associated with characteristic changes in electroencephalographic ( EEG ) activity . AIM . To determine whether EEG activity during a working memory task is affected by acute alcohol consumption , and if these EEG patterns vary in relation to different phases of the menstrual cycle . 24 women who drank a moderate dose of alcohol or placebo during the follicular and early luteal phases of the menstrual cycle . The EEG activity was recorded during performance of viso-spatial working memory task . Although the alcohol did not deteriorate the performance of working memory task , it caused in the EEG a decrease of relative theta power and lower right fronto-parietal correlation in theta and alpha2 bands . Only women who drank alcohol in the follicular phase had a higher relative potency of alpha1 , which could indicate a lower level of arousal and attention . These results contribute to a better understanding of the brain mechanisms underlying cognitive changes with alcohol and its relationship to the menstrual cycle .
rewrite: Alcohol metabolism and cognitive functions may fluctuate across the menstrual cycle. Additionally, alcohol intake and hormonal shifts during menstruation are linked to distinct alterations in electroencephalographic (EEG) activity. This study aimed to assess whether EEG activity during a working memory task is influenced by acute alcohol consumption and whether these EEG responses differ by menstrual cycle phase. Twenty-four women consumed a moderate alcohol dose or a placebo during the follicular and early luteal phases. EEG was monitored during a visuospatial working memory task. While alcohol did not impair task performance, it led to reduced relative theta power and diminished right fronto-parietal correlation in theta and alpha2 bands in the EEG. Only women who drank alcohol in the follicular phase showed increased relative alpha1 power, possibly reflecting lower arousal and attention. These findings enhance insight into the neural mechanisms of alcohol-related cognitive shifts and their interaction with the menstrual cycle.

text: To determine if brief primary care interventions can affect children 's media viewing habits and exposure to violence . English - and Spanish-speaking parents of 2 - to 12-year-old children presenting to a pediatric primary care clinic participated in a randomized controlled trial . There were 2 intervention groups ; one group viewed 5 minutes from the Play Nicely program and another received a handout , `` Pulling the Plug on TV Violence . '' There were 2 control groups ; the primary control group received standard primary care , and the alternative control group viewed a program about obesity prevention . The outcome measure was parental report of changes in media viewing habits and changes in exposure to violence . A total of 312 of 443 parents who were randomized completed a 2-week follow-up survey . Compared with the primary control group , parents in the video intervention group were more likely to report a change in their children 's media viewing habits ( odds ratio [ OR ] 3.29 ; 95 % confidence interval [ CI ] 1.66-6 .51 ) and a change in their children 's exposure to violence ( OR 4.26 ; 95 % CI 1.95-9 .27 ) . Compared with the primary control group , parents in the handout group were more likely to report a change in their children 's media viewing habits ( OR 4.35 ; 95 % CI 2.20-8 .60 ) and a change in their children 's exposure to violence ( OR 3.35 ; 95 % CI 1.52-7 .35 ) . Brief primary care interventions can affect children 's media viewing habits and children 's exposure to violence . These results have implications for how to improve primary care services related to decreasing children 's media exposure and violence prevention .
rewrite: This study assessed whether brief primary care interventions could influence children's media viewing habits and exposure to violence. English- and Spanish-speaking parents of children aged 2 to 12 attending a pediatric primary care clinic were enrolled in a randomized controlled trial. Two intervention groups were included: one watched a 5-minute segment from the Play Nicely program, while the other received a handout titled "Pulling the Plug on TV Violence." Two control groups were also used: the primary control group received standard primary care, and an alternative control group viewed a program on obesity prevention. Outcomes were measured by parental reports of changes in media viewing habits and exposure to violence. Of 443 randomized parents, 312 completed a 2-week follow-up survey. Compared to the primary control group, parents in the video intervention group were more likely to report changes in their children's media viewing habits (odds ratio [OR] 3.29; 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.66–6.51) and changes in exposure to violence (OR 4.26; 95% CI 1.95–9.27). Similarly, compared to the primary control group, parents in the handout group were more likely to report changes in media viewing habits (OR 4.35; 95% CI 2.20–8.60) and changes in exposure to violence (OR 3.35; 95% CI 1.52–7.35). Brief primary care interventions can impact children's media viewing habits and exposure to violence. These findings suggest ways to enhance primary care services aimed at reducing children's media exposure and preventing violence.

text: Non-invasive near-infrared spectroscopy ( NIRS ) offers the possibility to determine regional cerebral oxygen saturation ( rSO2 ) in patients with cardiac arrest . Limited data from recent studies indicate a potential for early prediction of neurological outcome . Sixty cardiac arrest patients were prospectively enrolled , 22 in-hospital cardiac arrest ( IHCA ) and 38 out-of-hospital cardiac arrest ( OHCA ) patients respectively . NIRS of frontal brain was started after return of spontaneous circulation ( ROSC ) during admission to ICU and was continued until normothermia . Outcome was determined at ICU discharge by the Pittsburgh Cerebral Performance Category ( CPC ) and 6 months after cardiac arrest . A good outcome ( CPC 1-2 ) was achieved in 23 ( 38 % ) patients , while 37 ( 62 % ) had a poor outcome ( CPC 3-5 ) . Patients with good outcome had significantly higher rSO2 levels ( CPC 1-2 : rSO2 68 % ; CPC 3-5 : rSO2 58 % ; p < 0.01 ) . For good and poor outcome median rSO2 within the first 24h period was 66 % and 59 % respectively and for the following 16h period 68 % and 59 % ( p < 0.01 ) . Outcome prediction by area of rSO2 below a critical threshold of rsO2 = 50 % within the first 40h yielded 70 % specificity and 86 % sensitivity for poor outcome . On average , rSO2 within the first 40h after ROSC is significantly lower in patients with poor outcome , but rSO2 ranges largely overlap between outcome groups . Our data indicate limited potential for prediction of poor outcome by frontal brain rSO2 measurements .
rewrite: Non-invasive near-infrared spectroscopy (NIRS) enables the assessment of regional cerebral oxygen saturation (rSO2) in cardiac arrest patients. Recent studies with limited data suggest its potential for early neurological outcome prediction. Sixty cardiac arrest patients were prospectively enrolled, including 22 in-hospital (IHCA) and 38 out-of-hospital (OHCA) cases. Frontal brain NIRS monitoring began after return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC) upon ICU admission and continued until normothermia. Outcome was assessed at ICU discharge using the Pittsburgh Cerebral Performance Category (CPC) and six months post-arrest. A good outcome (CPC 1-2) was observed in 23 (38%) patients, while 37 (62%) had a poor outcome (CPC 3-5). Patients with good outcomes showed significantly higher rSO2 levels (CPC 1-2: 68%; CPC 3-5: 58%; p<0.01). Median rSO2 in the first 24 hours was 66% for good and 59% for poor outcomes, and 68% versus 59% in the subsequent 16 hours (p<0.01). Predicting outcome based on rSO2 below a critical threshold of 50% within the initial 40 hours achieved 70% specificity and 86% sensitivity for poor outcome. On average, rSO2 in the first 40 hours post-ROSC is significantly lower in poor-outcome patients, though rSO2 ranges substantially overlap between groups. Our findings indicate limited utility of frontal brain rSO2 measurements for predicting poor outcomes.

text: We examined the impact of school water , sanitation , and hygiene ( WASH ) interventions on diarrhea-related outcomes among younger siblings of school-going children . We conducted a cluster-randomized trial among 185 schools in Kenya from 2007 to 2009 . We assigned schools to 1 of 2 study groups according to water availability . Multilevel logistic regression models , adjusted for baseline measures , assessed differences between intervention and control arms in 1-week period prevalence of diarrhea and 2-week period prevalence of clinic visits among children younger than 5 years with at least 1 sibling attending a program school . Among water-scarce schools , comprehensive WASH improvements were associated with decreased odds of diarrhea ( odds ratio [ OR ] = 0.44 ; 95 % confidence interval [ CI ] = 0.27 , 0.73 ) and visiting a clinic ( OR = 0.36 ; 95 % CI = 0.19 , 0.68 ) , relative to control schools . In our separate study group of schools with greater water availability , school hygiene promotion and water treatment interventions and school sanitation improvements were not associated with differences in diarrhea prevalence between intervention and control schools . In water-scarce areas , school WASH interventions that include robust water supply improvements can reduce diarrheal diseases among young children .
rewrite: We investigated the effects of school water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH) programs on diarrhea outcomes in younger siblings of enrolled students. A cluster-randomized trial was carried out across 185 Kenyan schools between 2007 and 2009. Schools were categorized into one of two groups based on water availability. Using multilevel logistic regression adjusted for baseline data, we compared intervention and control schools on 1-week diarrhea prevalence and 2-week clinic visit prevalence among children under 5 years with a sibling in a program school. In water-scarce schools, comprehensive WASH upgrades were linked to reduced odds of diarrhea (OR = 0.44; 95% CI = 0.27, 0.73) and clinic visits (OR = 0.36; 95% CI = 0.19, 0.68) compared to controls. Among schools with better water access, hygiene promotion, water treatment, and sanitation improvements showed no significant difference in diarrhea prevalence between intervention and control groups. In water-scarce settings, school WASH interventions that incorporate substantial water supply enhancements can lower diarrheal disease in young children.

text: Erosive degenerative disc disease , also known as Modic type 1 changes , is usually characterized by low back pain with an inflammatory pain pattern , as seen in spondyloarthropathies . Intravenous pamidronate has proven to be effective in patients with ankylosing spondylitis who are refractory to nonsteroidal antiinflammatory drugs , and in painful bone diseases in general , such as Paget 's disease , fibrous dysplasia or vertebral fractures . We therefore hypothesize that pamidronate would be effective in treating low back pain associated with Modic type 1 changes . This study , called PEPTIDE ( short for the French title `` Etude Prospective sur l'Efficacit et la tolrance du PamidronaTe dans les dIscopathies Degeneratives Erosives '' ) , will be a double-blind , randomized , placebo-controlled , parallel group , phase two clinical trial . A total of 48 patients will be recruited . These patients will be randomly assigned to one of the two groups , with 24 patients in each group : one group will be given pamidronate and the other a placebo . Pamidronate will be administered at a dose of 90mg per day for two days consecutively , and every patient , irrespective of treatment group , will be given paracetamol to maintain blinding by preventing drug-induced fever . The primary outcome measure is a between-group difference of 30 points on a 100mm Visual Analogue Scale ( VAS ) at three months . Secondary outcome measures are improvement in functional status and the drug 's safety . Primary and secondary outcome measures will be assessed at each visit ( inclusion , at six weeks , three months , and six months ) . If the primary goal is not attained , the patient will be offered a rigid or semi-rigid back brace , irrespective of the treatment group . To date , only local treatments , for example intradiscal corticosteroid therapy , lumbar arthrodesis or back braces have been studied in randomized , controlled trials , with controversial results . This trial is currently ongoing and , if conclusive , should provide physicians with an acceptable alternative to those treatments . The results should be publicly available in spring 2015 . ClinicalTrials.gov number , NCT01799616 .
rewrite: Erosive degenerative disc disease, referred to as Modic type 1 changes, typically presents as low back pain with an inflammatory pattern, similar to spondyloarthropathies. Intravenous pamidronate has shown efficacy in ankylosing spondylitis patients unresponsive to NSAIDs, as well as in painful bone conditions like Paget's disease, fibrous dysplasia, or vertebral fractures. Consequently, we propose that pamidronate may be effective for low back pain linked to Modic type 1 changes.
