The lifestyle intervention failed to promote a shift toward more beneficial physical behavior in adolescents and young adults with spastic CP.

text: Zinc plays a role in skin health , and preliminary data have shown its beneficial effects for melasma . We compared the effect of topical zinc with that of hydroquinone as the standard treatment on severity of melasma . Ninety-three women with melasma were randomized to receive zinc sulfate 10 % or hydroquinone 4 % solutions once daily for 2months . They were followed for an additional 3months while using sunscreen . The severity of melasma was assessed at baseline and at 2 and 5months using the Melasma Area and Severity Index ( MASI ) . Eighty-two patients completed the study . The MASI score fell significantly in both groups , but a greater decrease was seen in those who received hydroquinone ( 43.515.5 % vs 18.620.8 % , p < .001 ) . Postinflammatory pigmentation occurred in 5.2 % of the zinc group and irritation in 30.9 % of the hydroquinone group . Topical zinc therapy is not highly effective in reducing the severity of melasma , but further trials are needed to determine whether adding zinc to current topical treatments could improve treatment response .
rewrite: Zinc contributes to skin health, and initial findings indicate its potential benefits for melasma. We evaluated the impact of topical zinc versus hydroquinone, the standard treatment, on melasma severity. Ninety-three women with melasma were randomly assigned to apply either 10% zinc sulfate or 4% hydroquinone solution once daily for two months. They were then monitored for an extra three months while using sunscreen. Melasma severity was measured at the start, after two months, and after five months using the Melasma Area and Severity Index (MASI). Eighty-two participants finished the study. MASI scores dropped significantly in both groups, but a larger reduction was observed in the hydroquinone group (43.5±15.5% vs. 18.6±20.8%, p < .001). Postinflammatory pigmentation affected 5.2% of the zinc group, while irritation occurred in 30.9% of the hydroquinone group. Topical zinc is not highly effective in lessening melasma severity, but additional studies are required to assess if combining zinc with existing topical treatments could enhance therapeutic outcomes.

text: In this study we tried to assess the efficacy of topical emollients in the treatment of patients with PUVA-induced pruritus . 41 patients over 18 years of age , who received PUVA treatment in the phototherapy unit , were included in the study . Patients were randomly divided into two groups ; Group I was administered with a 4 % urea lotion and Group II was administered with liquid petrolatum . The follow-up period was minimum 4 weeks . During the first 2 weeks , patients were administered topical emollients and received PUVA treatment together . The next 2 weeks , they continued PUVA treatment without any medication . When time-dependent changes in the visual analogue scale scores for pruritus of both groups were considered , both treatment methods were found to be remarkably successful ( p < 0.0001 ) . In addition , an insignificant group-time interaction was identified ( p = 0.753 ) . Topical emollients were found to be effective in the treatment of PUVA-induced pruritus . Both forms of medication can be successfully administered and increase the patient 's compliance with medication .
rewrite: This study evaluated the effectiveness of topical emollients for treating PUVA-induced pruritus. Forty-one adult patients receiving PUVA therapy in a phototherapy unit were enrolled. Participants were randomly assigned to two groups: Group I received a 4% urea lotion, while Group II was given liquid petrolatum. The follow-up duration was at least four weeks. For the initial two weeks, patients applied the topical emollients alongside their PUVA sessions. Over the subsequent two weeks, they continued PUVA treatment without any topical medication. Analysis of time-dependent changes in visual analogue scale scores for pruritus revealed that both treatments were highly effective (p < 0.0001). Moreover, a non-significant group-time interaction was observed (p = 0.753). Topical emollients proved effective in managing PUVA-induced pruritus. Both formulations can be used successfully and help improve patient adherence to treatment.

text: Individuals on hemodialysis have low physical function and activity levels . Clinical trials have shown improvements in these parameters with exercise programming . Pedometers have not been extensively evaluated in individuals on hemodialysis . This randomized clinical trial compared the effects of intradialytic cycling versus a pedometer program on physical function , physical activity and quality of life . Sixty patients were randomly assigned to two study groups . The ergometer group cycled during each hemodialysis session for 24 weeks . Pedometer participants followed a home-based walking program for 24 weeks . The primary outcome was aerobic capacity [ VO2peak and 6-minute walk ( 6MW ) test ] . Secondary outcomes included lower extremity strength [ sit-to-stand ( SS ) test ] , flexibility [ sit-and-reach ( SR ) test ] , physical activity ( accelerometer ) and health-related quality of life . Measurements were collected at baseline and at 12 and 24 weeks . At 12 and 24 weeks , there was no significant change in the VO2peak or 6MW test between or within study groups . SS testing in the ergometer group improved from 10.2 ( SD 3.4 ) to 11.4 ( SD 2.5 ) cycles from baseline to 24 weeks ( P < 0.005 ) . Similarly , in the pedometer group , SS cycles improved from 10.1 ( SD 3.3 ) to 12.2 ( SD 3.5 ) ( P < 0.005 ) . The SR test also significantly improved over time in both the study groups . No significant changes were noted for other secondary outcomes . Both intradialytic cycling and pedometer programming improved aspects of physical function . Neither intervention had a significant effect on aerobic capacity . No significant differences in any outcomes were identified between interventions groups .
rewrite: Patients undergoing hemodialysis often exhibit reduced physical function and activity. Exercise programs have been shown in clinical trials to enhance these measures. The use of pedometers has not been widely studied in this population. This randomized trial assessed the impact of intradialytic cycling versus a pedometer-based regimen on physical function, activity, and quality of life. Sixty participants were randomly allocated to two groups. The ergometer group cycled during each dialysis session over 24 weeks. The pedometer group adhered to a home walking program for the same duration. The primary endpoint was aerobic capacity, measured by VO2peak and the 6-minute walk test. Secondary outcomes involved lower limb strength via sit-to-stand testing, flexibility through sit-and-reach, physical activity via accelerometer, and health-related quality of life. Assessments were conducted at baseline, 12 weeks, and 24 weeks. At 12 and 24 weeks, no significant changes in VO2peak or 6MW test results were observed within or between groups. Sit-to-stand performance in the ergometer group increased from 10.2 (SD 3.4) to 11.4 (SD 2.5) cycles from baseline to 24 weeks (P < 0.005). In the pedometer group, it rose from 10.1 (SD 3.3) to 12.2 (SD 3.5) cycles (P < 0.005). The sit-and-reach test also showed significant improvement over time in both groups. Other secondary outcomes did not change significantly. Both intradialytic cycling and pedometer programs enhanced certain aspects of physical function. Neither intervention significantly affected aerobic capacity. No significant differences in outcomes were found between the two intervention groups.

text: Endotoxaemia is widely used as an experimental model to study sepsis under controlled conditions . Nighttime endotoxaemia induces a more pronounced inflammatory stress response compared to daytime . Previously , we have shown that melatonin has antioxidative and anti-inflammatory effects in inflammatory response to daytime endotoxaemia . Herein , we examined the effect of melatonin in response to human nighttime endotoxaemia . Twelve healthy male volunteers were enrolled in a randomized , placebo-controlled , double-blinded cross-over trial . Subjects were induced by lipopolysaccharide ( LPS ) endotoxin 0.3 ng/kg body weight intravenously at 24:00 . One hour prior to induction of endotoxaemia , an 8-h infusion of melatonin 100 mg or placebo was initiated . Blood samples were drawn before and 2 , 4 , 6 and 8 h after induction of endotoxaemia and plasma was tested for pro-inflammatory markers ( tumor necrosis factor alpha , TNF - , interleukin-1 , IL-1 , interleukin-1 , IL-6 , and YKL-40 ) , anti-inflammatory markers ( interleukin-1 receptor antagonist , IL-1Ra , interleukin-10 , IL-10 , soluble tumor necrosis factor receptors I and II , sTNF-RI and sTNF-RII ) , marker for oxidative damage ( malondialdehyde ( MDA ) ) and antioxidative enzyme ( ascorbic acid ( AA ) and dehydroascorbic acid ( DHA ) ) . Compared to placebo , melatonin did not reduce plasma levels of any of pro- and anti-inflammatory markers and it also failed to influence levels of AA , DHA and MDA . Melatonin has no beneficial effect on inflammation and oxidative damage induced by nighttime endotoxaemia in contrast to daytime endotoxaemia .
rewrite: Endotoxaemia is commonly employed as an experimental model to investigate sepsis in controlled settings. Nighttime endotoxaemia triggers a stronger inflammatory stress response than daytime exposure. Prior research has demonstrated melatonin's antioxidative and anti-inflammatory properties during daytime endotoxaemia. In this study, we assessed melatonin's impact on human nighttime endotoxaemia. Twelve healthy male volunteers participated in a randomized, placebo-controlled, double-blinded crossover trial. Participants received an intravenous lipopolysaccharide (LPS) endotoxin dose of 0.3 ng/kg body weight at midnight. An 8-hour infusion of 100 mg melatonin or placebo began one hour before endotoxaemia induction. Blood samples were collected before and at 2, 4, 6, and 8 hours post-induction, with plasma analyzed for pro-inflammatory markers (tumor necrosis factor alpha, TNF-α, interleukin-1β, IL-1β, interleukin-6, IL-6, and YKL-40), anti-inflammatory markers (interleukin-1 receptor antagonist, IL-1Ra, interleukin-10, IL-10, soluble tumor necrosis factor receptors I and II, sTNF-RI and sTNF-RII), a marker for oxidative damage (malondialdehyde, MDA), and antioxidative enzymes (ascorbic acid, AA, and dehydroascorbic acid, DHA). Compared to placebo, melatonin did not lower plasma levels of any pro- or anti-inflammatory markers and also did not affect AA, DHA, or MDA levels. Melatonin shows no beneficial effect on inflammation and oxidative damage from nighttime endotoxaemia, unlike its effects in daytime conditions.

text: Growth Hormone ( GH ) dosage in childhood is adjusted for body size , but there is no consensus whether body weight ( BW ) or body surface area ( BSA ) should be used . We aimed at comparing the biological effect and cost-effectiveness of GH treatment dosed per m2 BSA in comparison with dosing per kg BW in girls with Turner syndrome ( TS ) . Serum IGF-I , GH dose , and adult height gain ( AHG ) from girls participating in two Dutch and five Swedish studies on the efficacy of GH were analyzed , and the cumulative GH dose and costs were calculated for both dose adjustment methods . Additional medication included estrogens ( if no spontaneous puberty occurred ) and oxandrolone in some studies . At each GH dose , the serum IGF-I standard deviation score remained stable over time after an initial increase after the start of treatment . On a high dose ( at 1 m2 equivalent to 0.056-0 .067 mg/kg/day ) , AHG was at least equal on GH dosed per m2 BSA compared with dosing per kg BW . The cumulative dose and cost were significantly lower if the GH dose was adjusted for m2 BSA . Dosing GH per m2 BSA is at least as efficacious as dosing per kg BW , and is more cost-effective .
rewrite: Growth hormone (GH) dosing in children is tailored to body size, yet no agreement exists on using body weight (BW) or body surface area (BSA). This study compared the biological impact and cost-effectiveness of GH treatment dosed per m² BSA versus per kg BW in girls with Turner syndrome (TS). We analyzed serum IGF-I levels, GH doses, and adult height gain (AHG) from participants in two Dutch and five Swedish studies on GH efficacy, calculating cumulative GH doses and costs for both dosing approaches. Some studies also included estrogens (for absent spontaneous puberty) and oxandrolone. At each GH dose, serum IGF-I standard deviation scores stabilized over time following an initial rise after treatment began. On a high dose (equivalent to 0.056–0.067 mg/kg/day per m²), AHG was at least comparable with GH dosed per m² BSA relative to per kg BW. Cumulative dose and cost were significantly lower when adjusting GH for m² BSA. Dosing GH per m² BSA is at least as effective as per kg BW and more cost-efficient.

text: To describe the effects of six interventions for menopausal vasomotor symptoms relative to control in a pooled analysis , facilitating translation of the results for clinicians and symptomatic women . The Menopause Strategies : Finding Lasting Answers for Symptoms and Health network tested these interventions in three randomized clinical trials . An analysis of pooled individual-level data from three randomized clinical trials is presented . Participants were 899 perimenopausal and postmenopausal women with at least 14 bothersome vasomotor symptoms per week . Interventions included 10-20 mg escitalopram per day , nonaerobic yoga , aerobic exercise , 1.8 g per day omega-3 fatty acid supplementation , 0.5 mg low-dose oral 17-beta-estradiol ( E2 ) per day , and 75 mg low-dose venlafaxine XR per day . The main outcome measures were changes from baseline in mean daily vasomotor symptom frequency and bother during 8-12 weeks of treatment . Linear regression models estimated differences in outcomes between each intervention and corresponding control group adjusted for baseline characteristics . Models included trial-specific intercepts , effects of the baseline outcome measure , and time . The 8-week reduction in vasomotor symptom frequency from baseline relative to placebo was similar for escitalopram at -1.4 per day ( 95 % confidence interval [ CI ] -2.7 to -0.2 ) , low-dose E2 at -2.4 ( 95 % CI -3.4 to -1.3 ) , and venlafaxine at -1.8 ( 95 % CI -2.8 to -0.8 ) ; vasomotor symptom bother reduction was minimal and did not vary across these three pharmacologic interventions ( mean -0.2 to -0.3 relative to placebo ) . No effects on vasomotor symptom frequency or bother were seen with aerobic exercise , yoga , or omega-3 supplements . These analyses suggest that escitalopram , low-dose E2 , and venlafaxine provide comparable , modest reductions in vasomotor symptom frequency and bother among women with moderate hot flushes . ClinicalTrials.gov , www.clinicaltrials.gov , NCT00894543 ( MsFLASH 01 ) , NCT01178892 ( MsFLASH 02 ) , and NCT01418209 ( MsFLASH 03 ) .
rewrite: To evaluate the impact of six treatments for menopausal vasomotor symptoms compared to control in a combined analysis, aiding clinicians and affected women in interpreting the findings. The Menopause Strategies: Finding Lasting Answers for Symptoms and Health network examined these treatments across three randomized clinical trials. This report details a pooled analysis of individual-level data from these three randomized clinical trials. The study involved 899 perimenopausal and postmenopausal women experiencing at least 14 troublesome vasomotor symptoms weekly. Treatments comprised daily doses of 10-20 mg escitalopram, nonaerobic yoga, aerobic exercise, 1.8 g omega-3 fatty acid supplements, 0.5 mg low-dose oral 17-beta-estradiol (E2), and 75 mg low-dose venlafaxine XR. Primary outcomes were changes from baseline in mean daily vasomotor symptom frequency and bother over 8-12 weeks of treatment. Linear regression models assessed outcome differences between each treatment and its control group, adjusting for baseline traits. Models incorporated trial-specific intercepts, baseline outcome effects, and time. Over 8 weeks, reductions in vasomotor symptom frequency relative to placebo were comparable for escitalopram at -1.4 daily (95% CI -2.7 to -0.2), low-dose E2 at -2.4 (95% CI -3.4 to -1.3), and venlafaxine at -1.8 (95% CI -2.8 to -0.8); reductions in symptom bother were slight and consistent across these three drug treatments (mean -0.2 to -0.3 versus placebo). Aerobic exercise, yoga, and omega-3 supplements showed no effects on vasomotor symptom frequency or bother. These results indicate that escitalopram, low-dose E2, and venlafaxine offer similar, moderate reductions in vasomotor symptom frequency and bother for women with moderate hot flushes. ClinicalTrials.gov identifiers: NCT00894543 (MsFLASH 01), NCT01178892 (MsFLASH 02), and NCT01418209 (MsFLASH 03).

text: Few studies have examined consumer acceptability or comprehension of cholesterol-lowering claims on food labels . Our objective was to assess consumer attitudes and understanding of cholesterol-lowering claims regarding plant sterols ( PS ) and oat fibre ( OF ) . We conducted two studies on : ( 1 ) PS claims and ( 2 ) OF claims . Both studies involved a randomized mock-packaged experiment within an online survey administered to Canadian consumers . In the PS study ( n = 721 ) , we tested three PS-related claims ( disease risk reduction claim , function claim and nutrient content claim ) and a ` tastes great ' claim ( control ) on identical margarine containers . Similarly , in the OF study ( n = 710 ) , we tested three claims related to OF and a ` taste great ' claim on identical cereal boxes . In both studies , participants answered the same set of questions on attitudes and understanding of claims after seeing each mock package . All claims that mentioned either PS or OF resulted in more positive attitudes than the taste control claim ( P < 0.0001 ) , despite all products within each study having the same nutrition profile . How consumers responded to the nutrition claims between the two studies was influenced by contextual factors such as familiarity with the functional food/component and the food product that carried the claim . Permitted nutrition claims are approved based on physiological evidence and are allowed on any food product as long as it meets the associated nutrient criteria . However , it is difficult to generalize attitudes and understanding of claims when they are so highly dependent on contextual factors .
rewrite: Limited research has explored how consumers perceive or interpret cholesterol-reduction statements on food packaging. Our aim was to evaluate consumer perspectives and comprehension of claims concerning plant sterols (PS) and oat fibre (OF). Two investigations were carried out: one focused on PS claims and the other on OF claims. Each study utilized a randomized, simulated packaging design within an online survey of Canadian consumers. For the PS research (n = 721), three types of PS claims (disease risk reduction, function, and nutrient content) and a "tastes great" control claim were displayed on matching margarine packages. Likewise, the OF study (n = 710) tested three OF-related claims and a "tastes great" control on identical cereal boxes. Participants in both studies answered identical questions about their attitudes and understanding after viewing each mock package. All claims referencing PS or OF led to more favorable attitudes compared to the taste control (P < 0.0001), even though nutrition profiles were consistent across products within each study. Consumer reactions to the nutrition claims varied between studies, affected by contextual elements like familiarity with the functional food/ingredient and the product bearing the claim. Authorized nutrition claims are permitted based on physiological proof and can appear on any qualifying food product meeting specific nutrient standards. Yet, generalizing attitudes and comprehension of such claims remains challenging due to their strong reliance on contextual factors.

text: To evaluate the effect of a topical , nonsteroidal antiinflammatory drug , nepafenac 0.1 % , in eyes with noncentral diabetic macular edema . Multicenter , double-masked randomized trial . Individuals with good visual acuity and noncentral-involved diabetic macular edema were randomly assigned to nepafenac 0.1 % ( N = 61 ) or placebo ( nepafenac vehicle , N = 64 ) 3 times a day for 12 months . The primary outcome was mean change in optical coherence tomography retinal volume at 12 months . Mean baseline retinal volume was 7.8 mm . At 12 months , in the nepafenac and placebo groups respectively , mean change in retinal volume was -0.03 mm and -0.02 mm ( treatment group difference : -0.02 , 95 % confidence interval : -0.27 to 0.23 , P = 0.89 ) . Central-involved diabetic macular edema was present in 7 eyes ( 11 % ) and 9 eyes ( 14 % ) at the 12-month visit ( P = 0.79 ) , respectively . No differences in visual acuity outcomes were identified . One study participant developed a corneal melt after using nepafenac in the nonstudy eye , which had a history of severe dry eye . No additional safety concerns were evident . In eyes with noncentral diabetic macular edema and good visual acuity , topical nepafenac 0.1 % 3 times daily for 1 year likely does not have a meaningful effect on optical coherence tomography-measured retinal thickness .
rewrite: To assess the impact of a topical, nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory medication, nepafenac 0.1%, on eyes affected by noncentral diabetic macular edema. A multicenter, double-masked randomized trial was conducted. Participants with good visual acuity and noncentral-involved diabetic macular edema were randomly allocated to receive either nepafenac 0.1% (N = 61) or a placebo (nepafenac vehicle, N = 64) three times daily over 12 months. The primary endpoint was the average change in optical coherence tomography retinal volume at 12 months. Baseline mean retinal volume was 7.8 mm. After 12 months, the mean change in retinal volume was -0.03 mm in the nepafenac group and -0.02 mm in the placebo group (treatment group difference: -0.02, 95% confidence interval: -0.27 to 0.23, P = 0.89). Central-involved diabetic macular edema was observed in 7 eyes (11%) and 9 eyes (14%) at the 12-month visit (P = 0.79), respectively. No differences in visual acuity outcomes were found. One participant experienced a corneal melt after using nepafenac in the nonstudy eye, which had a history of severe dry eye. No further safety issues were apparent. In eyes with noncentral diabetic macular edema and good visual acuity, topical nepafenac 0.1% administered three times daily for one year likely does not produce a significant effect on retinal thickness as measured by optical coherence tomography.

text: Chronic Low Back Pain is a complex syndrome with multifactorial bio-psycho-social etiology and interdependences . Thereby , physical activity seems to play an essential role regarding the prevention and rehabilitation of LBP . In consequence , physical activity and exercise therapy is an integral part of musculoskeletal rehabilitation in LBP . However , adherence to self-directed exercise and implementing a health-enhancing physical activity in daily routine after rehabilitation is a common problem for patients and only a few patients integrate health-enhancing physical activity and/or sport activities in their lifestyle . The present paper describes a comprehensive multilevel approach combining face-to-face intervention , telephone and internet aftercare ( Movement Coaching ) . Aim of the trial presented in this study protocol is to evaluate effectiveness of Movement Coaching compared to a control intervention . The study is a prospective , single-blinded , monocenter randomized controlled trial ( RCT ) with three measuring points : T1 = start of inpatient rehabilitation ; T2 = six months follow-up ; T3 = twelve months follow-up . In total , 412 patients were recruited . The intervention involves small-group face-to-face contact during inpatient rehabilitation ( two times , week 2 & 3 ) and telephone aftercare ( week 8 & week 12 after rehabilitation ) as well as internet-based aftercare ( web 2.0 platform ; available until six months after rehabilitation ) . Primary outcome is physical activity , assessed by GPAQ questionnaire . The final data collection is expected by April 2015 . Due to the burden of physical inactivity , there is a need to develop , evaluate and disseminate approaches that are effective in promoting physical activity and especially promoting the maintenance of physical activity in relevant target groups . Considering the high prevalence and socioeconomic impact of low back pain and its multifactorial etiology , low back pain patients seem to be a relevant target group for physical activity promotion . A multilevel approach to bridge the interface of ( inpatient ) rehabilitation and self-directed physical activity will help to target group-specific PA promotion . German Clinical Trials Register ( DRKS ) - ID : DRKS00004878 .
rewrite: Chronic low back pain is a multifaceted syndrome involving interconnected bio-psycho-social factors. Consequently, physical activity is crucial for both preventing and rehabilitating LBP. As a result, exercise therapy forms a core component of musculoskeletal rehabilitation for LBP. Yet, maintaining self-directed exercise and incorporating health-enhancing physical activity into daily life post-rehabilitation remains a widespread challenge, with few patients adopting such activities long-term. This paper outlines a comprehensive multilevel strategy integrating in-person sessions, telephone support, and online aftercare (Movement Coaching). The trial described in this protocol aims to assess the effectiveness of Movement Coaching versus a control intervention. It is a prospective, single-blinded, monocenter randomized controlled trial (RCT) with three assessment points: T1 = start of inpatient rehabilitation; T2 = six-month follow-up; T3 = twelve-month follow-up. A total of 412 patients were enrolled. The intervention includes small-group face-to-face sessions during inpatient rehabilitation (twice, in weeks 2 & 3), telephone follow-ups (weeks 8 & 12 post-rehabilitation), and internet-based aftercare (via a web 2.0 platform available for six months after rehabilitation). The primary outcome is physical activity, measured using the GPAQ questionnaire. Final data collection is anticipated by April 2015. Given the risks of physical inactivity, there is a pressing need to create, test, and implement methods that effectively encourage physical activity and sustain it in key populations. Given the high prevalence, socioeconomic burden, and complex causes of low back pain, LBP patients represent a pertinent target for physical activity promotion. A multilevel approach to connect inpatient rehabilitation with self-managed physical activity can enhance tailored PA promotion for this group. German Clinical Trials Register (DRKS) – ID: DRKS00004878.

text: In the PARAMOUNT ( `` A Phase 3 , Double-Blind , Placebo-Controlled Study of Maintenance Pemetrexed plus Best Supportive Care vs. Best Supportive Care Immediately Following Induction Treatment with Pemetrexed Plus Cisplatin for Advanced Non-Squamous Non-Small-Cell Lung Cancer '' ) trial , patients with advanced nonsquamous non-small-cell lung cancer ( NS-NSCLC ) benefited from pemetrexed maintenance therapy after induction therapy with pemetrexed and cisplatin by extending survival , delaying disease progression , and maintaining quality of life ( QoL ) . However , low-grade 1 or 2 toxicities during long-term maintenance treatment may become burdensome and impact QoL . Patients in this double-blind study ( n = 539 ) , who had completed 4 induction cycles ( pemetrexed with cisplatin ) without progressive disease ( PD ) and had an ECOG performance status of 0/1 , were randomized 2:1 to pemetrexed maintenance ( 500 mg/m ( 2 ) , day 1 ) plus best supportive care ( BSC ) or placebo plus BSC until PD . Adverse events ( by maximum Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events [ CTCAE ] grade ) and QoL ( EuroQol 5-dimensional [ EQ-5D ] scale ) were assessed . A median of 4 maintenance cycles was administered ( range , pemetrexed 1-44 ; mean SD 7.9 8.3 ; placebo 1-38 ; mean SD 5.0 5.2 ) , with 28 % of pemetrexed and 12 % of placebo patients receiving 10 maintenance cycles . The pemetrexed dose intensity was 94 % . More patients receiving pemetrexed ( 12 % ) than placebo discontinued because of possible drug-related CTCAEs ( 4 % ; P = .005 ) . Overall , pemetrexed was associated with significantly more ( P < .05 ) low-grade events ( grade 1/2 nausea , grade 2 anemia , edema , and neutropenia ) than placebo . Overall , the incidence of low-grade fatigue , anemia , and neutropenia decreased with long-term pemetrexed exposure ; however , renal events increased across treatment arms . EQ-5D analyses demonstrated no treatment-by-time interaction or overall treatment differences between the 2 arms . PARAMOUNT demonstrated a low incidence of low-grade toxicities with long-term pemetrexed exposure without compromising QoL in patients with NS-NSCLC .
rewrite: In the PARAMOUNT trial ( "A Phase 3, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Study of Maintenance Pemetrexed plus Best Supportive Care versus Best Supportive Care Following Induction with Pemetrexed and Cisplatin for Advanced Non-Squamous Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer" ), patients with advanced nonsquamous non-small-cell lung cancer (NS-NSCLC) experienced survival extension, delayed disease progression, and preserved quality of life (QoL) with pemetrexed maintenance after pemetrexed-cisplatin induction. Yet, persistent low-grade (1/2) toxicities during prolonged maintenance could become onerous and affect QoL. This double-blind study enrolled 539 patients who, after four induction cycles (pemetrexed plus cisplatin) without progressive disease (PD) and with ECOG 0/1, were randomized 2:1 to pemetrexed maintenance (500 mg/m², day 1) plus best supportive care (BSC) or placebo plus BSC until PD. Adverse events (by maximum CTCAE grade) and QoL (EQ-5D scale) were evaluated. A median of 4 maintenance cycles was given (range: pemetrexed 1–44, mean ± SD 7.9 ± 8.3; placebo 1–38, mean ± SD 5.0 ± 5.2), with 28% on pemetrexed and 12% on placebo receiving ≥10 cycles. Pemetrexed dose intensity was 94%. More pemetrexed patients (12%) than placebo (4%) discontinued due to possibly drug-related CTCAEs (P = .005). Overall, pemetrexed led to significantly more (P < .05) low-grade events (grade 1/2 nausea, grade 2 anemia, edema, neutropenia) than placebo. While low-grade fatigue, anemia, and neutropenia incidence declined with long-term pemetrexed exposure, renal events increased in both arms. EQ-5D analyses showed no treatment-by-time interaction or overall QoL differences between arms. PARAMOUNT indicated a low incidence of low-grade toxicities with extended pemetrexed use, without detriment to QoL in NS-NSCLC patients.

text: In Korean medicine , the steamed root of Panax ginseng C.A. Meyer , known as Korean red ginseng ( KRG ) , is used to invigorate the body , enhance qi , and improve blood flow . It is a potential treatment for cold hypersensitivity in the hands and feet ( CHHF ) , a common complaint among Asians , especially women . However , few studies of its efficacy and safety for CHHF have been conducted . This randomized , double-blind , placebo-controlled trial included 80 female patients with CHHF at Kyung Hee University Hospital at Gangdong , Seoul , Korea . The participants took six capsules of 500-mg KRG powder or placebo twice daily for 8 weeks and were followed up for 4 weeks . The primary outcome measure was change in skin temperature of the hands . The secondary outcome measures included change in skin temperature of the feet , visual analog scale ( VAS ) scores of CHHF severity , recovered temperature ( RT ) of the hands after cold stress test , distal-dorsal difference ( DDD ) in temperature of the hands , power variables of heart rate variability ( HRV ) , and 36-item Short-Form Health Survey ( SF-36 ) scores . The KRG group had significantly higher skin temperature of the hands and feet , lower VAS scores , higher RT of the right 5th finger , and less parasympathetic activity than the placebo group at 8 weeks . No significant differences were noted in DDD of the hands and SF-36 scores . No serious adverse events were reported during the study . Peripheral vasodilation by KRG may alleviate CHHF . Further controlled studies are required to elucidate the effects of KRG on the autonomic nervous system .
rewrite: In Korean medicine, the steamed root of Panax ginseng C.A. Meyer, referred to as Korean red ginseng (KRG), is employed to strengthen the body, boost qi, and promote circulation. It shows potential for treating cold hypersensitivity in the hands and feet (CHHF), a frequent issue among Asians, particularly women. Yet, limited research exists on its effectiveness and safety for CHHF. This randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial involved 80 female CHHF patients at Kyung Hee University Hospital in Gangdong, Seoul, Korea. Participants consumed six capsules of 500-mg KRG powder or placebo twice daily for 8 weeks, with a 4-week follow-up. The primary outcome was change in hand skin temperature. Secondary outcomes included foot skin temperature changes, CHHF severity visual analog scale (VAS) scores, recovered temperature (RT) of the hands post-cold stress test, distal-dorsal difference (DDD) in hand temperature, heart rate variability (HRV) power variables, and 36-item Short-Form Health Survey (SF-36) scores. At 8 weeks, the KRG group showed significantly higher hand and foot skin temperatures, lower VAS scores, higher RT in the right 5th finger, and reduced parasympathetic activity compared to placebo. No significant differences were found in hand DDD or SF-36 scores. No serious adverse events occurred. KRG may relieve CHHF through peripheral vasodilation. Additional controlled studies are needed to clarify KRG's effects on the autonomic nervous system.

text: To compare the rates of neonatal morbidity and cerebral palsy among preterm neonates ( less than 37 weeks of gestation ) delivered by cesarean for a nonreassuring fetal heart rate ( FHR ) tracing compared with those who did not . This was a secondary analysis of a multicenter randomized trial of MgSO4 for the prevention of cerebral palsy . Newborns of women delivered by cesarean delivery for nonreassuring FHR were compared with a control group composed of the offspring of women who labored for 2 hours or longer but did not undergo cesarean delivery for nonreassuring FHR regardless of the mode of delivery . Using multivariable analysis to adjust for potential confounders , our objective was to compare two outcomes : 1 ) composite neonatal morbidity ( Apgar score 3 or less at 5 minutes , seizure , sepsis , necrotizing enterocolitis grade II or III , intraventricular hemorrhage grade III or IV , or death before discharge ) and 2 ) neurologic injury ( cerebral palsy ) at 2 years or more of corrected age between the groups . Of the 1,291 preterm neonates who met the inclusion criteria , 177 ( 14 % ) were delivered by cesarean for nonreassuring FHR compared with 1,114 ( 86 % ) in the control group . Composite neonatal morbidity was similar between the groups ( 30.5 compared with 22.2 % , adjusted odds ratio [ OR ] 1.4 , 95 % confidence interval [ CI ] 0.9-2 .1 ) . The rate of cerebral palsy of any severity ( 8.3 compared with 4.0 % , adjusted OR 2.3 , 95 % CI 1.2-4 .5 ) and moderate-to-severe cerebral palsy at 2 years of corrected age ( 6.0 compared with 2.2 % , adjusted OR 3.2 , 95 % CI 1.4-7 .1 ) was significantly higher in children born through cesarean delivery for nonreassuring FHR . Nonreassuring fetal tracing deemed so serious as to require cesarean delivery is associated with an increased risk of cerebral palsy in preterm neonates . II .
rewrite: This study aimed to compare neonatal morbidity and cerebral palsy rates in preterm neonates (<37 weeks gestation) delivered by cesarean due to nonreassuring fetal heart rate (FHR) tracings versus those who were not. It was a secondary analysis of a multicenter randomized trial on MgSO4 for cerebral palsy prevention. Newborns from cesarean deliveries for nonreassuring FHR were compared to a control group comprising offspring of women who labored ≥2 hours and did not have a cesarean for nonreassuring FHR, irrespective of final delivery mode. Using multivariable analysis to adjust for confounders, we compared: 1) composite neonatal morbidity (Apgar ≤3 at 5 minutes, seizure, sepsis, necrotizing enterocolitis grade II/III, intraventricular hemorrhage grade III/IV, or death before discharge) and 2) neurologic injury (cerebral palsy) at ≥2 years corrected age. Among 1,291 eligible preterm neonates, 177 (14%) were delivered by cesarean for nonreassuring FHR versus 1,114 (86%) controls. Composite neonatal morbidity was similar between groups (30.5% vs. 22.2%; adjusted OR 1.4, 95% CI 0.9–2.1). However, rates of any cerebral palsy (8.3% vs. 4.0%; adjusted OR 2.3, 95% CI 1.2–4.5) and moderate-to-severe cerebral palsy at ≥2 years corrected age (6.0% vs. 2.2%; adjusted OR 3.2, 95% CI 1.4–7.1) were significantly higher in the cesarean for nonreassuring FHR group. Thus, nonreassuring FHR severe enough to prompt cesarean delivery is linked to an elevated cerebral palsy risk in preterm neonates. II.

text: To evaluate the efficacy of a marketed stabilized stannous fluoride ( SnF2 ) dentifrice in reducing dentinal hypersensitivity as compared to a marketed sodium fluoride ( NaF ) / triclosan dentifrice over an eight-week period . Adults with confirmed dentinal hypersensitivity were enrolled in this randomized and controlled , parallel group , double blind , eight-week , single-center clinical trial . Random assignment to one of two dentifrice test groups via age , gender , and thermal sensitivity of enrolled test teeth was performed at baseline , with subjects assigned to twice-daily unsupervised brushing with either the marketed SnF2 dentifrice ( Oral-B Pro-Expert , 0.454 % SnF2 plus 0.077 % NaF ) or the marketed 0.32 % NaF with 0.3 % triclosan/copolymer dentifrice control ( Colgate Total Advanced ) . Tactile sensitivity ( Yeaple Probe ) and thermal sensitivity ( airblast/Schiff Air Index ) evaluations of the selected test teeth were performed at baseline pre-treatment , and again at Weeks 2 and 8 of product use to compare the dentifrices ' relative hypersensitivity protection effectiveness . Ninety-seven ( 97 ) of the 100 enrolled subjects completed the trial and were fully evaluable . At both Week 2 and Week 8 , for both the thermal and tactile evaluation measurements , subjects brushing with the marketed SnF2 dentifrice experienced statistically significantly ( p < 0.0001 ) superior average dentinal hypersensitivity improvement versus subjects assigned to the NaF/triclosan control dentifrice . Between groups , superior relative mean reduction in thermal Schiff Air Index favored SnF2 by 24 % at Week 2 and 68 % at Week 8 , while greater relative mean tactile Yeaple Probe benefits were observed for SnF2 relative to the control by 114 % after Week 2 and 184 % at Week 8 . The dentifrices were well-tolerated . Twice-daily brushing with a marketed SnF2 dentifrice provided superior dentinal hypersensitivity improvement versus a commercially available NaF/triclosan dentifrice , with significantly ( p < 0.0001 ) greater relief after two weeks , and even larger relative benefits at eight weeks .
rewrite: This study assessed the effectiveness of a commercial stabilized stannous fluoride (SnF₂) toothpaste in reducing dentinal hypersensitivity compared to a marketed sodium fluoride (NaF)/triclosan toothpaste over eight weeks. Adults with confirmed dentinal hypersensitivity participated in this randomized, controlled, parallel-group, double-blind, eight-week, single-center clinical trial. At baseline, participants were randomly assigned to one of two toothpaste groups, stratified by age, gender, and thermal sensitivity of the test teeth. Subjects brushed twice daily unsupervised with either the marketed SnF₂ toothpaste (Oral-B Pro-Expert, containing 0.454% SnF₂ and 0.077% NaF) or the control toothpaste with 0.32% NaF and 0.3% triclosan/copolymer (Colgate Total Advanced). Tactile sensitivity (using a Yeaple Probe) and thermal sensitivity (via airblast/Schiff Air Index) were evaluated on selected teeth at baseline before treatment, and again after 2 and 8 weeks of product use to compare the relative hypersensitivity protection of the toothpastes. Ninety-seven of the 100 enrolled subjects completed the trial and were fully evaluable. At both Week 2 and Week 8, for both thermal and tactile measures, subjects using the marketed SnF₂ toothpaste showed statistically significant (p < 0.0001) greater average improvement in dentinal hypersensitivity compared to those using the NaF/triclosan control toothpaste. Between groups, the superior relative mean reduction in thermal Schiff Air Index favored SnF₂ by 24% at Week 2 and 68% at Week 8, while greater relative mean tactile benefits on the Yeaple Probe were observed for SnF₂, exceeding the control by 114% after Week 2 and 184% at Week 8. Both toothpastes were well-tolerated. Twice-daily use of the marketed SnF₂ toothpaste provided superior improvement in dentinal hypersensitivity versus the commercially available NaF/triclosan toothpaste, with significantly (p < 0.0001) greater relief after two weeks and even larger relative benefits at eight weeks.

text: The association between the interleukin IL1 beta gene polymorphisms SNP-511 and SNP +3953 and susceptibility to the development of Hashimoto 's thyroiditis among adult Caucasian-Polish population were analyzed . The group studied comprised of 115 unrelated patients with Hashimoto 's thyroiditis ( 112 women and 3 men , mean age 53.3 years ) . All patients were euthyroid on thyroid replacement therapy , had extremely high serum anti-TPO levels and in 53 patients anti-TG levels were also increased . The control group consisted of 103 healthy blood donors without raised anti-TPO antibodies , in whom a personal and familial history of thyroid , autoimmune and inflammatory diseases was excluded . No goiter or thyroid dysfunction was found .2 polymorphisms of the IL1 beta were studied by PCR-RFLP analysis . To confirm the accuracy of the method used , randomly selected patients were analyzed by direct sequencing . In both groups allele frequencies were in Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium . The significant statistical differences between the frequency of C and T allele for both SNPs ( C-511T and C +3953 T ) in the group studied and in the controls were found ( p = 0.0081 ; OR = 1.846 ; 95 % CI : 1.183-2 .878 and p = 0.0099 ; OR = 1.953 ; 95 % CI : 1.183-3 .224 ) . The frequencies of the genotype C-511C compared to C-511T and T-511T as well as C +3953 C compared to C +3953 T and T +3953 T also differed significantly ( p = 0.0057 ; OR = 2.248 ; 95 % CI : 1.292-3 .912 and p = 0.0043 ; OR = 2.338 ; 95 % CI : 1.305-4 .191 ) between patients and controls . An association between the SNPs of the IL1 beta and susceptibility to Hashimoto 's thyroiditis among the group of Caucasian-Polish population studied was found .
rewrite: The study examined the link between IL1 beta gene polymorphisms SNP-511 and SNP+3953 and the risk of Hashimoto's thyroiditis in an adult Caucasian-Polish population. The patient group included 115 unrelated individuals with Hashimoto's thyroiditis (112 women, 3 men; mean age 53.3 years). All patients were euthyroid on thyroid replacement therapy, had very high serum anti-TPO levels, and 53 also showed elevated anti-TG levels. The control group comprised 103 healthy blood donors without elevated anti-TPO antibodies and no personal or family history of thyroid, autoimmune, or inflammatory diseases. No goiter or thyroid dysfunction was present. The two IL1 beta polymorphisms were analyzed using PCR-RFLP. Direct sequencing was performed on randomly selected patients to verify method accuracy. Allele frequencies in both groups followed Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium. Significant differences were observed in the frequencies of C and T alleles for both SNPs (C-511T and C+3953T) between patients and controls (p=0.0081; OR=1.846; 95% CI: 1.183–2.878 and p=0.0099; OR=1.953; 95% CI: 1.183–3.224). Genotype frequencies for C-511C versus C-511T and T-511T, and for C+3953C versus C+3953T and T+3953T, also differed significantly (p=0.0057; OR=2.248; 95% CI: 1.292–3.912 and p=0.0043; OR=2.338; 95% CI: 1.305–4.191). The findings indicate an association between IL1 beta SNPs and susceptibility to Hashimoto's thyroiditis in the studied Caucasian-Polish population.

text: To evaluate the thermal antinociceptive and sedative effects and duration of action of tramadol hydrochloride after oral administration to American kestrels ( Falco sparverius ) . 12 healthy 3-year-old American kestrels . Tramadol ( 5 , 15 , and 30 mg/kg ) and a control suspension were administered orally in a masked randomized crossover experimental design . Foot withdrawal response to a thermal stimulus was determined 1 hour before ( baseline ) and 0.5 , 1.5 , 3 , 6 , and 9 hours after treatment . Agitation-sedation scores were determined 3 to 5 minutes before each thermal stimulus test . The lowest dose of tramadol evaluated ( 5 mg/kg ) significantly increased the thermal foot withdrawal thresholds for up to 1.5 hours after administration , compared with control treatment values , and for up to 9 hours after administration , compared with baseline values . Tramadol at doses of 15 and 30 mg/kg significantly increased thermal thresholds at 0.5 hours after administration , compared with control treatment values , and up to 3 hours after administration , compared with baseline values . No significant differences in agitation-sedation scores were detected between tramadol and control treatments . Results indicated oral administration of 5 mg of tramadol/kg significantly increased thermal nociception thresholds for kestrels for 1.5 hours , compared with a control treatment , and 9 hours , compared with baseline values ; higher doses resulted in less pronounced antinociceptive effects . Additional studies with other types of stimulation , formulations , dosages , routes of administration , and testing times would be needed to fully evaluate the analgesic and adverse effects of tramadol in kestrels and other avian species .
rewrite: To assess the thermal antinociceptive and sedative effects, as well as the duration of action, of orally administered tramadol hydrochloride in American kestrels (Falco sparverius). Twelve healthy 3-year-old American kestrels were used. Tramadol (at 5, 15, and 30 mg/kg) and a control suspension were given orally in a masked, randomized crossover design. The foot withdrawal response to a thermal stimulus was measured 1 hour before (baseline) and at 0.5, 1.5, 3, 6, and 9 hours post-treatment. Agitation-sedation scores were recorded 3 to 5 minutes before each thermal test. The lowest tramadol dose (5 mg/kg) significantly raised thermal foot withdrawal thresholds for up to 1.5 hours compared to control, and up to 9 hours relative to baseline. Doses of 15 and 30 mg/kg significantly increased thresholds at 0.5 hours versus control, and up to 3 hours compared to baseline. No significant differences in agitation-sedation scores were found between tramadol and control treatments. Findings showed that 5 mg/kg of tramadol orally significantly elevated thermal nociception thresholds in kestrels for 1.5 hours relative to control and 9 hours versus baseline; higher doses produced less marked antinociceptive effects. Further research involving varied stimuli, formulations, dosages, administration routes, and testing intervals is necessary to comprehensively evaluate tramadol's analgesic and adverse effects in kestrels and other bird species.

text: Male and female condom ( FC ) functional performance failure declines with user experience . With the recent availability of a wider range of FCs , it is important to know if women with experience in using one type of FC are more proficient in using another type , even if the FC design is quite different . A randomized , noninferiority crossover clinical trial assessed the function of four FCs ( FC2 , Woman 's Condom , Cupid and VA w.o.w ) among 300 women in Durban , South Africa . FC functional failure ( breakage , slippage , invagination and misdirection ) by condom type and use period was investigated in women using five FCs of each type ( 20 FC uses in total ) . Of the 5364 condoms used during intercourse by 272 women , 200 clinical failures occurred in 195 condoms ( 190 condoms had one failure , and 5 had two failures ) . Total clinical failure was comparable across FC types . Of the 195 condoms in which failures occurred , the number of failures in the first condom use period was 103 ( 7.7 % ) , decreasing to 43 events ( 3.2 % ) in the second , 33 ( 2.5 % ) in the third and 16 ( 1.2 % ) in the fourth . Only 2 failures were reported in the 20th use of an FC compared to 29 in the first use , irrespective of condom type . FC failure rates decreased markedly after use of the first five condoms regardless of FC type and continued to fall across the next three use periods . FC failure rates decrease over 20 uses , regardless of FC condom type used . The decrease is higher at the beginning of use , indicating that improvement is greatest after the first five uses .
rewrite: Functional failure rates for male and female condoms (FC) diminish as users gain experience. Given the broader selection of FCs now available, it is crucial to determine whether women experienced with one FC type can effectively use another, even with distinct designs. A randomized, noninferiority crossover trial evaluated four FCs (FC2, Woman’s Condom, Cupid, and VA w.o.w.) in 300 women in Durban, South Africa. Functional failures (breakage, slippage, invagination, misdirection) by condom type and use period were examined, with each woman using five of each type (20 total FC uses). Among 5364 condoms used by 272 women during intercourse, 200 clinical failures occurred in 195 condoms (190 had one failure, 5 had two). Total clinical failure rates were similar across FC types. Of the 195 condoms with failures, 103 failures (7.7%) occurred in the first use period, declining to 43 (3.2%) in the second, 33 (2.5%) in the third, and 16 (1.2%) in the fourth. Only 2 failures were reported by the 20th FC use, versus 29 in the first, regardless of type. Failure rates dropped sharply after the first five condom uses, irrespective of FC type, and continued to decline over the next three periods. FC failure rates decrease over 20 uses, independent of condom type. The reduction is most pronounced initially, with the greatest improvement seen after the first five uses.

text: verification of a hypothesis assuming that 5-HT3 receptor blockade by intravenous administration of ondansetron reduces the incidence of hypotension and bradycardia in patients undergoing spinal anaesthesia for Caesarean section . The study design was approved by the Bioethics Committee and included 72 patients undergoing elective Caesarean section , randomly assigned to ondansetron group ( group 0 ) or placebo group ( group P ) . Finally group 0 encompassed 35 patients administered ondansetron 8 mg i.v. dissolved in 10 ml 0.9 % NaCl whereas group P consisted of 34 patients receiving 0.9 % NaCl 10 mg . Systolic and diastolic pressures were measured every 2 minutes since the onset of anaesthesia . Heart rate ( HR ) was monitored continuously The criterion of hypotension requiring ephedrine was a decrease in systolic pressure by 20 % compared to its baseline value or a decrease in systolic pressure below 90 mm Hg . The criterion of bradycardia was a decrease in HR below 60/min . Hypotension was observed in 14 group 0 patients ( 39 % ) and in 15 group P patients ( 44 % ) ; the difference was not statistically significant . Bradycardia was noted in 1 group 0 patient ( 3 % ) and in 2 group P patients ( 6 % ) ; the difference was not statistically significant . A hypothesis assuming a reduction in pressure following subarachnoid anaesthesia for Caesarean section after the administration of 8 mg of ondansetron was not confirmed .
rewrite: This study tested the hypothesis that intravenous ondansetron, by blocking 5-HT3 receptors, reduces hypotension and bradycardia during spinal anesthesia for Caesarean section. Approved by the Bioethics Committee, it involved 72 elective Caesarean patients randomly assigned to receive either ondansetron (Group O, n=35) or a placebo (Group P, n=34). Group O received 8 mg ondansetron in 10 ml 0.9% NaCl, while Group P received 10 ml of 0.9% NaCl alone. Systolic and diastolic blood pressures were recorded every two minutes from anesthesia onset, and heart rate was continuously monitored. Hypotension, defined as a ≥20% drop from baseline systolic pressure or a reading below 90 mm Hg, triggered ephedrine use. Bradycardia was defined as a heart rate below 60 bpm. Hypotension occurred in 14 patients (39%) in Group O and 15 (44%) in Group P, a non-significant difference. Bradycardia was noted in 1 patient (3%) in Group O and 2 (6%) in Group P, also a non-significant difference. The hypothesis that 8 mg of ondansetron reduces post-spinal hypotension in Caesarean section was not confirmed.

text: Neck pain , common among the elderly population , has considerable implications on health and quality of life . Evidence supports the use of spinal manipulative therapy ( SMT ) and exercise to treat neck pain ; however , no studies to date have evaluated the effectiveness of these therapies specifically in seniors . To assess the relative effectiveness of SMT and supervised rehabilitative exercise , both in combination with and compared to home exercise ( HE ) alone for neck pain in individuals ages 65 years or older . Randomized clinical trial . Individuals 65 years of age or older with a primary complaint of mechanical neck pain , rated 3 ( 0-10 ) for 12 weeks or longer in duration . Patient self-report outcomes were collected at baseline and 4 , 12 , 26 , and 52 weeks after randomization . The primary outcome was pain , measured by an 11-box numerical rating scale . Secondary outcomes included disability ( Neck Disability Index ) , general health status ( Medical Outcomes Study Short Form-36 ) , satisfaction ( 7-point scale ) , improvement ( 9-point scale ) , and medication use ( days per week ) . This study was funded by the US Department of Health and Human Services , Health Resources and Services Administration . Linear mixed model analyses were used for comparisons at individual time points and for short - and long-term analyses . Blinded evaluations of objective outcomes were performed at baseline and 12 weeks . Adverse event data were collected at each treatment visit . A total of 241 participants were randomized , with 95 % reporting primary outcome data at all time points . After 12 weeks of treatment , the SMT with home exercise group demonstrated a 10 % greater decrease in pain compared with the HE-alone group , and 5 % change over supervised plus home exercise . A decrease in pain favoring supervised plus HE over HE alone did not reach statistical significance . Compared with the HE group , both combination groups reported greater improvement at week 12 and more satisfaction at all time points . Multivariate longitudinal analysis incorporating primary and secondary patient-rated outcomes showed that the SMT with HE group was superior to the HE-alone group in both the short - and long-term . No serious adverse events were observed as a result of the study treatments . SMT with HE resulted in greater pain reduction after 12 weeks of treatment compared with both supervised plus HE and HE alone . Supervised exercise sessions added little benefit to the HE-alone program .
rewrite: Neck pain, frequently experienced by older adults, significantly impacts health and quality of life. While spinal manipulative therapy (SMT) and exercise are evidence-based treatments for neck pain, their effectiveness has not been specifically studied in seniors. This study aimed to evaluate the relative effectiveness of SMT and supervised rehabilitative exercise, both combined with and compared to home exercise (HE) alone, for neck pain in individuals aged 65 years or older. A randomized clinical trial was conducted with participants 65 or older having mechanical neck pain rated ≥3 (0-10 scale) for at least 12 weeks. Patient-reported outcomes were gathered at baseline and at 4, 12, 26, and 52 weeks post-randomization. The primary outcome was pain, assessed using an 11-point numerical rating scale. Secondary outcomes included disability (Neck Disability Index), general health status (SF-36), satisfaction (7-point scale), improvement (9-point scale), and medication use (days per week). Funding was provided by the US Department of Health and Human Services, Health Resources and Services Administration. Linear mixed models were used for comparisons at specific time points and for short- and long-term analyses. Blinded assessments of objective outcomes occurred at baseline and 12 weeks. Adverse events were recorded at each treatment visit. Of 241 randomized participants, 95% provided primary outcome data at all time points. After 12 weeks, the SMT with HE group showed a 10% greater pain reduction than the HE-alone group and a 5% greater reduction than supervised exercise plus HE. The difference in pain reduction favoring supervised exercise plus HE over HE alone was not statistically significant. Both combination groups reported greater improvement at week 12 and higher satisfaction at all time points compared to the HE group. Multivariate longitudinal analysis of patient-rated outcomes indicated the SMT with HE group was superior to HE alone in both short- and long-term assessments. No serious adverse events were reported from the treatments. SMT with HE led to greater pain reduction after 12 weeks compared to both supervised exercise plus HE and HE alone. Supervised exercise provided minimal additional benefit over the HE-alone program.

text: Motive-oriented therapeutic relationship ( MOTR ) was postulated to be a particularly helpful therapeutic ingredient in the early treatment phase of patients with personality disorders , in particular with borderline personality disorder ( BPD ) . The present randomized controlled study using an add-on design is the first study to test this assumption in a 10-session general psychiatric treatment with patients presenting with BPD on symptom reduction and therapeutic alliance . A total of 85 patients were randomized . They were either allocated to a manual-based short variant of the general psychiatric management ( GPM ) treatment ( in 10 sessions ) or to the same treatment where MOTR was deliberately added to the treatment . Treatment attrition and integrity analyses yielded satisfactory results . The results of the intent-to-treat analyses suggested a global efficacy of MOTR , in the sense of an additional reduction of general problems , i.e. symptoms , interpersonal and social problems ( F1 , 73 = 7.25 , p < 0.05 ) . However , they also showed that MOTR did not yield an additional reduction of specific borderline symptoms . It was also shown that a stronger therapeutic alliance , as assessed by the therapist , developed in MOTR treatments compared to GPM ( Z55 = 0.99 , p < 0.04 ) . These results suggest that adding MOTR to psychiatric and psychotherapeutic treatments of BPD is promising . Moreover , the findings shed additional light on the perspective of shortening treatments for patients presenting with BPD .
rewrite: The motive-oriented therapeutic relationship (MOTR) was proposed as a particularly beneficial component in the initial treatment phase for personality disorders, especially borderline personality disorder (BPD). This randomized controlled study, employing an add-on design, is the first to examine this hypothesis within a 10-session general psychiatric treatment for BPD patients, focusing on symptom reduction and therapeutic alliance. Eighty-five patients were randomized to either a manual-based short version of general psychiatric management (GPM) treatment (10 sessions) or the same treatment with MOTR intentionally integrated. Treatment attrition and integrity analyses produced satisfactory outcomes. Intent-to-treat analyses indicated a global efficacy for MOTR, evidenced by an additional decrease in general issues, such as symptoms, interpersonal, and social problems (F1, 73 = 7.25, p < 0.05). However, they also revealed that MOTR did not lead to an extra reduction in specific borderline symptoms. Additionally, therapists reported a stronger therapeutic alliance in MOTR treatments compared to GPM (Z55 = 0.99, p < 0.04). These findings imply that incorporating MOTR into psychiatric and psychotherapeutic approaches for BPD holds promise. Furthermore, the results offer further insight into the potential for shortening treatments for individuals with BPD.

text: Obesity is a chronic condition related to serious morbidity and mortality of increasing incidence and prevalence . Several studies show a significantly higher weight loss with acupuncture treatment . This is the first prospective , randomized , double-blinded study , testing the effects of auricular electroacupuncture on weight loss in obese female patients . 56 female obese patients ( age > 18 , Body Mass Index , BMI > 25 ) were randomized to receive either auricular acupuncture with electrical stimulation with a P-Stim device ( verum group , n = 28 ) or placebo treatment with a P-Stim dummy ( n = 28 ) for four days . Three auricular acupuncture points were chosen ( hunger 18 , stomach 87 and colon 91 ) . The treatment was performed once a week for a period of six weeks . A follow-up visit was performed after 4 weeks . At each visit body weight , BMI ( Body Mass Index ) and body fat were measured . Relative reduction of body weight was significantly greater in the verum group ( -3.73 % ; CI = -4.70 to -2.76 ) than in the placebo group ( -0.70 % ; CI = -1.57 to +0.16 ; p < 0.001 ) In addition we also observed a significant reduction of BMI ( p < 0.001 ) in the verum group ( -3.62 % ; CI = -4.39 to -2.84 ) compared to placebo ( -0.82 % ; CI = -1.55 to -0.10 ; p < 0.001 ) . No patient reported side effects related to acupuncture . In conclusion electrical auricular acupuncture could be a safe , additive , non-pharmacological treatment in obese patients .
rewrite: Obesity is a chronic condition associated with significant morbidity and mortality, with rising incidence and prevalence. Multiple studies indicate notably greater weight reduction through acupuncture therapy. This pioneering prospective, randomized, double-blinded study examines the impact of auricular electroacupuncture on weight loss in obese female patients. 56 obese female participants (age > 18, BMI > 25) were randomly assigned to receive either auricular acupuncture with electrical stimulation via a P-Stim device (verum group, n = 28) or placebo treatment using a P-Stim dummy (n = 28) over four days. Three auricular acupuncture points were selected (hunger 18, stomach 87, and colon 91). Treatments were administered weekly for six weeks, with a follow-up assessment after 4 weeks. At each session, body weight, BMI, and body fat were recorded. The verum group showed a significantly larger relative reduction in body weight (-3.73%; CI = -4.70 to -2.76) compared to the placebo group (-0.70%; CI = -1.57 to +0.16; p < 0.001). Additionally, a marked decrease in BMI was observed in the verum group (-3.62%; CI = -4.39 to -2.84) versus placebo (-0.82%; CI = -1.55 to -0.10; p < 0.001). No participants reported acupuncture-related side effects. In summary, electrical auricular acupuncture may offer a safe, supplementary, non-pharmacological approach for managing obesity.

text: Rates of self-harm are high and have recently increased . This trend and the repetitive nature of self-harm pose a significant challenge to mental health services . To determine the efficacy of a structured group problem-solving skills training ( PST ) programme as an intervention approach for self-harm in addition to treatment as usual ( TAU ) as offered by mental health services . A total of 433 participants ( aged 18-64 years ) were randomly assigned to TAU plus PST or TAU alone . Assessments were carried out at baseline and at 6-week and 6-month follow-up and repeated hospital-treated self-harm was ascertained at 12-month follow-up . The treatment groups did not differ in rates of repeated self-harm at 6-week , 6-month and 12-month follow-up . Both treatment groups showed significant improvements in psychological and social functioning at follow-up . Only one measure ( needing and receiving practical help from those closest to them ) showed a positive treatment effect at 6-week ( P = 0.004 ) and 6-month ( P = 0.01 ) follow-up . Repetition was not associated with waiting time in the PST group . This brief intervention for self-harm is no more effective than treatment as usual . Further work is required to establish whether a modified , more intensive programme delivered sooner after the index episode would be effective .
rewrite: Self-harm rates are elevated and have risen recently. This pattern, along with the recurrent nature of self-harm, presents a major challenge for mental health services. The study aimed to assess the effectiveness of a structured group problem-solving skills training (PST) program as an intervention for self-harm, in addition to treatment as usual (TAU) provided by mental health services. A total of 433 participants (aged 18–64 years) were randomly assigned to receive TAU plus PST or TAU alone. Evaluations were conducted at baseline, 6-week, and 6-month follow-ups, with repeated hospital-treated self-harm recorded at 12 months. The treatment groups showed no difference in rates of repeated self-harm at 6-week, 6-month, and 12-month follow-ups. Both groups demonstrated significant improvements in psychological and social functioning over time. Only one measure—needing and receiving practical help from close individuals—showed a positive treatment effect at 6-week (P = 0.004) and 6-month (P = 0.01) follow-ups. Repetition was not linked to waiting time in the PST group. This brief intervention for self-harm is not more effective than treatment as usual. Further research is needed to determine if a modified, more intensive program delivered shortly after the initial episode would be beneficial.

text: The authors analyzed headache relief after anterior cervical discectomy . Headache may be relieved after anterior cervical discectomy , but the mechanism is unknown . If headaches were directly referred from upper cervical pathology , more headache relief would be expected from surgery performed at higher cervical levels . If spinal kinesthetics were the mechanism , then headache relief may differ between arthroplasty and fusion . Headache relief after anterior cervical discectomy was quantified by the operated disc level and by the method of operation ( arthroplasty vs arthrodesis ) . The authors performed a post hoc analysis of an artificial disc trial . Data on headache pain were extracted from the Neck Disability Index ( NDI ) questionnaire . A total of 260 patients underwent single-level arthroplasty or arthodesis . Preoperatively , 52 % reported NDI headache scores of 3 or greater , compared with only 13 % -17 % postoperatively . The model-based mean NDI headache score at baseline was 2.5 ( 95 % CI 2.3-2 .7 ) and was reduced by 1.3 points after surgery ( 95 % CI 1.2-1 .4 , p < 0.001 ) . Higher cervical levels were associated with a greater degree of preoperative headache , but there was no association with headache relief . There was no significant difference in headache relief between arthroplasty and arthrodesis . Most patients with symptomatic cervical spondylosis have headache as a preoperative symptom ( 88 % ) . Anterior cervical discectomy with both arthroplasty and arthrodesis is associated with a durable decrease in headache . Headache relief is not related to the level of operation . The mechanism for headache reduction remains unclear .
rewrite: The authors examined headache improvement following anterior cervical discectomy. While headaches may diminish after this procedure, the underlying mechanism is not understood. If headaches were directly referred from upper cervical pathology, greater relief would be anticipated from surgery at higher cervical levels. If spinal kinematics were involved, headache relief might vary between arthroplasty and fusion. The extent of headache relief after anterior cervical discectomy was assessed by the operated disc level and surgical method (arthroplasty versus arthrodesis). A post hoc analysis of an artificial disc trial was conducted. Headache pain data were obtained from the Neck Disability Index (NDI) questionnaire. In total, 260 patients received single-level arthroplasty or arthrodesis. Preoperatively, 52% reported NDI headache scores of 3 or higher, compared to only 13%–17% postoperatively. The model-based mean baseline NDI headache score was 2.5 (95% CI 2.3–2.7), decreasing by 1.3 points after surgery (95% CI 1.2–1.4, p < 0.001).
